questions.explanation: 4, 8, 16, 32 has differences 4, 8, 16, which are not equal, so it is not arithmetic. The others have constant differences 3, −5 and 0.3.

questions.q: Given the arithmetic sequence 18, 11, 4, −3, …, find the common difference.
questions.hint: Subtract a term from the term after it.

questions.q: Find the common difference of the arithmetic sequence 2.5, 4, 5.5, 7, …
questions.hint: Subtract the first term from the second.

questions.q: Find the common difference d of each arithmetic sequence.
questions.hint: d = (second term) − (first term).

questions.q: Given the arithmetic sequence −20, −14, −8, −2, …, find the common difference.
questions.hint: Be careful subtracting negative numbers.

questions.q: Write an equation for the nth term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 9, 13, 17, …
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d and simplify.

questions.q: Which equation gives the nth term of the arithmetic sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, …?
questions.hint: Find d, then substitute into aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Match each arithmetic sequence with the equation for its nth term.
questions.hint: The coefficient of n is the common difference; check n = 1 gives the first term.

questions.q: For the arithmetic sequence −8, −3, 2, 7, …, complete the following.
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Fill in the values to make an arithmetic sequence: 7, 11, ___, 19, ___.
questions.hint: Find the common difference from the first two terms.

questions.q: Fill in the values to make an arithmetic sequence: 30, ___, 18, ___, 6.
questions.hint: From 30 to 18 takes two equal steps.
questions.explanation: Two steps change the value by 18 − 30 = −12, so d = −6. The terms are 30, 24, 18, 12, 6.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 2 and a₃ = 8. Complete the table.
questions.hint: From a₁ to a₃ is two steps of d.
questions.explanation: 2d = 8 − 2 = 6, so d = 3. Adding 3 each time gives 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17.

questions.q: Which two numbers complete the arithmetic sequence −5, ___, ___, 7?
questions.hint: There are three equal steps from −5 to 7.
questions.explanation: Three steps change the value by 7 − (−5) = 12, so d = 4. The sequence is −5, −1, 3, 7.

questions.q: What is the 30th term of the arithmetic sequence 6, 10, 14, 18, …?
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d with n = 30.

questions.q: What is the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence 50, 47, 44, 41, …?
questions.hint: Multiply d by (n − 1), not by n.

questions.q: For the arithmetic sequence −15, −11, −7, −3, …, complete the table.
questions.hint: aₙ = −15 + (n − 1)(4); for the last row solve for n.

questions.q: Consider the arithmetic sequence 2.5, 4, 5.5, 7, …
questions.hint: d = 1.5; use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Given a₁ = 12 and d = −5, find the equation of the nth term and the next four terms of the arithmetic sequence.
questions.hint: Substitute into aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d, then keep subtracting 5.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = −9 and d = 4. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Add the common difference 4 to get each next term.
questions.explanation: Starting at −9 and adding 4 each time: −5, −1, 3, 7. The equation is aₙ = 4n − 13.

questions.q: Given a₁ = 40 and d = −15, which is the equation of the nth term?
questions.hint: Distribute −15 over (n − 1) carefully.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = −3 and d = 2. Plot its first four terms as points (n, aₙ).
questions.hint: Find a₂, a₃ and a₄ by adding 2 each time.
questions.explanation: The terms are −3, −1, 1, 3, so the points are (1, −3), (2, −1), (3, 1) and (4, 3). They lie on a line with slope 2, the common difference.

questions.q: Given a₁ = 14 and d = −3, write an equation for the nth term and find the 20th term.
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d, then substitute n = 20.

questions.q: Given a₁ = −6 and d = 4, find the 25th term of the arithmetic sequence.
questions.hint: a₂₅ = a₁ + 24d.

questions.q: Given a₁ = 9 and d = 0.5, what is the 11th term of the arithmetic sequence?
questions.hint: Use n − 1 = 10 steps of 0.5.

questions.q: Match each first term and common difference with the equation for the nth term.
questions.hint: Expand a₁ + (n − 1)d for each one.

questions.q: Determine whether each sequence is arithmetic (yes or no). If it is, give d; if not, write none.
questions.hint: Compute every difference between consecutive terms, not just the first one.
questions.explanation: 3, 10, 17, 24 has d = 7. 2, 4, 8, 16 has differences 2, 4, 8 (not arithmetic). 90, 81, 72, 63 has d = −9. 1, −1, 1, −1 alternates −2 and +2 (not arithmetic). −4.5, −3, −1.5, 0 has d = 1.5.

questions.q: Match each sequence with its description.
questions.hint: Subtract consecutive terms and check that the difference never changes.
questions.explanation: 15 − 11 = 4 each time. 34 − 40 = −6 each time. 1, 4, 9, 16 has differences 3, 5, 7, so it is not arithmetic. −7 − (−9) = 2 each time.

questions.q: Which statement about the sequence 5, 12, 19, 27, 34, … is true?
options: It is not arithmetic because the differences are not all equal
questions.hint: Check every difference, including 27 − 19.
questions.explanation: The differences are 7, 7, 8, 7. Because 27 − 19 = 8 is different, there is no common difference, so the sequence is not arithmetic.

questions.q: Which description matches the graph of f(x) = 3 if x < 1, and f(x) = x − 2 if x ≥ 1?
options: A horizontal ray at y = 3 going left from an open circle at (1, 3); a ray with slope 1 going right from a closed dot at (1, 1)
A horizontal ray at y = 3 going right from an open circle at (1, 3); a ray with slope 1 going left from a closed dot at (1, −1)
A horizontal ray at y = 3 going left from a closed dot at (1, 3); a ray with slope 1 going right from an open circle at (1, −1)
A horizontal ray at y = 3 going left from an open circle at (1, 3); a ray with slope 1 going right from a closed dot at (1, −1)
questions.hint: < gives an open circle, ≥ gives a closed dot; evaluate each piece at x = 1.
questions.explanation: The piece f(x) = 3 is used for x < 1, so it goes left and ends with an open circle at (1, 3). The piece x − 2 is used for x ≥ 1; at x = 1 it equals −1, so it starts with a closed dot at (1, −1) and rises to the right with slope 1.

questions.q: For f(x) = x + 3 if x ≤ −1, and f(x) = −2 if x > −1, plot the points (x, f(x)) for x = −3, −1, 0 and 2.
questions.hint: Choose the piece by checking the condition for each x.
questions.explanation: x = −3 and x = −1 satisfy x ≤ −1, so f(−3) = 0 and f(−1) = 2. x = 0 and x = 2 satisfy x > −1, so f(0) = f(2) = −2. The points are (−3, 0), (−1, 2), (0, −2) and (2, −2).

questions.q: Consider f(x) = 4 if x ≤ −2, and f(x) = 2x if x > 1.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At (1, 2), is the circle open or closed?

questions.hint: Each x uses only the piece whose condition it satisfies; values between −2 and 1 are not used at all.
questions.explanation: −5 ≤ −2, so f(−5) = 4. 3 > 1, so f(3) = 2(3) = 6. The second piece uses x > 1, so its endpoint (1, 2) is an open circle. No piece covers −2 < x ≤ 1, so the domain is x ≤ −2 or x > 1.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 0, and f(x) = 3 − x if x ≥ 0.
questions.hint: x = 0 belongs to the second piece because of ≥.

questions.q: A car park charges AED 8 for every hour, and any fraction of an hour is rounded up to the next hour. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Round the time up to the next whole hour, then multiply by 8.
questions.explanation: 0.5 h and 1 h both count as 1 hour: AED 8. 1.25 h counts as 2 hours: AED 16. 3 h is exactly 3 hours: AED 24. 3.1 h counts as 4 hours: AED 32.

questions.q: A boat rental costs AED 20 for every hour, and any fraction of an hour is rounded up. Which describes the graph of cost against hours?
options: Horizontal segments, each with an open circle on its left end and a closed dot on its right end
One straight line through the origin with slope 20
Horizontal segments, each with a closed dot on its left end and an open circle on its right end
questions.hint: What does it cost for exactly 1 hour, and for just over 1 hour?
questions.explanation: Any time from just above 0 up to and including 1 hour costs AED 20, so each step includes its right end (closed dot) but not its left end (open circle). Just after 1 hour the cost jumps to AED 40.

questions.q: A bowling lane costs AED 15 per hour, and any fraction of an hour is rounded up to the next hour. How many dirhams (AED) does it cost to bowl for 2 hours 20 minutes?
questions.hint: Round 2 hours 20 minutes up to whole hours.
questions.explanation: 2 hours 20 minutes is more than 2 hours, so it is charged as 3 hours. 3 × 15 = AED 45.

questions.q: A delivery company charges AED 6 for every kilometre, and any part of a kilometre is rounded up. Match each distance with its charge.
questions.hint: Round each distance up to a whole number of kilometres.
questions.explanation: 0.4 km → 1 km → AED 6. 2 km → 2 km → AED 12. 2.1 km → 3 km → AED 18. 4.9 km → 5 km → AED 30.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = x + 4 if x ≤ −1, and f(x) = −2x + 1 if x > −1.
questions.hint: Use x + 4 for x ≤ −1 and −2x + 1 for x > −1.

questions.q: Find the domain and range of f(x) = x + 2 if x < 0, and f(x) = 5 if x ≥ 0.
questions.hint: Find the y-values each piece produces, then combine them.
questions.explanation: Every real x is used by one of the pieces, so the domain is all real numbers. For x < 0, x + 2 takes all values less than 2. For x ≥ 0 the only value is 5. The range is y < 2 or y = 5.

questions.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2x − 1 if x ≥ 2, and f(x) = −1 if x < 2?
questions.hint: Evaluate 2x − 1 at x = 2 to find where that piece starts.
questions.explanation: For x ≥ 2, 2x − 1 starts at 2(2) − 1 = 3 and increases, giving y ≥ 3. For x < 2 the value is always −1. So the range is y = −1 or y ≥ 3.

questions.q: For f(x) = 3x + 2 if x ≤ 0, and f(x) = x − 4 if x > 0, plot the points (x, f(x)) for x = −2, −1, 0, 2 and 4.
questions.hint: x = 0 uses the first piece because of ≤.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = 2⟦x⟧, where ⟦x⟧ is the greatest integer less than or equal to x.
questions.hint: For negative numbers, ⟦x⟧ rounds down to the next smaller integer.

questions.q: What is the range of f(x) = 4⟦x⟧?
questions.hint: ⟦x⟧ only takes integer values.
questions.explanation: ⟦x⟧ can be any integer, so 4⟦x⟧ can be …, −8, −4, 0, 4, 8, … The range is all integer multiples of 4.

questions.q: For f(x) = 5⟦x⟧, complete the following.
questions.hint: Find ⟦x⟧ first, then multiply by 5.
questions.explanation: ⟦2.6⟧ = 2, so f = 10. ⟦−0.4⟧ = −1, so f = −5. ⟦−3⟧ = −3, so f = −15. Any real number can be input, so the domain is all real numbers.

questions.q: Each step of f(x) = 2⟦x⟧ starts with a closed dot at an integer value of x. Plot these closed dots for x = −2, −1, 0, 1 and 2.
questions.hint: At an integer x, ⟦x⟧ = x.
questions.explanation: At integers f(x) = 2x: (−2, −4), (−1, −2), (0, 0), (1, 2), (2, 4). Each step is a horizontal segment 1 unit long starting at one of these dots, with an open circle at its right end.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = ⟦x⟧ + 2.
questions.hint: Find the greatest integer ≤ x, then add 2.

questions.q: For f(x) = ⟦x⟧ − 3, complete the following.
questions.explanation: ⟦4.7⟧ = 4, so f = 1. ⟦−1.2⟧ = −2, so f = −5. Every real x can be used, so the domain is all real numbers. ⟦x⟧ − 3 is always an integer and can be any integer, so the range is all integers.

questions.q: For f(x) = ⟦x⟧ − 1, which values of x give f(x) = 2?
questions.hint: Solve ⟦x⟧ − 1 = 2 for ⟦x⟧ first.
questions.explanation: ⟦x⟧ − 1 = 2 means ⟦x⟧ = 3. The greatest integer of x is 3 for every x from 3 up to, but not including, 4. So 3 ≤ x < 4.

questions.q: Plot the closed dot at the left end of each step of f(x) = ⟦x⟧ + 1 for x = −2, −1, 0, 1 and 2.
questions.hint: At an integer x, ⟦x⟧ = x, so f(x) = x + 1.
questions.explanation: f(−2) = −1, f(−1) = 0, f(0) = 1, f(1) = 2, f(2) = 3. Each step starts at one of these closed dots and runs 1 unit to the right, ending in an open circle.

questions.q: Which describes the graph of g(x) = −|2x| + 4?
questions.hint: The negative sign outside the absolute value flips the V; solve −|2x| + 4 = 0 for the intercepts.
questions.explanation: When x = 0, g = 4, so the vertex is (0, 4), and the negative sign makes it open down. Setting −|2x| + 4 = 0 gives |2x| = 4, so x = ±2.

questions.q: Graph g(x) = −|x| + 3 by plotting its vertex and its two x-intercepts.
questions.hint: The vertex is where the expression inside the absolute value is 0.
questions.explanation: The vertex is (0, 3) and the graph opens down. Setting −|x| + 3 = 0 gives |x| = 3, so the x-intercepts are (−3, 0) and (3, 0).

questions.q: Graph g(x) = |2x| − 4 by plotting its vertex and its two x-intercepts.
questions.hint: Find g(0), then solve |2x| = 4.
questions.explanation: g(0) = −4, so the vertex is (0, −4) and the V opens up. |2x| − 4 = 0 gives |2x| = 4, so x = ±2 and the x-intercepts are (−2, 0) and (2, 0).

questions.q: For g(x) = −|3x| + 9, complete the following.
questions.hint: Solve −|3x| + 9 = 0.
questions.explanation: At x = 0, g = 9, so the vertex is (0, 9); the minus sign makes the graph open down. −|3x| + 9 = 0 gives |3x| = 9, so x = −3 or x = 3.

questions.q: The function k(x) = |x − 4| − 2 is translated 4 units ___ and 2 units ___ in relation to the parent function f(x) = |x|.
questions.hint: x − h inside moves right by h; subtracting outside moves down.
questions.explanation: In f(x − h) + k form, h = 4 and k = −2. A positive h shifts right 4, and a negative k shifts down 2.

questions.q: How is g(x) = |x + 1| + 5 translated from the parent function f(x) = |x|?
questions.explanation: x + 1 inside means h = −1, a shift 1 unit left. +5 outside shifts the graph 5 units up. The vertex moves from (0, 0) to (−1, 5).

questions.q: Match each function with how its graph is translated from f(x) = |x|.
questions.hint: Find the vertex (h, k) of each function.
questions.explanation: |x − 2| + 3 has vertex (2, 3): right 2, up 3. |x + 2| − 3 has vertex (−2, −3): left 2, down 3. |x| + 2 has vertex (0, 2): up 2. |x + 3| has vertex (−3, 0): left 3.

questions.q: Graph h(x) = |x + 2| − 1 by plotting its vertex and the points where x = −4 and x = 0.
questions.hint: The vertex is (−2, −1); move 2 units each side.
questions.explanation: The parent vertex (0, 0) moves 2 left and 1 down to (−2, −1). h(−4) = |−2| − 1 = 1 and h(0) = |2| − 1 = 1, giving (−4, 1) and (0, 1).

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = −|x − 5| is a reflection across which axis in relation to the parent function |x|? Write x-axis or y-axis.
questions.hint: The negative sign is outside the absolute value.
questions.explanation: The negative sign multiplies the whole output, so every y-value becomes its opposite. That flips the V upside down across the x-axis (then it is shifted 5 units right).

questions.q: Which function is the graph of f(x) = |x| reflected across the x-axis and then translated 3 units left?
questions.hint: Reflection across the x-axis puts a minus sign outside; left 3 puts x + 3 inside.
questions.explanation: Reflecting gives −|x|. Translating 3 units left replaces x with x + 3, giving −|x + 3|.

questions.q: Match each function with its transformation of f(x) = |x|.

right: reflection across the x-axis and translation 2 units up

questions.hint: A minus sign in front means reflection; numbers added outside move up or down.
questions.explanation: −|x| is only a reflection. |x| − 4 moves down 4. −|x| + 2 is reflected and then moved up 2. |x − 1| moves right 1.

questions.q: For g(x) = −|x − 1| + 4, complete the following.
questions.hint: Write the function as a|x − h| + k.
questions.explanation: a = −1 gives a reflection across the x-axis, so the graph opens down. h = 1 and k = 4, so the vertex is (1, 4).

questions.q: An absolute value graph h(x) has its vertex at (−1, −3), opens upward, and passes through (1, 1). Write its equation and find its domain and range.
questions.hint: Use h(x) = a|x − h| + k and substitute the point to find a.
questions.explanation: With vertex (−1, −3): h(x) = a|x + 1| − 3. Using (1, 1): 1 = a(2) − 3, so a = 2. The domain is all real numbers, and since the vertex is the lowest point the range is y ≥ −3.

questions.q: An absolute value graph has its vertex at (3, 4), opens downward, and passes through (5, 3). Which is its equation?
questions.hint: Find how much y changes when x moves 2 units from the vertex.
questions.explanation: Vertex (3, 4) gives h(x) = a|x − 3| + 4. Using (5, 3): 3 = a(2) + 4, so a = −1/2. The equation is h(x) = −(1/2)|x − 3| + 4.

questions.q: An absolute value graph has its vertex at (0, −2) and passes through (3, 4). Write its equation h(x).
questions.hint: Moving 3 units right from the vertex, the graph rises 6 units.
questions.explanation: The vertex (0, −2) gives h(x) = a|x| − 2. Using (3, 4): 4 = 3a − 2, so a = 2. The equation is h(x) = 2|x| − 2.

questions.q: Match each absolute value function with its range.
questions.hint: The range starts at the y-value of the vertex; the sign of a tells you the direction.
questions.explanation: |x − 1| + 5 opens up from y = 5. −|x + 2| + 3 opens down from y = 3. 2|x| − 5 opens up from y = −5. −3|x − 4| opens down from y = 0.

questions.q: Graph h(x) = −(1/2)|x + 2| + 3 by plotting the vertex and the points at x = −6, −4, 0 and 2.
questions.hint: The vertex is at x = −2; each 2 units away from it, the graph drops 1.
questions.explanation: The vertex is (−2, 3). h(−4) = h(0) = −(1/2)(2) + 3 = 2 and h(−6) = h(2) = −(1/2)(4) + 3 = 1. The graph is an upside-down V.

questions.q: Complete the table for h(x) = (2/3)|x − 3| − 2.
questions.hint: Find |x − 3| first, multiply by 2/3, then subtract 2.

questions.q: For h(x) = −2|x + 1| + 5, complete the following.
questions.hint: Compare with a|x − h| + k.
questions.explanation: Here a = −2, h = −1, k = 5. The vertex is (−1, 5). Because a is negative the graph is reflected across the x-axis and opens down, and |a| = 2 is a vertical stretch. The vertex is the highest point, so the range is y ≤ 5.

questions.q: Which describes the transformations of h(x) = (1/3)|x − 6| − 4 from the parent function f(x) = |x|?
options: Vertical stretch by 3, translated 6 units right and 4 units down
Reflection across the x-axis, translated 6 units right and 4 units down
Vertical compression by 1/3, translated 6 units right and 4 units down
Vertical compression by 1/3, translated 6 units left and 4 units down
questions.hint: A factor between 0 and 1 is a compression; x − 6 means right 6.
questions.explanation: a = 1/3 is between 0 and 1, so the graph is compressed vertically (and not reflected since a > 0). x − 6 shifts right 6 and −4 shifts down 4.

questions.q: A bottle should hold 500 mL of juice. The actual amount a may differ from 500 mL by at most 8 mL. Which equation gives the highest and lowest allowed amounts?
questions.hint: Difference from a target is the absolute value of (amount − target).
questions.explanation: The distance between a and 500 is |a − 500|. The extreme amounts are exactly 8 mL away, so |a − 500| = 8, which gives a = 508 or a = 492.

questions.q: The ideal temperature in a greenhouse is 22 °C. The temperature t may vary from this by 3 °C. Write an absolute value equation to find the highest and lowest temperatures.
questions.hint: Use |actual − target| = allowed difference.
questions.explanation: The difference between t and 22 is |t − 22|. The highest and lowest temperatures are exactly 3 °C away, so |t − 22| = 3 (t = 25 or t = 19).

questions.q: A cereal box should weigh 250 g. The equation |w − 250| = 6 gives the heaviest and lightest acceptable weights w. Solve it.
questions.hint: Split into w − 250 = 6 and w − 250 = −6.

questions.q: Match each situation with the equation that gives its highest and lowest values.

left: A bag of rice should be 5 kg, allowed to differ by 0.2 kg.
A board should be 2 m long, allowed to differ by 0.05 m.
A class average should be 75, allowed to differ by 10 points.

questions.hint: Inside the absolute value goes (variable − target); the allowed difference goes on the right.
questions.explanation: Each equation has the form |amount − target| = allowed difference: |r − 5| = 0.2, |L − 2| = 0.05 and |s − 75| = 10.

questions.q: Which equation represents a line passing through (4, −2) with a slope of −3?
questions.hint: Substitute the point into y = −3x + b and solve for b.
questions.explanation: −2 = −3(4) + b gives −2 = −12 + b, so b = 10. The equation is y = −3x + 10.

questions.q: Write the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line through (−2, 7) with a slope of 4.
questions.hint: Use y = mx + b with x = −2 and y = 7 to find b.
questions.explanation: 7 = 4(−2) + b gives 7 = −8 + b, so b = 15. The equation is y = 4x + 15.

questions.q: Graph the line that passes through (3, −1) with a slope of −2.
questions.hint: Find b, or step from (3, −1) using down 2, right 1 (or up 2, left 1).
questions.explanation: −1 = −2(3) + b gives b = 5, so the line is y = −2x + 5. It passes through (3, −1) and (0, 5).

questions.q: A line has slope 1/2 and passes through (6, 1).
questions.hint: Substitute x = 6 and y = 1 into y = (1/2)x + b.
questions.explanation: 1 = (1/2)(6) + b gives 1 = 3 + b, so b = −2. The equation is y = (1/2)x − 2.

questions.q: Which equation represents a line that passes through the points (2, 1) and (5, 10)?
questions.hint: Find the slope, then use one point to find b.
questions.explanation: Slope = (10 − 1)/(5 − 2) = 9/3 = 3. Using (2, 1): 1 = 6 + b, so b = −5. The equation is y = 3x − 5.

questions.q: Write the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line through (−1, 6) and (3, −2).
questions.hint: Slope = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁).

questions.q: For each pair of points, find the slope, the y-intercept and the equation of the line through them.
questions.hint: Compute the slope first, then substitute a point to find b.

questions.q: Match each description to the equation of the line it represents.
questions.hint: In y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: Write each line as y = mx + b with m = slope and b = y-intercept. Slope 3, intercept −2 gives y = 3x − 2; slope −2, intercept 3 gives y = −2x + 3; slope −3, intercept 2 gives y = −3x + 2; slope 2, intercept 3 gives y = 2x + 3.

questions.q: Which equation represents the line with slope −1.5 and y-intercept 4?
questions.hint: The slope multiplies x; the y-intercept is the constant term.
questions.explanation: Slope-intercept form is y = mx + b. With m = −1.5 and b = 4, the equation is y = −1.5x + 4.

questions.q: Graph the line that has slope −1/2 and y-intercept 3.
questions.hint: Start at (0, 3), then move right 2 and down 1.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept 3 gives the point (0, 3). A slope of −1/2 means down 1 for every 2 to the right, so (2, 2) is also on the line. Draw the line through these points.

questions.q: For the line y = −0.75x + 6, complete: slope = ___, y-intercept = ___.
questions.hint: Compare the equation with y = mx + b.
questions.explanation: The equation is already in the form y = mx + b. The coefficient of x is m = −0.75, and the constant is b = 6.

questions.q: A gym charges a one-time joining fee of AED 200 plus AED 45 for each personal-training session. Write an equation for the total cost y (in AED) for x sessions.
questions.hint: The fixed fee is the constant; the per-session fee multiplies x.
questions.explanation: The cost per session, 45, is the rate of change, so it multiplies x. The joining fee, 200, is paid once, so it is the constant. The equation is y = 45x + 200.

questions.q: A tutoring centre charges a registration fee of AED 150 plus AED 25 per lesson, so the total cost is y = 25x + 150 for x lessons. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Substitute x into y = 25x + 150; for the last row solve 25x + 150 = 400.

questions.q: A swimming club charges a membership fee of AED 300 per month plus AED 90 for each lesson. Which equation gives the monthly cost y for x lessons?
questions.hint: Which amount changes with the number of lessons?
questions.explanation: The AED 90 is charged for each lesson, so it multiplies x. The AED 300 membership is a fixed amount added once. So y = 90x + 300.

questions.q: A dance studio's monthly cost is y = 35x + 500, where x is the number of classes attended. One month a member paid AED 815. How many classes did the member attend?
questions.hint: Set 35x + 500 equal to 815 and solve.
questions.explanation: Solve 35x + 500 = 815. Subtract 500: 35x = 315. Divide by 35: x = 9 classes.

questions.q: A refillable water bottle costs AED 12.00 and each refill costs AED 0.75. Write an equation in slope-intercept form for the total cost y (in AED) after x refills.
questions.hint: The price of the bottle is the starting value; the refill price is the rate.
questions.explanation: The rate of change is AED 0.75 per refill, so m = 0.75. The starting cost is the bottle, AED 12, so b = 12. The equation is y = 0.75x + 12.

questions.q: A taxi charges a base fare of AED 12 plus AED 2.50 per kilometre. The fare y for x km is y = mx + b. Complete the parts.
questions.hint: The per-km charge is the slope; the base fare is the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: The rate is 2.50 per km, so m = 2.5, and the base fare is b = 12. So y = 2.5x + 12. For x = 8: y = 2.5(8) + 12 = 20 + 12 = 32 AED.

questions.q: A coffee gift card starts with AED 8 and each coffee costs AED 2, so the balance after x coffees is y = −2x + 8. Graph this line.
questions.hint: Plot the starting balance at x = 0, then use the slope −2.
questions.explanation: At x = 0 the balance is 8, giving (0, 8). Each coffee lowers the balance by 2, so after 4 coffees it is 0, giving (4, 0). Draw the line through these points.

questions.q: A bowling alley charges AED 4 for shoe rental plus AED 5.50 per game. Which equation models the total cost y for x games?
questions.hint: The rental is paid once; the game price is paid for each game.
questions.explanation: The cost per game, 5.50, is the slope and multiplies x. The one-time shoe rental, 4, is the y-intercept. So y = 5.5x + 4.

questions.q: A line with slope 3/4 passes through the point (8, 5). What is the y-intercept of the line?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 8, y = 5 and m = 3/4 into y = mx + b.
questions.explanation: Substitute into y = mx + b: 5 = (3/4)(8) + b. Then 5 = 6 + b, so b = −1.

questions.q: A line with slope 2/3 passes through the point (2, 4). What is the y-intercept? Round to the nearest tenth.
questions.hint: Substitute the point and slope into y = mx + b and solve for b.

questions.q: Each row gives the slope m of a line and a point on it. Find the y-intercept b.
questions.hint: Use b = y − mx for each row.

questions.q: A line has slope −4 and passes through (−2, 3). Which is its equation in slope-intercept form?
questions.hint: Find b from 3 = −4(−2) + b.
questions.explanation: Substitute: 3 = −4(−2) + b, so 3 = 8 + b and b = −5. The equation is y = −4x − 5.

questions.q: Which point is on the graph of y − 3 = −2(x + 1)?
questions.hint: Substitute each point and check whether both sides are equal.
questions.explanation: The equation is in point-slope form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with (x₁, y₁) = (−1, 3). Check: 3 − 3 = 0 and −2(−1 + 1) = 0, so (−1, 3) is on the line. The other points give unequal sides, e.g. (1, −3): −6 ≠ −4.

questions.q: Graph the line y + 2 = (1/3)(x − 3).
questions.hint: The point-slope form shows the point (3, −2); the slope is 1/3.
questions.explanation: Compare with y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): the line passes through (3, −2) with slope 1/3. Move right 3 and up 1 to reach (6, −1). Draw the line through these points.

questions.q: Complete the table of points on the line y − 1 = 2(x − 4).
questions.hint: Rewrite as y = 2(x − 4) + 1, then substitute.

questions.q: The point (k, 5) lies on the graph of y − 1 = (2/3)(x + 3). Find k.
questions.hint: Substitute y = 5 and x = k, then solve.

questions.q: Which equation represents the line parallel to the x-axis that passes through (4, −3)?
questions.hint: A line parallel to the x-axis is horizontal, so y stays the same.
questions.explanation: Every point on a horizontal line has the same y-coordinate. The line passes through (4, −3), so every point has y = −3. The equation is y = −3.

questions.q: Graph the line that is parallel to the x-axis and passes through (2, 5).
questions.hint: Horizontal lines have the form y = k.
questions.explanation: A line parallel to the x-axis is horizontal. Since it passes through (2, 5), its equation is y = 5, so it goes through (0, 5), (2, 5) and every other point with y = 5.

questions.q: Match each equation to the description of its graph.
questions.hint: y = number is horizontal; x = number is vertical.
questions.explanation: y = −2 keeps y fixed, so it is horizontal. x = 7 keeps x fixed, so it is vertical. y = 4x has slope 4 and y-intercept 0, so it is a slanted line through the origin.

questions.q: Which of the following linear equations has a slope of 2?
questions.hint: Solve each equation for y.
questions.explanation: 2x − y = 3 gives y = 2x − 3, slope 2. The others give y = −2x + 3 (slope −2), y = (1/2)x − 3/2 (slope 1/2) and y = −(1/2)x + 3/2 (slope −1/2).

questions.q: Find the slope of each line. Write a whole number or a fraction.
questions.hint: Rearrange each equation into y = mx + b.
questions.explanation: x + y = 7 → y = −x + 7, slope −1. y − x = 4 → y = x + 4, slope 1. 3x + y = 2 → y = −3x + 2, slope −3. 4x − 2y = 6 → y = 2x − 3, slope 2. y = 5 is horizontal, slope 0.

questions.q: What is the slope of the line 6x + 3y = 9?
questions.hint: Solve for y.
questions.explanation: Subtract 6x: 3y = −6x + 9. Divide by 3: y = −2x + 3. The slope is −2.

questions.q: Which equation has a slope of −1/3?
questions.hint: Rewrite each in the form y = mx + b.
questions.explanation: x + 3y = 6 gives 3y = −x + 6, so y = −(1/3)x + 2, slope −1/3. The others have slopes −3, 1/3 and 3.

questions.q: Which equation represents a straight line that is parallel to the y-axis?
questions.hint: A line parallel to the y-axis is vertical.
questions.explanation: On a vertical line every point has the same x-coordinate, so its equation has the form x = k. Only x = −4 has this form.

questions.q: Write the equation of the line that is parallel to the y-axis and passes through (−6, 2).
questions.hint: Vertical lines have equations of the form x = k.
questions.explanation: A line parallel to the y-axis is vertical, so every point on it has the same x-coordinate as (−6, 2). The equation is x = −6.

questions.q: Graph the line that is parallel to the y-axis and passes through (−3, 4).
questions.hint: Every point on this line has x = −3.
questions.explanation: A line parallel to the y-axis is vertical. Since it passes through (−3, 4), its equation is x = −3, so it passes through (−3, 0), (−3, 4) and all points with x = −3.

questions.q: Consider the line x = 5. Complete each part.
questions.hint: Picture a vertical line through x = 5.
questions.explanation: x = 5 is a vertical line, so its slope is undefined. It never meets the y-axis (x = 0), so it has no y-intercept. It crosses the x-axis at (5, 0).

questions.q: Match each description to the equation of the straight line.
questions.hint: Solve for y to read the slope; y = k is horizontal and x = k is vertical.
questions.explanation: 3x − 3y = 2 gives y = x − 2/3, slope 1. y = −4 is horizontal, parallel to the x-axis. x = 1 is vertical, parallel to the y-axis. x + y = 8 gives y = −x + 8, slope −1 (2x + y = 8 has slope −2).

questions.q: Complete the table. For type, write horizontal, vertical, or slanted.
questions.hint: y = k is horizontal, x = k is vertical; otherwise solve for y.
questions.explanation: y = 6 is horizontal with slope 0. x = −2 is vertical with undefined slope. x − y = 4 gives y = x − 4, a slanted line with slope 1.

questions.q: Which line has a slope of 0?
questions.hint: A slope of 0 means a horizontal line.
questions.explanation: y + 3 = 0 means y = −3, a horizontal line with slope 0. x + 3 = 0 is vertical (undefined slope), x + y = 3 has slope −1, and x − y = 0 has slope 1.

questions.q: Which equation represents a line that passes through the points (3, 2) and (5, 8)?
questions.hint: Find the slope first, then use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with one of the points.
questions.explanation: Slope m = (8 − 2)/(5 − 3) = 6/2 = 3. Using the point (3, 2) in y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) gives y − 2 = 3(x − 3).

questions.q: A line passes through (−1, 4) and (2, −5). Complete the parts.
questions.hint: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.

questions.q: Graph the line y + 3 = 2(x + 2).
questions.hint: The equation shows the point (−2, −3) and slope 2.
questions.explanation: In point-slope form the line passes through (−2, −3) with slope 2. Move right 2 and up 4 to reach (0, 1). Draw the line through these points.

questions.q: Write the equation, in point-slope form using the point (4, −1), of the line through (4, −1) and (6, 3).
questions.hint: Find the slope, then substitute into y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

questions.q: Which equation represents a line passing through the points (5, 0) and (0, 2)?
questions.hint: Substitute both points into each equation.
questions.explanation: Check 2x + 5y = 10: (5, 0) gives 10 + 0 = 10 and (0, 2) gives 0 + 10 = 10. Both points work. For 5x + 2y = 10, (5, 0) gives 25, so it fails.

questions.q: Write the equation of the line through (−3, 0) and (0, 6) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Find the slope and y-intercept first, then rearrange.
questions.explanation: m = (6 − 0)/(0 − (−3)) = 2 and the y-intercept is 6, so y = 2x + 6. Subtract y and 6 from both sides: 2x − y = −6.

questions.q: Complete the table of points on the line 3x + 2y = 12.
questions.hint: Substitute the known value and solve for the other.

questions.q: Plot the x-intercept and the y-intercept of the line 4x − 3y = 12.
questions.hint: Set y = 0 to find the x-intercept, and x = 0 for the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: When y = 0, 4x = 12 so x = 3, giving (3, 0). When x = 0, −3y = 12 so y = −4, giving (0, −4).

questions.q: Which shows the equation y = −(1/3)x + 4 written in standard form?
questions.hint: Move the x-term to the left, then multiply by 3 to clear the fraction.
questions.explanation: Add (1/3)x to both sides: (1/3)x + y = 4. Multiply every term by 3: x + 3y = 12.

questions.q: Which shows y = (3/4)x − 2 written in standard form?
questions.hint: Multiply every term by 4, then gather x and y on one side.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4: 4y = 3x − 8. Subtract 4y and add 8 to both sides: 8 = 3x − 4y, so 3x − 4y = 8.

questions.q: Match each slope-intercept equation to the same line in standard form.
questions.hint: Rearrange so x and y are on the left with integer coefficients.
questions.explanation: y = 2x + 5 → 2x − y = −5. y = −x + 7 → x + y = 7. y = (1/2)x − 3: multiply by 2 to get 2y = x − 6, so x − 2y = 6.

questions.q: Write the equation of the line y = (3/5)x − 2 in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Multiply by 5 to clear the fraction.
questions.explanation: Multiply every term by 5: 5y = 3x − 10. Subtract 5y and add 10: 10 = 3x − 5y, so 3x − 5y = 10.

questions.q: Write y = −(4/3)x + 2 in standard form Ax + By = C with integers and A > 0. Give A, B and C.
questions.hint: Multiply by 3, then move the x-term to the left.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 3: 3y = −4x + 6. Add 4x to both sides: 4x + 3y = 6. So A = 4, B = 3, C = 6.

questions.q: Which is y = (1/4)x + 3 written in standard form?
questions.hint: Multiply by 4 first.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4: 4y = x + 12. Subtract 4y and 12 from both sides: x − 4y = −12.

questions.q: Write y + 3 = 4(x − 1) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Distribute, then collect x and y on the left.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y + 3 = 4x − 4. Subtract y and add 4: 7 = 4x − y, so 4x − y = 7.

questions.q: Write y − 5 = −2(x + 3) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Distribute the −2 first.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y − 5 = −2x − 6. Add 2x and 5 to both sides: 2x + y = −1.

questions.q: Which is y + 1 = −6(x − 2) written in standard form?
questions.hint: Distribute, then move the x-term and the constant.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y + 1 = −6x + 12. Add 6x and subtract 1: 6x + y = 11.

questions.q: Rewrite y − 4 = 3(x + 5) step by step.
questions.hint: Distribute the 3, then rearrange.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y − 4 = 3x + 15. Add 4: y = 3x + 19. Subtract y and 19 from both sides: 3x − y = −19.

questions.q: Write y − 2 = 5(x + 1) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0. Give A, B and C.
questions.hint: Distribute, then move the y-term to the right side with x.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y − 2 = 5x + 5. Subtract y and 5 from both sides: −7 = 5x − y, so 5x − y = −7. A = 5, B = −1, C = −7.

questions.q: When y + 6 = −2(x − 3) is written in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0, what is C?
questions.hint: Distribute and simplify carefully.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y + 6 = −2x + 6. Add 2x and subtract 6: 2x + y = 0. So C = 0.

questions.q: Write each equation in standard form Ax + By = C with integers and A > 0, and fill in A, B and C.
questions.hint: Distribute or clear fractions, then put x and y on the left.
questions.explanation: y − 1 = 4x − 8 gives 4x − y = 7. y + 3 = −x − 5 gives x + y = −8. Multiplying y = (2/3)x + 1 by 3 gives 3y = 2x + 3, so 2x − 3y = −3.

questions.q: Write y − 1 = (1/2)(4x − 6) in standard form.
questions.hint: Distribute the 1/2 first.
questions.explanation: (1/2)(4x − 6) = 2x − 3, so y − 1 = 2x − 3. Then y = 2x − 2, and moving terms gives 2x − y = 2.

questions.q: Write y + 4 = −(2/5)(x − 10) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Distribute, then multiply by 5.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y + 4 = −(2/5)x + 4. Subtract 4: y = −(2/5)x. Multiply by 5: 5y = −2x, so 2x + 5y = 0.

questions.q: Which is y − 3 = −(1/4)(x + 8) written in standard form?
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 4 to clear the fraction.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4: 4y − 12 = −(x + 8) = −x − 8. Add x and 12: x + 4y = 4.

questions.q: A line on a coordinate grid passes through the points (−2, 5) and (2, 3). Which equation models the line?
questions.hint: Find the slope, then use point-slope form with one marked point.

questions.q: Graph the line y − 1 = (3/2)(x + 2).
questions.hint: The equation shows the point (−2, 1); the slope 3/2 means up 3, right 2.
questions.explanation: The line passes through (−2, 1). From there go right 2 and up 3 to reach (0, 4). Draw the line through these points.

questions.q: A line on a grid passes through the marked points (−4, −1) and (2, 2). Complete the parts.
questions.hint: Slope = rise ÷ run between the two points.

questions.q: The equation for line p is y = (4/5)x − 1. Which equation represents a line perpendicular to line p?
questions.hint: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals.
questions.explanation: Line p has slope 4/5. The negative reciprocal is −5/4. Only y = −(5/4)x + 3 has slope −5/4.

questions.q: Match the slope of each line to the slope of a line perpendicular to it.
questions.hint: Flip the fraction and change the sign.
questions.explanation: The negative reciprocal of 3 is −1/3; of −2/7 is 7/2; of 1/6 is −6; of −1 is 1. Each pair multiplies to −1.

questions.q: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to 2x − 5y = 10?
questions.hint: Find the slope of the given line first.
questions.explanation: 2x − 5y = 10 gives −5y = −2x + 10, so y = (2/5)x − 2 with slope 2/5. The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal, −5/2.

questions.q: Write the equation in slope-intercept form of the line that is parallel to y + 2x = 1 and passes through (3, −4).
questions.hint: Parallel lines have the same slope.
questions.explanation: y + 2x = 1 gives y = −2x + 1, so the slope is −2. Substitute (3, −4): −4 = −2(3) + b, so b = 2. The line is y = −2x + 2.

questions.q: A line is parallel to 3x − y = 4 and passes through (−1, 5). Complete the parts.
questions.hint: Rewrite 3x − y = 4 in slope-intercept form.
questions.explanation: 3x − y = 4 gives y = 3x − 4, slope 3. Substitute (−1, 5): 5 = 3(−1) + b, so b = 8. The equation is y = 3x + 8.

questions.q: Graph the line that is parallel to y = (1/2)x + 4 and passes through (2, −1).
questions.hint: Use slope 1/2 and the point (2, −1).
questions.explanation: The parallel line has slope 1/2. Substitute (2, −1): −1 = (1/2)(2) + b, so b = −2. The line is y = (1/2)x − 2, passing through (0, −2) and (2, −1).

questions.q: Which line is parallel to y − 4x = 2 and passes through (1, 1)?
questions.hint: Find the slope of y − 4x = 2 first.
questions.explanation: y − 4x = 2 gives y = 4x + 2, slope 4. Substitute (1, 1): 1 = 4 + b, so b = −3. The line is y = 4x − 3.

questions.q: Write the equation in slope-intercept form of the line that is perpendicular to 3x + y = 2 and passes through (3, 4).
questions.hint: The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of the given slope.
questions.explanation: 3x + y = 2 gives y = −3x + 2, slope −3. The perpendicular slope is 1/3. Substitute (3, 4): 4 = (1/3)(3) + b, so b = 3. The line is y = (1/3)x + 3.

questions.q: Which line is perpendicular to y = 2x − 7 and passes through (4, 1)?
questions.hint: Use slope −½ and substitute the point.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is −½. Substitute (4, 1): 1 = −½(4) + b = −2 + b, so b = 3. The line is y = −½x + 3.

questions.q: Graph the line that is perpendicular to y = −(2/3)x + 1 and passes through (0, −3).
questions.hint: The perpendicular slope is 3/2.
questions.explanation: The negative reciprocal of −2/3 is 3/2. The line passes through (0, −3), so it is y = (3/2)x − 3. From (0, −3) go right 2 and up 3 to (2, 0).

questions.q: A line is perpendicular to x − 4y = 8 and passes through (−1, 6). Complete the parts.
questions.hint: Solve x − 4y = 8 for y to find its slope.
questions.explanation: x − 4y = 8 gives y = (1/4)x − 2, slope 1/4. The perpendicular slope is −4. Substitute (−1, 6): 6 = −4(−1) + b, so b = 2. The line is y = −4x + 2.

questions.q: A line passes through the points (−3, 6) and (1, −2). Complete the parts.
questions.hint: Use m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁), then find b.

questions.q: A line passes through (2, 1) and (6, 9). Complete the table of points on this line.
questions.hint: Find the equation of the line first.
questions.explanation: m = (9 − 1)/(6 − 2) = 2 and 1 = 2(2) + b gives b = −3, so y = 2x − 3. x = 0 gives −3, x = 4 gives 5, and y = 11 gives 2x = 14, x = 7.

questions.q: Find the slope of the line through (−5, 3) and (5, −1). Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Subtract the y-values and the x-values in the same order.

questions.q: Which is the equation of the line through (1, 4) and (3, 10)?
questions.hint: Find the slope, then substitute a point to find b.
questions.explanation: m = (10 − 4)/(3 − 1) = 6/2 = 3. Substitute (1, 4): 4 = 3 + b, so b = 1. The equation is y = 3x + 1.

questions.q: Line m is y = −(3/4)x + 2. Match each equation to the term that describes its relationship to line m.
questions.hint: Compare each slope with −3/4: equal means parallel; negative reciprocal means perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Line m has slope −3/4 = −0.75. y = −0.75x − 5 has the same slope, so it is parallel. 4/3 is the negative reciprocal, so y = (4/3)x + 1 is perpendicular. Slopes 3/4 and −4/3 are neither.

questions.q: Line p is y = 5x − 1. Which line is parallel to line p?
questions.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
questions.explanation: Line p has slope 5. Only y = 5x + 8 also has slope 5 (with a different y-intercept), so it is parallel. y = −(1/5)x − 1 would be perpendicular.

questions.q: Line n is 2x + 6y = 1. Complete the parts.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Slope of any line parallel to n:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Slope of any line perpendicular to n:

questions.hint: Solve 2x + 6y = 1 for y.
questions.explanation: 6y = −2x + 1, so y = −(1/3)x + 1/6 and the slope is −1/3. Parallel lines have slope −1/3; perpendicular lines have the negative reciprocal, 3.

questions.q: Are the graphs of each pair parallel, perpendicular, or neither? Type parallel, perpendicular, or neither.
questions.hint: Write each equation in slope-intercept form and compare slopes.
questions.explanation: Slopes 4 and 4 are equal: parallel. x + 3y = 6 has slope −1/3, and −1/3 × 3 = −1: perpendicular. 2x − y = 5 has slope 2 and 2x + y = 5 has slope −2: neither. x = 3 is vertical and y = −1 is horizontal: perpendicular.

questions.q: Are the graphs of 4x − 2y = 8 and y = −½x + 3 parallel, perpendicular, or neither?
questions.hint: Find the slope of 4x − 2y = 8.
questions.explanation: 4x − 2y = 8 gives y = 2x − 4, slope 2. The other slope is −½. Since 2 × (−½) = −1, the lines are perpendicular.

questions.q: Are the graphs of 3x + 4y = 12 and 6x + 8y = 5 parallel, perpendicular, or neither?
questions.hint: Compare slopes and y-intercepts.
questions.explanation: 3x + 4y = 12 gives y = −(3/4)x + 3. 6x + 8y = 5 gives y = −(3/4)x + 5/8. The slopes are equal and the intercepts differ, so the lines are parallel.

questions.q: Find the value of a so that the lines 3x + 2y = 5 and ax − 6y = 1 are perpendicular.
questions.hint: Find each slope; perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.

questions.q: Find the value of k so that the line y = (k/2)x + 3 is parallel to 5x − y = 2.
questions.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
questions.explanation: 5x − y = 2 gives y = 5x − 2, slope 5. Set k/2 = 5, so k = 10.

questions.q: Find the value of a so that the lines x − 4y = 3 and ax + 2y = 7 are perpendicular.
questions.hint: Write both slopes in terms of a, then multiply to get −1.
questions.explanation: x − 4y = 3 has slope 1/4. ax + 2y = 7 gives y = −(a/2)x + 7/2, slope −a/2. Set (1/4)(−a/2) = −1: −a/8 = −1, so a = 8.

questions.q: Consider the lines 4x + by = 3 and 2x − y = 9. Find the value of b for each condition.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: b if the lines are parallel:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: b if the lines are perpendicular:

questions.hint: The slope of 4x + by = 3 is −4/b.
questions.explanation: 2x − y = 9 has slope 2, and 4x + by = 3 has slope −4/b. Parallel: −4/b = 2, so b = −2. Perpendicular: −4/b = −1/2, so b = 8.

questions.q: The slope of the line containing (3, −1) and (x, 7) is 2. Find the value of x.
The slope of the line containing (−2, y) and (4, 5) is −1/2. Find the value of y.
The slope of the line containing (1, 4) and (x, −8) is 3. What is x?
questions.hint: Write (−8 − 4)/(x − 1) = 3 and solve.

questions.q: Each row gives two points on a line and its slope. Find the missing coordinate.
questions.hint: Substitute into slope = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) and solve.

questions.q: Find the value of y so that the line containing (2, 3) and (4, y) is perpendicular to a line with slope −2/3.
questions.hint: The required slope is the negative reciprocal of −2/3.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is 3/2. So (y − 3)/(4 − 2) = 3/2, giving y − 3 = 3 and y = 6.

questions.q: Find the value of y so that the line containing (−1, y) and (5, 2) is perpendicular to a line with slope 3.
questions.hint: The required slope is −1/3.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is −1/3. So (2 − y)/(5 − (−1)) = −1/3, giving (2 − y)/6 = −1/3. Then 2 − y = −2, so y = 4.

questions.q: Find the value of y so that the line containing (0, 1) and (3, y) is parallel to a line with slope 2/3.
questions.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes.

questions.q: Line k contains (1, 2) and (5, 4). Line m contains (3, 1) and (x, −3). Find x so that line m is perpendicular to line k.
questions.hint: Find the slope of k, then use the negative reciprocal for m.

questions.q: Line k contains (0, 5) and (4, −3). Line m contains (−1, 3) and (2, y). Find y so that line m is parallel to line k.
questions.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes.

questions.q: Line k contains (−3, 1) and (3, 5). Line m contains (2, 2) and (x, −4) and is perpendicular to line k. Complete the parts.
questions.hint: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals.
As x increases, does y tend to go up, go down, or neither?
questions.explanation: In Set A, y falls from 9 to 3 as x increases, so it shows a negative correlation. In Set B, y rises from 2 to 8 as x increases, so it shows a positive correlation.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows outdoor temperature (x) and the number of hot drinks sold (y). The points fall from the upper left to the lower right. What kind of correlation does it show?
questions.hint: Think about what happens to y as x increases.
questions.explanation: Points falling from upper left to lower right mean y decreases as x increases. That is a negative correlation.

questions.q: Match each pair of quantities to the correlation you would most likely see in a scatter plot.

left: Age of a car and its resale value
Height of a student and their shoe size
A person's birth month and their test score

questions.hint: Ask whether one quantity tends to rise, fall, or not change as the other rises.
questions.explanation: As a car gets older its value tends to drop: negative. Taller students tend to have bigger feet: positive. Birth month has no link to test scores: no correlation.

questions.q: Match each data set to its description.
questions.hint: Look at how the y-values change as x goes from 1 to 6.
questions.explanation: In Set P, y drops from 7 to 2: negative correlation. In Set Q, y stays around 4 with no trend: no correlation. In Set R, y rises from 1 to 7: positive correlation.

questions.q: The points of a scatter plot form a horizontal band, with no upward or downward trend. What does the plot show?
questions.hint: A trend needs y to rise or fall as x increases.
questions.explanation: In a horizontal band, y does not tend to increase or decrease as x increases, so there is no correlation.

questions.q: For each situation, write the type of correlation: positive, negative, or none.

rows: Hours a heater is on and electricity used
Number of school absences and final grade
Shoe size and last digit of phone number

questions.hint: Does one quantity tend to go up or down when the other goes up?
questions.explanation: More heating hours use more electricity: positive. More absences tend to lower grades: negative. Shoe size has nothing to do with a phone number: none.

questions.q: Which data set shows a negative correlation?
questions.hint: Look for y-values that go down as x goes up.
questions.explanation: In the first set, y decreases from 10 to 2 as x increases, which is a negative correlation. The second set rises (positive), the third has no pattern, and the fourth is constant (no correlation).

questions.q: Plot X: points rise from lower left to upper right. Plot Y: points fall from upper left to lower right. Plot Z: points are scattered with no pattern. Write X, Y, or Z.
questions.hint: Negative means y decreases as x increases.
questions.explanation: Plot Y falls as x increases, so it shows negative correlation. Plot X rises as x increases, so it shows positive correlation. Plot Z shows no correlation.

questions.q: Which situation would most likely show a positive correlation?
options: Speed of a car and time to travel 100 km
Hours of piano practice and number of mistakes
questions.hint: Positive means both quantities tend to increase together.
questions.explanation: Driving farther uses more fuel, so both increase together: positive. More practice means fewer mistakes and higher speed means less time (negative); hair colour and maths score are unrelated.

questions.q: Each description is of a line drawn on a scatter plot. Decide whether each line is a good line of fit.

left: The points trend downward and the line falls with them, with 4 points above it and 4 below it.
The line passes through the first and last points, but every other point lies above it.
The points trend downward, but the line rises from left to right.
The points trend upward and the line rises with them, with about as many points on each side.
right: Not a good line of fit

questions.hint: A good line of fit follows the direction of the trend and has about as many points above it as below it.
questions.explanation: Lines 1 and 4 follow the trend and split the points evenly, so they are good lines of fit. Line 2 has all the other points on one side, so it is too low. Line 3 goes in the wrong direction.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the points (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 5) and (5, 7). Which line is the best line of fit?
questions.hint: The points rise from left to right, and a good line should have points on both sides of it.
questions.explanation: The points rise, so the slope must be positive, which rules out y = −1.2x + 8. The line y = 1.2x + 3 lies above every point, and y = 0.2x + 2 is far too flat. The line y = 1.2x + 0.8 gives 2, 3.2, 4.4, 5.6, 6.8, which is close to every point with points on both sides.

questions.q: A student draws a line on a scatter plot of 10 points. The line follows the direction of the trend, but 9 points lie below the line and 1 point lies on it. What is the best conclusion?
options: The line is too high; it should be moved down so the points are balanced above and below it.
The line is the line of best fit because it passes through a data point.
The line is the line of best fit because it follows the trend.
The line should be made steeper so it passes through more points.
questions.hint: Check how many points are on each side of the line.
questions.explanation: A line of best fit follows the trend and has roughly the same number of points above and below it. Here almost all points are below the line, so the line is too high. Moving it down while keeping the same direction would give a better fit.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the points (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 3), (4, 6), (5, 5) and (6, 7). Line A is y = x + 1 and Line B is y = x + 3. Which line is the better line of fit? Type Line A or Line B.
questions.hint: For each line, count how many points lie above it and how many lie below it.
questions.explanation: Line A gives 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, so the points are 0, 1 above, 1 below, 1 above, 1 below and 0: they are balanced. Line B gives 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, so every point lies below it. Line A is the better line of fit.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the points (0, 8), (2, 7), (4, 5), (6, 4) and (8, 2). Line P is y = −0.75x + 8 and Line Q is y = −0.75x + 5. Which statement is correct?
options: Neither line fits, because no point lies exactly on either line.
Line Q is the better fit, because it is lower on the graph.
Line P is the better fit, because the points are spread on both sides of it.
Line Q is the better fit, because it has a negative slope.
questions.hint: Both lines have the same slope, so compare where the points sit relative to each line.
questions.explanation: Line P gives 8, 6.5, 5, 3.5, 2 at the five x-values, so the points are on or close to the line on both sides. Line Q gives 5, 3.5, 2, 0.5, −1, so every point lies above it. Both lines have a negative slope, so slope alone does not decide it; Line P fits better.

questions.q: For the line of fit y = x + 1, complete the table. In the last column write above, below or on to describe where the data point is compared with the line.
questions.hint: Substitute each x into y = x + 1, then compare with the actual y.
questions.explanation: The line gives 2, 3, 5 and 6. The actual values 3 and 6 are bigger than 2 and 5, so those points are above; 2 is less than 3, so that point is below; and 6 equals 6, so that point is on the line.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the points (1, 9), (2, 8), (3, 6), (4, 6), (5, 4) and (6, 3). Which equation represents the best line of fit?
questions.hint: Decide the sign of the slope first, then check which line passes through the middle of the points.
questions.explanation: The points fall from left to right, so the slope is negative, ruling out y = 1.2x + 2. The line y = −1.2x + 6 is below almost every point and y = −0.3x + 7 is too flat (it gives 5.2 at x = 6, but the point is 3). y = −1.2x + 10.2 gives 9, 7.8, 6.6, 5.4, 4.2, 3, which is very close to every point.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the points (2, 3), (4, 4), (6, 6), (8, 7) and (10, 9). Which equation represents the best line of fit?
questions.hint: Look for a positive slope and a line that goes through the middle of the data.
questions.explanation: The points rise, so the slope is positive. y = 0.75x + 5 lies above every point, and y = 2x − 4 is too steep (it gives 16 at x = 10, but the point is 9). y = 0.75x + 1.3 gives 2.8, 4.3, 5.8, 7.3, 8.8, which is close to all the points.

questions.q: Match each scatter plot description to the equation that best fits it.

left: Points trend upward and start near y = 2 when x = 0
Points trend downward and start near y = 9 when x = 0
Points trend upward and start near y = 9 when x = 0
Points trend downward and start near y = 2 when x = 0

questions.hint: The trend gives the sign of the slope, and the starting value gives the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: An upward trend means a positive slope and a downward trend means a negative slope. The value of y where x = 0 is the y-intercept. Combine the two facts to pick each equation.

questions.q: A line of fit for a scatter plot passes through the points (2, 5) and (8, 9). What is the slope of the line? Round to the nearest tenth.
questions.hint: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.
questions.explanation: Slope = (9 − 5) ÷ (8 − 2) = 4 ÷ 6 ≈ 0.67. Rounded to the nearest tenth, the slope is about 0.7.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the points (1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 3), (5, 4) and (6, 4). What is the approximate slope of the line of best fit, to the nearest tenth?
questions.hint: y goes up by about 2 while x goes up by about 5.
questions.explanation: The points rise, so the slope is positive. From about (1, 2) to (6, 4.5) the line rises 2.5 over a run of 5, or using the trend, y increases by 1 for every 2 steps in x. That gives a slope of about 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5. The value 2.0 is the run over the rise, upside down.

questions.q: A line of fit for hours studied (x) and test score (y) passes through (2, 60) and (7, 85). What is the slope of the line of fit?
questions.hint: Divide the change in score by the change in hours.
questions.explanation: Slope = (85 − 60) ÷ (7 − 2) = 25 ÷ 5 = 5. The score increases by about 5 points for each extra hour of study.

questions.q: Match each data set to the type of correlation it shows.

left: Cinema ticket price (AED) each year from 2010 to 2016: 30, 32, 33, 35, 36, 38, 40
Hours of TV per day and test score: (1, 88), (2, 81), (3, 75), (4, 70), (5, 62)
Birth month and height of 30 students: the points form a random cloud
Age of a car (years) and its resale value: the older the car, the lower the value

questions.hint: Ask: as x increases, does y tend to go up, go down, or show no pattern?
questions.explanation: Ticket prices go up as the years go up: positive. Test scores go down as TV hours go up: negative. Birth month and height show no pattern: no correlation. Resale value goes down as age goes up: negative.

questions.q: The number of visitors to a museum (in thousands) from 2015 to 2021 was 120, 128, 135, 141, 150, 158 and 163. Complete each statement about a scatter plot of year (x) and visitors (y).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Type of correlation (positive, negative or none):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The number of visitors was generally (increasing, decreasing or staying the same):

questions.hint: Look at whether the visitor numbers rise or fall as the years go by.
questions.explanation: Every year the number of visitors is larger than the year before, so the points rise from left to right. That is a positive correlation, and visitors were increasing.

questions.q: From 2005 to 2020, the number of homes in a city with a landline phone went down almost every year. Which describes a scatter plot of year (x) and number of homes with a landline (y)?
options: A correlation cannot be described for years
questions.hint: When x increases and y decreases, what kind of correlation is it?
questions.explanation: As the year increases, the number of landlines decreases. Points that fall from left to right show a negative correlation.

questions.q: The number of members in a sports club is modelled with x = years since 2010. Two points on the line of fit are (2, 40) and (8, 70).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Slope of the line of fit:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Equation of the line of fit: y =

questions.hint: Find the slope, use point-slope form, then remember that 2024 is x = 14.

questions.q: The price of a gadget (in AED, y) is modelled with x = years since 2012. A line of fit passes through (3, 52) and (9, 34). Write the equation of the line of fit in slope-intercept form.
questions.hint: Find the slope first, then substitute one point to find the y-intercept.

questions.q: A line of fit for the average length of a concert (minutes) is y = 2.5x + 140, where x is the number of years since 2000. Complete the table.
questions.hint: x is the year minus 2000; to go backwards from y, solve 2.5x + 140 = y.

questions.q: A line of fit was made from data collected from 2005 to 2017. Which prediction from this line is likely to be the least reliable?
questions.hint: Predictions are most reliable inside or just outside the range of the data.
questions.explanation: Predicting inside the data range (2010, 2016) or just after it (2018) is fairly reliable. 2060 is more than 40 years beyond the data, and the trend may change a lot in that time, so this extrapolation is the least reliable.

questions.q: Complete the statement: A strong negative correlation between two variables ______ indicates that one variable causes the other.
questions.hint: Think about whether correlation proves causation.
questions.explanation: Two variables can be strongly correlated because one causes the other, or because both depend on a third factor, or just by coincidence. So a strong correlation, positive or negative, only sometimes indicates causation.

questions.q: Decide whether each statement is always, sometimes or never true.

left: A scatter plot whose points form a random cloud shows a strong correlation.
A correlation between two variables means one variable causes the other.
If the points rise from left to right, the data show a positive correlation.
Two strongly correlated variables are both affected by a third factor.

questions.hint: Remember: correlation does not automatically mean causation.
questions.explanation: A random cloud has no correlation, so statement 1 is never true. Correlation sometimes comes with causation, so statement 2 is sometimes true. Rising points always show positive correlation. A hidden third factor is sometimes, but not always, the reason for a correlation.

questions.q: Type always, sometimes or never: A scatter plot that shows no correlation ______ has its points lying close to a straight line with a nonzero slope.
questions.hint: Points close to a slanted line would show a strong correlation.
questions.explanation: If points lie close to a line that slants up or down, the variables are strongly correlated. A plot with no correlation has no such pattern, so this never happens.

questions.q: Decide whether each situation illustrates correlation and causation, correlation but not causation, or neither.

left: As the outdoor temperature rises, a kiosk sells more cold drinks.
In summer, both ice-cream sales and the number of sunburns increase.
A survey finds no relationship between students' favourite colour and their math scores.
The more kilometres a car is driven, the more fuel it uses.

questions.hint: First ask if the variables are related; then ask if one directly causes the other.
questions.explanation: Hot weather makes people buy cold drinks, and driving farther uses more fuel: correlation and causation. Ice cream does not cause sunburn; both are caused by sunny weather: correlation but not causation. Colour and math score are not related: neither.

questions.q: Cities with more fire stations tend to have more fires each year. Which best describes this situation?
questions.hint: Is there a third factor that could increase both quantities?
questions.explanation: The two quantities are correlated, but fire stations do not cause fires. Larger cities have both more fire stations and more fires, so city size is the hidden factor. This is correlation but not causation.

questions.q: Amira notices that her phone battery runs down faster on days when she plays more games on it. Which best describes this situation?
questions.hint: Does playing games actually use battery power?
questions.explanation: More game time goes with faster battery drain, so the variables are correlated. Running games uses the screen and processor, which directly drains the battery, so it is also causation.

questions.q: For ten days, a student recorded the minutes she practised typing and her typing speed in words per minute. The points on her scatter plot fell close to a line rising to the right. What type of relationship most likely exists?
questions.hint: Does practising typing directly improve typing speed?
questions.explanation: Points close to a rising line show a strong positive correlation. Practising typing directly makes a person faster, so there is causation as well.

questions.q: A town recorded the number of umbrellas sold and the number of car accidents each day. There was a strong positive correlation. What type of relationship most likely exists?
questions.hint: Think about what could cause both umbrella sales and accidents to rise.
questions.explanation: The data are correlated, but buying umbrellas does not cause accidents. Rainy weather increases both umbrella sales and car accidents, so this is correlation without causation.

questions.q: Complete the table. Write yes or no in each blank.

rows: Minutes a tap is left running vs litres of water used
Shoe size vs reading level of children aged 5 to 12
Last digit of a phone number vs height

questions.hint: Look for a hidden factor (like age) that might link two variables without one causing the other.
questions.explanation: A running tap directly uses more water: correlation and causation. Older children have bigger feet and read better, so shoe size and reading level are correlated because of age, not causation. Phone digits and height are unrelated: neither.

questions.q: A café owner sees a strong positive correlation between daily hot-chocolate sales and the number of scarves sold at the shop next door. She decides that advertising scarves will increase her hot-chocolate sales. Is this a reasonable conclusion?
options: No; both are probably caused by cold weather, so the correlation does not show causation.
No; because the correlation is positive, increasing one will decrease the other.
Yes; because the correlation is positive, increasing one will increase the other.
Yes; a strong positive correlation shows that scarf sales cause hot-chocolate sales.
questions.hint: Ask what makes people buy both scarves and hot chocolate.
questions.explanation: Cold weather makes people buy both scarves and hot chocolate. Selling more scarves will not change the weather, so it will not cause more hot-chocolate sales. Correlation alone does not prove causation.

questions.q: A shop manager notices a strong negative correlation between daily sales of heaters and sales of ice cream. He thinks that if the shop stops selling heaters, ice-cream sales will go up. Is this reasonable?
options: Yes; any strong correlation shows causation.
No; a negative correlation means the two sales are not related at all.
Yes; a negative correlation means removing heaters raises ice-cream sales.
No; the season or temperature affects both, so removing heaters will not cause more ice-cream sales.
questions.hint: A negative correlation is still a correlation; it does not show cause.
questions.explanation: Heaters sell well in cold weather and ice cream sells well in hot weather, so temperature drives both. Removing heaters does not make the weather warmer, so ice-cream sales will not rise because of it.

questions.q: A study finds a strong positive correlation between the number of lifeguards on duty at a beach and the number of swimmers rescued each day.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Type of correlation (positive, negative or none):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Would hiring fewer lifeguards reduce the number of people who need rescuing? (yes or no)

questions.hint: Think about why a beach would have more lifeguards on some days.
questions.explanation: As one number goes up, so does the other, so the correlation is positive. On busy days there are more swimmers, so more lifeguards are hired and more people need help. Fewer lifeguards would not make swimmers safer, so the answer is no.

questions.q: Consider the scenario. Identify the sentence that is NOT mathematically accurate. A coach made a scatter plot of hours of practice and goals scored for each player. The points formed a decreasing pattern. The coach concluded that there was a positive correlation. He decided to collect more data before making a decision.
options: The coach concluded that there was a positive correlation.
A coach made a scatter plot of hours of practice and goals scored for each player.
He decided to collect more data before making a decision.
The points formed a decreasing pattern.
questions.hint: What kind of correlation does a decreasing pattern show?
questions.explanation: A decreasing pattern means that as one variable increases the other decreases, which is a negative correlation. Concluding a positive correlation is therefore not accurate; the other sentences are fine.

questions.q: Consider the scenario. Identify the sentence that is NOT mathematically accurate. A researcher compared the number of libraries and the number of reported crimes in 20 cities. The data formed an increasing linear pattern. The researcher said there was a positive correlation between libraries and crimes. Because of this, the researcher believed that building libraries causes crime.
options: The data formed an increasing linear pattern.
The researcher said there was a positive correlation between libraries and crimes.
Because of this, the researcher believed that building libraries causes crime.
A researcher compared the number of libraries and the number of reported crimes in 20 cities.
questions.hint: Correlation does not prove causation.
questions.explanation: An increasing pattern does show a positive correlation, so the first three sentences are accurate. Larger cities have both more libraries and more crimes, so population is a third factor. Claiming that libraries cause crime is not supported by the data.

questions.q: Decide whether each statement is mathematically accurate.

left: Points rising from left to right show a positive correlation.
A strong correlation proves that one variable causes the other.
Points with no clear pattern show no correlation.
A negative correlation means that as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease.
Points falling from left to right show a positive correlation.

questions.hint: Check the direction of the points and whether a cause is being claimed.
questions.explanation: Rising points mean positive correlation and falling points mean negative correlation, so statement 5 is wrong. Random points show no correlation. A correlation never proves causation by itself, so statement 2 is not accurate.

questions.q: In a garden, the weekly harvests (cucumbers kg, tomatoes kg) for five weeks were (3, 4), (5, 5.5), (6, 7), (8, 8) and (10, 9.5).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Type of correlation (positive, negative or none):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Does this show correlation or causation?

questions.hint: Look at whether tomatoes go up or down as cucumbers go up.
questions.explanation: As the cucumber harvest increases, the tomato harvest also increases, so the correlation is positive. Cucumbers do not make tomatoes grow; both depend on things like weather, sunlight and watering, so this is correlation, not causation.

questions.q: A farmer records the weekly harvest (apples, pears) in crates for five weeks: (1, 6), (2, 5), (4, 4), (5, 2) and (7, 1). Plot the five points to make a scatter plot.
questions.hint: Move right by the apples value, then up by the pears value.
questions.explanation: Plot each ordered pair (apples, pears). The points fall from left to right, which shows a negative correlation.

questions.q: Over five weeks, the hours of rain were 2, 5, 8, 10 and 14 and the numbers of visitors to an outdoor pool were 300, 260, 210, 180 and 120. Which statement is true?
options: There is a positive correlation: as the hours of rain increase, the number of visitors increases.
There is a negative correlation: as the hours of rain increase, the number of visitors decreases.
There is a negative correlation, so fewer visitors cause more rain.
There is no correlation between hours of rain and visitors.
questions.hint: Look at how the visitor numbers change as rain increases.
questions.explanation: Rain hours go up while visitor numbers go down every week, so the correlation is negative. Visitors cannot cause rain, so the last option reverses the cause.

questions.q: A relation is {(−2, 5), (0, −1), (4, 3)}. Complete the table for the inverse of the relation.
questions.hint: To find an inverse, swap the x- and y-coordinates of every pair.
questions.explanation: Swapping each pair gives (5, −2), (−1, 0) and (3, 4). So the missing values are −2, 0 and 3.

questions.q: A table defines a relation with x-values 1, 2, 6 and matching y-values −3, 4, 0. Which set shows the inverse of the relation?
questions.hint: Swap the coordinates; do not change any signs.
questions.explanation: The relation is {(1, −3), (2, 4), (6, 0)}. Swapping x and y gives {(−3, 1), (4, 2), (0, 6)}. The other choices change signs instead of swapping.

questions.q: Match each point of a relation to the matching point of its inverse.
questions.hint: (a, b) becomes (b, a).
questions.explanation: Swap each pair: (2, −7) → (−7, 2), (−3, 4) → (4, −3), (0, 6) → (6, 0), and (5, 5) stays (5, 5) because both coordinates are equal.

questions.q: Find the inverse of the relation {(1, 8), (3, 6), (−2, 0)}. Give the inverse point for each pair.
questions.hint: Swap the order of the coordinates in each pair.
questions.explanation: The inverse switches x and y, so (1, 8) → (8, 1), (3, 6) → (6, 3) and (−2, 0) → (0, −2).

questions.q: Find the inverse of the relation {(5, −1), (0, 4), (−3, 9)}.
questions.hint: Switch the x- and y-coordinates of every pair.
questions.explanation: Swapping gives (−1, 5), (4, 0) and (9, −3). Changing signs is not the same as finding an inverse, and every pair must be swapped, including (0, 4).

questions.q: Plot the inverse of the relation {(1, 3), (−2, 4), (5, 0)}.
questions.hint: Swap each pair before you plot it.
questions.explanation: The inverse is {(3, 1), (4, −2), (0, 5)}. Plot these three points.

questions.q: A graph shows a relation made of the points (−3, 2), (1, 0) and (4, −1). Which ordered pairs represent the inverse of the relation?
questions.hint: Read each point as (x, y) and write (y, x).
questions.explanation: Swapping the coordinates gives (2, −3), (0, 1) and (−1, 4). The other choices change signs, which reflects the points instead of swapping the coordinates.

questions.q: A graph shows a relation made of the points (−4, 1), (−1, 3), (2, −2) and (3, 3). Plot the points of the inverse relation.
questions.hint: Each point (x, y) becomes (y, x).
questions.explanation: The inverse points are (1, −4), (3, −1), (−2, 2) and (3, 3). The point (3, 3) stays the same because it lies on the line y = x.

questions.q: The point (−5, 2) is on the graph of a relation. What point must be on the graph of its inverse? Write it as an ordered pair.
questions.hint: Swap the coordinates.
questions.explanation: The inverse of a relation switches every x-coordinate with its y-coordinate, so (−5, 2) becomes (2, −5).

questions.hint: This is point-slope form: read the point (x₁, y₁) and the slope m.
questions.explanation: The line passes through (3, 1) with slope 2/3. From (3, 1) go up 2 and right 3 to reach (6, 3). The point (0, −1) is also on the line.

questions.hint: The point is (1, −4); be careful with the signs.
questions.explanation: The line passes through (1, −4) with slope −3/2. From (1, −4) go up 3 and left 2 to reach (−1, −1), or down 3 and right 2 to reach (3, −7).

questions.q: Complete the table of values for y + 2 = 3(x − 1).
questions.hint: Rewrite the equation as y = 3x − 5 first.
questions.explanation: y + 2 = 3x − 3, so y = 3x − 5. Then x = 0 gives −5, x = 1 gives −2, x = 2 gives 1. For y = 4: 3x − 5 = 4, so x = 3.

questions.q: Which point and slope are shown by the equation y − 5 = −4(x + 2)?
questions.hint: Point-slope form is y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
questions.explanation: Write x + 2 as x − (−2), so x₁ = −2. The y-part is y − 5, so y₁ = 5. The slope is the number in front of the brackets, −4.

questions.q: Graph the inverse of f(x) = 4x.
questions.hint: Swap x and y in y = 4x and solve for y.
questions.explanation: Swapping gives x = 4y, so y = x/4. The inverse is the line through (0, 0) and (4, 1), rising 1 for every 4 to the right.

questions.q: Graph the inverse of f(x) = −(1/2)x.
questions.hint: Write x = −(1/2)y and solve for y.
questions.explanation: Swapping gives x = −(1/2)y, so y = −2x. The inverse passes through (0, 0) and (1, −2).

questions.q: What is the inverse of f(x) = (5/2)x?
questions.hint: Swap x and y, then divide by 5/2.
questions.explanation: From x = (5/2)y, multiply both sides by 2/5 to get y = (2/5)x. The slope of the inverse is the reciprocal of the original slope, with the same sign.

questions.q: Graph the inverse of f(x) = x + 3.
questions.hint: The inverse undoes adding 3.
questions.explanation: Swapping gives x = y + 3, so y = x − 3. The inverse passes through (0, −3) and (3, 0).

questions.q: Which function is the inverse of f(x) = 3x + 12?
questions.hint: Swap x and y, then solve for y step by step.
questions.explanation: Write x = 3y + 12. Subtract 12: x − 12 = 3y. Divide by 3: y = (1/3)x − 4. Dividing only x by 3 and not the 12 gives the wrong answer (1/3)x − 12.

questions.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = 4x − 8. Write f⁻¹(x) in slope-intercept form.
questions.hint: Swap x and y, add 8, then divide by 4.

questions.q: Match each function to its inverse.
questions.hint: For each function, swap x and y and solve for y.
questions.explanation: x = 2y + 10 gives y = (1/2)x − 5. x = (1/2)y + 5 gives y = 2x − 10. x = 5y − 2 gives y = (x + 2)/5. x = −y + 5 gives y = −x + 5, so this function is its own inverse.

questions.q: Find the equation of the inverse of f(x) = (2/5)x + 3. Write it in slope-intercept form.
questions.hint: Swap x and y, subtract 3, then multiply by 5/2.

questions.q: What is the inverse of f(x) = (2/3)x − 4?
questions.hint: Add 4 before multiplying by 3/2.
questions.explanation: x = (2/3)y − 4, so x + 4 = (2/3)y. Multiply by 3/2: y = (3/2)(x + 4) = (3/2)x + 6. Forgetting to multiply the 4 by 3/2 gives the wrong answer (3/2)x + 4.

questions.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = (1/4)x + 3/2 and complete each statement.
questions.hint: Swap x and y, subtract 3/2, then multiply by 4.
questions.explanation: x = (1/4)y + 3/2, so x − 3/2 = (1/4)y and y = 4x − 6. The slope is 4 and the y-intercept is −6. Then f⁻¹(10) = 40 − 6 = 34; check: f(34) = 8.5 + 1.5 = 10.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the inverse of y = −3x + 7?
