questions.q: In parallelogram PQRS, the diagonals meet at T. PQ = 14, QR = 9, PT = 8, QT = 6 and m∠P = 72°. Match each measure to its value.
questions.hint: Opposite sides are equal, diagonals bisect each other, consecutive angles are supplementary.
questions.explanation: RS = PQ = 14 and PS = QR = 9. TR = PT = 8 and QS = 2 × 6 = 12. m∠Q = 180 − 72 = 108°.

questions.q: Three congruent rhombus tiles meet at one point with no gaps or overlaps (like the visible faces of a cube drawing). Each tile has the same angle at the shared point.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Angle of each tile at the shared point (degrees) =

questions.hint: The angles around a point add to 360°.
questions.explanation: The three equal angles fill 360°, so each is 120°. Consecutive angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so the other angle is 180 − 120 = 60°.

questions.q: Points A, B and C lie on a straight line in that order. Above the line, two congruent parallelogram tiles have angles ∠ABX and ∠YBC at B, and these two angles are equal. A rhombus tile fills the gap between them with m∠XBY = 70°. What is m∠ABX?
questions.hint: The three angles at B form a straight angle.
questions.explanation: m∠ABX + 70° + m∠YBC = 180° and the two outer angles are equal, so 2·m∠ABX = 110° and m∠ABX = 55°.

questions.q: Six congruent rhombus tiles meet at one point to form a star, each with its acute angle at the point and no gaps. What is the obtuse angle of each rhombus, in degrees?
questions.hint: Find the acute angle first using 360°.
questions.explanation: Six equal acute angles fill 360°, so each is 60°. The obtuse angle is 180 − 60 = 120°.

questions.q: Quadrilateral QRST has vertices Q(−3, −1), R(−1, 3), S(4, 4) and T(2, 0). Complete the table using the distance formula. Give exact lengths.
questions.hint: d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).
questions.explanation: QR = √(2² + 4²) = √20, RS = √(5² + 1²) = √26, ST = √(2² + 4²) = √20, TQ = √(5² + 1²) = √26. Both pairs of opposite sides are congruent, so QRST is a parallelogram.

questions.q: Quadrilateral ABCD has vertices A(−4, 1), B(−2, 4), C(3, 4) and D(2, 1). Is ABCD a parallelogram?
options: No, only one pair of opposite sides is parallel.
No, because no sides are parallel.
questions.hint: Compare the slopes of AB and DC, and of BC and AD.
questions.explanation: BC and AD are both horizontal, so they are parallel. Slope AB = 3/2 but slope DC = (4 − 1) ÷ (3 − 2) = 3, so AB is not parallel to DC. ABCD is a trapezoid, not a parallelogram.

questions.q: Q(−2, 0), R(−4, 3) and S(1, 4) are three vertices of parallelogram QRST. Plot the fourth vertex T.
questions.hint: The move from R to S equals the move from Q to T.
questions.explanation: From R(−4, 3) to S(1, 4): 5 right, 1 up. Apply to Q(−2, 0): T = (3, 1).

questions.q: Match each parallelogram (base and height in cm) to its area in cm².
questions.hint: Area of a parallelogram = base × height.

questions.q: A parallelogram has a base of 10 cm and a slanted side of 13 cm. A perpendicular drawn from an upper vertex to the base cuts off 5 cm of the base. What is the area?
questions.hint: Use the Pythagorean theorem to find the height first.
questions.explanation: The height h satisfies h² + 5² = 13², so h² = 144 and h = 12 cm. Area = base × height = 10 × 12 = 120 cm². Using the slanted side (10 × 13 = 130) is a common mistake.

questions.q: Complete the table for parallelograms (lengths in cm, area in cm²).
questions.hint: A = b × h, so b = A ÷ h and h = A ÷ b.

questions.q: A parallelogram has a base of 20 cm and a slanted side of 10 cm. The height drawn from an upper vertex meets the base 6 cm from the nearest corner. What is the area?
questions.hint: Find the height from the right triangle with hypotenuse 10 cm and leg 6 cm.
questions.explanation: h² + 6² = 10², so h² = 64 and h = 8 cm. Area = 20 × 8 = 160 cm².

questions.q: A parallelogram has a slanted side of 17 cm and a base of 21 cm. The height from an upper vertex cuts off 8 cm along the base.
questions.hint: Use the Pythagorean theorem: h² + 8² = 17².

questions.q: A parallelogram has area 96 cm², base 12 cm and slanted side 10 cm. A height is drawn from an upper vertex to the base. How far along the base (in cm) is the foot of the height from the nearest corner?
questions.hint: Find the height from the area, then use the Pythagorean theorem.
questions.explanation: Height = 96 ÷ 12 = 8 cm. The slanted side, the height and the base piece form a right triangle: piece² + 8² = 10², so piece² = 36 and the piece is 6 cm.

questions.q: In rectangle PQRS, the diagonals meet at T. If PR = 4x − 6 and QT = x + 7, what is QS?
questions.hint: The diagonals are congruent, and QS = 2 × QT.
questions.explanation: QS = 2(x + 7) = 2x + 14 and PR = QS, so 4x − 6 = 2x + 14, giving x = 10. QS = 2(17) = 34.

questions.q: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals meet at E. If AE = 2y + 1 and DE = 4y − 7, find BD.
questions.hint: In a rectangle the diagonals are congruent and bisect each other, so all four half-diagonals are equal.
questions.explanation: AE = DE: 2y + 1 = 4y − 7, so y = 4 and DE = 9. BD = 2 × 9 = 18.

questions.q: In rectangle JKLM, the diagonals meet at N. JL = 5a − 3 and KM = 3a + 9.
questions.hint: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent.
questions.explanation: 5a − 3 = 3a + 9 gives a = 6, so JL = 27. N is the midpoint of JL, so JN = 27 ÷ 2 = 13.5.

questions.q: Rectangle ABCD has A at top-left, B at top-right, C at bottom-right and D at bottom-left. Its diagonals meet at E, and m∠AEB = 110°. Find each angle in degrees.
questions.hint: EA = EB, so triangle AEB is isosceles.
questions.explanation: Base angles of triangle AEB: (180 − 110) ÷ 2 = 35°, so m∠EAB = m∠EBA = 35°. ∠BEC and ∠AEB form a linear pair, so m∠BEC = 70°. m∠EBC = 90 − 35 = 55°.

questions.q: In rectangle WXYZ (vertices in order), the diagonals meet at P and m∠PWX = 28°. What is m∠WPX?
questions.hint: PW = PX, so triangle WPX is isosceles.

questions.q: In rectangle KLMN (vertices in order), the diagonals meet at O and m∠KOL = 64°. Find m∠OLM in degrees.
questions.hint: Find the base angles of isosceles triangle KOL first.

questions.q: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals meet at E. Each row gives one length; fill in the others.
questions.hint: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so all four half-diagonals are equal.
questions.explanation: Each half-diagonal is half of a full diagonal, and both diagonals are equal. Row 1: halves 7, diagonals 14. Row 2: diagonals 30, halves 15. Row 3: halves 4.5, diagonals 9.

questions.q: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals meet at E. If AE = 3x + 1 and CE = x + 9, what is BD?
questions.hint: E is the midpoint of AC, and BD = AC.
questions.explanation: 3x + 1 = x + 9 gives x = 4, so AE = 13 and AC = 26. The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent, so BD = 26.

questions.q: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals meet at E. AC = 6x − 4 and BE = 2x + 3.
questions.hint: BD = 2 × BE and BD = AC.
questions.explanation: 6x − 4 = 2(2x + 3) = 4x + 6 gives x = 5. AC = 26, and DE = BE = 13.

questions.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Which additional statement proves it is a rectangle?
questions.hint: Which diagonal property belongs only to rectangles?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle. Perpendicular diagonals, congruent consecutive sides, or a diagonal bisecting an angle make it a rhombus instead.

questions.q: Match each description to whether it is always a rectangle.

left: A parallelogram with one right angle
A quadrilateral with four right angles
A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other and are congruent

questions.hint: An isosceles trapezoid has congruent diagonals; a rhombus has perpendicular diagonals.
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with one right angle has four right angles. Four right angles is the definition. Bisecting diagonals make a parallelogram, and congruent diagonals then make it a rectangle. An isosceles trapezoid has congruent diagonals, and a rhombus has perpendicular diagonals, but neither is always a rectangle.

questions.q: Which statement CANNOT be used to prove a quadrilateral is a rectangle?
options: The quadrilateral has two right angles.
The quadrilateral has four right angles.
The quadrilateral is a parallelogram with one right angle.
The quadrilateral is a parallelogram with congruent diagonals.
questions.hint: Think of a right trapezoid.
questions.explanation: A right trapezoid has two right angles but is not a rectangle. The other three statements are rectangle tests.

questions.q: Rectangle ABCD has A at top-left, B at bottom-left, C at bottom-right and D at top-right. Its diagonals meet at E, and m∠BDC = 58°. Find each angle in degrees.
questions.hint: The half-diagonals are equal, so the four small triangles are isosceles.
questions.explanation: ∠ADC = 90°, so m∠ADB = 90 − 58 = 32°. Triangle AED is isosceles with EA = ED, so m∠EAD = 32° and m∠AED = 180 − 64 = 116°. AD ∥ BC, so m∠ACB = m∠CAD = 32°.

questions.q: In rectangle PQRS, diagonal PR makes a 40° angle with side PQ. What is the acute angle formed where the diagonals intersect?
questions.hint: Let the diagonals meet at T; triangle PTQ is isosceles.
questions.explanation: In triangle PTQ, m∠TPQ = m∠TQP = 40°, so m∠PTQ = 100°. The acute angle between the diagonals is 180 − 100 = 80°.

questions.q: In rectangle WXYZ (vertices in order), the diagonals meet at V and m∠WVX = 130°. Find m∠VWZ in degrees.
questions.hint: Find the base angles of triangle WVX first.

questions.q: In parallelogram PQRS, PQ = x + 2, QR = x, PR = 2x − 2 and QS = 10. What value of x makes PQRS a rectangle?
questions.hint: A parallelogram is a rectangle when its diagonals are congruent.
questions.explanation: Set PR = QS: 2x − 2 = 10, so x = 6. Check: PQ = 8, QR = 6 and 8² + 6² = 100 = 10², so angle Q is a right angle.

questions.q: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 12, BC = 5 and diagonal AC = 3y + 1. What value of y makes ABCD a rectangle?
questions.hint: In a rectangle, triangle ABC is a right triangle.
questions.explanation: For a rectangle, AC² = 12² + 5² = 169, so AC = 13. Then 3y + 1 = 13 and y = 4.

questions.q: In parallelogram JKLM, the diagonals are JL = 5n − 3 and KM = 3n + 7. For JKLM to be a rectangle:

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Distance from J to where the diagonals meet =

questions.hint: Set the diagonals equal.
questions.explanation: 5n − 3 = 3n + 7 gives n = 5, so each diagonal is 22. The diagonals bisect each other, so the distance is 22 ÷ 2 = 11.

questions.q: Quadrilateral PQRS is a rhombus. Which statement must be true?
questions.hint: Recall the diagonal properties of a rhombus.
questions.explanation: Each diagonal of a rhombus bisects a pair of opposite angles. Congruent diagonals and right angles happen only when the rhombus is also a square.

questions.q: Write yes or no for whether each property is true for every shape.
questions.hint: Rectangles add congruent diagonals; rhombi add perpendicular diagonals and equal sides.
questions.explanation: All parallelograms have diagonals that bisect each other. Only rectangles are guaranteed congruent diagonals. Only rhombi are guaranteed perpendicular diagonals and four congruent sides.

questions.q: In rhombus ABCD, the diagonals meet at E. AB = 10 and AE = 6. Match each measure to its value.
questions.hint: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular and bisect each other.
questions.explanation: The diagonals are perpendicular, so m∠AEB = 90°. All sides are equal, so BC = 10. In right triangle AEB, BE = √(10² − 6²) = 8. AC = 2 × 6 = 12.

questions.q: In rhombus ABCD, m∠BAC = 32°. What is m∠ABC?
questions.hint: Diagonal AC bisects ∠BAD.
questions.explanation: m∠BAD = 2 × 32 = 64°. Consecutive angles are supplementary, so m∠ABC = 180 − 64 = 116°.

questions.q: In rhombus PQRS, the diagonals meet at T and m∠PQR = 110°. Find each angle in degrees.
questions.hint: Diagonals bisect the angles and are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: m∠QPS = 180 − 110 = 70°, and diagonal PR bisects it, so m∠QPR = 35°. The diagonals are perpendicular, so m∠PTQ = 90°. Diagonal QS bisects ∠PQR, so m∠PQT = 55°.

questions.q: In rhombus WXYZ, m∠XWY = (3x + 5)° and m∠ZWY = (5x − 15)°. Find m∠XWZ in degrees.
questions.hint: Diagonal WY bisects ∠XWZ.
questions.explanation: 3x + 5 = 5x − 15 gives x = 10, so each half is 35°. m∠XWZ = 2 × 35 = 70°.

questions.q: A quadrilateral is a rhombus. It must be a square if it is also a ______.
questions.hint: A rhombus already has four equal sides; what is still missing for a square?
questions.explanation: A square needs four equal sides and four right angles. A rhombus gives the equal sides, and a rectangle gives the right angles. Every rhombus is already a parallelogram, so only 'rectangle' adds the missing property.

questions.q: Match each description to the most specific name of the quadrilateral.

left: A rectangle whose diagonals are perpendicular
A rhombus with one right angle
A parallelogram whose diagonals are congruent
A parallelogram whose diagonals are perpendicular

questions.hint: Congruent diagonals turn a parallelogram into a rectangle; perpendicular diagonals turn it into a rhombus.
questions.explanation: A rectangle with perpendicular diagonals is also a rhombus, so it is a square. A rhombus with a right angle is also a rectangle, so it is a square. A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle, and one with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus.

questions.q: For each statement, type Always, Sometimes, or Never.
questions.hint: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus, but not every rectangle or rhombus is a square.
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides and four right angles, so it is always a rhombus and always a rectangle. A rhombus is a square only when its angles are 90°, and a rectangle is a square only when its sides are all equal, so those are 'sometimes'.

questions.q: Quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus. Which additional fact would prove that ABCD is a square?
questions.hint: Look for the fact that a rhombus does not already have.
questions.explanation: Every rhombus already has perpendicular diagonals, equal sides, and diagonals that bisect its angles. A right angle is the only listed fact that a rhombus does not always have. A rhombus with a right angle is also a rectangle, so it is a square.

questions.q: Quadrilateral PQRS is a rectangle. Which additional fact would prove that PQRS is a square?
questions.hint: A rectangle already has congruent diagonals and right angles.
questions.explanation: Rectangles always have congruent diagonals, parallel opposite sides, and equal angles. If the diagonals are also perpendicular, the rectangle is a rhombus too. A quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus is a square.

questions.q: Decide whether each quadrilateral must be a square. Type Yes or No.

rows: A rectangle whose diagonals bisect each other
A rectangle with two consecutive sides congruent

questions.hint: A square must be both a rhombus and a rectangle; check which extra fact gives the missing property.
questions.explanation: A rhombus with congruent diagonals is a rectangle, so it is a square. Every rhombus has perpendicular diagonals and every rectangle has diagonals that bisect each other, so those facts add nothing. A rectangle with perpendicular diagonals, or with two consecutive sides equal, is a rhombus, so it is a square.

questions.q: Type Yes if the quadrilateral always has the property and No if it does not.
questions.hint: Parallelograms' diagonals bisect each other; right angles add congruent diagonals and equal sides add perpendicular diagonals.
questions.explanation: Every parallelogram, including rectangles and rhombuses, has diagonals that bisect each other. A rectangle's diagonals are also congruent, and a rhombus's diagonals are also perpendicular. A kite's diagonals are perpendicular, but only one of them is bisected, so they do not bisect each other.

questions.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are both congruent and perpendicular?
questions.hint: Congruent diagonals come from a rectangle and perpendicular diagonals come from a rhombus.
questions.explanation: A rectangle's diagonals are congruent but not always perpendicular. A rhombus's diagonals are perpendicular but not always congruent. A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus, so its diagonals are both.

questions.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other and are perpendicular, but they are not congruent. Name the most specific type of quadrilateral.
questions.hint: Diagonals that bisect each other make a parallelogram; what does perpendicular add?
questions.explanation: Diagonals that bisect each other make the shape a parallelogram. A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. Because the diagonals are not congruent, it is not a rectangle, so it is not a square.

questions.q: In square ABCD the diagonals intersect at E. What is m∠AEB?
questions.hint: Think about how the diagonals of a square (a rhombus) meet.
questions.explanation: A square is a rhombus, and the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. So the diagonals meet at right angles, and m∠AEB = 90°. The 45° angles are between a diagonal and a side, not between the two diagonals.

questions.q: A rhombus-shaped tile has an angle of 120° at vertex P. The diagonal drawn from P meets each side at P at what angle? Give the number of degrees.
questions.hint: In a rhombus each diagonal bisects the angles at its endpoints.
questions.explanation: The diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angle at each vertex it joins. So it splits the 120° angle into two equal parts. 120° ÷ 2 = 60°.

questions.q: Square WXYZ has diagonals WY and XZ that meet at O. Complete each measure (in degrees).
questions.hint: Diagonals of a square bisect the 90° corners and are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Diagonal WY bisects the 90° angle at W, so m∠XWY = 45°. The diagonals are perpendicular, so m∠WOX = 90°. In triangle WOX, the remaining angle is 180° − 90° − 45° = 45°.

questions.q: PQRS is a parallelogram with diagonal PR. If m∠QPR = 3x + 7 and m∠SPR = 5x − 9, for what value of x is PQRS a rhombus?
questions.hint: In a rhombus, a diagonal bisects the angles at its endpoints.
questions.explanation: For PQRS to be a rhombus, diagonal PR must bisect ∠QPS, so the two angles are equal. 3x + 7 = 5x − 9 gives 16 = 2x, so x = 8. Check: both angles are 31°.

questions.q: ABCD is a parallelogram with diagonal AC, m∠BAC = 4x − 6 and m∠DAC = 2x + 18. If ABCD is a rhombus, what is m∠BAD?
questions.hint: First set the two angle expressions equal, then add the two halves.
questions.explanation: In a rhombus, AC bisects ∠BAD, so 4x − 6 = 2x + 18, giving x = 12. Each half is 4(12) − 6 = 42°. So m∠BAD = 42° + 42° = 84°.

questions.q: JKLM is a parallelogram with diagonal JL, m∠KJL = 6x − 2 and m∠MJL = 4x + 10. JKLM is a rhombus. Complete the following.
questions.hint: A rhombus diagonal splits the vertex angle into two equal parts.
questions.explanation: Set 6x − 2 = 4x + 10, so 2x = 12 and x = 6. Then m∠KJL = 6(6) − 2 = 34°. The full angle ∠KJM is 34° + 34° = 68°.

questions.q: In square PQRS the diagonals meet at T. If PT = 2x + 5 and QS = 7x − 5, find PR.
questions.hint: PR = 2·PT, and the diagonals of a square are congruent.
questions.explanation: T is the midpoint of PR, so PR = 2(2x + 5) = 4x + 10. The diagonals of a square are congruent, so 4x + 10 = 7x − 5, giving x = 5. PR = 4(5) + 10 = 30.

questions.q: In square ABCD the diagonals AC and BD meet at M. AM = 3y − 4 and BD = 4y + 2. Complete the following.
questions.hint: AC = 2·AM and AC = BD in a square.
questions.explanation: AC = 2(3y − 4) = 6y − 8. Since the diagonals are congruent, 6y − 8 = 4y + 2, so y = 5. BD = 4(5) + 2 = 22, and BM is half of BD, so BM = 11.

questions.q: In rectangle WXYZ the diagonals meet at E. If WE = 4x − 3 and XZ = 5x + 6, what is XZ?
questions.hint: Rectangles also have congruent diagonals that bisect each other.
questions.explanation: WY = 2·WE = 8x − 6, and WY = XZ, so 8x − 6 = 5x + 6, giving x = 4. XZ = 5(4) + 6 = 26. The value 13 is only WE, half a diagonal.

questions.q: In rhombus KLMN, KL = 3x + 2 and MN = 5x − 8. What is the perimeter of KLMN?
questions.hint: All four sides of a rhombus are congruent.
questions.explanation: Set 3x + 2 = 5x − 8, so x = 5. Each side is 3(5) + 2 = 17. The perimeter is 4 × 17 = 68.

questions.q: A rhombus has a perimeter of 52 cm. What is the length of one side, in cm?
questions.hint: A rhombus has four equal sides.
questions.explanation: The four sides of a rhombus are equal. So each side is 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm.

questions.q: In rhombus ABCD, AB = 9. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Every side of a rhombus has the same length.
questions.explanation: A rhombus has four congruent sides, so BC = CD = DA = 9. The perimeter is 4 × 9 = 36.

questions.q: In square ABCD the diagonals AC and BD meet at E. If AE = 4x − 1 and BD = 6x + 4, find DE.
questions.hint: AC = 2·AE, AC = BD, and E is the midpoint of BD.
questions.explanation: AC = 2(4x − 1) = 8x − 2. The diagonals are congruent, so 8x − 2 = 6x + 4, giving x = 3. BD = 6(3) + 4 = 22, and DE is half of BD, so DE = 11.

questions.q: In square ABCD the diagonals meet at E. If AE = 2x + 1 and BE = 3x − 4, what is AC?
questions.hint: The diagonals of a square are congruent and bisect each other, so all four half-diagonals are equal.

questions.q: Square ABCD has diagonals AC and BD that meet at E, and AC = 18. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Square diagonals are congruent, bisect each other, and are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: E is the midpoint of AC, so AE = 9. The diagonals are congruent, so BD = 18 and BE = 9. They are also perpendicular, so m∠AEB = 90°.

questions.q: The diagonals of a rhombus meet at a right angle. The half-diagonals measure 8 cm and 6 cm. Find the area of the rhombus in cm².
questions.hint: Double each half-diagonal first, then use A = ½·d₁·d₂.
questions.explanation: The full diagonals are 2 × 8 = 16 cm and 2 × 6 = 12 cm. Area = ½ × 16 × 12 = 96 cm².

questions.q: A rhombus has diagonals of 14 m and 10 m. What is its area?
questions.hint: Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × 14 × 10 = ½ × 140 = 70 m². 140 forgets the ½, and 24 just adds the diagonals.

questions.q: Complete the table for rhombuses with diagonals d₁ and d₂ (Area = ½·d₁·d₂).
questions.hint: Use Area = ½·d₁·d₂ and solve for whichever value is missing.
questions.explanation: ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 and ½ × 20 × 5 = 50. For row 2, ½ × 8 × d₂ = 48 gives 4d₂ = 48, so d₂ = 12. For row 4, ½ × d₁ × 14 = 84 gives 7d₁ = 84, so d₁ = 12.

questions.q: A rhombus has sides of 13 cm and one diagonal of 24 cm. Complete the following.
questions.hint: The diagonals are perpendicular bisectors, so each side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to half-diagonals.
questions.explanation: Half of the 24 cm diagonal is 12 cm. In the right triangle with hypotenuse 13, the other leg is √(13² − 12²) = √25 = 5, so the other diagonal is 10 cm. Area = ½ × 24 × 10 = 120 cm².

questions.q: In trapezoid ABCD, the bases are AB = 9 and DC = 15. MN is the midsegment. Find MN.
questions.hint: The midsegment is the average of the bases.
questions.explanation: Midsegment = ½(9 + 15) = ½(24) = 12.

questions.q: A trapezoid has bases of length 7 and 12. What is the length of its midsegment?
questions.hint: Add the bases, then divide by 2.
questions.explanation: Midsegment = ½(7 + 12) = ½(19) = 9.5. 19 forgets to halve, and 5 is the difference of the bases.

questions.q: Complete the table for trapezoids (midsegment = ½(base₁ + base₂)).
questions.hint: The two bases must add to twice the midsegment.
questions.explanation: ½(4 + 10) = 7 and ½(3.5 + 8.5) = 6. For row 2, the bases add to 2 × 16 = 32, so base 1 = 32 − 20 = 12. For row 3, the bases add to 28, so base 2 = 28 − 11 = 17.

questions.q: Kite ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD. If m∠A = 64° and m∠C = 98°, find m∠B in degrees.
questions.hint: In a kite, the angles between the pairs of unequal sides (∠B and ∠D) are congruent.
questions.explanation: ∠B and ∠D are the non-vertex angles, so they are congruent. The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°, so 2·m∠B = 360° − 64° − 98° = 198°. m∠B = 99°.

questions.q: Kite PQRS has PQ = PS and RQ = RS. If m∠P = 50° and m∠Q = 115°, what is m∠R?
questions.hint: ∠Q and ∠S are congruent; then use the 360° angle sum.

questions.q: Kite WXYZ has WX = WZ and YX = YZ, so ∠X ≅ ∠Z. Complete the angle measures (in degrees) for two different kites.
questions.hint: ∠X and ∠Z are equal, and all four angles add to 360°.

questions.q: ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with bases BC ∥ AD and legs AB and CD. If m∠A = 65°, match each angle to its measure.
questions.hint: Base angles of an isosceles trapezoid are congruent; angles along a leg are supplementary.
questions.explanation: ∠A and ∠D are base angles of base AD, so m∠D = 65°. ∠A and ∠B lie along leg AB between parallel lines, so m∠B = 180° − 65° = 115°. ∠C is the other base angle of BC, so m∠C = 115°.

questions.q: JKLM is an isosceles trapezoid with JK ∥ ML and legs JM and KL. If m∠J = 112°, what is m∠M?
questions.hint: ∠J and ∠M lie along the same leg between the parallel bases.
questions.explanation: ∠J and ∠M are consecutive angles along leg JM, so they are supplementary. m∠M = 180° − 112° = 68°.

questions.q: In isosceles trapezoid PQRS with PQ ∥ SR, m∠S = 3x + 10 and m∠R = 5x − 20. Find m∠P in degrees.
questions.hint: ∠S and ∠R are base angles of the same base, so they are equal.
questions.explanation: Set 3x + 10 = 5x − 20, so x = 15 and m∠S = 55°. ∠P and ∠S lie along leg PS, so they are supplementary. m∠P = 180° − 55° = 125°.

questions.q: Trapezoid ABCD has vertices A(0, 0), B(2, 6), C(8, 6), and D(14, 0). What is the length of its midsegment?
questions.hint: Find the lengths of the two horizontal bases first.
questions.explanation: BC is on y = 6 with length 8 − 2 = 6. AD is on y = 0 with length 14 − 0 = 14. Midsegment = ½(6 + 14) = 10.

questions.q: Trapezoid PQRS has vertices P(−4, −2), Q(−2, 4), R(4, 4), and S(6, −2), with bases QR and PS. Plot the two endpoints of the midsegment (the midpoints of legs PQ and RS).
questions.hint: Use the midpoint formula ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2) on each leg.
questions.explanation: Midpoint of PQ = ((−4 + −2)/2, (−2 + 4)/2) = (−3, 1). Midpoint of RS = ((4 + 6)/2, (4 + −2)/2) = (5, 1). The midsegment runs from (−3, 1) to (5, 1), so it has length 8, which equals ½(6 + 10).

questions.q: A trapezoid has vertices (1, 1), (3, 5), (7, 5), and (11, 1). What is the length of its midsegment?
questions.hint: The bases are the horizontal sides on y = 5 and y = 1.
questions.explanation: The top base runs from x = 3 to x = 7, length 4. The bottom base runs from x = 1 to x = 11, length 10. Midsegment = ½(4 + 10) = 7.

questions.q: Type Yes or No for each quadrilateral.

headers: Diagonals bisect both pairs of opposite angles

questions.hint: Equal sides are what make a diagonal bisect the angles at its ends.
questions.explanation: In a rhombus and a square all four sides are equal, so both diagonals bisect the angles and are perpendicular. A kite's diagonals are perpendicular, but only one diagonal bisects a pair of angles. A general parallelogram or rectangle has neither property.

questions.q: Kite ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD. Which diagonal bisects ∠A and ∠C?
questions.hint: The kite's line of symmetry passes through the vertices where the congruent sides meet.
questions.explanation: A and C are the vertices where each pair of congruent sides meets. Diagonal AC is the kite's line of symmetry, so it bisects ∠A and ∠C. Diagonal BD does not bisect ∠B or ∠D.

questions.q: In rhombus ABCD, m∠ABC = 130°. Find m∠ABD in degrees.
questions.hint: Each diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angles at its endpoints.
questions.explanation: Diagonal BD bisects ∠ABC. So m∠ABD = 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.

questions.q: A trapezoid has bases 4x + 3 and 2x − 7. Write a simplified expression for the length of its midsegment.
questions.hint: Add the bases and divide by 2.
questions.explanation: Midsegment = ½[(4x + 3) + (2x − 7)] = ½(6x − 4). This simplifies to 3x − 2.

questions.q: A trapezoid has bases 5x − 1 and x + 9. Which expression gives the length of its midsegment?
questions.hint: Combine like terms, then halve every term.
questions.explanation: (5x − 1) + (x + 9) = 6x + 8. Half of that is 3x + 4. 6x + 8 forgets to halve, and 3x + 8 only halves the x-term.

questions.q: A trapezoid has bases 3x + 2 and 5x − 6. Complete the following.
questions.hint: Midsegment = ½(base₁ + base₂).
questions.explanation: ½[(3x + 2) + (5x − 6)] = ½(8x − 4) = 4x − 2. When x = 5, 4(5) − 2 = 18. Check: the bases are 17 and 19, and ½(36) = 18.

questions.q: PQRS is an isosceles trapezoid with longer base PQ, shorter base SR, and legs PS and QR. L and M are the midpoints of the legs. If m∠Q = 63°, match each angle to its measure.
questions.hint: Base angles are congruent; angles along a leg are supplementary.
questions.explanation: ∠P and ∠Q are base angles of PQ, so m∠P = 63°. ∠Q and ∠R lie along leg QR, so m∠R = 180° − 63° = 117°. ∠S is the other base angle of SR, so m∠S = 117°. The midsegment does not change the angles.

questions.q: Isosceles trapezoid ABCD has bases AB = 30 (bottom) and DC = 18 (top), with legs AD and BC. If m∠D = 104°, find m∠B in degrees.
questions.hint: The base lengths are not needed; use base angles and the supplementary angles along a leg.
questions.explanation: ∠D and ∠C are base angles of DC, so m∠C = 104°. ∠C and ∠B lie along leg BC, so m∠B = 180° − 104° = 76°.

questions.q: EFGH is an isosceles trapezoid with bases EF and HG. If m∠E = 72°, what is m∠F?
questions.hint: ∠E and ∠F share the same base.
questions.explanation: In an isosceles trapezoid, each pair of base angles is congruent. ∠E and ∠F are both angles of base EF, so m∠F = 72°.

questions.q: In a trapezoid the bases are 3x − 1 and x + 5, and the midsegment is 20. What is x?
questions.hint: Twice the midsegment equals the sum of the bases.
questions.explanation: (3x − 1) + (x + 5) = 2(20), so 4x + 4 = 40. Then 4x = 36 and x = 9. Forgetting to double the midsegment gives x = 4.

questions.q: In trapezoid ABCD, MN is the midsegment, AB = 2x + 4, DC = 6x − 2, and MN = 13. Find x.
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 2: 26 = 8x + 2. Then 8x = 24, so x = 3. Check: the bases are 10 and 16, and ½(26) = 13.

questions.q: A trapezoid has bases x + 6 and 3x − 4, and its midsegment is 15. Complete the following.
questions.hint: The sum of the bases is 2 × 15.

questions.q: EF is the midsegment of trapezoid ABCD with AB = x + 4, EF = 2x + 1, and DC = 34. Complete the following.
questions.hint: Set 2(midsegment) equal to the sum of the bases.

questions.q: Kite JKLM has JK = JM and LK = LM, with JK = 3y − 2, JM = y + 10, LK = 2x + 1, and LM = x + 9. Complete the following.
questions.hint: Set each pair of congruent adjacent sides equal.
questions.explanation: 3y − 2 = y + 10 gives y = 6, so JK = JM = 16. 2x + 1 = x + 9 gives x = 8, so LK = LM = 17. Perimeter = 16 + 16 + 17 + 17 = 66.

questions.q: Kite ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD. If AB = 5, BC = 3x + 1, and CD = 13, what is the perimeter of the kite?
questions.hint: Use the two pairs of equal sides to find all four side lengths.
questions.explanation: CB = CD, so 3x + 1 = 13 and x = 4, making BC = 13. AD = AB = 5. Perimeter = 5 + 5 + 13 + 13 = 36.

questions.q: A trapezoid has bases of 10 cm and 14 cm and a height of 5 cm. Find its area in cm².
questions.hint: Area = ½(b₁ + b₂)h.
questions.explanation: Add the bases: 10 + 14 = 24. Multiply by the height: 24 × 5 = 120. Take half: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 cm².

questions.q: A trapezoid-shaped garden bed has parallel sides of 9 m and 15 m, and the distance between them is 6 m. What is its area?
questions.hint: Use the average of the parallel sides times the height.
questions.explanation: Area = ½(9 + 15)(6) = ½(24)(6) = 72 m². 144 forgets the ½, and 810 multiplies all three numbers.

questions.q: Complete the table for trapezoids (Area = ½(b₁ + b₂)h).
questions.hint: Substitute the known values into A = ½(b₁ + b₂)h and solve.

questions.q: A kite has diagonals of 18 in. and 12 in. What is its area in square inches?
questions.hint: Area of a kite = ½ × d₁ × d₂.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × 18 × 12 = ½ × 216 = 108 square inches.

questions.q: A kite has an area of 96 cm² and one diagonal of 16 cm. How long is the other diagonal?
questions.hint: Solve 96 = ½ × 16 × d.
questions.explanation: 96 = ½ × 16 × d = 8d, so d = 12 cm. 6 cm comes from forgetting the ½, and 80 comes from subtracting.

questions.q: Complete the table for kites with diagonals d₁ and d₂.
questions.hint: Area = ½·d₁·d₂; solve for the missing value.
questions.explanation: Row 1: ½ × 20 × 9 = 90. Row 2: ½ × 14 × d₂ = 56 gives 7d₂ = 56, so d₂ = 8. Row 3: ½ × d₁ × 25 = 150 gives d₁ = 300 ÷ 25 = 12.

questions.q: Square ABCD has side length 4. It is dilated to square EFGH with side length 10. What is the scale factor of the dilation from ABCD to EFGH?
questions.hint: Scale factor = image length ÷ original length.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = 10 ÷ 4 = 5/2. 2/5 divides in the wrong order, and 6 is the difference of the lengths.

questions.q: A rectangle that is 12 cm by 8 cm is dilated to a rectangle that is 3 cm by 2 cm. What is the scale factor? Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Divide an image side by the matching original side.
questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 12 = 1/4 and 2 ÷ 8 = 1/4. Both pairs give the same ratio, so the scale factor is 1/4.

questions.q: Complete the table for dilations (scale factor = image side ÷ original side).
questions.hint: Image = scale factor × original.
questions.explanation: 9 ÷ 6 = 3/2 and 2 ÷ 8 = 1/4. The missing image side is 0.4 × 10 = 4. The missing original side is 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

questions.q: Match each scale factor k with the type of dilation it produces.
questions.hint: Compare k with 1.
questions.explanation: When k > 1 the image is larger (3/2 and 2.5 are enlargements). When 0 < k < 1 the image is smaller (0.8 and 1/3 are reductions). When k = 1 the image is the same size as the original.

questions.q: Which scale factor produces a reduction?
questions.hint: A reduction has a scale factor between 0 and 1.
questions.explanation: A dilation is a reduction when 0 < k < 1. Only 3/4 is between 0 and 1. 4/3 and 2 are enlargements, and 1 keeps the same size.

questions.q: A dilation maps a 6 cm segment to a 15 cm segment. Complete the following.
questions.hint: Scale factor = image ÷ original; compare it with 1.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = 15 ÷ 6 = 5/2. Since 5/2 is greater than 1, the image is larger, so the dilation is an enlargement.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has AB = 12. It is dilated to triangle DEF with DE = 4. Complete: the transformation from ABC to DEF is a(n) ____ (enlargement or reduction) with a scale factor of ____.
questions.hint: Compare the image side DE with the original side AB.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = DE ÷ AB = 4 ÷ 12 = 1/3. Since 1/3 is between 0 and 1, the image is smaller, so it is a reduction.

questions.q: Rectangle ABCD has AB = 5. Rectangle EFGH is its image under a dilation, with EF = 20. Which statement is true?
options: It is a reduction with scale factor 1/4
It is an enlargement with scale factor 4
It is an enlargement with scale factor 1/4
It is an enlargement with scale factor 15
questions.hint: Scale factor = image side ÷ original side.
questions.explanation: EF ÷ AB = 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Because 4 > 1, the image is larger, so it is an enlargement with scale factor 4. 1/4 divides the wrong way, and 15 is the difference.

questions.q: Square JKLM has side 8. It is dilated to square NOPQ with side 20. What is the scale factor of the dilation from JKLM to NOPQ? Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Divide the new side by the original side.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = 20 ÷ 8 = 5/2. It is greater than 1, so this is an enlargement.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, 6), B(3, 0), and C(6, 9). A dilation centered at the origin with scale factor 2/3 maps it onto triangle A'B'C'. Plot the vertices of A'B'C'.
questions.hint: Multiply both coordinates of each vertex by 2/3.

questions.q: Triangle PQR has vertices P(−4, 2), Q(2, 4), and R(6, −2). A dilation centered at the origin with scale factor 1/2 maps it onto triangle P'Q'R'. Plot the vertices of P'Q'R'.
questions.hint: Halve each coordinate.

questions.q: Triangle PQR is dilated about the origin with scale factor 3/2. Complete the image coordinates.
questions.hint: Multiply both coordinates by 3/2.
questions.explanation: P(2, 4) → (3, 6). Q(−4, 0) → (−6, 0). R(6, −2) → (9, −3). Each coordinate is multiplied by 1.5.

questions.q: A dilation centered at the origin with scale factor 3 maps point (−2, 5) to which point?
questions.hint: Multiply, do not add.
questions.explanation: (−2 × 3, 5 × 3) = (−6, 15). Adding 3 gives (1, 8), and dividing by 3 gives (−2/3, 5/3).

questions.q: A rectangular park is 45 m wide and 72 m long. On a scale drawing, 1 cm represents 9 m. Find the dimensions of the drawing.
questions.hint: Divide each real length by 9 m per cm.
questions.explanation: Width: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 cm. Length: 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm.

questions.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 25 km. Two cities are 7.5 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance in km?
questions.hint: Multiply the map distance by 25.
questions.explanation: Each centimetre stands for 25 km. 7.5 × 25 = 187.5 km.

questions.q: A floor plan uses the scale 1 inch : 12 feet. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Drawing → actual: multiply by 12. Actual → drawing: divide by 12.

questions.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps the point (2, 5) to the point (6, 15). What is the scale factor?
questions.hint: Divide an image coordinate by the matching original coordinate.
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Both coordinates were multiplied by 3, so k = 3.

questions.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps (−4, 8) to (−1, 2). What is the scale factor?
questions.hint: Image coordinate ÷ original coordinate.
questions.explanation: −1 ÷ −4 = 1/4 and 2 ÷ 8 = 1/4. So k = 1/4, a reduction. 4 divides the wrong way.

questions.q: Each pair shows a point and its image under a dilation centered at the origin. Match each pair with its scale factor.
questions.hint: Divide the image x-coordinate by the original x-coordinate, then check with y.
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. 1 ÷ 5 = 1/5. −5 ÷ −2 = 5/2. 6 ÷ 8 = 3/4. In each case the y-coordinates give the same ratio.

questions.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps (4, 10) to (3, 15/2). What is the scale factor? Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Solve 4k = 3.

questions.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps (6, −3) to (5, −5/2). What is the scale factor?
questions.hint: Image ÷ original for one coordinate, then check the other.
questions.explanation: 5 ÷ 6 = 5/6. Check: −3 × 5/6 = −15/6 = −5/2. So k = 5/6; 6/5 divides the wrong way.

questions.q: Each row describes a dilation centered at the origin. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Image = k × point, so point = image ÷ k.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 6), B(−4, 2), and C(8, −4). A dilation centered at (0, 0) with scale factor 3/2 maps it onto A'B'C'. Match each image point with its coordinates.
questions.hint: Multiply both coordinates by 3/2.

questions.q: Triangle DEF has vertices D(−6, 3), E(3, 9), and F(6, −3). A dilation centered at (0, 0) with scale factor 1/3 maps it onto D'E'F'. Plot the vertices of D'E'F'.
questions.hint: Divide each coordinate by 3.

questions.q: A dilation centered at (0, 0) with scale factor 1/4 maps point K(8, −12) to K'. What are the coordinates of K'?
questions.hint: Multiply each coordinate by 1/4.

questions.q: A triangle has a perimeter of 45 cm. It is dilated by a scale factor of 2/3. What is the perimeter of the image, in cm?
questions.hint: Every side is multiplied by the scale factor, so the perimeter is too.
questions.explanation: Perimeter of the image = 45 × 2/3 = 30 cm.

questions.q: A square with a perimeter of 20 inches is enlarged by a scale factor of 4. What is the perimeter of the enlarged square?
questions.hint: Perimeter is a length, so multiply it by the scale factor once.
questions.explanation: Perimeter of the image = 20 × 4 = 80 inches. 320 multiplies by 4² (that is the area rule), and 24 adds 4.

questions.q: A rectangle 3 cm wide and 5 cm long is dilated by a scale factor of 2.5. Complete the following.
questions.hint: Multiply each side by 2.5.
questions.explanation: 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 cm and 5 × 2.5 = 12.5 cm. New perimeter = 2(7.5 + 12.5) = 40 cm. Check: the original perimeter 16 × 2.5 = 40.

questions.q: Mariam draws a regular hexagonal table. Each side on the drawing is 3 cm, and 1 cm on the drawing represents 0.4 m. What is the perimeter of the actual table in metres?
questions.hint: Find the actual side length first, then multiply by the number of sides.
questions.explanation: Actual side = 3 × 0.4 = 1.2 m. A hexagon has 6 sides, so the perimeter = 6 × 1.2 = 7.2 m.

questions.q: A square patio is drawn with side 2.5 inches. On the drawing, 1 inch represents 4 feet. What is the perimeter of the actual patio?
questions.hint: Convert one side to feet, then multiply by 4 sides.
questions.explanation: Actual side = 2.5 × 4 = 10 ft. Perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40 ft. 10 ft is only one side.

questions.q: Each regular polygon is shown on a scale drawing. Complete the actual perimeter in feet.
questions.hint: Actual side = drawing side × scale; then multiply by the number of sides.
questions.explanation: Triangle: 4 × 2 = 8 ft per side, 3 × 8 = 24 ft. Hexagon: 1.5 × 3 = 4.5 ft, 6 × 4.5 = 27 ft. Octagon: 2 × 2.5 = 5 ft, 8 × 5 = 40 ft.

questions.q: Rectangle PQRS is similar to rectangle WXYZ. PQ = 12 and QR = 9. If WX = 8, what is XY?
questions.hint: Corresponding sides of similar rectangles are in the same ratio.
questions.explanation: PQ corresponds to WX and QR corresponds to XY. So 12/8 = 9/XY. Cross-multiplying gives 12·XY = 72, so XY = 6.

questions.q: Rectangle ABCD is similar to rectangle EFGH. AB = 15, BC = 6 and EF = 10. What is FG?
questions.hint: Write AB/EF = BC/FG.
questions.explanation: The scale factor from ABCD to EFGH is 10/15 = 2/3. So FG = 6 × 2/3 = 4.

questions.q: A rectangle has length 10 and width 4. Complete the table for rectangles similar to it (scale factor = new ÷ original).
questions.hint: Multiply both original sides by the same scale factor.
questions.explanation: Each new side = scale factor × original side. Factor 2 gives 20 by 8; factor 0.5 gives width 2. Length 15 means factor 15/10 = 1.5, so width 6. Width 10 means factor 10/4 = 2.5, so length 25.

questions.q: A dilation maps rectangle KLMN onto rectangle K′L′M′N′. KL = 10, LM = 4, K′L′ = 25 and L′M′ = 10. What is the scale factor of the dilation?
questions.hint: Divide an image length by the matching original length.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = K′L′/KL = 25/10 = 5/2. Check: L′M′/LM = 10/4 = 5/2.

questions.q: A dilation maps a segment of length 18 cm onto an image segment of length 6 cm. What is the scale factor of the dilation? Give a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Scale factor = image ÷ original.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = 6/18 = 1/3. It is less than 1, so the dilation is a reduction.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 2), B(3, 1) and C(2, 3). Plot the image A′B′C′ after a dilation with scale factor 2 centred at the origin.
questions.hint: Multiply both coordinates of each vertex by 2.
questions.explanation: A dilation centred at the origin with factor 2 maps (x, y) to (2x, 2y). A′(2, 4), B′(6, 2), C′(4, 6).

questions.q: A rectangle measuring 3 cm by 5 cm is dilated with a scale factor of 1.5.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: New length of the 5 cm side (cm):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: New length of the 3 cm side (cm):

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Is the dilation an enlargement or a reduction?

questions.hint: Multiply each side by 1.5.
questions.explanation: 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 and 3 × 1.5 = 4.5. A scale factor greater than 1 makes the figure larger, so it is an enlargement.

questions.q: Rectangle ABDE has A top-left, B top-right, D bottom-right and E bottom-left. Point F is on AE and point C is on BD so that FC ∥ ED, forming rectangle CDEF at the bottom. ED = 6 and FE = 4. If rectangle ABDE is similar to rectangle CDEF (in that vertex order), what is AF?
questions.hint: Match AB with CD and BD with DE.
questions.explanation: AB = 6 and CD = FE = 4. From AB/CD = BD/DE: 6/4 = BD/6, so BD = 9. Then AE = BD = 9, and AF = 9 − 4 = 5.

questions.q: Rectangle ABDE (A top-left, B top-right, D bottom-right, E bottom-left) is split by segment FC, with F on AE and C on BD, into rectangle ABCF on top and rectangle CDEF below. ED = 8 and FE = 4. Rectangle ABDE ~ rectangle CDEF. What is AF?
questions.hint: Set AB/CD = BD/DE.
questions.explanation: AB = 8 and CD = 4, so 8/4 = BD/8 and BD = 16. AE = 16, so AF = 16 − 4 = 12.

questions.q: In the same set-up (rectangle ABDE split by FC into ABCF on top and CDEF below, with ABDE ~ CDEF), ED = 10 and FE = 5.
questions.hint: AB equals ED, and CD equals FE.

questions.q: Rectangle ABDE is split by segment FC (F on AE, C on BD) so that rectangle CDEF is at the bottom, and ABDE ~ CDEF. Complete the table.
questions.hint: From AB/CD = BD/DE with AB = ED and CD = FE, BD = ED²/FE.
questions.explanation: BD = ED × ED ÷ FE, then AF = BD − FE. Row 1: 36/3 = 12, AF = 9. Row 2: 36/4 = 9, AF = 5. Row 3: 64/4 = 16, AF = 12.

questions.q: Quadrilateral PQRS is similar to quadrilateral WXYZ. m∠P = 70°, m∠Q = 110°, m∠R = 95° and m∠S = 85°.
questions.hint: Corresponding angles of similar polygons are congruent; match letters in order.
questions.explanation: W ↔ P, X ↔ Q, Y ↔ R and Z ↔ S. So m∠W = 70°, m∠X = 110° and m∠Z = 85°.

questions.q: Quadrilateral JKLM is similar to quadrilateral TUVW. m∠J = 60°, m∠K = 120° and m∠L = 80°. What is m∠W?
questions.hint: ∠W corresponds to ∠M; the angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°.

questions.q: Quadrilateral ABCD ~ quadrilateral GHEF. Match each angle of ABCD to its corresponding angle.
questions.hint: Line up the letters of ABCD with the letters of GHEF in order.
questions.explanation: A ↔ G, B ↔ H, C ↔ E and D ↔ F, because the order in the similarity statement gives the correspondence.

questions.q: Quadrilateral ABCD ~ quadrilateral EFGH. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°.
questions.explanation: The correspondence is A↔E, B↔F, C↔G, D↔H. m∠C = 360° − 92° − 68° − 115° = 85°.

questions.q: Segments PS and QT intersect at R, forming ΔPQR and ΔSTR with ΔPQR ~ ΔSTR. PR = 18, SR = 12, PQ = 5x − 2 and ST = 3x. Find x.
questions.hint: PQ/ST = PR/SR.
questions.explanation: (5x − 2)/(3x) = 18/12 = 3/2. Cross-multiply: 2(5x − 2) = 9x, so 10x − 4 = 9x and x = 4. Check: PQ = 18, ST = 12.

questions.q: Segments AD and BC intersect at E, forming ΔABE ~ ΔDCE. AE = 21, DE = 14, AB = x + 5 and DC = x. What is x?
questions.hint: AB corresponds to DC and AE to DE.

questions.q: Segments AD and BE cross at C, and ΔABC ~ ΔDEC. Complete the table.
questions.hint: The scale factor from ΔABC to ΔDEC is 20/30.
questions.explanation: AB ↔ DE, AC ↔ DC, BC ↔ EC. The ratio ABC:DEC is 30/20 = 3/2. DE = 24 × 2/3 = 16 and BC = 14 × 3/2 = 21.

questions.q: Parallelogram ABCD ~ parallelogram PQRS. AB = 15, BC = 9, PQ = x + 4 and QR = x. Find x.
questions.hint: AB/PQ = BC/QR.
questions.explanation: 15/(x + 4) = 9/x. Cross-multiply: 15x = 9x + 36, so 6x = 36 and x = 6. Check: PQ = 10, QR = 6, ratio 1.5.

questions.q: Rectangle JKLM ~ rectangle WXYZ. JK = 18, KL = 6, WX = 2x + 3 and XY = x. What is x?
questions.hint: Set JK/WX = KL/XY.
questions.explanation: 18/(2x + 3) = 6/x. Then 18x = 12x + 18, so 6x = 18 and x = 3. WX = 9 and XY = 3.

questions.q: Trapezoid ABCD ~ trapezoid EFGH. AB = 16, BC = 10, EF = x + 2 and FG = x − 1.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Scale factor from ABCD to EFGH:

questions.explanation: 16(x − 1) = 10(x + 2) gives 16x − 16 = 10x + 20, so x = 6. EF = 8 and FG = 5, so ABCD → EFGH has scale factor 8/16 = 1/2.

questions.q: Pentagon ABCDE ~ pentagon PQRST. AB = 10, PQ = 4 and DE = 15. What is ST?
questions.hint: DE corresponds to ST.

questions.q: Hexagon ABCDEF ~ hexagon UVWXYZ. Complete the side lengths.
questions.hint: The scale factor from ABCDEF to UVWXYZ is 6/8 = 3/4.
questions.explanation: Multiply ABCDEF sides by 3/4 to get UVWXYZ sides, or divide by 3/4 (multiply by 4/3) to go back. 12 → 9, 15 → 20, 10 → 7.5, 3 → 4.

questions.q: Quadrilateral RSTU ~ quadrilateral KLMN. RS = 9, KL = 6, TU = 12 and MN = 2y. Find y.
questions.hint: TU corresponds to MN.

questions.q: In ΔPQR, PQ = 4 cm, QR = 5 cm and RP = 6 cm. ΔPQR ~ ΔXYZ and YZ = 15 cm. What is the perimeter of ΔXYZ?
questions.hint: Perimeters scale by the same factor as sides.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = YZ/QR = 15/5 = 3. Perimeter of ΔPQR = 15 cm, so ΔXYZ has perimeter 3 × 15 = 45 cm.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have perimeters 24 cm and 36 cm. The shortest side of the smaller triangle is 5 cm. How long is the shortest side of the larger triangle, in cm?
questions.hint: The ratio of perimeters equals the ratio of corresponding sides.
questions.explanation: Scale factor = 36/24 = 1.5. Shortest side of the larger triangle = 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 cm.

questions.q: ΔABC, ΔDEF and ΔGHI are similar, with sides listed in corresponding order. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Find each scale factor from the one known side.
questions.explanation: ΔDEF is 9/6 = 1.5 times ΔABC: 12, 15, perimeter 36. ΔGHI is 4/8 = 0.5 times ΔABC: 3, 5, perimeter 12. ΔABC perimeter = 24.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with AB = 8 and DE = 12. The perimeter of ΔABC is 30.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Ratio of perimeters ABC : DEF as a fraction:

questions.hint: Perimeter ratio = side ratio.
questions.explanation: AB/DE = 8/12 = 2/3, so the perimeters are in ratio 2/3. Perimeter of ΔDEF = 30 × 3/2 = 45.

questions.q: In ΔJKL, m∠J = 48° and m∠K = 67°. In ΔMNP, m∠M = 48° and m∠N = 67°. Which postulate or theorem proves ΔJKL ~ ΔMNP?
questions.hint: Count the pairs of congruent angles.
questions.explanation: ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. Two pairs of congruent angles are enough, so the triangles are similar by AA.

questions.q: Match each piece of information about two triangles to what it proves.

left: Two pairs of corresponding angles are congruent
All three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional
Two pairs of sides are proportional and the included angles are congruent
Two pairs of sides are proportional and a non-included angle is congruent

questions.hint: SAS needs the angle between the two sides.
questions.explanation: AA uses two angle pairs, SSS uses three proportional side pairs, and SAS needs the congruent angle to be between the two proportional sides. A non-included angle (SSA) does not prove similarity.

questions.q: In ΔABC, m∠A = 50° and m∠B = 70°. In ΔDEF, m∠D = 50° and m∠F = 60°. Which statement is true?
options: No, the triangles are not similar
questions.hint: Find the third angle of each triangle first.

questions.q: In ΔABC, m∠A = 40° and m∠B = 85°. In ΔDEF, m∠D = 40°. Which additional fact proves ΔABC ~ ΔDEF?
questions.hint: Find m∠C, then look for a second matching angle.
questions.explanation: m∠C = 180° − 40° − 85° = 55°. If m∠F = 55°, then ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠C ≅ ∠F, so the triangles are similar by AA.

questions.q: In ΔJKL, JK = 6, JL = 9 and m∠J = 50°. In ΔPQR, PQ = 8 and m∠P = 50°. Which additional fact proves ΔJKL ~ ΔPQR by SAS?
questions.hint: The sides must be around the congruent angle and in the same ratio.
questions.explanation: PQ/JK = 8/6 = 4/3, so we need PR/JL = 4/3, giving PR = 9 × 4/3 = 12. With ∠J ≅ ∠P between those sides, SAS applies.

questions.q: In ΔXYZ, m∠X = 35° and m∠Y = 100°. In ΔRST, m∠R = 35°. What must m∠T be (in degrees) so that ΔXYZ ~ ΔRST?
questions.hint: ∠T corresponds to ∠Z.
questions.explanation: m∠Z = 180° − 35° − 100° = 45°. For ΔXYZ ~ ΔRST we need ∠T ≅ ∠Z, so m∠T = 45°.

questions.q: In ΔABC, AB = 4, AC = 6 and m∠A = 70°. In ΔDEF, DE = 10. Fill in what is needed to prove ΔABC ~ ΔDEF by SAS.
questions.hint: The included angles must match and the side ratios must be equal.
questions.explanation: ∠D must be congruent to ∠A, so m∠D = 70°. DE/AB = 10/4 = 2.5, so DF = 6 × 2.5 = 15.

questions.q: ΔPQR has a right angle at R, m∠Q = 55° and PQ = 12. A similarity transformation with ratio 3 maps ΔPQR onto ΔP′Q′R′.
questions.hint: Lengths multiply by 3; angles stay the same.
questions.explanation: P′Q′ = 3 × 12 = 36. m∠P = 180° − 90° − 55° = 35°, and similarity keeps angle measures, so m∠P′ = 35°.

questions.q: A similarity transformation with ratio 1/2 maps ΔABC onto ΔA′B′C′. A′B′ = 9 and m∠B′ = 48°. What are AB and m∠B?
questions.hint: The image is half the size of the original.
questions.explanation: A′B′ = ½ × AB, so AB = 2 × 9 = 18. Angle measures are unchanged, so m∠B = 48°.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(−2, 1), B(1, 1) and C(−2, 3). Plot ΔA′B′C′, the image after a dilation with scale factor 2 centred at the origin.
questions.hint: Multiply each coordinate by 2.
questions.explanation: (x, y) → (2x, 2y): A′(−4, 2), B′(2, 2), C′(−4, 6). The image has the same angles and sides twice as long.

questions.q: In ΔGHI, m∠G = 50° and m∠H = 60°. Which triangle is similar to ΔGHI?
questions.hint: Find all three angles of each triangle.
questions.explanation: ΔGHI has angles 50°, 60°, 70°. A triangle with 70° and 60° has third angle 50°, so it matches by AA. The others give 50°-80°-50°, 60°-80°-40° and 40°-70°-70°.

questions.q: In ΔJKL, JK = 6, KL = 8 and m∠K = 40°. Which triangle is similar to ΔJKL?
options: Sides 9 and 12 with a 40° angle opposite the side 12
Sides 6 and 12 with a 40° angle between them
Sides 9 and 12 with a 40° angle between them
Sides 12 and 18 with a 40° angle between them
questions.hint: Use SAS: proportional sides with the congruent angle between them.
questions.explanation: 9/6 = 12/8 = 1.5 and the 40° angle is included, so it is similar by SAS. 6/6 ≠ 12/8 and 12/6 ≠ 18/8, and an angle not between the sides does not prove similarity.

questions.q: A triangle T has sides 3, 4 and 5. Match each triangle to its relationship with T.
questions.hint: Divide each side by the matching side of T.

questions.q: Layla is 150 cm tall. She stands so that the tip of her shadow and the tip of a tree's shadow meet at the same point. She is 2 m from that point and the tree is 6 m beyond her. How tall is the tree in metres?
questions.hint: The distance from the tip to the tree is 2 + 6 = 8 m.
questions.explanation: Convert 150 cm to 1.5 m. Similar triangles: h/8 = 1.5/2, so h = 8 × 0.75 = 6 m.

questions.q: A 1.8 m tall man stands 4 m from the tip of his shadow, which ends at the same point as a pole's shadow. The pole is 10 m beyond the man. How tall is the pole?
questions.hint: Use the full distance from the tip to the pole.
questions.explanation: Distance from the tip to the pole = 4 + 10 = 14 m. h/14 = 1.8/4, so h = 14 × 0.45 = 6.3 m.

questions.q: A boy who is 60 inches tall stands so his shadow tip meets a lamp post's shadow tip. His shadow is 6 ft long and the lamp post is 12 ft beyond him.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Distance from the shadow tip to the lamp post (ft):

questions.hint: 12 inches = 1 foot.
questions.explanation: 60 ÷ 12 = 5 ft. The tip-to-post distance is 6 + 12 = 18 ft. h/18 = 5/6, so h = 15 ft.

questions.q: At the same time of day, heights and shadow lengths are proportional. A 2 m stick casts a 3 m shadow. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Shadow = height × 3/2.
questions.explanation: Every shadow is 1.5 times the height. Tree: 12 ÷ 1.5 = 8 m. Building: 30 × 1.5 = 45 m. Lamp post: 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 m.

questions.q: In ΔABC, AB = 12, AC = 18 and m∠A = 45°. In ΔDEF, DE = 8, DF = 12 and m∠D = 45°. Which postulate or theorem proves ΔABC ~ ΔDEF?
questions.hint: Compare the sides around the 45° angles.
questions.explanation: AB/DE = 12/8 = 3/2 and AC/DF = 18/12 = 3/2. The included angles ∠A and ∠D are both 45°, so the triangles are similar by SAS.

questions.q: In ΔPQR and ΔXYZ, PQ = 21, PR = 27, XY = 28, XZ = 36 and m∠P = m∠X = 72°. Complete the table.

rows: PQ/XY as a fraction in simplest form
PR/XZ as a fraction in simplest form

questions.hint: Simplify each ratio.
questions.explanation: 21/28 = 3/4 and 27/36 = 3/4. The ratios are equal and the included angles are congruent, so yes, ΔPQR ~ ΔXYZ by SAS.

questions.q: In ΔRST, RS = 14, RT = 20 and m∠R = 65°. In ΔUVW, UV = 21 and m∠U = 65°. What length UW makes ΔRST ~ ΔUVW by SAS?
questions.hint: UW/RT must equal UV/RS.

questions.q: Match each pair of triangles ABC and DEF to the reason they are similar, or to Not similar.

left: AB = 6, BC = 8, CA = 10 and DE = 9, EF = 12, FD = 15

questions.hint: Check whether side ratios are equal.
questions.explanation: 10/4 = 15/6 = 2.5 with the included angle equal: SAS. 9/6 = 12/8 = 15/10 = 1.5: SSS. 10/4 = 2.5 but 15/5 = 3: not similar. Two equal angle pairs: AA.

questions.q: Segments AE and BD intersect at C, forming ΔABC and ΔEDC. ∠A ≅ ∠E. Which reason proves ΔABC ~ ΔEDC?
options: AA Similarity, using ∠A ≅ ∠E and vertical angles at C
questions.hint: What do you know about the angles at C?
questions.explanation: ∠ACB and ∠ECD are vertical angles, so they are congruent. Together with ∠A ≅ ∠E, two pairs of angles are congruent, so the triangles are similar by AA.

questions.q: In ΔPQR, S is on PQ and T is on PR with ST ∥ QR. Which reason proves ΔPST ~ ΔPQR?
questions.hint: Parallel lines make congruent corresponding angles.
questions.explanation: ∠PST ≅ ∠PQR because they are corresponding angles for parallel lines ST and QR. ∠P is shared by both triangles. Two congruent angle pairs give AA.

questions.q: Segments AE and BD intersect at C, with ∠A ≅ ∠E, so ΔABC ~ ΔEDC. AB = 8, AC = 6 and EC = 3.
questions.hint: Vertical angles are always congruent.
questions.explanation: The angles at C are vertical angles, so ΔABC ~ ΔEDC by AA. AC/EC = 6/3 = 2, so ED = AB ÷ 2 = 4.

questions.q: In ΔABC, AB = 4.8, BC = 4 and m∠B = 62°. In ΔDEF, DE = 6, EF = 5 and m∠E = 62°. Is ΔABC ~ ΔDEF?
options: No, because the triangles are different sizes
No, the side ratios are not equal
questions.hint: Compare AB/DE and BC/EF.
questions.explanation: AB/DE = 4.8/6 = 0.8 and BC/EF = 4/5 = 0.8. The ratios are equal and the included angles are congruent, so yes, by SAS.

questions.q: In ΔABC, AB = 5, BC = 6 and m∠B = 40°. In ΔDEF, DE = 7.5, EF = 10 and m∠E = 40°. Is ΔABC ~ ΔDEF?
options: No, the side ratios are not equal
questions.hint: Both ratios must be the same.
questions.explanation: AB/DE = 5/7.5 = 2/3 but BC/EF = 6/10 = 3/5. The ratios differ, so the triangles are not similar.

questions.q: In each row, ∠B ≅ ∠E and these are the included angles. Complete the table (ratios as fractions in simplest form, last column yes or no).
questions.hint: SAS needs both ratios to be equal.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔXZY. Which pair of angles must be congruent?
questions.hint: Match the letters by position.
questions.explanation: The order gives A ↔ X, B ↔ Z and C ↔ Y, so ∠B ≅ ∠Z.

questions.q: In ΔPQR, PQ = 4, QR = 6 and PR = 5. In ΔXYZ, XY = 6 and YZ = 9. Match each extra statement to whether it is enough to prove ΔPQR ~ ΔXYZ.
questions.hint: XY/PQ = YZ/QR = 1.5 already; check what else is needed.
questions.explanation: XZ = 7.5 makes all three ratios 1.5, so SSS. ∠Q and ∠Y are between the proportional sides, so SAS. ∠P is not between PQ and QR, so it is not enough. XZ = 10 gives ratio 2, which does not match.

questions.q: ΔJKL has JK = 3, KL = 5 and JL = 6. ΔMNO has MN = 4.5 and NO = 7.5. What length MO proves ΔJKL ~ ΔMNO by SSS?
questions.hint: All three ratios must be equal.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. AB = 12, DE = 9, BC = 5x + 2 and EF = 3x + 3. Find x.
questions.hint: AB/DE = BC/EF.

questions.q: ΔPQR ~ ΔSTU. PQ = 15, ST = 10, QR = 7x − 3 and TU = 4x + 1. What is x?
questions.hint: Simplify 15/10 first.

questions.q: ΔBCD ~ ΔEFG. BD = 14, EG = 7, CD = 3x + 4 and FG = 2x − 1.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Scale factor from ΔBCD to ΔEFG as a fraction:

questions.hint: CD/FG = BD/EG = 2.
questions.explanation: BD/EG = 14/7 = 2, so EFG is ½ of BCD. 3x + 4 = 2(2x − 1) gives 3x + 4 = 4x − 2, so x = 6. CD = 22 and FG = 11.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. AB = 5 corresponds to DE = x − 2, and AC = 15 corresponds to DF = x + 2. What is x?
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply: 5(x + 2) = 15(x − 2). 5x + 10 = 15x − 30, so 10x = 40 and x = 4.

questions.q: ΔJKL ~ ΔPQR. JK = 9 corresponds to PQ = x + 1, and JL = 15 corresponds to PR = 2x + 1. Find x.
questions.explanation: 9(2x + 1) = 15(x + 1) gives 18x + 9 = 15x + 15, so 3x = 6 and x = 2. Then PQ = 3 and PR = 5, ratio 3/5 = 9/15.

questions.q: ΔABC has AB = 6 and AC = 12. ΔDEF has DE = x − 3 and DF = x + 1. Complete the table, writing DE/DF as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Substitute x; similarity needs DE/DF = AB/AC = 1/2.

questions.q: If PQ/YX = QR/XZ = RP/ZY, which similarity statement is correct?
questions.hint: Read off which vertex pairs with P, Q and R.
questions.explanation: PQ ↔ YX means P ↔ Y and Q ↔ X. QR ↔ XZ gives R ↔ Z. So ΔPQR ~ ΔYXZ.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔFDE. Match each part of ΔABC to its corresponding part of ΔFDE.
questions.hint: A ↔ F, B ↔ D, C ↔ E.
questions.explanation: From the order, A ↔ F, B ↔ D, C ↔ E. So AB ↔ FD, BC ↔ DE, CA ↔ EF, ∠A ↔ ∠F and ∠B ↔ ∠D.

questions.q: ΔKLM ~ ΔRTS. Which side of ΔRTS corresponds to LM?
questions.hint: L is second and M is third in the first triangle.
questions.explanation: The correspondence is K ↔ R, L ↔ T, M ↔ S. So LM corresponds to TS.

questions.q: One triangular frame has sides 8, 10 and 12. Another has sides 12, 15 and 18. Omar says they are similar; Khalid says they are not. Who is correct?
options: Omar, because all three side ratios equal 1.5
Khalid, because the perimeters are different
Omar, because both triangles have a side of length 12
Khalid, because the shortest sides differ by 4
questions.hint: Compare shortest with shortest, middle with middle, longest with longest.
questions.explanation: 12/8 = 15/10 = 18/12 = 1.5. All three ratios are equal, so the triangles are similar by SSS and Omar is correct.

questions.q: Triangle 1 has sides 6, 9 and 12. Triangle 2 has sides 4, 6 and 9. Are they similar?
options: Yes, by SSS with scale factor 2
Yes, by SSS with scale factor 1.5
questions.hint: Check every pair of sides in order of size.
questions.explanation: 6/4 = 1.5 and 9/6 = 1.5, but 12/9 ≈ 1.33. Not all ratios are equal, so the triangles are not similar.

questions.q: Complete the ratios of corresponding sides (sides listed from shortest to longest).
questions.hint: Divide each ΔABC side by the matching ΔDEF side.
questions.explanation: 9/6 = 12/8 = 15/10 = 1.5. Since all three ratios are equal, ΔABC ~ ΔDEF by SSS.

questions.q: Triangle 1 has sides 7, 10 and 12. Triangle 2 has sides 14, 20 and x, where x is the longest side.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Value of x that makes the triangles similar:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Scale factor from Triangle 1 to Triangle 2:

questions.explanation: The scale factor is 14/7 = 20/10 = 2, so x = 12 × 2 = 24.

questions.q: Right triangle ABC has legs 6 and 8. Right triangle DEF has legs 9 and 12. Are they similar, and why?
questions.hint: The right angles are the included angles between the legs.
questions.explanation: 9/6 = 12/8 = 1.5 and the right angles between the legs are congruent, so the triangles are similar by SAS.

questions.q: Right triangle PQR has legs 5 and 7. Right triangle STU has legs 10 and 15. Are they similar?
questions.hint: Compare short leg to short leg and long leg to long leg.
questions.explanation: 10/5 = 2 but 15/7 ≈ 2.14. The leg ratios are different, so the triangles are not similar.

questions.q: A right triangle has a short leg of 4 and a long leg of 10. Complete the table for right triangles similar to it.
questions.hint: The long leg is always 2.5 times the short leg.

questions.q: In ΔABC, m∠A = 35° and m∠B = 75°. In ΔDEF, m∠D = 75° and m∠F = 70°. Which statement is correct?
options: No, the triangles are not similar
questions.hint: Find m∠C and m∠E.
questions.explanation: m∠C = 180° − 35° − 75° = 70° and m∠E = 180° − 75° − 70° = 35°. So A ↔ E, B ↔ D, C ↔ F, and ΔABC ~ ΔEDF by AA.

questions.q: Find the third angle of each triangle and decide whether it is similar to ΔPQR (yes or no).
questions.hint: Third angle = 180° − the other two.
questions.explanation: ΔPQR: 65°. ΔSTU: 180 − 67 − 65 = 48°, giving 48°, 65°, 67° like ΔPQR, so yes. ΔXYZ: 62°, giving 48°, 62°, 70°, so no.

questions.q: In ΔJKL, m∠J = 52° and m∠K = 46°. In ΔMNP, m∠M = 46° and m∠N = 82°. The triangles are similar by AA. What is m∠P in degrees?
questions.hint: Find the third angle of ΔMNP.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. AB = 12, DE = 18, BC = 3x − 1 and EF = 4x + 3. Find x.
questions.hint: 12/18 simplifies to 2/3.

questions.q: ΔMNP ~ ΔSQV. MN = 8, SQ = 12, NP = x + 5 and QV = 2x + 1. What is x?
questions.hint: MN/SQ = NP/QV.

questions.q: ΔGHI ~ ΔJKL. GH = 6, JK = 9, HI = 2x and KL = x + 12.
questions.explanation: 6(x + 12) = 9(2x) gives 6x + 72 = 18x, so x = 6. HI = 12 and KL = 18 (ratio 2/3).

questions.q: ΔDEF ~ ΔXYZ. EF = 12, YZ = 4, DF = 2(x + 3) and XZ = x − 1. Find x.
questions.hint: The scale factor from ΔXYZ to ΔDEF is 12/4 = 3.
questions.explanation: DF = 3·XZ, so 2x + 6 = 3x − 3 and x = 9. Check: DF = 24, XZ = 8.

questions.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR. AB = 15, PQ = 6, AC = 5(x − 2) and PR = x. What is x?
questions.hint: AB/PQ = 2.5.

questions.q: ΔDEF ~ ΔXYZ. Complete the table.
questions.hint: EF/YZ gives the scale factor.

questions.q: Choose the postulate or theorem that proves each pair of triangles similar, or choose Not similar.

left: 70° angle between sides 5 and 8; 70° angle between sides 15 and 24

questions.hint: Find missing angles and compare side ratios.
questions.explanation: 8/6 = 12/9 = 16/12 = 4/3: SSS. 15/5 = 24/8 = 3 with equal included angles: SAS. 42°, 63°, 75° in both: AA. 40°-60°-80° vs 30°-60°-90°: not similar. 15/7 ≠ 2: not similar.

questions.q: A right triangle has an acute angle of 28°. Another right triangle has an acute angle of 62°. Are they similar?
questions.hint: Find the other acute angle of the first triangle.
questions.explanation: The first triangle's angles are 90°, 28° and 62°. The second also has 90° and 62°. Two congruent angle pairs give AA.

questions.q: For each pair of triangles ABC and DEF, write AA, SAS, SSS or Not similar.
questions.hint: Check side ratios carefully.
questions.explanation: 15/5 = 21/7 = 27/9 = 3: SSS. Proportional sides around congruent angles: SAS. Two angle pairs: AA. 6/3 = 8/4 = 2 but 10/6 ≠ 2: not similar.

questions.q: In ΔPQR, S is on PQ and T is on PR with ST ∥ QR. PS = 6, SQ = 4, PT = 9 and TR = x. Which proportion can be used to find x?
questions.hint: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally.
questions.explanation: By the Triangle Proportionality Theorem, PS/SQ = PT/TR, so 6/4 = 9/x.

questions.q: In ΔPQR, S is on PQ and T is on PR with ST ∥ QR. PS = 6, SQ = 4 and PT = 9. Find TR.
questions.hint: PS/SQ = PT/TR.
questions.explanation: 6/4 = 9/TR, so 6·TR = 36 and TR = 6.

questions.q: In ΔACE, B is on AC and D is on AE with BD ∥ CE, so AB/BC = AD/DE. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Write AB/BC = AD/DE and solve for the blank.

questions.q: DE is a midsegment of ΔABC, parallel to BC. If BC = 15, what is DE?
questions.hint: A midsegment is half the third side.
questions.explanation: The Triangle Midsegment Theorem says DE = ½ BC = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5.

questions.q: DE is a midsegment of ΔABC parallel to BC. DE = 2x + 1 and BC = 5x − 4. What is x?
questions.hint: BC = 2·DE.
questions.explanation: 5x − 4 = 2(2x + 1) = 4x + 2, so x = 6. Then DE = 13 and BC = 26.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, 6), B(−4, −2) and C(4, −2). Plot the endpoints of the midsegment parallel to BC (the midpoints of AB and AC).
questions.hint: Average the coordinates of each pair of endpoints.
questions.explanation: Midpoint of AB = ((0 − 4)/2, (6 − 2)/2) = (−2, 2). Midpoint of AC = ((0 + 4)/2, (6 − 2)/2) = (2, 2). The midsegment has length 4, half of BC = 8.

questions.q: Complete the table for midsegments of triangles (the midsegment is parallel to the third side).
questions.hint: Midsegment = ½ × third side.
questions.explanation: Halve the third side or double the midsegment: 6, 9, 8.5, 22.

questions.q: A leaning shelf has a slanted side 60 inches long. Three parallel shelves divide its height into 4 equal vertical gaps of 15 inches. How long is the part of the slanted side between two neighbouring shelves, in inches?
questions.hint: Equal gaps on one transversal give equal gaps on the other.
questions.explanation: The parallel shelves cut the slanted side into 4 equal parts, so each part is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 inches.

questions.q: Four parallel shelves cut a vertical post into gaps of 10, 10 and 15 inches. A slanted side crossing the same shelves has total length 49 inches. How long is the slanted piece between the shelves that are 15 inches apart?
questions.hint: Parallel lines divide transversals proportionally.
questions.explanation: The total vertical height is 35 in. The 15 in gap is 15/35 of it, so the slanted piece is 49 × 15/35 = 21 in.

questions.q: Parallel shelves cut a vertical post and a slanted side proportionally. A vertical gap of 8 in matches 10 in on the slanted side. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Slanted length = vertical gap × 10/8.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut congruent segments of length 7 on one transversal. On a second transversal they cut segments 3x − 1 and x + 9. Find x.
questions.hint: Congruent segments on one transversal mean congruent segments on every transversal.
questions.explanation: Set 3x − 1 = x + 9. Then 2x = 10 and x = 5.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two equal segments on one transversal. On another transversal the segments are 5x − 8 and 2x + 7. What is x?
questions.hint: Set the two expressions equal.
questions.explanation: 5x − 8 = 2x + 7 gives 3x = 15, so x = 5 (each segment is 17).

questions.q: Four parallel lines cut three congruent segments on one transversal. On a second transversal the segments are 2x + 1, 4y + 1 and 9.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Total length cut on the second transversal:

questions.hint: All three segments on the second transversal are equal to 9.
questions.explanation: 2x + 1 = 9 gives x = 4. 4y + 1 = 9 gives y = 2. Total = 3 × 9 = 27.

questions.q: Three parallel streets (1st, 2nd and 3rd) cross two straight roads. Along Road 1, the distance from 1st St. to 2nd St. is 0.4 km and from 2nd St. to 3rd St. is 0.6 km. Along Road 2, the distance from 1st St. to 2nd St. is 0.5 km. Find the distance along Road 2 from 2nd St. to 3rd St., in km.
questions.hint: Parallel lines cut transversals into proportional segments.
questions.explanation: Set up 0.4/0.6 = 0.5/x. Cross-multiply: 0.4x = 0.3, so x = 0.75 km.

questions.q: Three parallel streets cross a straight road (Main St.) and a slanted boulevard. Along Main St. the blocks measure 0.3 mi and 0.45 mi. Along the boulevard the first block measures 0.4 mi. What is the total distance along the boulevard from the first street to the third street?
questions.hint: Find the missing block first, then add both blocks.
questions.explanation: 0.3/0.45 = 0.4/x gives 0.3x = 0.18, so x = 0.6 mi. The total is 0.4 + 0.6 = 1 mi. Answering 0.6 mi forgets to add the first block.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two transversals. On transversal 1 the segments are a (top) and b (bottom); on transversal 2 they are c (top) and d (bottom), so a/b = c/d. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Use a/b = c/d and cross-multiply.
questions.explanation: Row 1: 2/3 = 4/d gives d = 6. Row 2: 5/b = 10/8 gives b = 4. Row 3: a/9 = 6/18 gives a = 3. Row 4: 1.5/2.5 = c/5 gives c = 3.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two transversals. On the first transversal the segments between the lines are 6 cm and 9 cm. On the second transversal the total length between the first and third lines is 20 cm. Find the two segments on the second transversal.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Segment next to the 6 cm segment (cm):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Segment next to the 9 cm segment (cm):

questions.hint: The segments on the second transversal are in the same ratio 6 : 9 = 2 : 3.
questions.explanation: 6 : 9 = 2 : 3, so split 20 into 5 equal parts of 4. The segments are 2 × 4 = 8 cm and 3 × 4 = 12 cm. Check: 6/9 = 8/12.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with DE ∥ BC. AD = 6, DB = 3, AE = x + 2 and EC = x − 1. Find x.
questions.hint: Use AD/DB = AE/EC.

questions.q: In triangle PQR, S is on PQ and T is on PR with ST ∥ QR. PS = 10, PQ = 15, PT = 3x − 1 and TR = x + 2. Find x.
questions.hint: First find SQ = PQ − PS.
questions.explanation: SQ = 15 − 10 = 5. By the Triangle Proportionality Theorem, PS/SQ = PT/TR, so 10/5 = (3x − 1)/(x + 2). Then 2(x + 2) = 3x − 1, so 2x + 4 = 3x − 1 and x = 5.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with DE ∥ BC, so AD/DB = AE/EC. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Cross-multiply AD × EC = DB × AE.
questions.explanation: Row 1: 4/6 = 6/EC gives EC = 9. Row 2: 8/DB = 10/5 gives DB = 4. Row 3: AD/3 = 12/4 gives AD = 9. Row 4: 5/2 = AE/3 gives AE = 7.5.

questions.q: In triangle XYZ, A is on XY and B is on XZ with AB ∥ YZ. XY = 30, AY = 10, XB = 4x and BZ = x + 3.
questions.hint: Find XA = XY − AY, then use XA/AY = XB/BZ.
questions.explanation: XA = 30 − 10 = 20. Then 20/10 = 4x/(x + 3), so 2(x + 3) = 4x, giving 2x + 6 = 4x and x = 3. XB = 12 and BZ = 6, so XZ = 18.

questions.q: A triangle has two segments drawn parallel to its base. Along the left side, starting at the top vertex, the parallel segments cut pieces of length 3, 3 and 6. The base has length 16. What is the length of the lower parallel segment (the one 6 units from the top vertex)?
questions.hint: Each parallel segment forms a smaller similar triangle with the top vertex.
questions.explanation: The lower parallel segment is 3 + 3 = 6 units from the top along a side of length 12. The scale factor is 6/12 = 1/2, so its length is 16 × 1/2 = 8.

questions.q: A triangle has two segments drawn parallel to its base. Along the left side, from the top vertex down, the pieces are 2, 4 and 4. Along the right side, the top piece is 3. The base is 15.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Middle piece on the right side:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Bottom piece on the right side:

questions.hint: The right side is divided in the same ratio 2 : 4 : 4 as the left side.
questions.explanation: The ratio 2 : 4 : 4 with first piece 3 gives 3 : 6 : 6 on the right. The left side is 10. The upper segment is 2/10 of the way down, so it is 15 × 2/10 = 3. The lower segment is 6/10 of the way down, so it is 15 × 6/10 = 9.

questions.q: In a triangle, one side measures 20 and the base measures 30. Segments are drawn parallel to the base. Each row gives how far a parallel segment is from the top vertex (measured along the side of length 20) and its length. Complete the table.
questions.hint: The ratio length/distance equals 30/20 = 1.5.
questions.explanation: Each parallel segment cuts off a triangle similar to the whole, so length = 1.5 × distance. 4 → 6, 10 → 15, 24 ÷ 1.5 = 16, and 15 → 22.5.

questions.q: A triangle has two segments drawn parallel to its base. Along the left side, from the top vertex down, the pieces are 5, 5 and 10. The upper parallel segment (5 units from the top) has length 4. Find the length of the base.
questions.hint: Compare the distance from the top for the upper segment and for the base.
questions.explanation: The base is 5 + 5 + 10 = 20 units from the top along the side, and the upper segment is 5 units from the top. The scale factor is 20/5 = 4, so the base is 4 × 4 = 16.

questions.q: DE is a midsegment of triangle ABC and is parallel to BC. DE = 3x − 2 and BC = 5x + 2. Find x.
questions.hint: A midsegment is half the length of the parallel side, so BC = 2 × DE.
questions.explanation: 2(3x − 2) = 5x + 2, so 6x − 4 = 5x + 2 and x = 6. Check: DE = 16 and BC = 32.

questions.q: In triangle PQR, M is the midpoint of PQ and N is the midpoint of PR. If MN = 17.5 cm, how long is QR, in cm?
questions.hint: MN is a midsegment.
questions.explanation: By the Triangle Midsegment Theorem, MN = ½QR, so QR = 2 × 17.5 = 35 cm.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(−4, −2), B(2, 6) and C(6, −2). Plot D, the midpoint of AB, and E, the midpoint of AC, the endpoints of midsegment DE.
questions.hint: Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates of each pair of endpoints.

questions.q: Each row describes a midsegment of a triangle and the side it is parallel to. Complete the table.
questions.hint: The midsegment is half of the parallel side.
questions.explanation: Double the midsegment to get the side, or halve the side to get the midsegment: 9 → 18, 26 → 13, 7.5 → 15, 3.4 → 1.7.

questions.q: In triangle FEG, H is on FE and I is on FG. FH = 6, HE = 4, FI = 9 and IG = 6. Which statement is true?
options: HI is not parallel to EG, because FH ≠ FI
It cannot be decided without angle measures
questions.hint: Use the converse of the Triangle Proportionality Theorem.
questions.explanation: FH/HE = 6/4 = 3/2 and FI/IG = 9/6 = 3/2. Since the sides are divided proportionally, HI ∥ EG by the converse of the Triangle Proportionality Theorem.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC. Match each set of lengths to the correct conclusion.

right: DE is not parallel to BC

questions.hint: Compare AD/DB with AE/EC.
questions.explanation: 4/6 = 6/9 = 2/3, so parallel. 5/3 ≠ 8/5, so not parallel. 3/3 = 7/7 = 1, so parallel (DE is a midsegment). 2/5 = 0.4 but 3/7 ≈ 0.43, so not parallel.

questions.q: In triangle FEG, H is on FE and I is on FG with HI ∥ EG. FH = 8, HE = 4 and FI = 10.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: FH/FE as a fraction in simplest form:

questions.hint: Use FH/HE = FI/IG, and remember HI/EG = FH/FE, not FH/HE.
questions.explanation: 8/4 = 10/IG gives IG = 5. FE = 8 + 4 = 12, so FH/FE = 8/12 = 2/3. Triangle FHI ~ triangle FEG, so HI = 2/3 × 18 = 12.

questions.q: In triangle FEG, H is on FE and I is on FG. FH = 6, HE = 2 and FI = 9. What must IG be for HI to be parallel to EG?
questions.hint: The two sides must be divided in the same ratio.
questions.explanation: For HI ∥ EG we need FH/HE = FI/IG, so 6/2 = 9/IG. Then 3 = 9/IG and IG = 3.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two transversals. On the first transversal the segments are 3x + 2 (top) and 7 (bottom). On the second transversal the matching segments are 22 (top) and 14 (bottom). Find x.
questions.hint: Parallel lines divide transversals proportionally.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two transversals. On one transversal the segments are x + 4 and 6. On the other the matching segments are 15 and 10. Find x.
questions.hint: Set (x + 4)/6 equal to 15/10.
questions.explanation: (x + 4)/6 = 15/10 = 3/2, so x + 4 = 9 and x = 5. The answer 9 is the length x + 4, not x.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two transversals. Each row gives the upper and lower segments on transversal 1 and on transversal 2. Complete the table.
questions.hint: T1 upper / T1 lower = T2 upper / T2 lower.

questions.q: Three parallel lines cut two transversals. On one transversal the segments are 2x and x + 3. On the other the matching segments are 12 and 10.
questions.hint: Cross-multiply 2x/(x + 3) = 12/10.

questions.q: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, with BC corresponding to EF. The altitude from A to BC is 12, BC = 18 and EF = 12. What is the altitude from D to EF?
