questions.explanation: log₂(x(x − 6)) = 4 gives x² − 6x = 16, so x² − 6x − 16 = 0 and (x − 8)(x + 2) = 0. x = −2 is rejected because log₂(−2) is undefined, so x = 8.

questions.q: Solve log(x + 3) + log x = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Equation after rewriting in exponential form:

questions.hint: log A + log B = log(AB), and log means base 10.
questions.explanation: log(x(x + 3)) = 1 gives x² + 3x = 10, so x² + 3x − 10 = 0 and (x + 5)(x − 2) = 0. x = −5 makes log x undefined, so the only solution is x = 2.

questions.q: If log 3 ≈ 0.4771, what is the approximate value of log 3000?
Given log 2 ≈ 0.3010, complete the table. Give 4 decimal places.
questions.hint: Write each number as 2 times a power of 10.

questions.q: If log 5 ≈ 0.6990, approximate log 0.005. Give 4 decimal places.
Evaluate log₄ 48 − log₄ 6 + log₄ 10 − log₄ 5 + log₄ 2 by writing it as log₄ N.
questions.hint: Subtracting logs divides arguments; adding logs multiplies them.

questions.q: Evaluate log₅ 100 − log₅ 4 + log₅ 2 − log₅ 10.
questions.hint: Combine everything into a single logarithm first.

questions.q: Evaluate log₇ 20 + log₇ 6 − log₇ 4. Round to the nearest ten-thousandth.
questions.hint: Condense to one logarithm, then use the change of base formula.
questions.explanation: log₇(20 × 6 ÷ 4) = log₇ 30. By change of base, log₇ 30 = ln 30 / ln 7 ≈ 3.4012 / 1.9459 ≈ 1.7479.

questions.q: Solve log₅(x² + 3x − 36) = log₅(12x). Check for extraneous solutions and give only the valid solution.
questions.hint: Set the arguments equal and factor the quadratic.
questions.explanation: x² + 3x − 36 = 12x gives x² − 9x − 36 = 0, so (x − 12)(x + 3) = 0. x = −3 makes 12x = −36, so it is extraneous. x = 12 gives 144 on both sides.

questions.q: Solve log₂(x² − 4x) = log₂(x + 6). Check for extraneous solutions.
questions.hint: Check each candidate in BOTH arguments.
questions.explanation: x² − 4x = x + 6 gives x² − 5x − 6 = 0, so (x − 6)(x + 1) = 0. For x = 6 both arguments are 12. For x = −1, x² − 4x = 5 and x + 6 = 5 are both positive, so both solutions are valid.

questions.q: The equation log₃(x² + 2x − 20) = log₃(10x) gives candidates x = 10 and x = −2. Complete the table and type yes or no in the last column.
questions.hint: A candidate is valid only if both arguments are positive.
questions.explanation: For x = 10: 100 + 20 − 20 = 100 and 10x = 100, both positive, so it is valid. For x = −2: 4 − 4 − 20 = −20 and 10x = −20, both negative, so x = −2 is extraneous.

questions.q: Match each equation to its solution set (check for extraneous solutions).
questions.hint: Solve each quadratic, then make sure every argument is positive.
questions.explanation: x² − 2x − 8 = 0 gives 4 or −2, and −2 is extraneous. x² − 4x − 5 = 0 gives 5 or −1, and −1 is extraneous. x² − 5x + 4 = 0 gives 1 or 4, and both keep 5x and x² + 4 positive. x² − 4x + 4 = 0 gives only x = 2, but then x − 4 = −2, so there is no solution.

questions.q: Solve log₇(x² − 3) = log₇(2x).
questions.hint: Solve the quadratic, then test each root in 2x and x² − 3.
questions.explanation: x² − 3 = 2x gives x² − 2x − 3 = 0, so (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0. x = −1 makes 2x = −2 and x² − 3 = −2, so it is extraneous. Only x = 3 works.

questions.q: Solve log(x² − 12) = log x.
questions.hint: Set x² − 12 = x and factor.
questions.explanation: x² − x − 12 = 0 factors as (x − 4)(x + 3) = 0. x = 4 gives log 4 on both sides. x = −3 makes log x undefined, so it is extraneous.

questions.q: Condense 4 log₃ x − 2 log₃(x − 5) into a single logarithm.
questions.hint: Power rule first, then the quotient rule.
questions.explanation: 4 log₃ x = log₃ x⁴ and 2 log₃(x − 5) = log₃(x − 5)². Subtracting gives log₃(x⁴ / (x − 5)²).

questions.q: Condense −2 log₅(x + 3) + 2 log₅(4x).
questions.hint: (4x)² = 16x², not 4x².
questions.explanation: 2 log₅(4x) = log₅(4x)² = log₅ 16x² and −2 log₅(x + 3) = −log₅(x + 3)². The difference is log₅(16x² / (x + 3)²).

questions.q: Match each expression (x, y > 0) to its condensed form.
questions.hint: Move each coefficient up as an exponent before combining.
questions.explanation: log x² + log y = log(x²y); log x³ − log y = log(x³/y); log √x + log 5 = log(5√x); log 2 − log x² = log(2/x²).

questions.q: Which equation could be used to solve 3^(2x) = 50?
questions.hint: Take the log of both sides and use the power rule.
questions.explanation: log 3^(2x) = log 50 gives 2x log 3 = log 50. Dividing by 2 log 3 gives x = log 50 / (2 log 3).

questions.q: Match each equation to the expression for its solution x.
questions.hint: Take logs: a^(kx) = b gives kx log a = log b.
questions.explanation: 4^x = 9 gives x = log 9/log 4; 9^x = 4 gives x = log 4/log 9; 4^(2x) = 9 gives x = log 9/(2 log 4); 9^(2x) = 4 gives x = log 4/(2 log 9).

questions.q: Write the exact solution of 7^x = 20 as a quotient of common logarithms.
questions.hint: Take the common log of both sides.
questions.explanation: log 7^x = log 20 gives x log 7 = log 20, so x = log 20 / log 7.

questions.q: Solve 5^(2x) = 60. Round to the nearest ten-thousandth.
questions.hint: Take ln of both sides; the exponent 2x comes down in front.
questions.explanation: 2x ln 5 = ln 60, so x = ln 60 / (2 ln 5) ≈ 4.0943 / 3.2189 ≈ 1.2720. Forgetting to divide by 2 gives 2.5440.

questions.q: Solve 3^(4x) = 100. Round to the nearest ten-thousandth.
questions.hint: Use x = ln 100 / (4 ln 3).

questions.q: Solve each equation. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Take logs of both sides and isolate x.

questions.q: Which equation is equivalent to 20 = 4 + 24 log₉ x?
questions.hint: Isolate log₉ x first, then use change of base.
questions.explanation: Subtract 4: 16 = 24 log₉ x, so log₉ x = 16/24 = 2/3. By change of base log₉ x = log x / log 9, so 2/3 = log x / log 9.

questions.q: Given 11 = 3 + 12 log₅ x, find the value of log₅ x as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Subtract 3, then divide by 12.
questions.explanation: 11 − 3 = 8, so 12 log₅ x = 8 and log₅ x = 8/12 = 2/3.

questions.q: Solve 7 = −5 + 18 log₄ x.
questions.hint: Isolate the logarithm, then write x = 4^(value).

questions.q: A climber reaches a peak at an altitude of 2480 m. Use a = 15,500(5 − log P), where a is the altitude in metres and P is the air pressure in pascals. Find the air pressure at the peak, to the nearest pascal.
questions.hint: Divide by 15,500 first, then isolate log P.

questions.q: Use a = 15,500(5 − log P), where a is the altitude in metres and P is the air pressure in pascals. At what altitude is the air pressure 10,000 pascals?
Use a = 15,500(5 − log P), where a is the altitude in metres and P is the air pressure in pascals. Complete the table (round P to the nearest pascal).
A hiker is at an altitude of 1240 m. Use a = 15,500(5 − log P), where a is the altitude in metres and P is the air pressure in pascals.
questions.explanation: 1240 = 15,500(5 − log P) gives 5 − log P = 0.08, so log P = 4.92. Then P = 10^4.92 ≈ 83,176 pascals.

questions.q: Solve 3^(k + 2) = 20. Round to the nearest ten-thousandth.
questions.hint: Take logs, then subtract 2.

questions.q: Which is the exact solution of 5^(k − 3) = 12?
questions.hint: Take logs of both sides, divide by log 5, then add 3.
questions.explanation: (k − 3) log 5 = log 12, so k − 3 = log 12 / log 5 and k = log 12 / log 5 + 3.

questions.q: Solve each equation for k. Give exact answers where possible; otherwise round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: When the right side is a power of the base, compare exponents.

questions.q: Solve 3^(k − 2) > 7^k.
questions.hint: ln(3/7) is negative, so dividing by it reverses the inequality.
questions.explanation: (k − 2) ln 3 > k ln 7 gives k ln 3 − k ln 7 > 2 ln 3, so k ln(3/7) > 2 ln 3. Since ln(3/7) < 0, dividing flips the sign: k < 2 ln 3 / ln(3/7) (about −2.59).

questions.q: Solve 5^(k + 1) < 2^k. Write the answer as an inequality with the bound rounded to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Take ln of both sides and collect the k terms.
questions.explanation: (k + 1) ln 5 < k ln 2 gives k(ln 5 − ln 2) < −ln 5. Since ln 2.5 > 0 the sign stays: k < −ln 5 / ln 2.5 ≈ −1.6094 / 0.9163 ≈ −1.76.

questions.q: Solve 4^(k − 1) ≥ 9^k by taking ln of both sides, which leads to k·ln(4/9) ≥ ln 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Inequality sign after dividing by ln(4/9) (≤ or ≥):

questions.hint: 4/9 is less than 1.
questions.explanation: (k − 1) ln 4 ≥ k ln 9 gives k(ln 4 − ln 9) ≥ ln 4, i.e. k ln(4/9) ≥ ln 4. Since 4/9 < 1, ln(4/9) is negative, so the sign flips: k ≤ ln 4 / ln(4/9) ≈ 1.3863 / (−0.8109) ≈ −1.71.

questions.q: Match each logarithmic equation to an equivalent exponential equation.
questions.hint: ln A = c means e^c = A.
questions.explanation: The value of the ln becomes the exponent of e and the argument becomes the result: e³ = 7x, e^(7x) = 3, e⁴ = x + 1 and e^(x + 1) = 4.

questions.q: Which equation is equivalent to e^(3x) = 20?
questions.hint: e^c = A is equivalent to ln A = c.
questions.explanation: Here the exponent is 3x and the result is 20, so ln 20 = 3x.

questions.q: Rewrite ln(5x) = 8 in exponential form.
questions.hint: The natural log has base e.
questions.explanation: ln(5x) = 8 means log base e of 5x is 8, so e⁸ = 5x.

questions.q: Complete the table so that each row shows equivalent equations.
questions.hint: e^c = A and ln A = c say the same thing.
questions.explanation: e⁴ = 9x becomes ln 9x = 4. ln 6 = 2x becomes e^(2x) = 6. e^(0.5x) = 12 becomes ln 12 = 0.5x.

questions.q: Which shows ⅓ ln 27 + ln 10 − ln 6 as a single logarithm?
questions.hint: Use the power rule first: ⅓ ln 27 = ln 27^(1/3).
questions.explanation: ⅓ ln 27 = ln ∛27 = ln 3. Then ln 3 + ln 10 − ln 6 = ln(3 × 10 ÷ 6) = ln(30/6) = ln 5.

questions.q: Write 2 ln 3 + ln 4 − ln 6 as a single logarithm in simplest form.
questions.hint: Move the coefficient 2 inside as an exponent, then multiply for + and divide for −.
questions.explanation: 2 ln 3 = ln 3² = ln 9. Then ln 9 + ln 4 − ln 6 = ln(9 × 4 ÷ 6) = ln(36/6) = ln 6.

questions.q: Match each expression to the equivalent single logarithm.
questions.hint: Addition of logs means multiply the arguments; subtraction means divide.
questions.explanation: ln 12 − ln 3 = ln(12/3) = ln 4. 3 ln 2 + ln 5 = ln 8 + ln 5 = ln 40. ½ ln 36 − ln 2 = ln 6 − ln 2 = ln 3. ln 2 + ln 7 = ln 14.

questions.q:
Determine whether each statement is true or false for all positive x and y. Type True or False.
a. ln(xy) = ln x + ln y
b. ln(x + y) = ln x + ln y
c. ln(x³) = 3 ln x
d. ln(1/e²) = 2

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: ln(x + y) = ln x + ln y

questions.hint: The product rule works for ln of a product, not ln of a sum.
questions.explanation: (a) is the product rule, so it is true. (b) is false: there is no rule for the log of a sum. (c) is the power rule, so it is true. (d) is false because ln(1/e²) = ln e⁻² = −2.

questions.q: Match each expression to an equivalent expression (x, a, b > 0).
questions.hint: ln and e^x undo each other; the power rule brings the exponent to the front.
questions.explanation: The quotient rule gives ln(a/b) = ln a − ln b. The power rule gives ln(aᵏ) = k ln a. Since ln and e^x are inverses, ln e^(5x) = 5x and e^(ln 7) = 7.

questions.q: Which statement is true for all positive x and y?
options: ln(x − y) = ln x ÷ ln y
ln(x + y) = ln x · ln y
questions.hint: Only one of these is a real logarithm rule.
questions.explanation: The quotient rule states ln(x/y) = ln x − ln y. The others mix up the rules: (ln x)² is not 2 ln x (that is ln x²), and there are no rules for ln of a sum or difference.

questions.q: Which expression is equal to −ln(1/x⁴) for x > 0?
questions.hint: Write 1/x⁴ as x⁻⁴ and use the power rule.
questions.explanation: 1/x⁴ = x⁻⁴, so ln(1/x⁴) = −4 ln x. Then −ln(1/x⁴) = −(−4 ln x) = 4 ln x.

questions.q: Solve ln(3x − 6)³ < 9, where (3x − 6)³ is the argument of the logarithm. Write the answer as a compound inequality with exact values.
questions.hint: Use the power rule to get 3 ln(3x − 6) < 9, and remember the argument must be positive.
questions.explanation: By the power rule, 3 ln(3x − 6) < 9, so ln(3x − 6) < 3. Exponentiate: 3x − 6 < e³, so x < (e³ + 6)/3. The argument must be positive: 3x − 6 > 0 gives x > 2. So 2 < x < (e³ + 6)/3.

questions.q: Solve ln(x + 4) > 2.
questions.hint: Raise e to both sides; ln is increasing, so the inequality direction stays the same.
questions.explanation: ln(x + 4) > 2 means x + 4 > e². So x > e² − 4. This already makes x + 4 positive, so the domain condition is satisfied.

questions.q: Solve 2 ln(x − 3) ≤ 4 by completing each step.
questions.hint: Divide by 2 first, then exponentiate, and keep the argument positive.
questions.explanation: The argument must be positive, so x > 3. Dividing by 2 gives ln(x − 3) ≤ 2, so x − 3 ≤ e² and x ≤ e² + 3. Combining: 3 < x ≤ e² + 3.

questions.q: Solve ln(4x)⁵ < 10, where (4x)⁵ is the argument of the logarithm.
questions.hint: Bring the 5 to the front, then exponentiate.
questions.explanation: 5 ln(4x) < 10 gives ln(4x) < 2, so 4x < e² and x < e²/4. The argument must be positive, so x > 0. The solution is 0 < x < e²/4.

questions.q: Solve 3e^(x − 2) + 5 = 41. Give the exact answer.
questions.hint: Isolate e^(x − 2) first, then take ln of both sides.
questions.explanation: Subtract 5: 3e^(x − 2) = 36. Divide by 3: e^(x − 2) = 12. Take ln: x − 2 = ln 12, so x = ln 12 + 2.

questions.hint: Get e^(2x) by itself before using ln.
questions.explanation: Subtract 9: −4e^(2x) = −20. Divide by −4: e^(2x) = 5. Take ln: 2x = ln 5, so x = (ln 5)/2.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: x rounded to the nearest hundredth:

questions.hint: Add 7, divide by 5, then take ln.
questions.explanation: Add 7: 5e^(x + 1) = 25, so e^(x + 1) = 5. Take ln: x + 1 = ln 5, so x = ln 5 − 1. Since ln 5 ≈ 1.6094, x ≈ 0.61.

questions.q: Complete the table: isolate e^x in each equation, then give the exact solution.
questions.hint: Undo the addition or multiplication around e^x, then take ln.
questions.explanation: e^x + 3 = 10 gives e^x = 7, so x = ln 7. 2e^x = 18 gives e^x = 9, so x = ln 9. 4 − e^x = 1 gives e^x = 3, so x = ln 3.

questions.q: A patient takes 500 mg of a medicine. The amount left after t hours is f(t) = 500e^(−0.25t). After how many hours will only 100 mg remain? Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Set f(t) = 100, divide by 500, then take ln.

questions.q: A bacteria culture grows by P(t) = 300e^(0.2t), where t is in hours. To the nearest hundredth, when will the population reach 1200?
questions.hint: Divide 1200 by 300 first, then use ln (not log base 10).

questions.q: A radioactive sample decays by A(t) = 80e^(−0.05t) grams, where t is in years. Round each answer to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: For (a) substitute t = 10; for (b) set A(t) = 20 and solve with ln.

questions.q: A drug level in the blood follows C(t) = 64e^(−0.5t) mg, t in hours. Complete the table with the time when each amount remains, rounded to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Solve e^(−0.5t) = amount ÷ 64, then t = −ln(amount ÷ 64) ÷ 0.5.

questions.q: Write ln x = 2.4 in exponential form.
questions.hint: ln means log base e: ln x = y means e^y = x.
questions.explanation: ln x = 2.4 means log base e of x is 2.4. In exponential form the base e is raised to 2.4, so x = e^2.4.

questions.q: Match each logarithmic equation to its exponential form.
questions.hint: ln a = b is the same as e^b = a.
questions.explanation: Use ln a = b ⇔ e^b = a. So ln x = 3 gives x = e³, ln 5 = x gives e^x = 5, ln y = 0.7 gives y = e^0.7, and ln 1 = 0 gives e⁰ = 1.

questions.q: Write ln(x + 2) = 4 in exponential form and solve for x. Give the exact value.
questions.hint: Rewrite as e⁴ = x + 2.
questions.explanation: ln(x + 2) = 4 means e⁴ = x + 2. Subtract 2 to get x = e⁴ − 2 (about 52.60).

questions.q: What is e^(−2) = y in logarithmic form?
questions.hint: In e^b = a, the exponent b is the answer to ln a.
questions.explanation: e^b = a is the same as ln a = b. Here a = y and b = −2, so ln y = −2.

questions.q: Rewrite each exponential equation in logarithmic form (use ln).
questions.hint: The exponent of e becomes the value of the ln.
questions.explanation: e^b = a becomes ln a = b. So e³ = 20.09 gives ln 20.09 = 3, e^0.5 = k gives ln k = 0.5, and e^a = 9 gives ln 9 = a.

questions.q: Write e^(2t) = 7 in logarithmic form.
questions.hint: The whole exponent 2t is what ln 7 equals.
questions.explanation: e^b = a is equivalent to ln a = b. With a = 7 and b = 2t, the logarithmic form is ln 7 = 2t.

questions.q: Write ½ ln 25 + ln 6 − ln 10 as a single logarithm in simplest form.
questions.hint: ½ ln 25 = ln √25.
questions.explanation: ½ ln 25 = ln 5. Then ln 5 + ln 6 − ln 10 = ln(5 × 6 ÷ 10) = ln(30/10) = ln 3.

questions.q: Which shows ¼ ln 16 − ln 5 + ln 3 as a single logarithm?
questions.hint: Apply the power rule first: ¼ ln 16 = ln ⁴√16.
questions.explanation: ¼ ln 16 = ln 2. Then ln 2 − ln 5 + ln 3 = ln(2 × 3 ÷ 5) = ln(6/5).

questions.q: Condense 3 ln 2 + ½ ln 9 − ln 4 step by step.
questions.hint: Use the power rule on each term with a coefficient, then combine.
questions.explanation: 3 ln 2 = ln 2³ = ln 8 and ½ ln 9 = ln √9 = ln 3. Then ln 8 + ln 3 − ln 4 = ln(8 × 3 ÷ 4) = ln 6.

questions.q: Solve ln(x + 2) + ln(x − 1) = ln(4x − 2). Check for extraneous solutions.
questions.hint: Combine the left side, set the arguments equal, then check every answer in the original logs.
questions.explanation: ln((x + 2)(x − 1)) = ln(4x − 2), so x² + x − 2 = 4x − 2, which gives x² − 3x = 0 and x = 0 or x = 3. At x = 0, ln(x − 1) = ln(−1) is undefined, so 0 is extraneous. The only solution is x = 3.

questions.q: Solve ln x + ln(x + 5) = ln 14. Check your solution(s).
questions.hint: Use the product rule, set arguments equal, and reject any value that makes a log argument negative.
questions.explanation: ln(x(x + 5)) = ln 14 gives x² + 5x − 14 = 0, so (x + 7)(x − 2) = 0 and x = −7 or x = 2. x = −7 makes ln x undefined, so the only solution is x = 2.

questions.q: Solve ln(x + 4) + ln(x + 1) = 2 ln(x − 2).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Candidate value of x after solving the algebra:

questions.hint: Write the right side as ln(x − 2)², set arguments equal, and check the domain.
questions.explanation: (x + 4)(x + 1) = (x − 2)² gives x² + 5x + 4 = x² − 4x + 4, so 9x = 0 and x = 0. But then x − 2 = −2, and ln(−2) is undefined. So the candidate is extraneous and the equation has no solution.

questions.q: Solving ln x + ln(x − 3) = ln 10 gives the candidates x = 5 and x = −2. Complete the check.
questions.hint: Every log argument must be positive.
questions.explanation: At x = 5: ln 5 + ln 2 = ln 10, and both arguments are positive, so it is valid. At x = −2: ln(−2) is undefined, so it is extraneous.

questions.q: Expand ln((5x − 1)/(2√x)) completely.
questions.hint: Quotient rule first, then product rule, then write √x as x^(1/2).

questions.q: Which is the full expansion of ln(x³√y / z)?
options: 3 ln x + ½ ln y − ln z
3 ln x − ½ ln y + ln z
ln 3x + ½ ln y − ln z
3 ln x + 2 ln y − ln z
questions.hint: √y = y^(1/2); exponents become coefficients.
questions.explanation: ln(x³√y/z) = ln x³ + ln y^(1/2) − ln z = 3 ln x + ½ ln y − ln z.

questions.q: Match each logarithm to its expanded form (x > 0).
questions.hint: Product → add, quotient → subtract, power → multiply.
questions.explanation: ln(7x) = ln 7 + ln x; ln(x/9) = ln x − ln 9; ln ∛x = ln x^(1/3) = ⅓ ln x; ln(x⁴) = 4 ln x.

questions.q: Expand ln((2a + 1)²/(5b)) into the form __ ln(2a + 1) − __ − ln b.
questions.hint: The denominator 5b splits into ln 5 + ln b.

questions.q: Condense 2 ln x + ln(x + 3) − ln(x − 2) into a single logarithm.
questions.hint: Move the 2 up as an exponent, then multiply for + and divide for −.
questions.explanation: 2 ln x = ln x². Then ln x² + ln(x + 3) = ln(x²(x + 3)), and subtracting ln(x − 2) divides: ln(x²(x + 3)/(x − 2)).

questions.q: Which is ln(2x − 1) − 3 ln x + ln(x + 4) as a single logarithm?
questions.hint: Only the term with a minus sign goes in the denominator.
questions.explanation: −3 ln x = −ln x³. The positive terms ln(2x − 1) and ln(x + 4) multiply in the numerator, and x³ goes in the denominator: ln((2x − 1)(x + 4)/x³).

questions.q: Condense 5 ln y − ln(y + 2) − 2 ln(y − 1) into the form ln(N/D).
questions.hint: Each subtracted term goes into the denominator, with its coefficient as an exponent.
questions.explanation: 5 ln y = ln y⁵ and 2 ln(y − 1) = ln(y − 1)². Both subtracted logs go in the denominator, so the result is ln(y⁵/((y + 2)(y − 1)²)).

questions.q: Match each expression to its condensed form (a, b > 0).
questions.hint: Coefficients become exponents first.
questions.explanation: ln a + ln b = ln(ab). ln a − 2 ln b = ln a − ln b² = ln(a/b²). 3 ln a + ln b = ln(a³b). ½ ln a − ln b = ln √a − ln b = ln(√a/b).

questions.q: Simplify (x² + 6x)/(x² + 9x + 18).
questions.hint: Factor the numerator and denominator before cancelling.
questions.explanation: x² + 6x = x(x + 6) and x² + 9x + 18 = (x + 3)(x + 6). Cancel (x + 6) to get x/(x + 3).

questions.q: Simplify (x² + 4x)/(x² + x − 12).
questions.hint: Look for a common binomial factor.
questions.explanation: x² + 4x = x(x + 4) and x² + x − 12 = (x + 4)(x − 3). Cancelling (x + 4) leaves x/(x − 3).

questions.q: The function f(x) = (x² + 3x)/x simplifies to a linear function (with a hole at x = 0). Graph the simplified line.
questions.hint: Factor x out of the numerator and cancel.
questions.explanation: (x² + 3x)/x = x(x + 3)/x = x + 3 for x ≠ 0. The line y = x + 3 passes through (−3, 0) and (1, 4); the point (0, 3) is a hole in the original function.

questions.q: Simplify each rational expression.
questions.hint: Factor each part completely, then cancel common factors.

questions.q: Simplify (3x² + 5x − 2)/(3x² + 11x − 4).
questions.hint: Both quadratics share a factor of (3x − 1).

questions.q: Simplify (2x² − x − 3)/(2x² − 7x + 6).
questions.hint: Factor both quadratics; you cannot cancel the 2x² terms directly.

questions.q: Simplify (2x² + 7x + 3)/(4x² − 1).
questions.hint: The denominator is a difference of squares.

questions.q: Simplify (x² + 2x)/(x − 5) · (x − 1)/(x + 2).
questions.hint: Factor x² + 2x first.
questions.explanation: x² + 2x = x(x + 2). The product is x(x + 2)(x − 1)/((x − 5)(x + 2)). Cancel (x + 2) to get x(x − 1)/(x − 5).

questions.q: Simplify (x² + 4x)/(x − 2) · (x − 2)/(x² − 16).
questions.hint: Factor x² + 4x and x² − 16, then cancel.
questions.explanation: x² + 4x = x(x + 4) and x² − 16 = (x − 4)(x + 4). The product is x(x + 4)(x − 2)/((x − 2)(x − 4)(x + 4)), which simplifies to x/(x − 4).

questions.q: Match each product to its simplified form.
questions.hint: Factor, multiply, and cancel common factors.
questions.explanation: In the first, (x + 1) cancels, leaving x/(x − 3). In the second, (x − 3)(x + 3)·x/(x(x + 3)) = x − 3. In the third, x(x + 2)/(x²(x + 2)) = 1/x. In the fourth, x(x + 1)(x − 1)/((x − 1)x) = x + 1.

questions.q: Simplify (12m⁵n²/25) · (10n³/(9m²)). Write the answer with positive exponents.
questions.hint: Multiply coefficients and simplify the fraction, then use exponent rules.
questions.explanation: Coefficients: 12 × 10 = 120 and 25 × 9 = 225, and 120/225 = 8/15. Variables: m⁵/m² = m³ and n² · n³ = n⁵. So the result is 8m³n⁵/15.

questions.q: Simplify (21x²y⁵/16) · (12/(14x⁴y²)).
questions.hint: Subtract exponents when dividing like bases.
questions.explanation: Coefficients: (21 × 12)/(16 × 14) = 252/224 = 9/8. x²/x⁴ = 1/x² and y⁵/y² = y³. The product is 9y³/(8x²).

questions.q: Simplify (18a⁴b/5) · (15/(27a²b³)).
questions.hint: Simplify 270/135, then handle a and b separately.
questions.explanation: Coefficients: (18 × 15)/(5 × 27) = 270/135 = 2. a⁴/a² = a² and b/b³ = 1/b². So the result is 2a²/b².

questions.hint: Factor all four quadratics and cancel common factors across both fractions.

questions.q: Multiply (x² + x − 6)/(x² − 6x + 5) · (x² − 4x − 5)/(x² + 6x + 9). Give the product in two equivalent forms.
questions.hint: Factor every quadratic, cancel, then multiply out what remains.
questions.explanation: The factors are (x + 3)(x − 2), (x − 5)(x − 1), (x − 5)(x + 1) and (x + 3)². Cancel (x − 5) and one (x + 3) to get (x − 2)(x + 1)/((x − 1)(x + 3)). Expanding gives (x² − x − 2)/(x² + 2x − 3).

questions.q: Match each quadratic to its factored form.
questions.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to the constant and add to the x-coefficient.
questions.explanation: −7 and 4 give −28 and −3. 7 and 2 give 14 and 9. −7 and −4 give 28 and −11. 4 and −2 give −8 and 2.

questions.q: Which expression is equivalent to (x − 4)(x + 3)/((x + 1)(x − 6))?
questions.hint: Expand the numerator and denominator with FOIL.

questions.q: Simplify (a³/b²) ÷ (3a/b⁵).
questions.hint: Multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
questions.explanation: (a³/b²) · (b⁵/(3a)) = a³b⁵/(3ab²). Subtract exponents: a³/a = a² and b⁵/b² = b³. The result is a²b³/3.

questions.q: Simplify (6m⁴/n) ÷ (4m/n³). Write the answer with positive exponents.
questions.hint: Flip the second fraction and multiply.
questions.explanation: (6m⁴/n) · (n³/(4m)) = 6m⁴n³/(4mn). Simplify: 6/4 = 3/2, m⁴/m = m³, n³/n = n². The result is 3m³n²/2.

questions.q: Simplify each quotient. Use positive exponents.
questions.hint: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal.
questions.explanation: (x/y)(y/x²) = 1/x. (4x³/y)(y²/(2x)) = 2x²y. (y²/x)(x³/y) = x²y.

questions.q: Simplify (x² + 5x)/(x − 3) ÷ (x² + 3x − 10)/(x² − 9).
questions.hint: Flip the second fraction, factor everything, and cancel.
questions.explanation: x² + 5x = x(x + 5), x² + 3x − 10 = (x + 5)(x − 2), and x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3). The expression becomes x(x + 5)/(x − 3) · (x − 3)(x + 3)/((x + 5)(x − 2)). Cancel (x + 5) and (x − 3) to get x(x + 3)/(x − 2).

questions.q: Simplify (x² − 2x)/(x + 1) ÷ (x² − 4)/(x² + x).
questions.hint: Multiply by the reciprocal (x² + x)/(x² − 4).
questions.explanation: Factor: x² − 2x = x(x − 2), x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2), x² + x = x(x + 1). Then x(x − 2)/(x + 1) · x(x + 1)/((x − 2)(x + 2)) = x²/(x + 2) after cancelling (x − 2) and (x + 1).

questions.q: Simplify (x² − 1)/(x + 4) ÷ (x − 1)/(x² + 4x).
questions.hint: Change ÷ to × and flip only the second fraction.
questions.explanation: The reciprocal is (x² + 4x)/(x − 1). Then (x − 1)(x + 1)/(x + 4) · x(x + 4)/(x − 1); cancel (x − 1) and (x + 4) to get x(x + 1).

questions.hint: Factor out 3 from 3k − 6 and factor both quadratics.
questions.explanation: 3k − 6 = 3(k − 2), k² + 2k − 3 = (k + 3)(k − 1), k² + 5k + 6 = (k + 3)(k + 2). Multiply by the reciprocal: 3(k − 2)/((k + 3)(k − 1)) · (k + 3)(k + 2)/(k − 2). Cancel to get 3(k + 2)/(k − 1).

questions.q: Simplify (4m + 8)/(m² − m − 6) ÷ (m + 2)/(m² − 9).
questions.hint: Write the division as multiplication by (m² − 9)/(m + 2).

questions.q: Match each expression to its factored form.
questions.hint: Look for a GCF, a difference of squares, or two numbers with the right sum and product.
questions.explanation: 2d + 10 = 2(d + 5). d² + 4d − 5: 5 and −1 multiply to −5 and add to 4. d² + 6d + 5: 5 and 1. d² − 1 is a difference of squares, (d − 1)(d + 1).

questions.q: Simplify (x² − 2x − 15)/(x² − 25).
questions.hint: Factor the numerator as a trinomial and the denominator as a difference of squares.

questions.q: Simplify (x² + x − 42)/(x² − 36).
questions.hint: Find the common factor of both.

questions.q: The function f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x + 1) simplifies to a linear function (with a hole at x = −1). Graph the simplified line.
questions.hint: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares.
questions.explanation: (x² − 1)/(x + 1) = (x − 1)(x + 1)/(x + 1) = x − 1 for x ≠ −1. The line y = x − 1 passes through (0, −1) and (2, 1); the point (−1, −2) is a hole in f.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x + 2). Type undefined where f does not exist.
questions.hint: f simplifies to x − 2, except where the original denominator is 0.
questions.explanation: (x² − 4)/(x + 2) = (x − 2)(x + 2)/(x + 2) = x − 2 for x ≠ −2. So f(0) = −2, f(3) = 1, f(5) = 3. At x = −2 the denominator is 0, so f(−2) is undefined.

questions.q: Simplify (x² − 49)/(7x − x²).
Simplify (4 − x)/(x² − 16).
questions.hint: Rewrite 4 − x as −(x − 4).
questions.explanation: 4 − x = −(x − 4) and x² − 16 = (x − 4)(x + 4). Cancel (x − 4) to get −1/(x + 4).

questions.q: Simplify (3x − x²)/(x² − 2x − 3).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Numerator written with a factor of (x − 3):

questions.hint: Factor out −x from the numerator.
questions.explanation: 3x − x² = −x(x − 3) and x² − 2x − 3 = (x − 3)(x + 1). Cancel (x − 3) to get −x/(x + 1).

questions.q: Match each expression to an equal expression.
questions.hint: Factor out −1 and change every sign inside.

questions.q: Simplify (6a²b⁻³/(9a⁵b)) · (12a⁻¹b⁴/(8b²)). Use positive exponents.
questions.hint: Multiply all numerators and all denominators, then subtract exponents.
questions.explanation: Numerator: 6 · 12 · a²a⁻¹ · b⁻³b⁴ = 72ab. Denominator: 9 · 8 · a⁵ · b·b² = 72a⁵b³. So the result is a⁻⁴b⁻² = 1/(a⁴b²).

questions.q: Simplify (5x⁴y⁻²/(15x⁻²y³)) · (9y/(2x³)). Use positive exponents.
questions.hint: Simplify the first fraction first: x⁴/x⁻² = x⁶.
questions.explanation: 5x⁴y⁻²/(15x⁻²y³) = x⁶/(3y⁵). Multiply by 9y/(2x³): 9x⁶y/(6x³y⁵) = 3x³/(2y⁴).

questions.q: Simplify each expression using only positive exponents.
questions.hint: A negative exponent moves a factor across the fraction bar.
questions.explanation: a⁻³b² = b²/a³. x⁵/x⁻² = x⁵⁻⁽⁻²⁾ = x⁷. (2m⁻¹)(3m⁴) = 6m³. y⁻²/y³ = y⁻⁵ = 1/y⁵.

questions.q: For which value of x is (x − 2)/(x + 7) undefined? Find the domain.
questions.hint: Set the denominator equal to zero.
questions.explanation: x + 7 = 0 when x = −7, so the expression is undefined there. The domain is all real numbers except −7.

questions.q: What is the domain of (2x + 1)/(x − 9)?
questions.hint: Only the denominator matters for the domain.
questions.explanation: The expression is undefined when x − 9 = 0, i.e., x = 9. The numerator can be zero, so −½ is allowed. Domain: all real numbers except 9.

questions.q: For each expression, find the value of x that makes it undefined.
questions.hint: Solve denominator = 0 each time.
questions.explanation: x − 4 = 0 gives 4. 2x + 6 = 0 gives −3. 5x = 0 gives 0. 4x − 2 = 0 gives 1/2.

questions.q: Which value is excluded from the domain of f(x) = 4/(5x + 3)? Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.hint: Set the denominator equal to zero.
questions.explanation: 5x + 3 = 0 gives 5x = −3, so x = −3/5. This value is excluded from the domain.

questions.q: Which value is excluded from the domain of g(x) = (x + 2)/(2x − 7)?
questions.hint: The numerator does not affect the domain.
questions.explanation: 2x − 7 = 0 gives x = 7/2. The value −2 only makes the numerator zero, which is allowed.

questions.q: Match each function to the value excluded from its domain.
questions.hint: Solve each denominator = 0.
questions.explanation: 2x − 5 = 0 gives 5/2. 4x + 1 = 0 gives −1/4. 6 − 3x = 0 gives 2. x + 8 = 0 gives −8.

questions.q: For which values of x is h(x) = 5/(2x² − 32) undefined?
questions.hint: Factor out 2, then use a difference of squares.
questions.explanation: 2x² − 32 = 0 gives x² = 16, so x = 4 or x = −4. Both make the denominator zero.

questions.q: Find all values of x for which 7/(x² − 3x − 10) is undefined. Separate them with a comma.
questions.hint: Factor the denominator and set each factor equal to zero.

questions.q: f(x) = (x + 1)/(4x² − 36). Find the values of x for which f is undefined.
questions.hint: Set 4x² − 36 = 0.
questions.explanation: 4x² − 36 = 0 gives x² = 9, so x = −3 or x = 3. The numerator does not matter.

questions.q: Plot points on the x-axis, (x, 0), at each x-value where f(x) = 1/(x² − 4) is undefined.
questions.hint: Solve x² − 4 = 0.
questions.explanation: x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2) = 0 gives x = −2 and x = 2. So plot (−2, 0) and (2, 0).

questions.q: Find the values of q for which q(q + 1)/(3q(q² − q − 12)) is undefined. List them from smallest to largest.
questions.hint: Set every factor of the denominator equal to zero, including 3q.
questions.explanation: The denominator is 3q(q² − q − 12) = 3q(q − 4)(q + 3). It is zero when q = 0, q = 4 or q = −3. In order: −3, 0, 4.

questions.q: For which values of n is (n² − 4)/(2n(n² − 7n + 10)) undefined?
questions.hint: Only the denominator decides where the expression is undefined.
questions.explanation: 2n(n² − 7n + 10) = 2n(n − 2)(n − 5) = 0 gives n = 0, 2, 5. The numerator's zeros (±2) do not make the expression undefined.

questions.q: Which value of x does NOT make (x² + x)/(x(x² − 9)) undefined?
questions.hint: Find the zeros of the denominator x(x − 3)(x + 3).
questions.explanation: The denominator is x(x − 3)(x + 3), which is zero at 0, 3 and −3. At x = −1 only the numerator is zero, so the expression is defined (it equals 0).

questions.q: Simplify 4x(x + 2)(x² − x − 12) / (12x³(x² − 2x − 8)).
questions.hint: Factor both quadratics; they share (x − 4).

questions.q: Simplify 10x²(x + 1)(x² − 4x − 5) / (5x(x − 5)(x² + 2x + 1)).
questions.explanation: The numerator is 10x²(x + 1)(x − 5)(x + 1) and the denominator is 5x(x − 5)(x + 1)². Cancel (x − 5), (x + 1)², 5 and x to get 2x.

questions.q: Simplify 6x(x + 3)(x² − 4) / (9x²(x² + x − 6)).
questions.hint: Also factor x² − 4 as a difference of squares.

questions.q: What is the least common multiple of x² − 7x + 12 and x² − x − 6?
questions.hint: Factor both; use each distinct factor once at its highest power.
questions.explanation: x² − 7x + 12 = (x − 3)(x − 4) and x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x + 2). The shared factor (x − 3) is used once, so the LCM is (x − 3)(x − 4)(x + 2).

questions.q: Find the least common multiple of x² − 9 and x² + 6x + 9. Write it in factored form.
questions.hint: One expression has (x + 3) squared.
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and x² + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)². Take (x − 3) once and (x + 3) to the highest power 2: (x − 3)(x + 3)².

questions.q: Factor each polynomial and then find their least common multiple.
questions.hint: The common factor (x + 5) appears only once in the LCM.
questions.explanation: x² + 2x − 15 = (x + 5)(x − 3) and x² − 25 = (x − 5)(x + 5). The LCM uses (x + 5), (x − 3) and (x − 5) once each: (x + 5)(x − 3)(x − 5).

questions.q: Match each pair of expressions to its least common multiple.
questions.hint: Take every factor at its highest power, not the product of everything.

questions.q: Find the least common multiple of 9x² − 4 and 6x² + 2x − 4. Write it in factored form.
questions.hint: Factor out 2 from the second polynomial first.

questions.q: What is the least common multiple of 4x² − 1 and 4x² + 8x + 3?
questions.hint: Both polynomials contain (2x + 1).
questions.explanation: 4x² − 1 = (2x − 1)(2x + 1) and 4x² + 8x + 3 = (2x + 1)(2x + 3). Using the shared (2x + 1) once, the LCM is (2x − 1)(2x + 1)(2x + 3).

questions.q: Find the least common multiple of 25x² − 9 and 10x² − 4x − 6.
questions.hint: Take out the GCF 2 before factoring the trinomial.

questions.q: Simplify 4/(x − 1) + 1/(x + 3).
questions.hint: Use the common denominator (x − 1)(x + 3).

questions.q: Simplify 3/(x + 4) − 2/(x − 1).
questions.hint: Distribute the minus sign to the whole second numerator.
questions.explanation: Common denominator (x + 4)(x − 1). Numerator: 3(x − 1) − 2(x + 4) = 3x − 3 − 2x − 8 = x − 11. Result: (x − 11)/((x + 4)(x − 1)).

questions.q: Simplify 5/(x + 2) + 2/(x − 3).
questions.hint: Multiply each numerator by the other fraction's denominator.
questions.explanation: The common denominator is (x + 2)(x − 3). Numerator: 5(x − 3) + 2(x + 2) = 5x − 15 + 2x + 4 = 7x − 11. So the sum is (7x − 11)/((x + 2)(x − 3)).

questions.q: Simplify (5x + 5)/(x² + x − 6) − 3/(x − 2).
questions.hint: Factor x² + x − 6 first, then rewrite 3/(x − 2) over the same denominator.
questions.explanation: x² + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2), so 3/(x − 2) = 3(x + 3)/((x + 3)(x − 2)). The numerator becomes 5x + 5 − 3x − 9 = 2x − 4 = 2(x − 2). Cancelling (x − 2) leaves 2/(x + 3).

questions.q: Simplify (5x − 6)/(x² − x − 12) − 2/(x − 4). Give your answer in simplest form.
questions.hint: x² − x − 12 = (x − 4)(x + 3); multiply the second fraction by (x + 3)/(x + 3).
questions.explanation: The LCD is (x − 4)(x + 3). The numerator is 5x − 6 − 2(x + 3) = 5x − 6 − 2x − 6 = 3x − 12 = 3(x − 4). Cancelling (x − 4) gives 3/(x + 3).

questions.q: Simplify (4x + 1)/(x² − 4x − 5) − 3/(x − 5). Complete each step.
questions.hint: Factor x² − 4x − 5 and remember to distribute the −3 to every term.
questions.explanation: x² − 4x − 5 = (x − 5)(x + 1), which is the LCD. The numerator is 4x + 1 − 3(x + 1) = 4x + 1 − 3x − 3 = x − 2. Nothing cancels, so the result is (x − 2)/((x − 5)(x + 1)).

questions.q: What is the least common denominator of 3/(x² − 9) − 1/(x² + 5x + 6)?
questions.hint: Factor both denominators and use each different factor once.
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3). The shared factor (x + 3) is used once, so the LCD is (x − 3)(x + 3)(x + 2).

questions.hint: Factor both denominators; they share the factor (x + 3).
questions.explanation: x² + 2x − 3 = (x + 3)(x − 1) and x² − x − 12 = (x − 4)(x + 3), so the LCD is (x + 3)(x − 1)(x − 4). The numerator is −4(x − 4) + 7(x − 1) = 3x + 9 = 3(x + 3). Cancelling (x + 3) gives 3/((x − 1)(x − 4)) = 3/(x² − 5x + 4).

questions.q: Add and simplify: 2/(x² − 1) + 1/(x² + 3x + 2). Give your answer as a single fraction in simplest form.
questions.explanation: The LCD is (x − 1)(x + 1)(x + 2). The numerator is 2(x + 2) + 1(x − 1) = 3x + 3 = 3(x + 1). Cancelling (x + 1) gives 3/((x − 1)(x + 2)).

questions.q: Match each sum or difference with its simplified form.
questions.hint: Use the common denominator x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2) for every expression.

questions.q: Subtract and simplify: 3x/y² − 2y/x³. Write your answer as a single fraction.
questions.hint: The LCD of y² and x³ is x³y².
questions.explanation: Multiply the first fraction by x³/x³ to get 3x⁴/(x³y²) and the second by y²/y² to get 2y³/(x³y²). Subtract the numerators: (3x⁴ − 2y³)/(x³y²).

questions.q: Simplify a²/b − b²/a.
questions.hint: Use the common denominator ab.
questions.explanation: a²/b = a³/(ab) and b²/a = b³/(ab). Subtracting the numerators gives (a³ − b³)/(ab).

questions.q: Add xy/z² + x²/(yz). Complete each step.
questions.hint: Each denominator needs the factors it is missing from yz².
questions.explanation: The LCD is yz². Multiply xy/z² by y/y to get xy²/(yz²) and x²/(yz) by z/z to get x²z/(yz²). The sum is (xy² + x²z)/(yz²).

questions.q: Simplify 5/(2a²b) − 3/(4ab³).
questions.hint: The LCD is 4a²b³; find what each denominator must be multiplied by.
questions.explanation: 5/(2a²b) = 5·2b²/(4a²b³) = 10b²/(4a²b³) and 3/(4ab³) = 3a/(4a²b³). Subtracting gives (10b² − 3a)/(4a²b³).

questions.q: A rectangle has area 36 cm² and width x cm. Write an expression for its perimeter in terms of x.
questions.hint: First write the length as area ÷ width.
questions.explanation: Length = 36/x. Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(36/x + x) = 2x + 72/x.

questions.q: A rectangle has area 24 m² and length (x + 2) m. Which expression gives its perimeter?
questions.hint: Width = area ÷ length; then double the sum of length and width.

questions.q: A rectangle has area 48 cm² and width x cm, so its length is 48/x and its perimeter is P(x) = 2x + 96/x. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Length = 48 ÷ width; perimeter = 2 × (length + width).
questions.explanation: For x = 2: length 24, perimeter 2(26) = 52. For x = 4: length 12, perimeter 32. For x = 6: perimeter 2(14) = 28. For x = 8: length 6, perimeter 28.

questions.q: Simplify (x + 7)/(3x − 6) − (2x + 5)/(6x − 12). Give your answer in simplest form.
questions.hint: Factor: 3x − 6 = 3(x − 2) and 6x − 12 = 6(x − 2); the LCD is 6(x − 2).
questions.explanation: Multiply the first fraction by 2/2: (2x + 14)/(6(x − 2)). Subtract: 2x + 14 − (2x + 5) = 9. So the result is 9/(6(x − 2)) = 3/(2(x − 2)) = 3/(2x − 4).

questions.hint: The LCD is 6(x − 3); watch the sign when subtracting the whole second numerator.
questions.explanation: Rewrite the first fraction as 2(x + 4)/(6(x − 3)). The numerator is 2x + 8 − 4x − 2 = −2x + 6 = −2(x − 3). So the expression is −2(x − 3)/(6(x − 3)) = −1/3.

questions.q: Simplify (5x + 1)/(2x + 2) − (3x − 1)/(x + 1). Complete each step.
questions.hint: 2x + 2 = 2(x + 1), so multiply the second fraction by 2/2.
questions.explanation: The LCD is 2(x + 1). The numerator is 5x + 1 − 2(3x − 1) = 5x + 1 − 6x + 2 = 3 − x. The result is (3 − x)/(2(x + 1)).

questions.hint: The LCD is 4(x − 3); multiply the first fraction by 2/2.
questions.explanation: 2(x + 4) − (3x + 2) = 2x + 8 − 3x − 2 = 6 − x. The result is (6 − x)/(4x − 12), which does not simplify further.

questions.q: Simplify 6/(3x + 3) + 1/(x² + 4x + 3). Give your answer as a single fraction.
questions.hint: Reduce 6/(3x + 3) to 2/(x + 1) first, then factor x² + 4x + 3.

questions.q: Simplify 3/(2x − 4) + 2/(x² − 4).
questions.hint: 2x − 4 = 2(x − 2) and x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2), so the LCD is 2(x − 2)(x + 2).
questions.explanation: 3/(2(x − 2)) becomes 3(x + 2)/(2(x − 2)(x + 2)) and 2/(x² − 4) becomes 4/(2(x − 2)(x + 2)). The numerator is 3x + 6 + 4 = 3x + 10, over 2(x² − 4) = 2x² − 8.

questions.q: Simplify 5/(x² − x − 6) + 2/(x − 3). Complete each step.
questions.hint: The LCD is the factored form of x² − x − 6.
questions.explanation: x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x + 2). Rewrite 2/(x − 3) as 2(x + 2)/((x − 3)(x + 2)). The numerator is 5 + 2x + 4 = 2x + 9, and x cannot be 3 or −2.

questions.q: Which description matches the graph of f(x) = 3/(x − 2) + 1?
options: Asymptotes x = 2 and y = 1; branches in the upper-left and lower-right
Asymptotes x = 1 and y = 2; branches in the upper-right and lower-left
Asymptotes x = 2 and y = 1; branches in the upper-right and lower-left
Asymptotes x = −2 and y = 1; branches in the upper-right and lower-left
questions.hint: x − 2 moves the graph right 2, +1 moves it up 1, and a positive numerator keeps the branches like 1/x.
questions.explanation: The denominator is 0 at x = 2, so the vertical asymptote is x = 2; the +1 shift gives y = 1. Since 3 > 0, the branches sit upper-right and lower-left of the asymptotes, just like y = 1/x.

questions.q: For f(x) = 4/(x − 1) + 2, plot the points of the graph at x = −3, −1, 0, 2, 3 and 5.
questions.hint: Substitute each x-value: subtract 1, divide 4 by the result, then add 2.
questions.explanation: f(−3) = 4/(−4) + 2 = 1, f(−1) = −2 + 2 = 0, f(0) = −4 + 2 = −2, f(2) = 4 + 2 = 6, f(3) = 2 + 2 = 4, f(5) = 1 + 2 = 3. The points lie on two branches around the asymptotes x = 1 and y = 2.

questions.q: Match each function with its asymptotes.
questions.hint: For y = a/(x − h) + k, the asymptotes are x = h and y = k.
questions.explanation: x + 4 means h = −4, x − 4 means h = 4, x + 2 means h = −2 and x − 2 means h = 2. The constant added at the end is the horizontal asymptote in each case.

questions.q: Which function's graph is the graph of y = 1/x shifted 5 units left and 3 units down?
questions.hint: A shift left by 5 replaces x with x + 5.
questions.explanation: Left 5 changes x to x + 5 and down 3 subtracts 3 from the output, giving y = 1/(x + 5) − 3 with asymptotes x = −5 and y = −3.

questions.q: Which is the equation of the vertical asymptote of y = 1/(x − 6) + 2?
questions.hint: Set the denominator equal to zero.
questions.explanation: x − 6 = 0 when x = 6, so the vertical asymptote is x = 6. The +2 affects only the horizontal asymptote y = 2.

questions.q: Write the equation of the horizontal asymptote of y = 3/x + 7.
questions.hint: As x gets very large, 3/x gets close to 0.
questions.explanation: 3/x approaches 0 as x grows in either direction, so y approaches 0 + 7 = 7. The horizontal asymptote is y = 7.

questions.q: For y = −2/x − 4, find the following.
questions.hint: For the x-intercept, set y = 0 and solve.
questions.explanation: The denominator x is 0 at x = 0, so the VA is x = 0, and the −4 shift gives the HA y = −4. Setting −2/x − 4 = 0 gives −2/x = 4, so x = −1/2.

questions.q: The asymptotes of g(x) = 1/(x − 3) + 5 are:
questions.hint: Vertical asymptote: denominator = 0. Horizontal asymptote: the constant added.
questions.explanation: x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3. The graph of 1/(x − 3) is shifted up 5, so the horizontal asymptote is y = 5.

questions.q: For h(x) = 6/(x + 2) − 3, find:
questions.hint: Find h(0) for the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: x + 2 = 0 gives the VA x = −2, and the −3 shift gives the HA y = −3. h(0) = 6/2 − 3 = 0, so the graph passes through the origin.

questions.q: For f(x) = 1/(x − 4) − 3, plot the point where the two asymptotes cross, and the points of the graph at x = 3 and x = 5.
questions.hint: The asymptotes are x = 4 and y = −3.
questions.explanation: The asymptotes x = 4 and y = −3 cross at (4, −3). f(3) = 1/(−1) − 3 = −4 and f(5) = 1/1 − 3 = −2, giving (3, −4) and (5, −2).

questions.q: Given f(x) = −6/(x − 2) + 3, answer the questions.
questions.hint: The graph is a shifted hyperbola: shifted right 2 and up 3.
questions.explanation: x = 2 makes the denominator 0, so it is excluded and is the vertical asymptote. The +3 shift gives the horizontal asymptote y = 3, so 3 is excluded from the range. f(0) = −6/(−2) + 3 = 6.

questions.q: For f(x) = −2/(x − 1) − 2, plot the points of the graph at x = −1, 0, 2 and 3.
questions.hint: Substitute each x: subtract 1, divide −2 by it, then subtract 2.
questions.explanation: f(−1) = −2/(−2) − 2 = −1, f(0) = −2/(−1) − 2 = 0, f(2) = −2 − 2 = −4, f(3) = −1 − 2 = −3. The branches are upper-left and lower-right of the asymptotes x = 1 and y = −2.

questions.q: What is the range of f(x) = 5/(x + 4) − 2?
questions.hint: The range excludes the y-value of the horizontal asymptote.
questions.explanation: 5/(x + 4) can be any value except 0, so f(x) can be any value except 0 − 2 = −2. The range is all real numbers except −2.

questions.q: Complete the table of values for f(x) = −4/(x + 2) + 1.
questions.hint: Add 2 to x, divide −4 by that, then add 1.

questions.q: Which is the vertical asymptote of f(x) = (6x + 1)/(4x + 20)?
questions.hint: Set only the denominator equal to zero.
questions.explanation: 4x + 20 = 0 gives x = −5, and the numerator is not 0 there, so x = −5 is the vertical asymptote. (3/2 is the horizontal asymptote value 6/4.)

questions.q: Find the vertical asymptote of g(x) = −(2x + 7)/(3x − 12). Write it as an equation.
questions.hint: Solve 3x − 12 = 0.
questions.explanation: 3x − 12 = 0 gives x = 4. The numerator is 2(4) + 7 = 15 ≠ 0 there, so x = 4 is a vertical asymptote.

questions.q: Match each function with its vertical asymptote.
questions.hint: Find the zero of each denominator.
questions.explanation: 2x − 8 = 0 at x = 4; 3x + 9 = 0 at x = −3; x + 6 = 0 at x = −6; 7x = 0 at x = 0. None of the numerators is zero at these values.

questions.q: Use f(x) = (3x² + 3x − 6)/(x² + 5x + 6) to answer the questions.
questions.explanation: The common factor (x + 2) gives a hole at x = −2; the remaining factor (x + 3) gives the VA x = −3. Equal degrees give the HA y = 3/1 = 3. The simplified form 3(x − 1)/(x + 3) at x = −2 is 3(−3)/1 = −9, so the hole is (−2, −9).

questions.q: Which describes the discontinuities of g(x) = (x² − 16)/(x² − x − 12)?
options: Vertical asymptotes at x = 4 and x = −3
Hole at x = −3; vertical asymptote at x = 4
Hole at x = 4; vertical asymptote at x = −3
questions.hint: Factor both; a factor that cancels gives a hole.
questions.explanation: g(x) = (x − 4)(x + 4)/((x − 4)(x + 3)). The factor (x − 4) cancels, so there is a hole at x = 4. The factor (x + 3) remains in the denominator, giving a vertical asymptote at x = −3.

questions.q: For h(x) = (x² − 1)/(x² + 4x + 3), match each feature with what it is.
questions.explanation: (x + 1) cancels, so x = −1 is a hole; (x + 3) stays, so x = −3 is a vertical asymptote. Equal degrees with leading coefficients 1 and 1 give y = 1. The remaining numerator factor (x − 1) gives the x-intercept at x = 1.

questions.q: State the domain of f(x) = (x + 5)/(x² − 2x − 15).
questions.hint: Factor the denominator and exclude its zeros.
questions.explanation: x² − 2x − 15 = (x − 5)(x + 3), which is 0 at x = 5 and x = −3. The domain is all real numbers except 5 and −3.

questions.q: f(x) = p(x)/h(x), where p(x) has degree 4 with leading coefficient 6 and h(x) has degree 4 with leading coefficient 2. What is the horizontal asymptote?
questions.hint: When the degrees are equal, divide the leading coefficients.
questions.explanation: The degrees are equal (n = k = 4), so the horizontal asymptote is y = 6/2 = 3.

questions.q: Match each function with its horizontal asymptote.
questions.hint: Compare the degree of the numerator n with the degree of the denominator k.
questions.explanation: Degree 1 over degree 2 (n < k) gives y = 0. Degree 2 over degree 2 gives y = 5/2. Degree 3 over degree 1 (n > k) has none. Degree 1 over degree 1 gives y = −3/6 = −1/2.

questions.q: f(x) = p(x)/h(x), where p has degree n and h has degree k. Complete each statement with one word or number.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: If n = k + 1, the graph has a(n) ___ asymptote.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: If n < k, the horizontal asymptote is y = ___.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If n = k, the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of the ___ coefficients.

questions.hint: Think about the end behaviour as x gets very large.
questions.explanation: When the numerator's degree is exactly one more, long division gives a linear quotient: an oblique (slant) asymptote. When n < k the fraction tends to 0, so y = 0. When n = k the asymptote is y = (leading coefficient of p)/(leading coefficient of h).

questions.q: Determine the asymptotes, if any, of f(x) = (2x² − 1)/(x² + 4).
questions.hint: Can x² + 4 ever equal 0? Then compare degrees.
questions.explanation: x² + 4 = 0 has no real solutions, so there is no vertical asymptote. The degrees are equal, so the horizontal asymptote is y = 2/1 = 2.

questions.q: Find the asymptotes of g(x) = 5x/(x² − 9).
questions.hint: Factor x² − 9 and compare the degrees.
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) is 0 at x = ±3, and the numerator 5x is not 0 there, so both are vertical asymptotes. The numerator has lower degree, so y = 0 is the horizontal asymptote.

questions.q: Which function has no vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote y = 0?
questions.hint: You need a denominator that is never zero and a numerator of lower degree.
questions.explanation: x² + 5 is never 0, so there is no vertical asymptote, and degree 1 < degree 2 gives y = 0. The second option has y = 1, the third has vertical asymptotes x = ±√5, and the fourth has no horizontal asymptote.

questions.q: Match the characteristics that describe the graph of f(x) = (10x − 3)/(2x + 8).
questions.hint: Equal degrees give a horizontal asymptote; the zero of the denominator gives the vertical one.
questions.explanation: 2x + 8 = 0 gives x = −4. The degrees are equal, so the horizontal asymptote is y = 10/2 = 5. A function with a horizontal asymptote has no oblique asymptote.

questions.q: Match the characteristics that describe the graph of g(x) = (x² + 1)/(x − 2).
questions.hint: The numerator's degree is one more than the denominator's, so divide.
questions.explanation: x − 2 = 0 gives the vertical asymptote x = 2. Dividing, x² + 1 = (x − 2)(x + 2) + 5, so g(x) = x + 2 + 5/(x − 2) and the oblique asymptote is y = x + 2. Since n > k there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.q: For h(x) = (6x + 7)/(3x − 9), give each asymptote (write none if it does not exist).
questions.hint: Compare the degrees, then set the denominator to zero.
questions.explanation: Equal degrees give y = 6/3 = 2. 3x − 9 = 0 gives x = 3. A graph with a horizontal asymptote has no oblique asymptote.

questions.q: For f(x) = (x³ − 8)/(x² − 4), which statement is FALSE?
options: There is a vertical asymptote at x = −2
There is a zero at x = 2
There is an oblique asymptote y = x
There is a hole at x = 2
questions.hint: Factor x³ − 8 = (x − 2)(x² + 2x + 4) and x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2).
questions.explanation: (x − 2) cancels, so x = 2 is a hole, not a zero. (x + 2) remains, giving the VA x = −2. The simplified form (x² + 2x + 4)/(x + 2) = x + 4/(x + 2), so the oblique asymptote is y = x.

questions.q: For g(x) = (x³ + 27)/(x² − 9), find the features.
questions.explanation: (x + 3) cancels, giving a hole at x = −3, and (x − 3) gives the vertical asymptote x = 3. Dividing x² − 3x + 9 by x − 3 gives x with remainder 9, so g(x) = x + 9/(x − 3) for x ≠ −3 and the oblique asymptote is y = x.

questions.q: For h(x) = (x² − x − 6)/(x − 1), match each feature with its value.
questions.hint: Divide x² − x − 6 by x − 1 to find the oblique asymptote.
questions.explanation: x − 1 = 0 gives x = 1. x² − x − 6 = (x − 1)·x − 6, so h(x) = x − 6/(x − 1) and the oblique asymptote is y = x. The numerator (x − 3)(x + 2) gives zeros 3 and −2, and h(0) = −6/(−1) = 6.

questions.q: Match each function with the description of its graph.

right: a line with a hole at x = 2
VA x = 2 and slant asymptote y = x + 2

questions.hint: Simplify or divide each function and compare degrees.
questions.explanation: f(x) = (x − 2)(x + 2)/(x − 2) = x + 2 with a hole at x = 2. g has equal degrees, so HA y = 1, and VA x = 2. h(x) = x + 2 + 4/(x − 2), so it has VA x = 2 and slant asymptote y = x + 2.

questions.q: Which function's graph is a straight line with a hole at x = −3?
questions.hint: The numerator must contain the factor (x + 3).
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), so (x² − 9)/(x + 3) = x − 3 for x ≠ −3: a line with a hole at x = −3. The other numerators are not divisible by x + 3, so those graphs have a vertical asymptote at x = −3.

questions.q: A graph has a vertical asymptote x = 1 and, far to the left and right, both ends rise like a parabola. Which function could it be?
questions.hint: Ends like a parabola mean the numerator's degree is 2 more than the denominator's.
questions.explanation: (x³ + 2)/(x − 1) has degree 3 over degree 1, so it behaves like x² far out, and x = 1 is not a zero of x³ + 2, so x = 1 is a VA. (x² + 2)/(x − 1) has a slant asymptote, (x + 2)/(x − 1) has HA y = 1, and (x³ − 1)/(x − 1) has a hole, not a VA, at x = 1.

questions.q: g(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1). Plot the x-intercept, the y-intercept and the location of the hole.
questions.hint: Simplify: (x² − 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1 for x ≠ 1.
questions.explanation: g(x) = (x − 1)(x + 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1 with x ≠ 1. The x-intercept is (−1, 0), the y-intercept is (0, 1), and the hole is at x = 1, y = 1 + 1 = 2, i.e. (1, 2).

questions.q: For f(x) = (3x² + 5x − 2)/(x² − 4), find the asymptotes and intercepts.
questions.explanation: (x + 2) cancels, so x = −2 is a hole and x = 2 is the only vertical asymptote. Equal degrees give y = 3/1 = 3. f(0) = −2/(−4) = 1/2, and 3x − 1 = 0 gives the x-intercept 1/3.

questions.q: For f(x) = (2x − 4)/(x + 2), plot the x-intercept, the y-intercept, the point where the asymptotes cross, and the points of the graph at x = −4 and x = −1.
questions.hint: Asymptotes: x = −2 and y = 2/1 = 2.

questions.q: What is the y-intercept of g(x) = (x² + 4x − 12)/(x² − 9)?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 0.
questions.explanation: g(0) = −12/(−9) = 4/3, so the y-intercept is (0, 4/3).

questions.q: Given f(x) = (x² − 2x − 8)/(x² − 9), find the intercepts.
questions.hint: Set the numerator equal to 0 for x-intercepts; find f(0) for the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: x² − 2x − 8 = (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0 gives x = 4 and x = −2 (neither makes the denominator 0). f(0) = −8/(−9) = 8/9.

questions.q: Plot all the intercepts of g(x) = (x² + x − 12)/(x² − 4).
questions.hint: Factor the numerator for the x-intercepts and substitute x = 0 for the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: x² + x − 12 = (x + 4)(x − 3), so the x-intercepts are (−4, 0) and (3, 0). g(0) = −12/(−4) = 3, so the y-intercept is (0, 3).

questions.q: What are the x-intercepts of h(x) = (x² − 5x + 6)/(x² − 4)?
questions.hint: Factor and check whether any zero of the numerator also makes the denominator 0.
questions.explanation: h(x) = (x − 2)(x − 3)/((x − 2)(x + 2)). The factor (x − 2) cancels, so x = 2 is a hole, not an intercept. The only x-intercept is x = 3.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (3x² + x − 2)/(x² − 1), answer the questions.
questions.hint: Factor: 3x² + x − 2 = (3x − 2)(x + 1) and x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1).
questions.explanation: (x + 1) cancels, leaving (3x − 2)/(x − 1). The hole is at x = −1 with y = (−5)/(−2) = 5/2, and x = 1 is the vertical asymptote. Equal degrees give y = 3. f(0) = −2/(−1) = 2.

questions.q: Where is the hole in the graph of g(x) = (x² + 2x − 8)/(x² − 4)?
questions.hint: Cancel the common factor, then substitute into the simplified form.
questions.explanation: g(x) = (x + 4)(x − 2)/((x − 2)(x + 2)) = (x + 4)/(x + 2) for x ≠ 2. At x = 2 the simplified form is 6/4 = 3/2, so the hole is (2, 3/2).

questions.q: Find the domain of h(x) = (2x² − 7x + 3)/(x² − 9).
questions.hint: The domain excludes every zero of the original denominator, even ones that cancel.
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) = 0 at x = 3 and x = −3. Even though (x − 3) cancels with the numerator (2x − 1)(x − 3), x = 3 is still excluded. The domain is all real numbers except ±3.

questions.q: Complete the table of values for f(x) = (x³ + 8)/(2x − 2). Give exact values as integers or fractions.
questions.hint: Work out the numerator and denominator separately, then divide.

questions.q: For g(x) = (x³ − 27)/(6x + 12), find the intercepts and asymptotes.
questions.hint: Compare the degrees of the numerator and denominator for the horizontal asymptote.
questions.explanation: x³ − 27 = 0 gives x = 3. g(0) = −27/12 = −9/4. 6x + 12 = 0 gives x = −2. Degree 3 > degree 1, so there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.q: Which statement about f(x) = (x³ + 1)/(8x − 4) is true?
options: VA x = 2 and no horizontal asymptote
VA x = 1/2 and no horizontal asymptote
questions.hint: Solve 8x − 4 = 0 and compare degrees 3 and 1.
questions.explanation: 8x − 4 = 0 gives x = 1/2, and the numerator is not 0 there, so it is a vertical asymptote. The numerator's degree (3) exceeds the denominator's (1), so there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.q: Plot the x-intercept and the y-intercept of g(x) = (x³ − 8)/(x + 4).
questions.hint: Solve x³ − 8 = 0, and evaluate g(0).
questions.explanation: x³ = 8 gives x = 2, so (2, 0) is the x-intercept. g(0) = −8/4 = −2, so (0, −2) is the y-intercept.

questions.q: If y varies inversely as x and y = 8 when x = 6, what is y when x = 16?
questions.hint: For inverse variation, xy = k stays constant.

questions.q: y varies inversely as x, and y = 12 when x = 3. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Find k = xy first; then y = k/x.

questions.q: y varies inversely as x, and y = −5 when x = 4. Find x when y = 2.
questions.hint: Find k = xy, then solve 2x = k.

questions.q: y varies directly as x and inversely as z. When x = 4 and z = 2, y = 6. Find y when x = 9 and z = 3.
questions.hint: Use y = kx/z and solve for k first.

questions.q: y varies directly as x and inversely as z. When x = 5 and z = 4, y = 10. Find y when x = 12 and z = 8.
questions.hint: Write y = kx/z and find k from the given values.

questions.q: y varies directly as the square of x and inversely as z. y = 18 when x = 3 and z = 2.
questions.hint: The equation is y = kx²/z.

questions.q: y varies directly as x and inversely as z, and y = 12 when x = 6 and z = 2. Complete the table.
questions.hint: First find k from y = kx/z, so k = yz/x.

questions.q: y varies jointly as x and z, and y = 24 when x = 2 and z = 3. Match each pair of values with y.
questions.hint: Find k from y = kxz first.

questions.q: y varies jointly as x and z, and y = −18 when x = 3 and z = 2. Find y when x = −4 and z = 5.
questions.hint: Use y = kxz.

questions.q: y varies jointly as x and z, and y = 45 when x = 5 and z = 3. Find the constant of variation k.
questions.hint: Joint variation: y = kxz.

questions.q: Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source. How many times brighter is the light at 2 m than at 6 m?
questions.hint: The ratio of intensities is the square of the inverse ratio of distances.
questions.explanation: I = k/d², so I(2)/I(6) = (6/2)² = 3² = 9. The light is 9 times brighter at 2 m.

questions.q: A satellite's distance from Earth's centre changes between 8,000 km and 10,000 km. Gravity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance. How many times greater is the force at 8,000 km than at 10,000 km? Round to the nearest tenth.
questions.hint: Square the ratio of the farther distance to the closer distance.

questions.q: Sound intensity I varies inversely as the square of the distance d from the speaker: I = k/d². At 3 m the intensity is 80 units.
questions.hint: Find k = I·d² first.

questions.q: The graph of distance y (km) against time x (minutes) for a train is a straight line through the origin and the point (15, 60). Answer the questions.
questions.hint: A line through the origin shows y = kx.
questions.explanation: A straight line through the origin means y varies directly as x. k = y/x = 60/15 = 4, so y = 4x (4 km per minute).

questions.q: y varies directly as x with constant of variation 3. Graph the relationship.
questions.hint: The equation is y = 3x, which passes through the origin.
questions.explanation: y = 3x passes through (0, 0) and, for x = 2, y = 6. Any two points on the line, such as (0, 0) and (2, 6), determine it.

questions.q: Which table shows y varying directly as x?
questions.hint: In direct variation, y/x is the same for every pair.
questions.explanation: For 5, 10, 15 the ratio y/x is 2.5 every time. The second table has ratios 3, 2, 5/3; the third shows inverse variation (xy = 24); the fourth is y = x².

questions.q: A cyclist's distance y (km) after x minutes is a straight line through the origin and the point (30, 45). Write the direct variation equation.
questions.hint: k = y ÷ x for the given point.

questions.q: If y varies directly as x, and y = −15 when x = 5, find y when x = −4.
questions.hint: Find k = y/x first.

questions.q: y varies directly as x, and y = 9 when x = 12. Find x when y = 15.
questions.hint: Find k = y/x, then solve 15 = kx.

questions.q: y varies directly as x, and y = −8 when x = 4. Graph the relationship.
questions.hint: Find k, then plot the line y = kx through the origin.
questions.explanation: k = −8/4 = −2, so y = −2x. The line passes through (0, 0) and (2, −4).

questions.q: Khalid's pay varies directly with the hours he works. He earns AED 450 for 6 hours. How much does he earn for 15 hours?
questions.hint: Find the pay per hour first.
questions.explanation: k = 450/6 = AED 75 per hour. For 15 hours: 75 × 15 = AED 1125.

questions.q: The cost of fuel varies directly with the number of litres bought. 25 litres cost AED 72.50. How much do 40 litres cost? Give your answer in AED.
questions.hint: Find the cost per litre.

questions.q: Mariam's earnings vary directly with the hours she works. She earns AED 220 for 4 hours. Complete the table.
questions.hint: The hourly rate is 220 ÷ 4.
questions.explanation: k = 220/4 = AED 55 per hour. 7 hours: 55 × 7 = 385. AED 660 needs 660/55 = 12 hours. 20 hours: 55 × 20 = 1100.

questions.hint: Multiply every term by (x − 5), then check the answer is not excluded.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by (x − 5): 3 + 2(x − 5) = 8, so 2x − 7 = 8 and x = 7.5. Since 7.5 ≠ 5, the solution is valid.

questions.hint: After solving, check whether your answer makes a denominator zero.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by (x − 4): x − 2(x − 4) = 4, so −x + 8 = 4 and x = 4. But x = 4 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous and there is no solution.

questions.hint: Multiply every term by (x + 2).
questions.explanation: x = −2 is excluded. Multiplying by (x + 2): 5 − (x + 2) = 3, so 3 − x = 3 and x = 0, which is allowed.

questions.q: Match each equation with its solution.
questions.hint: Clear the denominators, solve, and reject any value that makes a denominator zero.
questions.explanation: First: 1 + (x − 1) = 3 gives x = 3. Second: x = 2, but that makes x − 2 = 0, so there is no solution. Third: 4 − (x + 3) = 2 gives x = −1.

questions.q: Solve 3/x = 2/(x² − x) + 5/(x − 1). Check for extraneous solutions. Give your answer as a fraction or decimal.
questions.hint: x² − x = x(x − 1), so multiply every term by x(x − 1).
questions.explanation: Multiplying by x(x − 1): 3(x − 1) = 2 + 5x, so 3x − 3 = 2 + 5x and −2x = 5, giving x = −5/2. This is not 0 or 1, so it is valid.

questions.q: Solve x/(x − 2) − 1/x = 2/(x² − 2x).
questions.hint: Multiply by x(x − 2) and reject values that make a denominator zero.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by x(x − 2): x² − (x − 2) = 2, so x² − x = 0 and x = 0 or x = 1. x = 0 makes a denominator zero, so it is extraneous. The only solution is x = 1.

questions.q: Solve 5/(x + 3) = 2/x + 6/(x² + 3x). Complete each step.
questions.explanation: The LCD is x(x + 3), so x ≠ 0 and x ≠ −3. Multiplying: 5x = 2(x + 3) + 6, so 3x = 12 and x = 4, which is allowed.

questions.q: Solve the equation and check for extraneous solutions: 3x/(x + 1) − 1/(4 − x) = 5/(x² − 3x − 4). Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Rewrite −1/(4 − x) as +1/(x − 4) and note that x² − 3x − 4 = (x − 4)(x + 1).
questions.explanation: Since −1/(4 − x) = 1/(x − 4), multiply every term by (x − 4)(x + 1): 3x(x − 4) + (x + 1) = 5. This gives 3x² − 11x − 4 = 0, so (3x + 1)(x − 4) = 0 and x = −1/3 or x = 4. x = 4 makes a denominator zero, so it is extraneous; the only solution is x = −1/3.

questions.hint: Factor x² + 2x − 3 = (x + 3)(x − 1) and check each answer against the denominators.
questions.explanation: −1/(1 − x) = 1/(x − 1). Multiply by (x + 3)(x − 1): 4x(x − 1) + (x + 3) = 4, so 4x² − 3x − 1 = 0, giving (4x + 1)(x − 1) = 0. x = 1 makes a denominator zero, so it is extraneous. The only solution is x = −1/4.

questions.q: Consider the equation x/(x − 2) + 3 = 2/(x − 2). Complete:

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Value of x that is not allowed:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Solution of the equation after clearing fractions:

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Number of solutions of the original equation:

questions.hint: Multiply every term by (x − 2), then compare the result with the excluded value.
questions.explanation: x = 2 makes the denominator zero, so it is excluded. Multiplying by (x − 2) gives x + 3(x − 2) = 2, so 4x − 6 = 2 and x = 2. Since x = 2 is excluded, it is extraneous and the equation has no solution.

questions.hint: Factor x² − 3x = x(x − 3) and multiply every term by it.
questions.explanation: The LCD is x(x − 3), so x ≠ 0 and x ≠ 3. Multiplying gives (x − 3) + (2x + 3) = 4x − 9, so 3x = 4x − 9 and x = 9. x = 9 is allowed, so the solution is x = 9.

questions.hint: After clearing fractions, check your answer against the values that make x² − 4x zero.
questions.explanation: The LCD is x(x − 4), so x ≠ 0 and x ≠ 4. Multiplying gives 2(x − 4) + x + 6 = 5x − 10, so 3x − 2 = 5x − 10 and x = 4. But x = 4 makes a denominator zero, so it is extraneous and there is no solution.

questions.q: For the equation 3/x + (x + 4)/(x² + 2x) = (5x − 2)/(x² + 2x), complete:
questions.hint: Factor x² + 2x first; the excluded values make the LCD zero.
questions.explanation: x² + 2x = x(x + 2), so the LCD is x(x + 2) and x cannot be 0 or −2. Multiplying gives 3(x + 2) + (x + 4) = 5x − 2, so 4x + 10 = 5x − 2 and x = 12, which is allowed.

questions.q: Solve 1/x + 1/4 = 3. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Isolate 1/x first, then take the reciprocal.
questions.explanation: Subtract 1/4: 1/x = 3 − 1/4 = 11/4. Taking reciprocals of both sides gives x = 4/11.

questions.q: Solve 2/x − 1/3 = 1.
questions.hint: Add 1/3 to both sides first.
questions.explanation: Add 1/3: 2/x = 4/3. Cross-multiply: 4x = 6, so x = 6/4 = 3/2.

questions.q: Complete the table. For each equation, find the value of 1/x and then x. Write fractions in simplest form.
questions.hint: Move the constant fraction to the other side to find 1/x, then flip it.

questions.q: Solve 3/(4x) + 5/(4x) = 1/3 for x.
questions.hint: The fractions on the left already share a denominator, so add the numerators.
questions.explanation: 3/(4x) + 5/(4x) = 8/(4x) = 2/x. Then 2/x = 1/3, and cross-multiplying gives x = 6.

questions.q: Solve 7/(6x) − 1/(6x) = 3/5 for x. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Combine the two fractions on the left, then simplify.
questions.explanation: 7/(6x) − 1/(6x) = 6/(6x) = 1/x. So 1/x = 3/5, and taking reciprocals gives x = 5/3.

questions.q: For the equation 2/(3x) + 4/(3x) = 4, complete:
questions.hint: Add the numerators over the common denominator 3x, then simplify.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are solution(s) to x + 6/x = 5?
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by x to get a quadratic equation.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by x gives x² + 6 = 5x, so x² − 5x + 6 = 0 and (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. Both x = 2 and x = 3 are allowed (neither is 0), so both are solutions.

questions.q: Solve x − 8/x = 2. Complete:
questions.hint: Multiply every term by x and move everything to one side.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by x gives x² − 8 = 2x, so x² − 2x − 8 = 0. Factor: (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0, so x = −2 or x = 4. Neither is 0, so both are solutions.

questions.q: Match each equation with its solution set.
questions.hint: Multiply each equation by x and solve the quadratic.
questions.explanation: x² − 5x + 4 = 0 gives x = 1 or 4. x² − 4x + 4 = (x − 2)² = 0 gives x = 2 only. x² − 4x − 5 = (x − 5)(x + 1) = 0 gives x = 5 or −1. x² + 1 = 0 has no real solution.

questions.hint: Factor x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and multiply every term by it.
questions.explanation: Multiply by (x − 3)(x + 3): 2(x − 3) − 12 = 5(x − 3). Then 2x − 18 = 5x − 15, so −3 = 3x and x = −1. x = −1 does not make any denominator zero, so it is the solution.

questions.hint: The LCD is (x − 2)(x + 2).
questions.explanation: Multiply by (x − 2)(x + 2): 4(x + 2) + 8 = 3(x + 2). Then 4x + 16 = 3x + 6, so x = −10. x = −10 is allowed, so the solution is x = −10.

questions.q: For the equation 3/(x − 1) − 6/(x² − 1) = 1/(x + 1), complete:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Solution of the equation after clearing fractions:

questions.hint: Factor x² − 1 and remember to compare your answer with the excluded values.
questions.explanation: x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1), so x ≠ 1 and x ≠ −1. Multiplying gives 3(x + 1) − 6 = x − 1, so 3x − 3 = x − 1 and x = 1. Since x = 1 is excluded, it is extraneous and the equation has no solution.

questions.hint: Combine into one fraction, then test the intervals made by the zeros of the numerator and denominator.
questions.explanation: 1/(x + 2) + 1/(x − 4) = (2x − 2)/((x + 2)(x − 4)). The critical values are −2, 1 and 4. Testing x = −3, 0, 2, 5 gives signs −, +, −, +. The expression is ≤ 0 for x < −2 or 1 ≤ x < 4 (x = 1 is included because the expression equals 0 there; −2 and 4 are excluded).

questions.q: The expression 1/(x + 3) + 1/(x − 5) can be written as (2x − 2)/((x + 3)(x − 5)). Complete the sign chart by writing positive or negative for each interval.
questions.hint: Substitute each test value into (2x − 2)/((x + 3)(x − 5)) and look only at the sign.
questions.explanation: At x = −4: −10/((−1)(−9)) is negative. At x = 0: −2/((3)(−5)) is positive. At x = 2: 2/((5)(−3)) is negative. At x = 6: 10/((9)(1)) is positive.

questions.q: Solve 1/(x + 3) + 1/(x − 5) ≥ 0. Write your answer using inequalities, e.g. a < x ≤ b or x > c.
questions.hint: Combine into one fraction and use a sign chart with critical values −3, 1 and 5.
questions.explanation: The sum equals (2x − 2)/((x + 3)(x − 5)). The sign is − for x < −3, + for −3 < x < 1, − for 1 < x < 5 and + for x > 5. It equals 0 at x = 1 and is undefined at −3 and 5. So the solution is −3 < x ≤ 1 or x > 5.

questions.hint: Find where the numerator and denominator equal zero, then test each interval.
questions.explanation: The critical values are x = −2 and x = 3. Testing x = −3 gives (−1)/(−6) > 0, x = 0 gives 2/(−3) < 0, and x = 4 gives 6/1 > 0. So the solution is x < −2 or x > 3.

questions.q: Solve (x − 5)/(x + 1) ≤ 0. Write your answer using inequalities.
questions.hint: The numerator can be zero, but the denominator cannot.
questions.explanation: The critical values are x = −1 and x = 5. The fraction is negative between them (test x = 0: −5/1 < 0) and positive outside. It equals 0 at x = 5 (included) and is undefined at x = −1 (excluded). So −1 < x ≤ 5.

questions.q: Match each inequality with its solution.
questions.hint: The fraction is negative between −4 and 2; x = 2 can be included only for ≤ or ≥, and x = −4 never can.
questions.explanation: The critical values are −4 and 2. The fraction is negative for −4 < x < 2 and positive for x < −4 or x > 2. With ≤ or ≥ we add x = 2 (where it equals 0), but never x = −4 (undefined).

questions.q: Solve 1/(2k) + 1/(4k) < 3/8. Write your answer using inequalities.
questions.hint: Combine the left side, then consider k > 0 and k < 0 separately.
questions.explanation: 1/(2k) + 1/(4k) = 3/(4k). If k > 0, multiply by 8k: 6 < 3k, so k > 2. If k < 0, the left side is negative, which is always less than 3/8. So the solution is k < 0 or k > 2.

questions.hint: Combine the fractions, and remember that a negative a makes the left side negative.
questions.explanation: 1/(2a) + 1/(3a) = 5/(6a). If a < 0 the left side is negative, so it cannot be greater than 5/6. If a > 0, multiply by 6a: 5 > 5a, so a < 1. The solution is 0 < a < 1.

questions.q: Solve 1/(5m) + 3/(5m) < 2. Complete:
questions.hint: Combine to 4/(5m) and think about the sign of m before multiplying.
questions.explanation: m cannot be 0. The left side is 4/(5m). If m > 0, multiply by 5m: 4 < 10m, so m > 2/5. If m < 0, 4/(5m) is negative and always less than 2, so every m < 0 works. Solution: m < 0 or m > 2/5.

questions.q: Solve 10/x + 2/3 = 7/6 for x.
questions.hint: Subtract 2/3 from 7/6 using a common denominator of 6.
questions.explanation: 10/x = 7/6 − 4/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. Cross-multiplying gives x = 20.

questions.q: Solve 9/x − 1/2 = 1/4 for x.
questions.hint: Add 1/2 to both sides first.
questions.explanation: 9/x = 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4. Cross-multiply: 3x = 36, so x = 12.

questions.q: Solve each equation for x and complete the table.
questions.hint: Isolate the fraction with x, then cross-multiply.
questions.explanation: 6/x = 2/3 gives x = 9. 8/x = 2 gives x = 4. 15/x = 1 gives x = 15. 20/x = 1 gives x = 20.

questions.q: Amna has 50 ml of a 20% salt solution. How many ml of a 50% salt solution should she add to obtain a 30% salt solution?
questions.hint: Amount of salt before mixing = amount of salt in the mixture.
questions.explanation: Let x be the ml of 50% solution. Salt: 0.20(50) + 0.50x = 0.30(50 + x). So 10 + 0.5x = 15 + 0.3x, giving 0.2x = 5 and x = 25 ml.

questions.q: A lab has 60 ml of a 10% acid solution. How many ml of a 40% acid solution must be added to make a 20% acid solution?
questions.hint: Write an equation for the amount of pure acid.
questions.explanation: Let x be the ml of 40% solution. 0.10(60) + 0.40x = 0.20(60 + x), so 6 + 0.4x = 12 + 0.2x. Then 0.2x = 6 and x = 30 ml.

questions.q: A chemist mixes 30 ml of a 15% zinc sulfate solution with x ml of a 45% solution to make a 25% solution. Complete the table (use x in your expressions).
questions.hint: Amount of zinc sulfate = percent (as a decimal) × volume.
questions.explanation: 0.15 × 30 = 4.5 ml and 0.45 × x = 0.45x ml. The mixture volume is 30 + x, so it holds 0.25(30 + x) ml. Setting 4.5 + 0.45x = 7.5 + 0.25x gives x = 15 ml.

questions.q: Mona can stock the library shelves in 12 hours alone. Working with Sara, they finish in 8 hours. How many hours would Sara take alone?
questions.hint: Use rates: (Mona's rate) + (Sara's rate) = (combined rate).

questions.q: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B fills it in 3 hours. How long does it take both pipes together?
questions.hint: Add the hourly rates, then take the reciprocal.
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 tank per hour, so together they take 2 hours.

questions.q: Khalid paints a room in 10 hours alone. Omar paints at a rate of 1/15 of the room per hour. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Rate = 1 ÷ time, and rates add when people work together.
questions.explanation: Khalid's rate is 1/10. Omar's time is 15 hours. Together: 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6, so they take 6 hours.

questions.q: A distribution is skewed right (long tail toward the larger values) and has a mean of 22. Which value is most likely its median?
questions.hint: In a skewed distribution, the mean is pulled toward the tail.
questions.explanation: In a right-skewed distribution the long right tail pulls the mean up, so the mean is greater than the median. The median should be less than 22, so 18 is the best choice.

questions.q: Match each shape of distribution with the usual relationship between its mean and median.

right: mean is less than the median
mean and median are about equal
mean is greater than the median

questions.hint: The mean is pulled toward the long tail.
questions.explanation: In a symmetric distribution the mean and median are about the same. A left tail pulls the mean down below the median, and a right tail pulls the mean up above the median.

questions.q: Distribution P is symmetric with mean 40.2. Distribution Q is skewed right (long tail toward the larger values) with mean 45.6. The medians are 40.0 and 38.1. Write P or Q for each.
questions.hint: A symmetric distribution has its median close to its mean.
questions.explanation: P is symmetric, so its median is close to its mean of 40.2, which is 40.0. Q is skewed right, so its mean is pulled above the median; its median is 38.1, which is less than 45.6.

questions.q: Find the mean and the sample standard deviation (divide by n − 1) of the data 12, 15, 9, 18, 21, 14, 16, 11. Round to the nearest tenth if necessary.
questions.hint: Add the values and divide by 8 for the mean; you may use a calculator for the standard deviation.
questions.explanation: The sum is 116, so the mean is 116 ÷ 8 = 14.5. The squared deviations add to 106, and 106 ÷ 7 ≈ 15.14. The square root is about 3.9.

questions.q: For the data 4, 8, 6, 10, 12, which gives the mean and the sample standard deviation (rounded to the nearest tenth)?
questions.hint: For the sample standard deviation, divide the sum of squared deviations by n − 1.
questions.explanation: The mean is 40 ÷ 5 = 8. The deviations are −4, 0, −2, 2, 4 and their squares add to 40. 40 ÷ 4 = 10, and √10 ≈ 3.2. (Dividing by 5 instead would give 2.8.)

questions.q: The data 2, 5, 6, 9, 13 has mean 7. Complete the table of deviations.
questions.hint: Subtract 7 from each value, then square the result.
questions.explanation: The deviations are −5, −2, −1, 2, 6 and their squares are 25, 4, 1, 4, 36. Their sum, 70, is used to find the variance and standard deviation.

questions.q: Hamad sells juice at the same 6 markets each year. 2022 sales: 15, 22, 18, 30, 10, 25. 2023 sales: 21, 23, 20, 24, 22, 22. Write 2022 or 2023.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On average, he sold more in:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The sales were more varied in:

questions.hint: Compare the means, then compare the ranges.
questions.explanation: 2022: sum 120, mean 20, range 30 − 10 = 20. 2023: sum 132, mean 22, range 24 − 20 = 4. So the average is higher in 2023, and the sales were more varied in 2022.

questions.q: Two shops recorded daily sales. Shop A: 12, 18, 15, 20, 10. Shop B: 14, 16, 15, 17, 13. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Mean = sum ÷ 5; range = greatest − least.
