questions.hint: 'At least'/'at most' use ≤; 'more than'/'less than' use strict signs.
questions.explanation: At least 40 and at most 70 includes both ends: 40 ≤ s ≤ 70. More than 40 but less than 70 excludes both: 40 < s < 70. Speeds outside the range use 'or': s < 40 or s > 70.

questions.q: A gym class has at most 25 students and at least 12 students. Write a compound inequality for the number of students n in the class.
questions.hint: Put the smaller number on the left.
questions.explanation: At least 12 means n ≥ 12 and at most 25 means n ≤ 25. Combined: 12 ≤ n ≤ 25.

questions.q: The phones in a shop cost at most AED 1500 and at least AED 900. Which compound inequality describes the price p of a phone?
questions.hint: 'At least' and 'at most' both include the endpoint.
questions.explanation: At least 900 means p ≥ 900 and at most 1500 means p ≤ 1500. Written together with the smaller value first: 900 ≤ p ≤ 1500.

questions.q: Concert tickets cost at least AED 150 and at most AED 400. Write yes or no to say whether each price is possible, and write the inequality in the last row.
questions.hint: The prices allowed are from 150 to 400, including both.
questions.explanation: The prices satisfy 150 ≤ p ≤ 400. 150, 275 and 400 are in this range (the endpoints are included). 120 is too low and 410 is too high.

questions.q: A club rents a hall for AED 600 plus AED 25 per guest. The total cost must be between AED 1100 and AED 1600, inclusive. Which compound inequality represents the total cost for x guests?
questions.hint: Total cost = fixed fee + cost per guest × number of guests.
questions.explanation: The total cost is 600 + 25x. It must lie between 1100 and 1600 inclusive, so 1100 ≤ 25x + 600 ≤ 1600.

questions.q: A school trip costs 800 dirhams for the bus plus 40 dirhams per student. The total must be between 2000 and 3200 dirhams, inclusive. Let x be the number of students.
questions.hint: Subtract 800 from all three parts, then divide by 40.

questions.q: A taxi charges AED 12 plus AED 3 per km. A passenger wants the fare to be between AED 30 and AED 60, inclusive. Write a compound inequality (do not solve it) for the distance d in km.
questions.hint: The fare is 12 + 3d.
questions.explanation: The fare for d km is 3d + 12. It must be at least 30 and at most 60, so 30 ≤ 3d + 12 ≤ 60.

questions.q: A hall costs AED 600 plus AED 25 per guest. Complete the table of total costs.
questions.hint: Use cost = 25x + 600.

questions.q: Which absolute value equation has exactly one solution?
questions.hint: Isolate the absolute value: |A| = 0 has one solution, |A| = positive has two, |A| = negative has none.
questions.explanation: |x + 4| = 0 only when x = −4, so it has one solution. |x − 4| = 2 has two. |x| + 3 = 1 gives |x| = −2, no solution. |x| − 2 = 3 gives |x| = 5, two solutions.

questions.q: Match each equation to its number of solutions.
questions.hint: First get the absolute value alone on one side.
questions.explanation: |x − 3| = 5 has two solutions (−2 and 8). |x| + 6 = 6 gives |x| = 0, one solution. |x + 2| + 4 = 1 gives |x + 2| = −3, no solution. |x| − 7 = 2 gives |x| = 9, two solutions.

questions.q: For what value of k does the equation |x − 5| = k have exactly one solution?
questions.hint: Think about when the two cases A = k and A = −k give the same answer.
questions.explanation: |x − 5| = k splits into x − 5 = k and x − 5 = −k. These give the same x only when k = −k, so k = 0, and then the only solution is x = 5.

questions.q: Isolate the absolute value in each equation, then give the number of solutions.
questions.hint: Move the constant to the other side, then look at its sign.
questions.explanation: |x| + 2 = 9 gives |x| = 7: two solutions (±7). |x| + 9 = 2 gives |x| = −7: no solutions. |x − 1| − 3 = −3 gives |x − 1| = 0: one solution (x = 1).

questions.q: Solve |3x + 2| = −4 for x.
questions.hint: Can an absolute value ever equal a negative number?
questions.explanation: An absolute value is a distance, so it is always 0 or more. It can never equal −4, so the equation has no solution.

questions.q: Match each equation to its solution set.
questions.hint: Check the sign of the right side before splitting into two cases.
questions.explanation: |x − 4| = −2 is impossible. |x − 4| = 2 gives x = 6 or x = 2. |x − 4| = 0 gives only x = 4. |x + 4| = 2 gives x = −2 or x = −6.

questions.q: Solve |5x − 1| = −3. If there is no solution, type no solution.
questions.hint: Look at the right side first.
questions.explanation: The left side |5x − 1| is never negative, but the right side is −3. So no value of x works: there is no solution.

questions.q: Which of the following, if any, is/are the solution(s) of 2|x + 1| + 9 = 3?
questions.hint: Isolate the absolute value before splitting into cases.
questions.explanation: Subtract 9: 2|x + 1| = −6. Divide by 2: |x + 1| = −3. An absolute value cannot be negative, so there is no solution.

questions.hint: Subtract 5, then divide by 4.
questions.explanation: 4|x − 3| = 8, so |x − 3| = 2. Then x − 3 = 2 gives x = 5 and x − 3 = −2 gives x = 1.

questions.q: For each equation, isolate the absolute value and then give all solutions (type none if there are no solutions).
questions.hint: Undo the addition/subtraction first, then the multiplication.
questions.explanation: 2|x| = 10 gives |x| = 5, so x = ±5. 5|x + 1| = −10 gives |x + 1| = −2, which is impossible. 3|x − 4| = 0 gives |x − 4| = 0, so x = 4 only.

questions.hint: Dividing by −2 makes the right side positive.
questions.explanation: Subtract 3: −2|x − 6| = −10. Divide by −2: |x − 6| = 5. So x − 6 = 5 gives x = 11 and x − 6 = −5 gives x = 1.

questions.q: Solve |x + 2| − 3 = 1 for x.
questions.hint: Add 3 to both sides first.
questions.explanation: |x + 2| = 4. Then x + 2 = 4 gives x = 2 and x + 2 = −4 gives x = −6. Both are solutions.

questions.q: Solve |x − 4| + 2 = 7. Give both solutions separated by a comma.
questions.hint: Isolate |x − 4| and then use two cases.
questions.explanation: |x − 4| = 5. Then x − 4 = 5 gives x = 9 and x − 4 = −5 gives x = −1.

questions.q: Complete the table for the expression |x − 3| + 1, and write yes or no to say whether x solves |x − 3| + 1 = 4.
questions.hint: Subtract 3 from x, take the absolute value, then add 1.

questions.q: Solve the equation 4|y − 5| = 28.
questions.hint: Divide by 4 first.
questions.explanation: |y − 5| = 7. Then y − 5 = 7 gives y = 12 and y − 5 = −7 gives y = −2. The solution set is {−2, 12}.

questions.q: Solve 5|m + 3| = 20. Give both solutions separated by a comma.
questions.hint: Divide both sides by 5.
questions.explanation: |m + 3| = 4. Then m + 3 = 4 gives m = 1 and m + 3 = −4 gives m = −7.

questions.hint: Divide by 2, then solve 3x − 6 = 9 and 3x − 6 = −9.

questions.q: Match each equation to its solution set.
questions.hint: Divide to isolate the absolute value, then use two cases.
questions.explanation: |x + 1| = 5 gives 4 and −6. |x − 2| = 4 gives 6 and −2. |x| = 6 gives ±6. |x + 2| = 4 gives 2 and −6.

questions.q: A number line shows solid dots at exactly two points: −6 and 2. Which could be an equation for the graph?
questions.hint: Find the midpoint of the two dots and the distance from it to each dot.
questions.explanation: The midpoint is (−6 + 2)/2 = −2 and each dot is 4 units from −2. So |x − (−2)| = 4, which is |x + 2| = 4.

questions.q: A number line shows solid dots at −1 and 9 only. Write an absolute value equation for the graph.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Distance from the midpoint to each dot:

questions.hint: Midpoint = average of the two numbers.
questions.explanation: The midpoint is (−1 + 9)/2 = 4. The distance from 4 to 9 (or to −1) is 5. So the equation is |x − 4| = 5.

questions.q: Each description is a number line with two solid dots. Match it to its equation.
questions.hint: The center is the midpoint; the right side is the distance to each dot.
questions.explanation: −3 and 3 are centered at 0: |x| = 3. 1 and 7 are centered at 4: |x − 4| = 3. −8 and −2 are centered at −5: |x + 5| = 3. −1 and 5 are centered at 2: |x − 2| = 3.

questions.q: Plot the solutions of |x − 1| = 3 as points on the x-axis (each point has y = 0).
questions.hint: The solutions are 3 units to the left and right of 1.
questions.explanation: x − 1 = 3 gives x = 4 and x − 1 = −3 gives x = −2. Plot (−2, 0) and (4, 0).

questions.q: The maximum and minimum speeds of a fan (in revolutions per second) can be found by solving |s − 45| = 6. Find the minimum speed.
questions.hint: Solve both cases and choose the smaller value.
questions.explanation: s − 45 = 6 gives s = 51 and s − 45 = −6 gives s = 39. The minimum is 39.

questions.q: The heaviest and lightest acceptable bags of rice satisfy |w − 25| = 0.4, where w is in kg. Find the heaviest acceptable weight in kg.
questions.hint: Add 0.4 to the middle value.
questions.explanation: w − 25 = 0.4 gives w = 25.4 and w − 25 = −0.4 gives w = 24.6. The heaviest is 25.4 kg.

questions.q: A room thermostat keeps the temperature between a maximum and minimum given by |t − 22| = 1.5 (°C).
questions.hint: Split into t − 22 = 1.5 and t − 22 = −1.5.
questions.explanation: t − 22 = 1.5 gives t = 23.5 and t − 22 = −1.5 gives t = 20.5. So the maximum is 23.5°C and the minimum is 20.5°C.

questions.q: At a beach, the high and low tide levels (in feet) are the solutions of |h − 3.4| = 2.2.
questions.hint: Add and subtract 2.2 from 3.4.
questions.explanation: h − 3.4 = 2.2 gives h = 5.6 and h − 3.4 = −2.2 gives h = 1.2. High tide is 5.6 ft and low tide is 1.2 ft.

questions.q: The longest and shortest lengths of a spring (in cm) solve |L − 12.5| = 0.8. What are the longest and shortest lengths?
questions.explanation: L = 12.5 + 0.8 = 13.3 cm and L = 12.5 − 0.8 = 11.7 cm. The longest is 13.3 cm and the shortest is 11.7 cm.

questions.q: At a harbor, the high water mark is 7.2 ft and the low water mark is 2.6 ft. Write an equation of the form |M − c| = d whose solutions are these two marks.
questions.hint: c is the midpoint and d is half the difference.
questions.explanation: The midpoint is (7.2 + 2.6)/2 = 4.9. Half the difference is (7.2 − 2.6)/2 = 2.3. So |M − 4.9| = 2.3.

questions.q: Each equation gives the high and low water marks (in feet) at a harbor. Complete the table.
questions.hint: High = center + distance, low = center − distance.

questions.q: Solve |x − 3| ≤ 0 for x.
questions.hint: An absolute value is never negative, so it can only be ≤ 0 by being exactly 0.
questions.explanation: |x − 3| ≥ 0 always, so |x − 3| ≤ 0 only when |x − 3| = 0. That happens when x = 3.

questions.q: Match each inequality to its solution.
questions.hint: |x + 2| is 0 when x = −2 and positive for every other x.
questions.explanation: ≤ 0 needs |x + 2| = 0, so x = −2. < 0 is impossible. ≥ 0 is always true. > 0 is true except where |x + 2| = 0, i.e. all reals except −2.

questions.q: Solve |2x − 8| ≤ 0.
questions.hint: The absolute value must equal exactly 0.
questions.explanation: Since |2x − 8| cannot be negative, it must equal 0. 2x − 8 = 0 gives x = 4.

questions.q: Solve |x + 3| + 5 < 5 for x.
questions.hint: Subtract 5 from both sides first.
questions.explanation: |x + 3| < 0. An absolute value is never less than 0, so there is no solution.

questions.q: For each inequality, isolate the absolute value and then give the solution (type no solution, all real numbers, or a value of x).
questions.hint: Subtract 4 from both sides in every row.
questions.explanation: Each becomes |x − 2| compared with 0. |x − 2| < 0 never happens. |x − 2| ≤ 0 only when x − 2 = 0, so x = 2. |x − 2| ≥ 0 is true for all real numbers.

questions.q: Match each inequality to its solution.
questions.hint: Add 2 to both sides to isolate |x − 4|.
questions.explanation: |x − 4| < 0 has no solution. |x − 4| ≤ 0 gives x = 4. |x − 4| < 3 gives −3 < x − 4 < 3, so 1 < x < 7. |x − 4| ≥ 0 is always true.

questions.q: Solve 2|x − 5| + 6 < 6. If there is no solution, type no solution.
questions.hint: Subtract 6 and divide by 2.
questions.explanation: 2|x − 5| < 0, so |x − 5| < 0. An absolute value is never negative, so there is no solution.

questions.q: What is the equation of the line that has a slope of −4 and a y-intercept of 5?
questions.hint: Use y = mx + b with m = slope and b = y-intercept.
questions.explanation: In y = mx + b, m = −4 and b = 5, so y = −4x + 5.

questions.q: Write the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line with slope 3/4 and y-intercept −2.
questions.hint: Substitute m and b into y = mx + b.

questions.q: Graph the line with slope −1/2 and y-intercept 4. Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: Start at (0, 4), then go down 1 and right 2.
questions.explanation: The equation is y = −(1/2)x + 4. The y-intercept gives (0, 4). Moving right 2 and down 1 gives (2, 3). Other points include (4, 2) and (−2, 5).

questions.q: Complete the table. Each row describes one line in slope-intercept form.
questions.hint: The equation is y = mx + b.
questions.explanation: m = −1, b = 6 gives y = −x + 6. m = 5, b = 0 gives y = 5x. In y = 2x − 7 the slope is 2 and the y-intercept is −7.

questions.q: Which description matches the graph of y = −(3/4)x + 2?
options: Crosses the y-axis at (0, −2) and falls: down 3 for every 4 to the right
Crosses the y-axis at (0, 2) and falls: down 3 for every 4 to the right
Crosses the y-axis at (0, 2) and falls: down 4 for every 3 to the right
Crosses the y-axis at (0, 2) and rises: up 3 for every 4 to the right
questions.hint: b gives the y-intercept and the sign of m tells you rising or falling.
questions.explanation: b = 2, so the line crosses the y-axis at (0, 2). The slope −3/4 is negative, so the line falls, going down 3 units for every 4 units to the right.

questions.q: Graph the line y = −(2/5)x + 3. Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: Start at the y-intercept, then go down 2 and right 5.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is (0, 3). The slope −2/5 means down 2 for every 5 to the right, giving (5, 1). Another point is (−5, 5).

questions.q: Match each equation to the description of its graph.
questions.hint: Positive slope rises, negative slope falls; b is the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: y = 2x + 1 rises and crosses at 1. y = −2x + 1 falls and crosses at 1. y = 2x − 1 rises and crosses at −1. y = −2x − 1 falls and crosses at −1.

questions.q: A graphed line crosses the y-axis at (0, −2) and the x-axis at (3, 0). Which equation does it show?
questions.hint: Slope = rise ÷ run from (0, −2) to (3, 0).
questions.explanation: From (0, −2) to (3, 0) the rise is 2 and the run is 3, so m = 2/3. The y-intercept is −2, so y = (2/3)x − 2.

questions.q: A line passes through the points (2, 1) and (3, 5). Which is an equation of the line in point-slope form?
questions.hint: Find the slope, then use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

questions.q: A line passes through (−1, 3) and (1, −1). Write its equation in point-slope form using the point (−1, 3).
Graph the line y − 2 = −3(x + 1). Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: The point-slope form shows the point (−1, 2) and slope −3.
questions.explanation: The line passes through (−1, 2) with slope −3. From (−1, 2) go right 1 and down 3 to (0, −1). Plot both points.

questions.q: For the line y + 4 = (1/2)(x − 6), find:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A point on the line (from the equation):

questions.hint: Compare with y − y₁ = m(x − x₁); careful with signs.
questions.explanation: y + 4 = y − (−4), so the point is (6, −4) and the slope is 1/2. Expanding: y + 4 = (1/2)x − 3, so y = (1/2)x − 7 and the y-intercept is −7.

questions.q: Which point is on the graph of y − 3 = 2(x + 5)?
questions.hint: Read the point (x₁, y₁) from y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
questions.explanation: x + 5 = x − (−5) and y − 3 so the point is (−5, 3). Check: 3 − 3 = 0 and 2(−5 + 5) = 0.

questions.q: Complete the table for the line y + 1 = 3(x − 2).
questions.hint: Substitute x, then subtract 1 from 3(x − 2).

questions.q: Match each equation to the point (x₁, y₁) shown in its point-slope form.
questions.hint: The signs inside the form are the opposite of the coordinates.

questions.q: The point (4, k) lies on the line y + 2 = −(1/2)(x − 8). Find k.
questions.hint: Substitute x = 4 and y = k.

questions.q: Write the equation of the line through (−2, 1) and (2, 7).
questions.hint: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x; then use one point to find b.

questions.q: Write the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line through (1, −3) and (4, 3).
questions.hint: Find m first, then substitute a point into y = mx + b.

questions.q: A line passes through (−4, 5) and (2, 2).
questions.explanation: m = −3/6 = −1/2. Using (2, 2): 2 = −1 + b, so b = 3. The equation is y = −(1/2)x + 3.

questions.q: A line passes through (−1, −5) and (2, 1). Complete the table of points on this line.
questions.hint: Find the equation y = mx + b first.

questions.q: Answer both parts. i. Write the equation of the line through (−3, 2) and (0, −4). ii. Find b in y = 1.5x + b if the line passes through (2, 7.5).
questions.hint: In part i, the point with x = 0 gives the y-intercept.

questions.q: Find the value of b in the equation y = −0.25x + b if the line passes through (4, 2.5).
questions.hint: Substitute x = 4 and y = 2.5.

questions.q: Which is the equation of the line that passes through (0, 3) and (4, −5)?
questions.hint: (0, 3) is the y-intercept.

questions.q: Each line y = mx + b passes through the given point. Find b.
questions.hint: Substitute the point into y = mx + b and solve for b.

questions.q: A graphed line passes through the labeled points (−2, 7) and (−1, 4). Find the following.
questions.hint: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x between the two points.

questions.q: A graphed line passes through the points (−2, −4) and (2, −2). Which equation describes the line?
questions.hint: Find the slope, then use a point to get b.

questions.q: A line passes through (1, 5) and (3, 9). Complete the table.
questions.hint: After finding y = mx + b, set y = 0 for the x-intercept.

questions.q: Graph the line with slope −2 that passes through (−1, 3). Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: From (−1, 3), go right 1 and down 2.
questions.explanation: Starting at (−1, 3), a slope of −2 means down 2 for each 1 to the right, giving (0, 1). The equation is y = −2x + 1.

questions.q: Graph the line with a slope of 2 and a y-intercept of −4. Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: Plot (0, −4) first, then go up 2 and right 1.
questions.explanation: The equation is y = 2x − 4. Start at (0, −4); slope 2 means up 2, right 1, giving (1, −2) and then (2, 0).

questions.q: Graph the line with a slope of −1/3 and a y-intercept of 3. Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: From the y-intercept, go down 1 and right 3.
questions.explanation: The equation is y = −(1/3)x + 3. Start at (0, 3); move right 3 and down 1 to (3, 2).

questions.q: A line has slope −4 and y-intercept 1. Starting at the y-intercept and moving 1 unit to the right along the line, which point do you reach?
questions.hint: A slope of −4 means down 4 for every 1 to the right.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is (0, 1). Going right 1 and down 4 gives (1, 1 − 4) = (1, −3).

questions.q: Graph the line y = (1/3)x + 2. Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: Start at (0, 2) and go up 1, right 3.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is (0, 2) and the slope is 1/3. From (0, 2) move right 3 and up 1 to (3, 3). (−3, 1) is also on the line.

questions.q: Graph the line y = −(3/2)x + 1. Tap two points on the line.
questions.hint: From (0, 1), go down 3 and right 2.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is (0, 1). The slope −3/2 means down 3 for every 2 right, giving (2, −2). (−2, 4) is also on the line.

questions.q: Complete the table of values for y = (1/2)x − 3.
questions.hint: Half of x, then subtract 3.

questions.q: Which pair of points could be used to graph y = (3/4)x − 2?
questions.hint: Start at the y-intercept, then go up 3 and right 4.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is (0, −2). Moving right 4 and up 3 gives (4, 1). Check: (3/4)(4) − 2 = 1.

questions.q: A phone plan costs AED 45 per month plus AED 0.50 for every minute of international calls. Write an equation for the monthly cost y when x international minutes are used.
questions.hint: The fixed fee is the y-intercept; the per-minute charge is the slope.
questions.explanation: The cost changes by 0.50 per minute, so the slope is 0.5. The fixed fee 45 is the y-intercept. y = 0.5x + 45.

questions.q: A taxi charges a starting fee of AED 12 plus AED 2.50 per km. Which equation gives the total fare y for a trip of x km?
questions.hint: Per-km charge × distance + starting fee.
questions.explanation: Each km adds 2.50, so the slope is 2.5. The starting fee 12 is charged once, so it is the y-intercept: y = 2.5x + 12.

questions.q: A swimming club charges AED 400 per month plus AED 25 for each lesson. Complete the table of the monthly cost y for x lessons.
questions.hint: The equation is y = 25x + 400.

questions.q: Match each situation (y after x weeks) to its equation.

left: Starts at 50 and increases by 10 each week
Starts at 10 and increases by 50 each week
Starts at 50 and decreases by 10 each week
Starts at 0 and increases by 50 each week

questions.hint: The starting amount is b and the weekly change is m.
questions.explanation: Start 50, +10 per week: y = 10x + 50. Start 10, +50 per week: y = 50x + 10. Start 50, −10 per week: y = −10x + 50. Start 0, +50 per week: y = 50x.

questions.q: A line with a slope of 3/5 passes through the point (4, 9). What is the y-intercept of the line? Round to the nearest tenth if necessary.
questions.hint: Substitute into y = mx + b and solve for b.

questions.q: A line with slope −2/3 passes through (6, 1). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: Be careful: (−2/3)(6) is negative.
questions.explanation: 1 = (−2/3)(6) + b = −4 + b. Adding 4 gives b = 5.

questions.q: Each line has the given slope and passes through the given point. Find the y-intercept b (as a decimal).
questions.hint: Use b = y − m·x.

questions.q: A line with slope 4/3 passes through (2, 5). Find its y-intercept.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Exact value of b (fraction in simplest form):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: b rounded to the nearest tenth:

questions.q: Which of the following is the standard form of y − 3 = (2/5)(x + 10)?
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 5 to clear the fraction, then move x and y to one side.
questions.explanation: 5(y − 3) = 2(x + 10) gives 5y − 15 = 2x + 20. Subtract 5y and 20 from both sides: 2x − 5y = −35.

questions.q: Write y + 1 = −(2/3)(x − 6) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0 and integer coefficients.
questions.hint: Multiply by 3 first.
questions.explanation: 3(y + 1) = −2(x − 6) gives 3y + 3 = −2x + 12. Add 2x and subtract 3: 2x + 3y = 9.

questions.q: Match each point-slope equation to its standard form.
questions.hint: Clear fractions, distribute, and collect x and y on the left.
questions.explanation: y − 1 = 2x − 6 gives 2x − y = 5. 2y + 8 = x − 2 gives x − 2y = 10. y − 5 = −3x − 3 gives 3x + y = 2. 3y + 6 = −x − 3 gives x + 3y = −9.

questions.q: Convert y − 4 = (5/2)(x + 2) to standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: After multiplying by 2, distribute and move the y-term to the right side.

questions.q: Write the equation of the line y − 2 = (3/4)(x + 4) in standard form.
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 4 to clear the fraction first.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4: 4(y − 2) = 3(x + 4), so 4y − 8 = 3x + 12. Move the variables to the left: −3x + 4y = 20. Multiply by −1 so A is positive: 3x − 4y = −20.

questions.q: Write y + 3 = (2/5)(x − 1) in standard form Ax + By = C, where A, B and C are integers and A > 0.
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 5, then collect x and y on one side.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 5: 5y + 15 = 2x − 2. Subtract 2x and 15 from both sides: −2x + 5y = −17. Multiply by −1: 2x − 5y = 17.

questions.q: Write y − 4 = −(1/2)(x − 6) in standard form Ax + By = C with integer coefficients and A > 0. Give A, B and C.
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 2 to remove the fraction.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2: 2y − 8 = −(x − 6) = −x + 6. Add x and 8 to both sides: x + 2y = 14. So A = 1, B = 2, C = 14.

questions.q: Match each equation in point-slope form to the same line in standard form.
questions.hint: Distribute (clear any fraction first), then move x and y to the left side.
questions.explanation: y − 1 = 2x − 6 gives 2x − y = 5. y + 2 = −3x + 3 gives 3x + y = 1. Multiplying the third by 3: 3y − 15 = x + 3, so x − 3y = −18.

questions.q: Which best describes the slope of a vertical line?
questions.hint: On a vertical line, the x-value never changes.
questions.explanation: On a vertical line the run (change in x) is 0. Slope = rise ÷ run would need division by 0, which is impossible, so the slope is undefined.

questions.q: Find the slope of the line that passes through (−2, −6) and (5, −6).
questions.hint: Use slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).
questions.explanation: Slope = (−6 − (−6)) ÷ (5 − (−2)) = 0 ÷ 7 = 0. Both points have the same y-value, so the line is horizontal.

questions.q: Match each line to the best description of its slope.

left: A line that rises from left to right

questions.hint: Horizontal lines and vertical lines are the special cases; for the others look at the direction or the coefficient of x.
questions.explanation: Equal y-values mean a horizontal line, slope 0. x = −4 is vertical, so its slope is undefined. A line that rises left to right has positive slope, and y = −2x + 1 has slope −2, which is negative.

questions.q: Which equation has a graph with slope 0?
questions.hint: Slope 0 means the line is horizontal.
questions.explanation: y = 4 is a horizontal line: every point has y-value 4, so the rise is always 0 and the slope is 0. x = 4 is vertical (undefined slope), y = x has slope 1 and y = −x + 4 has slope −1.

questions.q: Complete the statements about the lines y = −3 and x = 7.
questions.hint: Decide which line is horizontal and which is vertical.
questions.explanation: y = −3 is a horizontal line: y never changes, so the slope is 0. x = 7 is a vertical line: x never changes, so the run is 0 and the slope is undefined.

questions.q: Complete the table. Write horizontal or vertical, and write the slope as a number or 'undefined'.
questions.hint: If the x-values are all equal the line is vertical; if the y-values are all equal it is horizontal.
questions.explanation: y = 5 and the line through (−4, 2) and (6, 2) are horizontal, so their slope is 0. x = −2 and the line through (3, 1) and (3, 8) are vertical: the change in x is 0, so the slope is undefined.

questions.q: Graph the line that has slope 0 and passes through (2, −3).
questions.hint: A line with slope 0 is horizontal.
questions.explanation: Slope 0 means the line is horizontal, so every point has the same y-value as (2, −3). The line is y = −3; for example it passes through (0, −3) and (2, −3).

questions.q: Given the line 3x + 4y = 24, which of the following is/are true?   I. The slope is −3/4.   II. The x-intercept is 8.   III. The y-intercept is 8.
questions.hint: Solve for y to read the slope and y-intercept; set y = 0 for the x-intercept.
questions.explanation: Solving for y: 4y = −3x + 24, so y = −(3/4)x + 6. The slope is −3/4 (I true) and the y-intercept is 6, not 8 (III false). With y = 0, 3x = 24 so x = 8 (II true). Answer: I and II only.

questions.q: For the line 5x − 2y = 20, find the slope, the x-intercept and the y-intercept.
questions.hint: Rewrite in the form y = mx + b, then set y = 0 to find the x-intercept.
questions.explanation: −2y = −5x + 20, so y = (5/2)x − 10: slope 5/2 and y-intercept −10. With y = 0, 5x = 20 so the x-intercept is 4.

questions.q: Complete the table for each line.
questions.hint: Slope = −A/B for Ax + By = C; x-intercept = C/A; y-intercept = C/B.
questions.explanation: 2x + y = 8 gives y = −2x + 8: slope −2, y-intercept 8. x − 3y = 9 gives y = (1/3)x − 3: slope 1/3, and x = 9 when y = 0. 4x + 6y = 12 gives y = −(2/3)x + 2: slope −2/3, y-intercept 2, and x = 3 when y = 0.

questions.q: Which line has slope −1/2 and y-intercept 3?
questions.hint: Solve each equation for y and compare with y = −(1/2)x + 3.
questions.explanation: x + 2y = 6 gives 2y = −x + 6, so y = −(1/2)x + 3. 2x + y = 3 has slope −2, x − 2y = 6 has slope 1/2, and x + 2y = 3 has y-intercept 3/2.

questions.q: The line 4x + By = 12 is vertical. Which statement is correct?
options: B = 0 and the line is x = 3
B = 0 and the line is y = 3
A = 0 and the line is y = 3
B = 4 and the line is x = 3
questions.hint: A vertical line has an equation of the form x = constant.
questions.explanation: For the line to be vertical the y-term must vanish, so B = 0. Then 4x = 12, which gives x = 3, a vertical line with undefined slope.

questions.q: Match each equation to the description of its graph.
questions.hint: If B = 0 the line is vertical; if A = 0 it is horizontal; otherwise the slope is −A/B.
questions.explanation: 3x = 12 is x = 4, vertical. 2y = −8 is y = −4, horizontal. x + y = 4 is y = −x + 4 with slope −1, and x − y = 4 is y = x − 4 with slope 1.

questions.q: Graph the line 2x = −6.
questions.hint: Solve for x; the result is a vertical line.
questions.explanation: Dividing by 2 gives x = −3. Every point on the line has x-value −3, such as (−3, 0) and (−3, 2), so it is a vertical line.

questions.q: A vertical line has equation Ax + By = C with A = 2, and it passes through (5, 1). Find B and C.
questions.hint: Vertical means no y-term; then substitute the point.
questions.explanation: A vertical line has B = 0, so the equation is 2x = C. The point (5, 1) is on it, so C = 2(5) = 10. The line is 2x = 10, that is x = 5.

questions.q: The line Ax + By = C is horizontal, has B = 4 and passes through (3, −2). What is C?
questions.hint: A horizontal line has A = 0, so only the y-term remains.
questions.explanation: Horizontal means A = 0, so the equation is 4y = C. Every point has y = −2, so C = 4(−2) = −8. The x-value 3 does not matter.

questions.q: Write the line 0x + 5y = 15 in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Divide both sides by the coefficient of y.
questions.explanation: The x-term is 0, so 5y = 15. Dividing by 5 gives y = 3, a horizontal line with slope 0.

questions.q: Graph the line 3y = 12.
questions.hint: Solve for y; the result is a horizontal line.
questions.explanation: Dividing by 3 gives y = 4. Every point on the line has y-value 4, such as (0, 4) and (1, 4), so it is horizontal with slope 0.

questions.q: Museum tickets cost AED 12 for adults and AED 8 for students. The equation 12x + 8y = 96 shows how many adults x and students y can visit with AED 96. If no students go, how many adults can visit?
questions.hint: No students means y = 0.
questions.explanation: Set y = 0: 12x = 96, so x = 8. Eight adult tickets use the whole AED 96.

questions.q: Cinema tickets cost AED 15 for adults and AED 10 for children: 15x + 10y = 150, where x is adults and y is children. If no adults go, how many children can go with AED 150?
questions.hint: No adults means x = 0.
questions.explanation: Set x = 0: 10y = 150, so y = 15 children.

questions.q: A shop sells small pizzas for AED 25 and large pizzas for AED 40. The equation 25x + 40y = 200 models buying x small and y large pizzas with AED 200.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: If only small pizzas are bought, how many?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: If only large pizzas are bought, how many?

questions.hint: Only small pizzas means y = 0; only large means x = 0.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: 25x = 200, so x = 8. With x = 0: 40y = 200, so y = 5.

questions.q: Notebooks cost AED 6 and pens cost AED 4. The equation 6x + 4y = 48 models buying x notebooks and y pens with AED 48. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Substitute the known value and solve for the other.

questions.q: Mariam can buy 3 kg of apples for AED 15 and 2 kg of grapes for AED 18. She has AED 45 to spend. If x is the number of kg of apples and y is the number of kg of grapes, which equation models the situation?
questions.hint: Find the price per kilogram of each fruit first.
questions.explanation: Apples cost 15 ÷ 3 = AED 5 per kg and grapes cost 18 ÷ 2 = AED 9 per kg. The total spent is 5x + 9y, and it must equal 45: 5x + 9y = 45.

questions.q: 5 pencils cost AED 10 and 4 erasers cost AED 12. Sara spends exactly AED 30 on x pencils and y erasers. Write a linear equation in standard form for the situation.
questions.hint: Work out the price of one pencil and one eraser.
questions.explanation: One pencil costs 10 ÷ 5 = AED 2 and one eraser costs 12 ÷ 4 = AED 3. So 2x + 3y = 30.

questions.q: Omar can buy 2 kg of almonds for AED 14 and 3 kg of cashews for AED 27. He spends AED 63 on x kg of almonds and y kg of cashews.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Pounds of almonds if he buys no cashews:

questions.hint: Divide each total price by the number of pounds.
questions.explanation: Almonds: 14 ÷ 2 = AED 7 per kg; cashews: 27 ÷ 3 = AED 9 per kg. The equation is 7x + 9y = 63. With y = 0, 7x = 63 so x = 9 kg.

questions.q: Identify the intercepts of the line 3x + 4y = 12.
questions.hint: Set y = 0 for the x-intercept and x = 0 for the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: 3x = 12, x = 4, giving (4, 0). With x = 0: 4y = 12, y = 3, giving (0, 3).

questions.q: Plot the x-intercept and the y-intercept of the line 5x − 2y = 10.
questions.hint: Set y = 0, then x = 0.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: 5x = 10, so x = 2 and the point is (2, 0). With x = 0: −2y = 10, so y = −5 and the point is (0, −5).

questions.q: Graph the line 4x + 3y = −12 using its intercepts.
questions.hint: Find where the line crosses each axis.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: 4x = −12, x = −3, giving (−3, 0). With x = 0: 3y = −12, y = −4, giving (0, −4). Draw the line through these two points.

questions.q: Which line has x-intercept 6 and y-intercept −2?
questions.hint: Check each equation with y = 0 and with x = 0.
questions.explanation: For x − 3y = 6: y = 0 gives x = 6, and x = 0 gives −3y = 6, y = −2. 3x − y = 6 has intercepts 2 and −6, x + 3y = 6 has 6 and 2, and −x + 3y = 6 has −6 and 2.

questions.q: The table shows pages read after x minutes. Minutes x: 1, 2, 3, 4. Pages y: 4, 7, 10, 13. Graph this linear function.
questions.hint: Plot two points from the table and draw the line through them.
questions.explanation: Each extra minute adds 3 pages, so the slope is 3. Going back one minute from (1, 4) gives the y-intercept 1, so the function is y = 3x + 1. Points such as (1, 4) and (2, 7) lie on it.

questions.q: A table of values shows x: 0, 1, 2, 3 and y: 5, 9, 13, 17. Write the equation of the linear function in slope-intercept form.
questions.hint: Find how much y increases each time x increases by 1.
questions.explanation: y increases by 4 for each increase of 1 in x, so the slope is 4. When x = 0, y = 5, so the y-intercept is 5. The function is y = 4x + 5.

questions.q: A linear function has the values below. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Find the constant change in y when x increases by 1.
questions.explanation: y increases by 2 each time x increases by 1, and y = 5 when x = 1, so y = 2x + 3. This gives 9 at x = 3, 11 at x = 4, 3 at x = 0 and 23 at x = 10.

questions.q: A table shows x: 1, 2, 3, 4 and y: 10, 8, 6, 4. Which function does the table represent?
questions.hint: Find the rate of change, then check with one point.
questions.explanation: y decreases by 2 each time x increases by 1, so the slope is −2. Using (1, 10): 10 = −2 + b, so b = 12. The function is y = −2x + 12; check (4, 4): −8 + 12 = 4.

questions.q: Complete the table of values for y = 2x − 1.
questions.hint: Substitute each x-value into 2x − 1.

questions.q: Graph the line y = −x + 4.
questions.hint: Start at the y-intercept, then use the slope −1.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is 4, so (0, 4) is on the line. With slope −1, move right 1 and down 1 each time; for example (4, 0) is also on the line.

questions.q: Complete the table of values for y = −3x + 2.
questions.hint: Be careful multiplying −3 by a negative x.

questions.q: Plot the points of y = (1/2)x + 1 for x = −2, 0, 2 and 4.
questions.hint: Substitute each x-value to get its y-value.
questions.explanation: x = −2 gives −1 + 1 = 0; x = 0 gives 1; x = 2 gives 2; x = 4 gives 3. Plot (−2, 0), (0, 1), (2, 2) and (4, 3).

questions.q: Graph −x = (1/3)y − 2 using its intercepts.
questions.hint: Set y = 0 to find the x-intercept and x = 0 to find the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: −x = −2, so x = 2, giving (2, 0). With x = 0: 0 = (1/3)y − 2, so y = 6, giving (0, 6). Draw the line through them.

questions.q: Find the intercepts of the line (1/2)x = y + 2.
questions.hint: Substitute y = 0, then x = 0.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: (1/2)x = 2, so x = 4, giving (4, 0). With x = 0: 0 = y + 2, so y = −2, giving (0, −2).

questions.q: Complete the table of values for the line 2x = y − 4.
questions.hint: Rewrite the equation as y = 2x + 4 first.
questions.explanation: Adding 4 to both sides gives y = 2x + 4. So x = −2 gives 0, x = 0 gives 4, x = 1 gives 6, and y = 2 gives 2x = −2, x = −1.

questions.q: Which point lies on the graph of −x = (1/4)y − 2?
questions.hint: Solve for y, or substitute each point into the equation.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4: −4x = y − 8, so y = −4x + 8. For x = 1, y = −4 + 8 = 4, so (1, 4) is on the line. (0, 2) gives y = 8, (4, 0) gives y = −8 and (2, 1) gives y = 0, so they are not.

questions.q: Write y = (3/4)x + 2 in standard form Ax + By = C with integer coefficients and A > 0.
questions.hint: Multiply every term by 4.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4: 4y = 3x + 8. Subtract 4y and 8: −8 = 3x − 4y, that is 3x − 4y = −8.

questions.q: Which is the standard form of y = −(2/5)x + 4?
questions.hint: Clear the fraction by multiplying by 5.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 5: 5y = −2x + 20. Add 2x to both sides: 2x + 5y = 20.

questions.q: Write y = (1/2)x − 3 in standard form Ax + By = C with integers and A > 0. Give A, B and C.
questions.hint: Multiply by 2, then move the x-term to the left.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2: 2y = x − 6. Subtract x: −x + 2y = −6. Multiply by −1: x − 2y = 6, so A = 1, B = −2, C = 6.

questions.q: Match each slope-intercept equation to its standard form.
questions.hint: Clear fractions, then bring x and y to the same side.
questions.explanation: y = 3x − 1 gives 3x − y = 1. Multiplying y = −(1/3)x + 2 by 3: 3y = −x + 6, so x + 3y = 6. Multiplying y = (5/2)x + 1 by 2: 2y = 5x + 2, so 5x − 2y = −2.

questions.q: Write y + 3 = 4(x − 2) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Distribute the 4, then move y to the right side.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y + 3 = 4x − 8. Subtract y and add 8: 11 = 4x − y, so 4x − y = 11.

questions.q: Write y − 6 = −2(x + 5) in standard form.
questions.hint: Distribute −2 to both terms in the bracket.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y − 6 = −2x − 10. Add 2x and 6 to both sides: 2x + y = −4.

questions.q: Write y − 1 = 5(x + 3) in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0. Give A, B and C.
questions.hint: Distribute 5, then move y to the right and the constant to the left.
questions.explanation: Distribute: y − 1 = 5x + 15. Subtract y and 15: −16 = 5x − y, so 5x − y = −16. A = 5, B = −1, C = −16.

questions.q: Write each equation in standard form Ax + By = C with A > 0.
questions.hint: Distribute, then collect the x- and y-terms on the left.
questions.explanation: y − 2 = 3x − 3 gives 3x − y = 1. y + 4 = −x + 6 gives x + y = 2. y − 7 = −3x − 3 gives 3x + y = 4.

questions.q: Fatima has AED 30 to spend on juice and water. Juice costs AED 5 per bottle and water costs AED 2 per bottle. Let x be the bottles of juice and y the bottles of water.
questions.hint: Cost = price × quantity for each item; the intercepts come from setting the other variable to 0.
questions.explanation: Juice costs 5x and water costs 2y, so 5x + 2y = 30. With y = 0, x = 6: she can buy 6 bottles of juice and no water. With x = 0, y = 15: she can buy 15 bottles of water and no juice.

questions.q: Rice costs AED 4 per kg and lentils cost AED 6 per kg. The equation 4x + 6y = 48 models spending AED 48 on x kg of rice and y kg of lentils. What does the x-intercept (12, 0) mean?
options: Buying 12 kg of rice and 8 kg of lentils uses the whole AED 48
Buying 12 kg of rice and no lentils uses the whole AED 48
Buying 12 kg of lentils and no rice uses the whole AED 48
questions.hint: On the x-intercept, y = 0.
questions.explanation: At (12, 0), x = 12 and y = 0: 4(12) + 6(0) = 48. So 12 kg of rice and 0 kg of lentils use all AED 48.

questions.q: Dates cost AED 3 per kg and figs cost AED 4 per kg. Khalid spends AED 24: 3x + 4y = 24, where x is kg of dates and y is kg of figs. Plot the x-intercept and the y-intercept.
questions.hint: Set y = 0, then x = 0.
questions.explanation: With y = 0: 3x = 24, x = 8, so (8, 0) means 8 kg of dates and no figs. With x = 0: 4y = 24, y = 6, so (0, 6) means 6 kg of figs and no dates.

questions.q: What is the equation of the line that passes through (2, 5) and is perpendicular to y = (2/3)x − 1?
questions.hint: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is −3/2. Substitute (2, 5): 5 = −(3/2)(2) + b = −3 + b, so b = 8. The line is y = −(3/2)x + 8.

questions.q: Write in slope-intercept form the line through (−4, 1) that is perpendicular to y = 2x + 7.
questions.hint: The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of 2.
questions.explanation: The slope is −1/2. Substitute (−4, 1): 1 = −(1/2)(−4) + b = 2 + b, so b = −1. The line is y = −(1/2)x − 1.

questions.q: Graph the line that passes through (3, 1) and is perpendicular to y = −3x + 4.
questions.hint: Find the perpendicular slope first, then use the given point.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is 1/3. Substitute (3, 1): 1 = (1/3)(3) + b, so b = 0. The line is y = (1/3)x, through (0, 0) and (3, 1).

questions.q: Line p passes through (5, −1) and is perpendicular to y = −(5/2)x + 1. Write p as y = mx + b.
questions.hint: Flip the fraction and change the sign to get the perpendicular slope.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is 2/5. Substitute (5, −1): −1 = (2/5)(5) + b = 2 + b, so b = −3. The line is y = (2/5)x − 3.

questions.q: What is the equation of the line that passes through (5, 4) and is parallel to y = (2/5)x − 3?
questions.hint: Parallel lines have the same slope.
questions.explanation: The slope is 2/5. Substitute (5, 4): 4 = (2/5)(5) + b = 2 + b, so b = 2. The line is y = (2/5)x + 2.

questions.q: Write in slope-intercept form the line through (−2, 3) that is parallel to y = −4x + 1.
questions.hint: Keep the slope −4 and find the new y-intercept.
questions.explanation: Substitute (−2, 3) into y = −4x + b: 3 = 8 + b, so b = −5. The line is y = −4x − 5.

questions.q: Graph the line that passes through (4, −1) and is parallel to y = (1/2)x + 5.
questions.hint: Use the same slope 1/2 and the given point.
questions.explanation: Substitute (4, −1) into y = (1/2)x + b: −1 = 2 + b, so b = −3. The line y = (1/2)x − 3 passes through (0, −3) and (4, −1).

questions.q: Line q passes through (−4, 6) and is parallel to y = −(3/4)x + 2. Write q as y = mx + b.
questions.hint: Parallel lines share the slope; substitute the point to find b.
questions.explanation: The slope is −3/4. Substitute (−4, 6): 6 = −(3/4)(−4) + b = 3 + b, so b = 3. The line is y = −(3/4)x + 3.

questions.q: Are the graphs of each pair of equations parallel, perpendicular, or neither?
questions.hint: Find each slope; equal slopes are parallel, slopes with product −1 are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: The first pair both have slope 4: parallel. The second pair have slopes −3/2 and 2/3, whose product is −1: perpendicular. Slopes 5 and −5 are neither. A horizontal line and a vertical line are perpendicular.

questions.q: How are the graphs of x − 2y = 4 and 2x − 4y = 10 related?
questions.hint: Write both equations in slope-intercept form.
questions.explanation: x − 2y = 4 gives y = (1/2)x − 2, and 2x − 4y = 10 gives y = (1/2)x − 5/2. Both have slope 1/2 but different y-intercepts, so the lines are parallel.

questions.q: Complete the table. In the last column write parallel, perpendicular or neither.
questions.hint: Solve 6x − 2y = 4 for y to find its slope.
questions.explanation: −3 × 1/3 = −1, so the first pair is perpendicular. 6x − 2y = 4 gives y = 3x − 2 with slope 3, the same as y = 3x + 8, so they are parallel. 2/3 and 3/2 are reciprocals but not negative reciprocals (product 1), so the last pair is neither.

questions.q: Match each description to the equation of the line.

left: A line parallel to the x-axis
A line parallel to the y-axis

questions.hint: Rewrite the slanted lines as y = mx + b; y = number is horizontal and x = number is vertical.
questions.explanation: 4x − 2y = 6 gives y = 2x − 3 (slope 2). y = −3 is horizontal, so parallel to the x-axis. x = 1 is vertical, so parallel to the y-axis. 2x + y = 4 gives y = −2x + 4 (slope −2).

questions.q: Which equation describes a line parallel to the y-axis?
questions.hint: Lines parallel to the y-axis are vertical.
questions.explanation: A vertical line has every point with the same x-value, so its equation is x = constant. x = −4 is vertical; y = −4 is horizontal and the other two are slanted.

questions.q: Find the slope of the line 3x − 3y = 7.
questions.hint: Solve the equation for y.
questions.explanation: −3y = −3x + 7, so y = x − 7/3. The coefficient of x is 1, so the slope is 1.

questions.q: Graph the line x + y = 3, which has slope −1.
questions.hint: Find the two intercepts.
questions.explanation: With x = 0, y = 3, and with y = 0, x = 3. The line through (0, 3) and (3, 0) goes down 1 for every 1 to the right, so its slope is −1.

questions.q: Line m is y = (3/4)x + 1. Match each equation to the term that describes its relationship to line m.
questions.hint: Write 3/4 as a decimal; perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.
questions.explanation: 3/4 = 0.75, so y = 0.75x − 2 is parallel. (3/4)(−4/3) = −1, so y = −(4/3)x + 5 is perpendicular. −0.75 is the opposite but not the reciprocal, and 4/3 is the reciprocal but not the opposite, so both are neither.

questions.q: Line n is y = −2.5x + 4. Which line is perpendicular to line n?
questions.hint: Write −2.5 as a fraction and take the negative reciprocal.
questions.explanation: −2.5 = −5/2, so the negative reciprocal is 2/5 = 0.4. y = 0.4x − 1 is perpendicular; check: −2.5 × 0.4 = −1.

questions.q: Line m is y = −(5/4)x + 2. Give each slope as a decimal.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Slope of a line parallel to m:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Slope of a line perpendicular to m:

questions.hint: Parallel keeps the slope; perpendicular flips it and changes the sign.
questions.explanation: A parallel line has the same slope −5/4 = −1.25. A perpendicular line has slope 4/5 = 0.8, because (−5/4)(4/5) = −1.

questions.q: Write in slope-intercept form the equation of the line parallel to y + 2x = 5 that passes through (3, 1).
questions.hint: Solve y + 2x = 5 for y to find its slope.
questions.explanation: y = −2x + 5 has slope −2. Substitute (3, 1) into y = −2x + b: 1 = −6 + b, so b = 7. The line is y = −2x + 7.

questions.q: Which line is parallel to 3y − 6x = 9 and passes through (−1, 4)?
questions.hint: Rewrite 3y − 6x = 9 in slope-intercept form first.
questions.explanation: 3y = 6x + 9 gives y = 2x + 3, slope 2. Substitute (−1, 4): 4 = −2 + b, so b = 6. The line is y = 2x + 6.

questions.q: Find the line parallel to 4x − 2y = 8 that passes through (2, 9).
questions.hint: Solve 4x − 2y = 8 for y.
questions.explanation: −2y = −4x + 8 gives y = 2x − 4, so the slope is 2. Substitute (2, 9): 9 = 4 + b, so b = 5. The line is y = 2x + 5.

questions.q: Graph the line that is parallel to x + y = 2 and passes through (−1, 2).
questions.hint: x + y = 2 has slope −1.
questions.explanation: x + y = 2 is y = −x + 2, slope −1. Substitute (−1, 2) into y = −x + b: 2 = 1 + b, so b = 1. The line y = −x + 1 passes through (−1, 2), (0, 1) and (1, 0).

questions.q: Write in slope-intercept form the equation of the line perpendicular to 3x + y = 4 that passes through (3, 2).
questions.hint: 3x + y = 4 has slope −3.
questions.explanation: y = −3x + 4 has slope −3, so the perpendicular slope is 1/3. Substitute (3, 2): 2 = 1 + b, so b = 1. The line is y = (1/3)x + 1.

questions.q: Which line is perpendicular to 2x − y = 5 and passes through (4, −3)?
questions.hint: Find the slope of 2x − y = 5, then take its negative reciprocal.
questions.explanation: 2x − y = 5 gives y = 2x − 5, slope 2, so the perpendicular slope is −1/2. Substitute (4, −3): −3 = −2 + b, so b = −1. The line is y = −(1/2)x − 1.

questions.q: Find the line perpendicular to x + 4y = 8 that passes through (1, 6).
questions.hint: x + 4y = 8 has slope −1/4.
questions.explanation: 4y = −x + 8 gives slope −1/4, so the perpendicular slope is 4. Substitute (1, 6): 6 = 4 + b, so b = 2. The line is y = 4x + 2.

questions.q: Graph the line that is perpendicular to x − 2y = 6 and passes through (2, −1).
questions.hint: x − 2y = 6 has slope 1/2.
questions.explanation: x − 2y = 6 gives y = (1/2)x − 3, slope 1/2, so the perpendicular slope is −2. Substitute (2, −1): −1 = −4 + b, so b = 3. The line y = −2x + 3 passes through (0, 3) and (2, −1).

questions.q: The slope of the line through (1, 4) and (x, 10) is 2. Find x.
questions.hint: Write the slope formula with the unknown and solve.

questions.q: The slope of the line through (x, 5) and (3, −1) is −2. Find x.
questions.hint: Use slope = (−1 − 5) ÷ (3 − x).

questions.q: Line t passes through (−2, 3) and (x, −5) and has slope 4.
questions.hint: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.
questions.explanation: The change in y is −5 − 3 = −8. Then −8 ÷ (x + 2) = 4, so x + 2 = −2 and x = −4.

questions.q: Each row gives two points on a line and its slope. Find the missing x-value.
questions.hint: Set (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁) equal to the slope and solve.

questions.q: Find the value of y so that the line through (8, y) and (2, −1) has slope 3/2.
Find y so that the line through (−3, 4) and (5, y) has slope −3/4.
questions.hint: The run is 5 − (−3) = 8.

questions.q: Each row gives two points and the slope of the line through them. Find the missing y-value.
questions.hint: Multiply the slope by the change in x to get the change in y.

questions.q: Find the value of a so that the lines 3x + 4y = 12 and ax − 6y = 5 are perpendicular.
questions.hint: Find both slopes; their product must be −1.
questions.explanation: 3x + 4y = 12 has slope −3/4. ax − 6y = 5 gives y = (a/6)x − 5/6, slope a/6. (−3/4)(a/6) = −1 gives −3a = −24, so a = 8.

questions.q: Find the value of a so that the lines 2x − 5y = 10 and ax − 10y = 3 are parallel.
questions.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
questions.explanation: 2x − 5y = 10 has slope 2/5. ax − 10y = 3 has slope a/10. Setting a/10 = 2/5 gives a = 4.

questions.q: The lines x + 2y = 6 and 4x + ky = 1 are perpendicular.
questions.hint: The slope of 4x + ky = 1 is −4/k.
questions.explanation: x + 2y = 6 gives slope −1/2, so the other line needs slope 2. Its slope is −4/k, so −4/k = 2 and k = −2.

questions.q: Line d contains (2, 3) and (4, y) and is perpendicular to a line with slope 2/3. Find y.
questions.hint: Line d's slope is the negative reciprocal of 2/3.
questions.explanation: Line d has slope −3/2. So (y − 3) ÷ (4 − 2) = −3/2, which gives y − 3 = −3 and y = 0.

questions.q: Line d contains (−1, y) and (3, 5) and is perpendicular to a line with slope −2. Find y.
questions.hint: The negative reciprocal of −2 is 1/2.
questions.explanation: Line d has slope 1/2. So (5 − y) ÷ (3 − (−1)) = 1/2, giving 5 − y = 2 and y = 3.

questions.q: Line p contains (0, 1) and (3, y). Line k has slope 2/3.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: y if p is parallel to k:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: y if p is perpendicular to k:

questions.hint: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: negative reciprocal.
questions.explanation: Parallel: (y − 1) ÷ 3 = 2/3, so y − 1 = 2 and y = 3. Perpendicular: slope −3/2, so (y − 1) ÷ 3 = −3/2, y − 1 = −9/2 and y = −7/2.

questions.q: Given the relation {(4, 1), (−1, 3), (0, 1), (4, −2)}, state the domain (D) and range (R).
questions.hint: The domain is the set of first coordinates; the range is the set of second coordinates.
questions.explanation: The x-values are 4, −1, 0, 4, so D = {−1, 0, 4} (list 4 once). The y-values are 1, 3, 1, −2, so R = {−2, 1, 3}.

questions.q: For the relation {(2, 5), (−3, 5), (0, −1), (6, 2)}, write the domain and the range in set notation, in increasing order.
questions.hint: List each value once, from least to greatest.
questions.explanation: First coordinates: 2, −3, 0, 6, so the domain is {−3, 0, 2, 6}. Second coordinates: 5, 5, −1, 2, so the range is {−1, 2, 5}.

questions.q: Match each relation to its domain.
questions.hint: Only the first coordinate of each pair belongs to the domain.
questions.explanation: The first coordinates are 1, 3, 5 for the first relation, 2, 4, 6 for the second, and 1, 1, 5 for the third, which gives {1, 5}.

questions.q: A mapping diagram has inputs −1, 0, 3 and outputs 2, 4, 6, with arrows −1 → 2, 0 → 4, 0 → 6 and 3 → 2. Which is/are true?   I. The relation is a function.   II. Domain: {−1, 0, 3}.   III. Range: {2, 4, 6}.
questions.hint: Check whether any input has more than one arrow leaving it.
questions.explanation: Input 0 has two arrows (to 4 and to 6), so the relation is not a function and I is false. The inputs are −1, 0, 3, so II is true. Every output 2, 4, 6 receives an arrow, so III is true.

questions.q: A mapping diagram has inputs 1, 2, 3, 4 and the outputs column lists 0, 5, 8, 9. The arrows are 1 → 5, 2 → 8, 3 → 5 and 4 → 0. Write True or False for each statement.
questions.hint: The range contains only outputs that actually receive an arrow.
questions.explanation: Each input has exactly one arrow, so it is a function, and its domain is {1, 2, 3, 4}. No arrow reaches 9, so the range is {0, 5, 8}, not {0, 5, 8, 9}. Inputs 1 and 3 both map to 5, so it is not one-to-one.

questions.q: Which mapping represents a function?
questions.hint: A function cannot send one input to two different outputs.
questions.explanation: In 1 → 4, 2 → 4, 3 → 4 each input has exactly one output; sharing an output is allowed. Each other choice sends one input (1 or 3) to two different outputs.

questions.q: A mapping diagram has inputs −3, 0, 2, 5 and the outputs column lists 1, 4, 6, 8. The arrows are −3 → 1, 0 → 1, 2 → 4 and 5 → 6.
questions.hint: The range only includes outputs that receive an arrow.
questions.explanation: The domain is all inputs, {−3, 0, 2, 5}. Only 1, 4 and 6 receive arrows, so the range is {1, 4, 6}. Each input has exactly one arrow, so it is a function.

questions.q: A mapping diagram has arrows 1 → 2, 1 → 7, 4 → 3 and 6 → 7.
questions.hint: Look for an input with two arrows.
questions.explanation: The inputs are 1, 4, 6 and the outputs used are 2, 3, 7. Input 1 is paired with both 2 and 7, so the relation is not a function.

questions.q: Why is the relation {(2, 3), (4, 5), (2, 6)} not a function?
options: The range has more elements than the domain
The input 2 is paired with two different outputs
questions.hint: Check whether any x-value repeats with a different y-value.
questions.explanation: The pairs (2, 3) and (2, 6) give the input 2 two different outputs. A function must give each input exactly one output, so this relation is not a function.

questions.q: Classify each relation.
questions.hint: First check repeated inputs, then repeated outputs.
questions.explanation: In the first relation every input is different but 1 and 2 share the output 3, so it is a function but not one-to-one. The second has no repeated inputs or outputs, so it is one-to-one. The third pairs 0 with both 1 and −1, so it is not a function.

questions.q: Which of the following is a one-to-one function?
questions.hint: Use the horizontal line test (and the vertical line test).
questions.explanation: y = 2x + 1 is a slanted line, so every horizontal line meets it once: it is one-to-one. y = x² and y = |x| give the same output for x and −x, and x = y² is not a function since it fails the vertical line test.

questions.q: Match each graph to its description.
questions.hint: Vertical line test: is it a function? Horizontal line test: is it one-to-one?
questions.explanation: A slanted line passes both tests, so it is a one-to-one function. The parabola and the horizontal line pass the vertical line test but a horizontal line can meet them more than once, so they are not one-to-one. The circle fails the vertical line test, so it is not a function.

questions.q: Consider the function y = x² − 1.
questions.hint: Substitute both x-values.
questions.explanation: (−2)² − 1 = 3 and 2² − 1 = 3. Two different inputs give the same output, so the horizontal line y = 3 meets the graph twice and the function is not one-to-one.

questions.hint: A relation fails to be a function when one input is paired with more than one output.
questions.explanation: In I every x-value appears once (repeated y-values are allowed), so I is a function. In II the input −2 is paired with 1 and 5, so it is not a function. In III the vertical line x = 2 pairs the input 2 with every y-value, so it is not a function. The answer is II and III only.

questions.q: Decide whether each relation is a function. Type yes or no.
questions.hint: Look for any x-value that is paired with two different y-values.
questions.explanation: {(2, 5), (3, 5), (4, 5)} has different inputs, so it is a function. {(1, 2), (1, −2), (4, 4)} pairs x = 1 with two outputs, so it is not. y = 3x − 1 is a non-vertical line, so it is a function, but x = −4 is a vertical line, so it is not. In the last table x = 1 appears with y = 4 and y = 6, so it is not a function.

questions.q: The relation {(−1, 4), (2, 7), (5, 0), (2, 9)} is not a function. Which x-value causes this?
questions.hint: Find the input that appears in two ordered pairs.
questions.explanation: The input 2 is paired with both 7 and 9. One input with two outputs means the relation is not a function, so the x-value is 2.

questions.q:
Which relation is a function?
I: the graph of the line y = −x + 2
II: the graph of the circle x² + y² = 9
III: the mapping 1 → 2, 1 → 5, 3 → 7
questions.hint: Use the vertical line test for graphs and check each input of the mapping.
questions.explanation: A non-vertical line passes the vertical line test, so I is a function. A vertical line through the circle (for example x = 0) hits it twice, at y = 3 and y = −3, so II is not a function. In III the input 1 maps to both 2 and 5, so it is not a function. Only I is a function.

questions.q: Complete the table for each graph. Type yes or no.
questions.hint: A graph is a function exactly when every vertical line meets it at most once.
questions.explanation: Any vertical line meets y = 2x + 1, y = x² − 4 and y = 5 at most once, so they are functions. The vertical line x = −3 overlaps itself everywhere, and a vertical line through the circle meets it twice, so those two are not functions.

questions.q: The relation {(4, 1), (6, −2), (8, 1), (a, 5)} is a function. The value of a is one of 4, 6, 8 or 10. Which value must a be?
questions.hint: If a repeated an input already used, that input would have two outputs.
questions.explanation: The inputs 4, 6 and 8 already have the outputs 1, −2 and 1. If a were 4, 6 or 8, that input would also be paired with 5, giving two outputs. So a must be 10.

questions.q: A table shows the temperature of water as it is heated. Time (min): 0, 5, 10, 15. Temperature (°C): 18, 30, 42, 54. The relation is {(0, 18), (5, 30), (10, 42), (15, 54)}.
questions.hint: The domain is the set of inputs (times) and the range is the set of outputs (temperatures).
questions.explanation: Each time appears once, so each input has exactly one output and the relation is a function. The domain is the set of times {0, 5, 10, 15}. The range is the set of temperatures {18, 30, 42, 54}.

questions.q: What is the range of the relation {(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 3), (4, 7)}?
questions.hint: The range is the set of y-values, each listed once.
questions.explanation: The y-values are 3, 5, 3 and 7. Listing each value once gives the range {3, 5, 7}. The set {1, 2, 3, 4} is the domain.

questions.q: A table shows air pressure inside a balloon pump. Write each column of the table as an ordered pair (input, output) to form the relation.
questions.hint: Write the input first and the output second: (strokes, pressure).
questions.explanation: Each row gives one ordered pair with the number of strokes as x and the pressure as y. The relation is {(0, 100), (10, 104), (20, 108), (30, 112)}.

questions.q: Is the relation {(2, 9), (4, 9), (6, 11), (4, 13)} a function? Answer yes or no.
questions.hint: Check whether any input appears twice with different outputs.
questions.explanation: The input 4 is paired with both 9 and 13. Because one input has two outputs, the relation is not a function. (The repeated output 9 is not a problem.)

questions.q: Aisha buys notebooks that cost 4 AED each and she can spend at most 40 AED. Let x be the number of notebooks she buys. Which is the reasonable domain?
questions.hint: Think about what kind of number x can be and the most notebooks 40 AED buys.
questions.explanation: You cannot buy part of a notebook or a negative number of notebooks, so x is a whole number. 40 ÷ 4 = 10, so she can buy at most 10. The domain is the whole numbers from 0 to 10.

questions.q: Match each situation to the best description of its domain.

left: x = mass of fruit bought, in kg
x = number of seats filled in a 250-seat theatre
x = minutes played in a 90-minute football match

questions.hint: Decide if the input is counted (whole numbers) or measured (real numbers), then look for an upper limit.
questions.explanation: Buses are counted with no upper limit given, so whole numbers x ≥ 0. Mass is measured, so any real number x ≥ 0. Seats are counted and cannot exceed 250. Minutes are measured from 0 up to 90.

questions.q: Every day Omar runs between 3 and 8 km, inclusive. He records the distance he runs, x (km), and the time it takes. Identify the constraint on the domain.
questions.hint: The domain is the set of distances Omar can actually run.
questions.explanation: Omar runs at least 3 km and at most 8 km each day, so the domain is 3 ≤ x ≤ 8. A distance can never be negative.

questions.q: A car park is open at most 14 hours a day. Let x be the number of hours a car is parked in one day. Write the domain constraint as an inequality.
questions.hint: Time parked cannot be negative and cannot exceed the opening hours.
questions.explanation: The time parked cannot be less than 0 hours and cannot be more than the 14 hours the car park is open. So the domain is 0 ≤ x ≤ 14.

questions.q:
Determine whether the function is linear. If it is, state the rate of change.
x: 1, 3, 5, 7
y: 10, 4, −2, −8
questions.hint: Find the change in y and the change in x between consecutive columns.
questions.explanation: Each time x increases by 2, y changes by −6 (10 to 4, 4 to −2, −2 to −8). The rate is constant, so the function is linear. Rate of change = −6 ÷ 2 = −3.

questions.q: For each table, decide whether the function is linear. If it is, give the rate of change; otherwise type none.
questions.hint: A table is linear when equal steps in x always give equal steps in y.
questions.explanation: In the first table y rises by 3 each time x rises by 1, so the rate is 3. In the third table y falls by 1 each time x rises by 2, so the rate is −1/2. The second table has differences 1, 2, 4 and the fourth has 3, 5, 7, so neither is linear.

questions.q:
The function is linear. Find its rate of change. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
x: 6, 3, 0, −3
y: −2, 0, 2, 4
questions.hint: Divide the change in y by the change in x between two columns.
questions.explanation: From x = 6 to x = 3, x changes by −3 while y changes from −2 to 0, a change of +2. The rate of change is 2 ÷ (−3) = −2/3, and it is the same for every pair of columns.

questions.q:
Determine whether the function is linear. If it is, state the rate of change.
x: 0, 2, 4, 6
y: 3, 7, 11, 17
questions.hint: Check the y-differences all the way to the last column.
questions.explanation: x increases by 2 each time. The y-differences are 4, 4 and 6. Because the last difference is different, the rate of change is not constant, so the function is not linear.

questions.q:
Which linear function fits the data?
x: 1, 2, 3, 4
y: 2, 5, 8, 11
questions.hint: Find the slope from the table, then use one point to find the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: y increases by 3 each time x increases by 1, so m = 3. Using (1, 2): 2 = 3(1) + b, so b = −1. The function is y = 3x − 1; check: x = 4 gives 12 − 1 = 11.

questions.q:
Write a linear function for the data in slope-intercept form.
x: 0, 2, 4, 6
y: 7, 3, −1, −5
questions.hint: The y-value at x = 0 is the y-intercept.
questions.explanation: The slope is (3 − 7) ÷ (2 − 0) = −4 ÷ 2 = −2. When x = 0, y = 7, so b = 7. The function is y = −2x + 7.

questions.q: The table shows a linear function: x: −2, 0, 2 and y: −3, −2, −1. Graph the line.
questions.hint: Plot two of the points from the table and draw the line through them.
questions.explanation: The points (−2, −3), (0, −2) and (2, −1) all lie on one line with slope 1/2 and y-intercept −2. Plotting (0, −2) and (2, −1) gives the line y = ½x − 2.

questions.q: The table shows a linear function. Complete the missing values.
questions.hint: Find how much y changes each time x increases by 1.
questions.explanation: y decreases by 3 each time x increases by 1, so the rule is y = −3x + 7. Then y(3) = −2, y(5) = −8 and y(0) = 7.

questions.q: Given f(x) = 4(x − 2) + 7, evaluate f(6).
questions.hint: Substitute 6 for x, then work inside the parentheses first.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = −2(x + 3) + 5.
questions.hint: Add 3 to x, multiply by −2, then add 5.

questions.q: Given g(x) = 5 − 3(x − 1), evaluate g(−2).
questions.hint: Be careful with the signs: −3 times a negative number is positive.

questions.q: For f(x) = 2(x − 1) − 3, match each expression to its value.
questions.hint: Substitute each input and simplify the parentheses first.

questions.q:
A student claimed that the rule for the data is y = 4x + 4.
x: 1, 2, 3, 4
y: 4, 8, 12, 16
Which statement is true?
options: The claim is incorrect; the rule is y = x + 4.
The claim is incorrect; the rule is y = 4x − 4.
The claim is correct; every point fits.
The claim is incorrect; the rule is y = 4x.
questions.hint: Test the claimed rule with x = 1.
questions.explanation: With x = 1 the rule y = 4x + 4 gives 8, but the table shows 4, so the claim is incorrect. Each y-value is 4 times x (4, 8, 12, 16), so the correct rule is y = 4x.

questions.q:
A student claims the rule for this data is y = 3x.
x: 1, 2, 3, 4
y: 3, 5, 7, 9
The claim is wrong. Write the correct rule.
questions.hint: Find how much y changes each time x increases by 1.
questions.explanation: The rule y = 3x gives 6 at x = 2, but the table shows 5, so it is wrong. y increases by 2 each time, so m = 2, and 3 = 2(1) + b gives b = 1. The correct rule is y = 2x + 1.

questions.q:
A student claims the rule for the data below is y = 6x − 2.
x: 0, 1, 2, 3
y: −2, 4, 10, 16

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Value the rule gives at x = 2:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Does the rule match every point? (yes/no)

questions.hint: Substitute each x-value into the rule and compare with the table.
questions.explanation: y = 6x − 2 gives −2, 4, 10 and 16 for x = 0, 1, 2, 3. These match every value in the table, so the claim is correct.

questions.q: A student claims the rule y = 3x + 2 fits the data. Complete the table to test the claim (type yes or no in the last column).
questions.hint: Work out 3x + 2 for each x.
questions.explanation: The rule gives 5, 8, 11 and 14. At x = 3 the table shows 10 instead of 11, so the rule does not fit all the data and the claim is incorrect.

questions.q: A taxi fare in AED is f(d) = 1.8d + 12, where d is the distance in km.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Distance in km if the fare is 39 AED:

questions.hint: The slope is the coefficient of d; the y-intercept is the cost when d = 0.
questions.explanation: The slope 1.8 means each km adds 1.8 AED. The y-intercept 12 is the fixed starting fare when d = 0. Solving 1.8d + 12 = 39 gives 1.8d = 27, so d = 15 km.

questions.q: A plumber charges C(h) = 45h + 60 AED for h hours of work. What does 60 represent?
options: a fixed call-out fee of 60 AED
questions.hint: The constant term is the cost when h = 0.
questions.explanation: When h = 0, C(0) = 60, so 60 AED is charged even before any work is done. That is a fixed call-out fee. The 45 is the cost per hour.

questions.q: A gym charges M(m) = 150m + 200 AED for m months, which includes a joining fee. Salem paid 1100 AED in total. For how many months did he join?
questions.hint: Set the expression equal to 1100 and solve for m.
questions.explanation: 150m + 200 = 1100, so 150m = 900 and m = 6. Salem joined for 6 months.

questions.q: The water in a tank is W(t) = 500 − 25t litres after t minutes. Match each item to its meaning or value.
questions.hint: The slope is a rate; the constant is the value when t = 0.
questions.explanation: The slope −25 means 25 L drains every minute, and 500 L is the starting amount. W(4) = 500 − 100 = 400 L. Setting 500 − 25t = 0 gives t = 20 minutes.

questions.q: A graph shows only these five points: (−2, −3), (−1, −1), (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5).
questions.hint: List the x-values for the domain and the y-values for the range.
questions.explanation: Each time x increases by 1, y increases by 2, so the points lie on the line y = 2x + 1 and the function is linear. Since only five points are shown, the domain is {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} and the range is {−3, −1, 1, 3, 5}.

questions.q: Which set of points lies on a linear function?
questions.hint: Check whether y changes by the same amount every time x increases by 1.
questions.explanation: In the first set y increases by 2 every time, so the points lie on y = 2x + 1. The other sets have changing differences (1, 2, 4), (1, 3, 5) and (−1, −2, −3), so they are not linear.

questions.q: The function y = −x + 2 has domain {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2}. Plot its graph (points only).
questions.hint: Substitute each x in the domain to get its y-value.
questions.explanation: y(−2) = 4, y(−1) = 3, y(0) = 2, y(1) = 1 and y(2) = 0. Because the domain has only five values, the graph is the five separate points, not a full line.

questions.q: A graph of a function shows only the points (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) and (4, 8). Write the range as a set.
questions.hint: The range is the set of y-values.
questions.explanation: The y-values of the plotted points are 2, 4, 6 and 8, so the range is {2, 4, 6, 8}.

questions.q: Determine whether each sequence is arithmetic. If it is, give d; otherwise type none.
questions.hint: Subtract each term from the next; the sequence is arithmetic only if all differences are equal.
questions.explanation: 3, 10, 17, 24 has d = 7; 50, 44, 38, 32 has d = −6; −7, −4.5, −2, 0.5 has d = 2.5. The sequence 2, 6, 18, 54 has differences 4, 12, 36 and 1, 4, 9, 16 has differences 3, 5, 7, so neither is arithmetic.

questions.q: Which sequence is arithmetic?
questions.hint: Look for a constant difference between consecutive terms.
questions.explanation: 12, 7, 2, −3 has differences −5, −5, −5, so it is arithmetic with d = −5. The others have differences 4, 5, 6 / 4, 8, 16 / −2, 2, −2, which are not constant.

questions.q: Find the common difference of the arithmetic sequence 2.4, 1.8, 1.2, 0.6, ...
questions.hint: Subtract the first term from the second term.
questions.explanation: 1.8 − 2.4 = −0.6, and every later difference is also −0.6. So d = −0.6.

questions.q: Match each arithmetic sequence to its common difference.
questions.hint: d = (second term) − (first term).

questions.q: Write a recursive formula for the explicit formula aₙ = 8 + 3n.
questions.hint: Find a₁ by substituting n = 1; the coefficient of n is d.
questions.explanation: a₁ = 8 + 3(1) = 11. The coefficient of n is 3, so each term is 3 more than the one before. The recursive formula is a₁ = 11, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 3.

questions.q: The explicit formula of an arithmetic sequence is aₙ = 20 − 4n.
questions.hint: Substitute n = 1 and n = 2; d is the coefficient of n.
questions.explanation: a₁ = 20 − 4 = 16 and a₂ = 20 − 8 = 12. The coefficient of n is −4, so d = −4 and the recursive formula is a₁ = 16, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ − 4.

questions.q: For the explicit formula aₙ = 7n − 2, the first term is a₁ = 5. Complete the recursive rule: aₙ = ____ (for n ≥ 2).
questions.hint: Each term is the previous term plus the common difference.
questions.explanation: The coefficient of n in 7n − 2 is 7, so d = 7. The recursive formula is a₁ = 5, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 7.

questions.q: Match each explicit formula to its recursive formula.
questions.hint: Get a₁ by putting n = 1, and d from the coefficient of n.

questions.q: Write the explicit formula for the arithmetic sequence −6, −1, 4, 9, ...
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Write the explicit formula for the arithmetic sequence 30, 26, 22, 18, ...
questions.hint: Find d first, then simplify a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Consider the arithmetic sequence 3, 11, 19, 27, ...
questions.hint: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d, then substitute n = 10.

questions.q: Plot the first four terms of the arithmetic sequence aₙ = 2n − 3 as points (n, aₙ).
questions.hint: Substitute n = 1, 2, 3 and 4.
questions.explanation: a₁ = −1, a₂ = 1, a₃ = 3 and a₄ = 5, so plot (1, −1), (2, 1), (3, 3) and (4, 5). The points lie on a line because an arithmetic sequence is a linear function of n.

questions.q: What are the first four terms of the sequence defined by a₁ = −2, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ − 4 for n > 1?
questions.hint: Start at a₁ and subtract 4 each time.

questions.q: A sequence is defined by a₁ = 7, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 6 for n > 1. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Each term is the previous term plus 6.

questions.q: A sequence is defined by a₁ = 40, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ − 7 for n > 1. Find a₅.
questions.hint: Subtract 7 four times from a₁.
questions.explanation: The terms are 40, 33, 26, 19, 12, so a₅ = 12.

questions.q: A sequence is defined by a₁ = 1, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 2 for n > 1. Plot the first four terms as points (n, aₙ).
questions.hint: Find each term by adding 2 to the previous one.
questions.explanation: The terms are 1, 3, 5, 7, so the points are (1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 5) and (4, 7). They rise by 2 for each step of 1 in n.

questions.q: Write the explicit formula for the arithmetic sequence 4, 10, 16, 22, ...
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d and simplify.

questions.q: Write the explicit formula for the arithmetic sequence −8, −3, 2, 7, ...
questions.hint: Find d, then simplify a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: Consider the arithmetic sequence 15, 12, 9, 6, ...
questions.hint: d is negative because the terms decrease.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has explicit formula aₙ = 3n + 4. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Substitute n for the missing aₙ; for the last row solve 3n + 4 = 34.
questions.explanation: a₁ = 7, a₂ = 10 and a₅ = 19. For aₙ = 34, 3n + 4 = 34 gives 3n = 30, so n = 10.

questions.q: Given a₁ = 2.5 and d = −1.5 for an arithmetic sequence, find the recursive formula and the next four terms.
questions.hint: Each term equals the previous term plus d.
questions.explanation: The recursive formula is a₁ = 2.5, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ − 1.5. Subtracting 1.5 repeatedly gives 1, −0.5, −2 and −3.5.

questions.q: Given a₁ = −4.6 and d = 1.2, what are the next four terms of the arithmetic sequence?
questions.hint: Add 1.2 to each term to get the next one.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 0.75 and d = 0.5. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Use aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 0.5.
questions.explanation: The recursive formula is a₁ = 0.75, aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 0.5. Adding 0.5 each time gives 1.25, 1.75, 2.25 and 2.75.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = −3.2 and d = 0.8. Find a₄.
questions.hint: a₄ is three steps of d after a₁.

questions.q: Given a₁ = 12 and d = −5, find the equation of the nth term and the next four terms.
questions.hint: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d and simplify.
questions.explanation: aₙ = 12 + (n − 1)(−5) = 12 − 5n + 5 = 17 − 5n. Subtracting 5 each time from 12 gives 7, 2, −3, −8.

questions.q: Given a₁ = −6 and d = 4, which is the equation of the nth term?
questions.hint: Substitute into aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 50 and d = −15. Find a₆.
questions.hint: a₆ = a₁ + 5d.

questions.q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 6 and d = −2. Plot its first four terms as points (n, aₙ).
questions.hint: Start at 6 and subtract 2 each time.
In a positive association, y tends to increase as x increases.
questions.explanation: In B the y-values rise from 2 to 6 as x goes from 1 to 5, so it shows a positive association. A falls (negative), C jumps up and down (no association) and D stays constant.

questions.q: Match each pair of quantities to the association you would expect.

left: age of a car and its resale value

questions.hint: Ask: as the first quantity grows, does the second tend to rise, fall, or neither?
questions.explanation: More study time tends to give higher scores (positive). Older cars tend to be worth less (negative). Shoe size has nothing to do with exam scores (no association).

questions.q: Each data set uses x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Describe the association as positive, negative or none.
questions.hint: Look at the overall trend of y as x increases.
questions.explanation: 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 rises steadily, so it is positive. 9, 8, 6, 5, 2 falls, so it is negative. 4, 9, 2, 8, 5 goes up and down with no trend, so there is no association.

questions.q: Make a scatter plot of the data: (1, 9), (2, 8), (4, 6), (5, 5), (7, 2).
questions.hint: Each ordered pair is one point.
questions.explanation: Plot all five points. They fall from left to right in a roughly straight pattern.

questions.q: The data (1, 9), (2, 8), (4, 6), (5, 5), (7, 2) are shown in a scatter plot. What type of association does it show?
questions.hint: Decide whether y goes up or down as x increases, and whether the points are close to a line.
questions.explanation: As x increases, y decreases from 9 to 2. The points lie close to a straight line, so the association is negative and linear.

questions.q: Make a scatter plot of the data: (0, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (5, 6), (6, 8), (8, 9).
questions.hint: Plot x across and y up for each pair.
questions.explanation: Plot all six points. They rise from left to right in a roughly straight band.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows the data (0, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (5, 6), (6, 8), (8, 9). Describe the association.
questions.hint: Check the trend and whether the points lie close to a line.
questions.explanation: As x increases, y increases from 2 to 9, so the association is positive. The points are close to a straight line, so it is linear.

questions.q: Match each scatter plot description to its correlation.

left: Plot P: as x increases from 1 to 8, y falls from about 20 to about 4.
Plot Q: points scattered between y = 5 and y = 15 with no pattern.
Plot R: as x increases, y rises steadily from about 2 to about 18.

questions.hint: Rising points mean positive, falling points mean negative.
questions.explanation: Plot P falls as x increases, so it has a negative correlation. Plot Q has no trend, so there is no correlation. Plot R rises as x increases, so it has a positive correlation.
