questions.q: Which pair of quantities would most likely show a negative correlation?
options: hours of exercise per week and resting heart rate
questions.hint: Negative correlation: as one quantity increases, the other tends to decrease.
questions.explanation: People who exercise more tend to have lower resting heart rates, so that is a negative correlation. Height and arm span, and hours worked and pay, rise together (positive). Birth month and test score are unrelated (no correlation).

questions.q: Data: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 with y = 30, 26, 25, 20, 18, 14. Does the scatter plot show a positive, negative, or no correlation? Type one word: positive, negative or none.
questions.hint: Check whether y tends to rise or fall as x increases.
questions.explanation: As x increases from 1 to 6, y falls from 30 to 14. So the data show a negative correlation.

questions.q: The data points are (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 5), (5, 7). Which line is the best line of fit?
questions.hint: A line of best fit follows the trend with points balanced above and below it.
questions.explanation: y = 1.2x + 0.8 gives 2, 3.2, 4.4, 5.6, 6.8, which are very close to the data with points on both sides. y = 3 is flat although the data rise, y = −x + 8 falls, and y = 2x + 4 lies above every point.

questions.q: For each description, decide if the line drawn is the line of best fit. Type 'best fit' or 'not'.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Plot A: an increasing line through the middle of rising data, with about half the points above and half below.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Plot B: an increasing line drawn below all the points.
answer: not the line of best fit

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Plot C: a decreasing line drawn through data that rise from left to right.
answer: not the line of best fit

questions.hint: The best line follows the direction of the data and splits the points evenly.
questions.explanation: In A the line follows the upward trend with points balanced on both sides, so it is the line of best fit. In B all points are above the line. In C the line goes the wrong direction, so neither B nor C is the best fit.

questions.q: A scatter plot shows data that fall from left to right. Must the slope of its line of best fit be positive or negative? Type positive or negative.
questions.hint: The line of best fit follows the direction of the data.
questions.explanation: When the data fall from left to right, y decreases as x increases. A line that follows this trend must have a negative slope.

questions.q: The data points are (1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 5), (5, 4), (6, 6). Line A is y = x and Line B is y = x + 3. Which represents the better line of fit?
options: Neither, the data have no correlation
questions.hint: Compare how many points lie above and below each line.
questions.explanation: Line A gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: two points are on it, two above and two below, so it is balanced. Line B gives 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, which is above every point. Line A is the better fit.

questions.q: The data points are (0, 10), (2, 8), (4, 7), (6, 4), (8, 2). Line P is y = −x + 10 and Line Q is y = −0.5x + 6. Which is the better line of fit? Type P or Q.
questions.hint: Find how far each point is from each line.
questions.explanation: Line P gives 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, which matches four points exactly and is 1 away from the other. Line Q gives 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, which is below almost every point by up to 4. Line P fits better.

questions.q: Test the line y = 2x + 1 against the data. Complete the predicted value and the residual (actual − predicted).
questions.hint: Predicted y = 2x + 1; residual = actual y − predicted y.
questions.explanation: The predictions are 3, 5, 7 and 9. The residuals are 0, 1, −1 and 0. They are small and balanced around 0, which shows the line is a good fit.

questions.q: The number of mobile phone users (millions) in a country from 2010 to 2017 was 4.1, 4.6, 5.0, 5.7, 6.1, 6.8, 7.2, 7.9. Complete the statements.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The scatter plot shows (a positive / a negative / no) correlation:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The number of users was generally (increasing / decreasing / staying the same):

questions.hint: Look at how the values change as the years increase.
questions.explanation: The number of users rises every year from 4.1 to 7.9 million. As the year increases, the number increases, so there is a positive correlation.

questions.q: The price (AED) of a TV model was 4000 in 2015, 3400 in 2016, 2900 in 2017, 2500 in 2018 and 2100 in 2019. Which statement describes the scatter plot of year against price?
options: a negative correlation; the price was generally decreasing
a negative correlation; the price was generally increasing
a positive correlation; the price was generally increasing
no correlation; the price stayed the same
questions.hint: As the year increases, does the price go up or down?
questions.explanation: The price falls every year from 4000 to 2100 AED. When one quantity increases and the other decreases, the correlation is negative.

questions.q: Visitors to a beach each year from 2018 to 2023 were 52, 52, 51, 53, 52, 52 thousand. Was the number of visitors generally increasing, decreasing, or staying the same?
questions.hint: Compare the first and last values and look for a trend.
questions.explanation: The values stay close to 52 thousand with tiny ups and downs and no trend. So the number of visitors was staying about the same (no correlation).

questions.q: A line of best fit passes through (2002, 120) and (2010, 80). Let x be the number of years since 2000 and y the number of items (thousands).
questions.hint: Convert the years to x-values first: 2002 gives x = 2.
questions.explanation: The points are (2, 120) and (10, 80), so the slope is −40 ÷ 8 = −5. 120 = −5(2) + b gives b = 130, so y = −5x + 130. Setting −5x + 130 = 55 gives x = 15, which is the year 2015.

questions.q: A line of best fit passes through (2005, 30) and (2015, 50). Let x be the number of years since 2000. Which is the equation of the line?
questions.hint: Write the points as (5, 30) and (15, 50).
questions.explanation: The slope is (50 − 30) ÷ (15 − 5) = 2. Using (5, 30): 30 = 2(5) + b, so b = 20. The equation is y = 2x + 20.

questions.q: A line of best fit is y = −0.5x + 60, where x is years since 2010 and y is sales in thousands. Predict the year when sales will be 48 thousand.
questions.hint: Solve for x, then add it to 2010.

questions.q: A line of best fit is y = 1.5x + 12, where x is the number of years since 2015. Complete the table.
questions.hint: x = year − 2015.
questions.explanation: 2015 gives x = 0 and y = 12. 2019 gives x = 4 and y = 1.5(4) + 12 = 18. For y = 27, 1.5x = 15 so x = 10, which is the year 2025.

questions.q: A line of best fit for hours of study (x) and test score in % (y) passes through (4, 60) and (16, 84).
questions.hint: Find the slope from the two points, then the y-intercept.

questions.q: A line of best fit passes through (2, 50) and (12, 75), where x is hours of practice and y is a score. Predict the score for 8 hours of practice.
questions.hint: Find the slope, then the equation, then substitute x = 8.

questions.q: A line of best fit passes through (5, 40) and (20, 70). Use it to predict y when x = 14.
questions.hint: Find the slope and the y-intercept first.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal. Match each given fact to the theorem that proves the lines are parallel.

right: Converse of Alternate Exterior Angles Theorem
Converse of Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem
Converse of Alternate Interior Angles Theorem

questions.hint: Each converse uses the same angle pair as its original theorem.
questions.explanation: Congruent corresponding angles use the Converse of the Corresponding Angles Postulate. Congruent alternate interior or alternate exterior angles use the matching converse theorems. Supplementary consecutive interior angles use the Converse of the Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem. Vertical angles say nothing about parallel lines.

questions.q: Lines p and q are cut by transversal t. ∠1 is at the intersection of t and p, above p and to the right of t. ∠5 is at the intersection of t and q, above q and to the right of t. Which statement must always be true?
options: If m∠1 + m∠5 = 180°, then p ∥ q
If p ∥ q, then m∠1 + m∠5 = 90°
questions.hint: ∠1 and ∠5 are in the same position at the two intersections.
questions.explanation: ∠1 and ∠5 are corresponding angles for lines p and q with transversal t. By the Converse of the Corresponding Angles Postulate, if they are congruent then p ∥ q. The transversal t cannot be parallel to p, since it crosses p.

questions.q: Lines a and b are cut by transversal c. ∠3 is at line a, between a and b, on the left of c. ∠6 is at line b, between a and b, on the right of c. Which statement must always be true?
options: If m∠3 + m∠6 = 180°, then a ∥ b
questions.hint: Angles between the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal are alternate interior angles.
questions.explanation: ∠3 and ∠6 are alternate interior angles for lines a and b. By the Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem, if they are congruent then a ∥ b. Supplementary alternate interior angles do not prove the lines parallel unless both are 90°.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles measure (5x − 12)° and (3x + 20)°. For what value of x are the lines parallel?
questions.hint: For parallel lines, corresponding angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: Set 5x − 12 = 3x + 20. Then 2x = 32, so x = 16. Each angle is 68°.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of consecutive (same-side) interior angles measure (4x + 15)° and (2x + 45)°. For what value of x are the lines parallel?
questions.hint: For parallel lines, consecutive interior angles are supplementary.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate interior angles measure (6x − 8)° and (4x + 22)°. The lines are parallel.
questions.hint: Alternate interior angles are congruent when the lines are parallel.
questions.explanation: 6x − 8 = 4x + 22 gives 2x = 30, so x = 15. Each angle is 6(15) − 8 = 82°.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate exterior angles measure (9x − 20)° and (5x + 36)°. For what value of x are the lines parallel?
questions.hint: Alternate exterior angles are congruent for parallel lines.
questions.explanation: 9x − 20 = 5x + 36 gives 4x = 56, so x = 14. Each angle is 106°.

questions.q: Two parallel vertical lines are cut by a transversal that slopes down to the right. At the left line the four angles are ∠1 (top-left), ∠3 (top-right), ∠2 (bottom-left) and ∠4 (bottom-right). At the right line they are ∠5 (top-left), ∠7 (top-right), ∠6 (bottom-left) and ∠8 (bottom-right). If m∠2 = 65°, which gives m∠7 with the correct reason?
questions.hint: ∠2 and ∠7 are both outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.
questions.explanation: ∠2 is outside the left line and ∠7 is outside the right line, on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate exterior angles. For parallel lines these are congruent, so m∠7 = 65°.

questions.q: Two parallel vertical lines are cut by a transversal that slopes down to the right. At the left line the four angles are ∠1 (top-left), ∠3 (top-right), ∠2 (bottom-left) and ∠4 (bottom-right). At the right line they are ∠5 (top-left), ∠7 (top-right), ∠6 (bottom-left) and ∠8 (bottom-right). Match each angle pair to its relationship.
questions.hint: Interior angles lie between the parallel lines; corresponding angles are in the same position at each line.
questions.explanation: ∠4 and ∠5 are between the lines on opposite sides of the transversal (alternate interior). ∠4 and ∠8 are both bottom-right (corresponding). ∠4 and ∠6 are between the lines on the same side, below the transversal (consecutive interior). ∠4 and ∠1 are opposite each other at one intersection (vertical).

questions.q: Two parallel vertical lines are cut by a transversal that slopes down to the right. At the left line the four angles are ∠1 (top-left), ∠3 (top-right), ∠2 (bottom-left) and ∠4 (bottom-right). At the right line they are ∠5 (top-left), ∠7 (top-right), ∠6 (bottom-left) and ∠8 (bottom-right). If m∠3 = 120°, complete the table.
questions.hint: Angles forming a linear pair add to 180°; corresponding and vertical angles are equal.
questions.explanation: ∠1 and ∠4 each form a linear pair with ∠3, so they are 60°. ∠3 and ∠2 are vertical (120°), and ∠6 corresponds to ∠2, so ∠6 = 120°. ∠8 corresponds to ∠4, so ∠8 = 60°.

questions.q: A straight curb is crossed by parallel parking-space lines. At line 1, ∠1 is the angle on the left side between the curb and the line. At line 2, ∠2 is the angle on the right side between the curb and the line, and m∠2 = 125°. What is m∠1?
questions.hint: The left angle at line 2 corresponds to ∠1 and forms a linear pair with ∠2.
questions.explanation: At line 2 the left angle and ∠2 form a linear pair, so the left angle is 180° − 125° = 55°. Because the parking lines are parallel, ∠1 corresponds to that angle, so m∠1 = 55°.

questions.q: Two parallel streets are crossed by a straight avenue. One angle at the first intersection, between the streets, measures 48°. What is the measure of the consecutive interior angle at the second intersection on the same side of the avenue? Give the answer in degrees.
questions.hint: Consecutive interior angles of parallel lines are supplementary.
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles add to 180°. So the angle is 180° − 48° = 132°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal and one of the angles measures 72°. Find the measure of each related angle.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The angle forming a linear pair with it (°):

questions.hint: Congruent pairs are equal; supplementary pairs add to 180°.
questions.explanation: Corresponding and vertical angles are congruent, so they are 72°. Consecutive interior angles and linear pairs are supplementary, so they are 180° − 72° = 108°.

questions.q: In a triangle, an exterior angle measures 130°. One of the two remote interior angles measures 48°. Find the other remote interior angle x.
questions.hint: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
questions.explanation: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, 130 = 48 + x, so x = 82°. (50° is the interior angle next to the exterior angle, not a remote one.)

questions.q: In a triangle, an exterior angle measures (5x + 10)° and the two remote interior angles measure 40° and (3x + 20)°. Find x.
questions.hint: Set the exterior angle equal to the sum of the remote interior angles.
questions.explanation: 5x + 10 = 40 + 3x + 20, so 5x + 10 = 3x + 60. Then 2x = 50 and x = 25. Check: exterior angle = 135° = 40° + 95°.

questions.q: In triangle ABC the exterior angle at C is formed by extending a side. Complete the table using the Exterior Angle Theorem.
questions.hint: Exterior angle at C = m∠A + m∠B.

questions.q: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles of an exterior angle measure 70° and 45°.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Interior angle adjacent to the exterior angle (°):

questions.hint: The exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles; it forms a linear pair with the adjacent interior angle.
questions.explanation: The exterior angle is 70° + 45° = 115°. The adjacent interior angle is 180° − 115° = 65°, and 70 + 45 + 65 = 180 checks.

questions.q: Three lines intersect to form triangle PQR. At vertex P, the angle outside the triangle that forms a linear pair with interior ∠P measures 130°. At vertex Q, the angle vertical to interior ∠Q measures 45°. Find the measure of interior ∠R in degrees.
questions.hint: Turn each given angle into an interior angle first, then use the triangle angle sum.
questions.explanation: Interior ∠P = 180° − 130° = 50° (linear pair). Interior ∠Q = 45° (vertical angles are congruent). So ∠R = 180° − 50° − 45° = 85°.

questions.q: Three lines intersect to form triangle ABC. The angle forming a linear pair with interior ∠A is 140°, and the angle vertical to interior ∠B is 65°. At vertex C, angle x lies outside the triangle and forms a linear pair with interior ∠C. What is x?
questions.hint: x is an exterior angle of the triangle, so it equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
questions.explanation: Interior ∠A = 180° − 140° = 40° and interior ∠B = 65° (vertical angles). The exterior angle at C equals the sum of the remote interior angles: x = 40° + 65° = 105°. (75° is the interior angle at C, not x.)

questions.q: Three lines intersect to form triangle ABC. Complete the table of angle measures (in degrees).

rows: Angle forming a linear pair with interior ∠A
Exterior angle at C (linear pair with ∠C)

questions.hint: Linear pairs add to 180°, vertical angles are equal, and the three interior angles add to 180°.
questions.explanation: ∠A = 180 − 118 = 62. ∠B = 71 (vertical angles). ∠C = 180 − 62 − 71 = 47. The exterior angle at C is 180 − 47 = 133, which also equals 62 + 71.

questions.q: Lines m and n are parallel. A transversal meets m at P and n at Q. At Q, the angle between the ray of n pointing left and segment QP measures 118°. At P, find the angle between the ray of m pointing left and segment PQ (in degrees).
questions.hint: Find the angle on the other side of the transversal at Q first; then look for alternate interior angles.
questions.explanation: At Q, the angle between n's right ray and QP is 180° − 118° = 62° (linear pair). The angle at P between m's left ray and PQ is alternate interior to it, so it is also 62°.

questions.q: Lines m ∥ n, with m above n. Point P is on m; points Q and R are on n, with R to the right of Q, forming triangle PQR. At Q, the angle outside the triangle between n's left ray and QP is 128°. At P, the angle between m's right ray and PR is 48°. Find each angle in degrees.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Angle between m's left ray and PQ =

questions.hint: Use a linear pair at Q, alternate interior angles for each segment, and the triangle angle sum.
questions.explanation: ∠PQR = 180° − 128° = 52°. ∠PRQ is alternate interior to the 48° angle, so it is 48°. ∠QPR = 180° − 52° − 48° = 80°. The angle between m's left ray and PQ is alternate interior to ∠PQR, so it is 52° (check: 52 + 80 + 48 = 180 along line m).

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Angle b lies below the upper line on the left side of the transversal. Angle c lies above the lower line on the right side of the transversal. How are b and c related?
options: Alternate interior angles, so b = c
Same-side interior angles, so b + c = 180°
questions.hint: Both angles are between the parallel lines, and they are on opposite sides of the transversal.
questions.explanation: Angles between the two parallel lines are interior angles. Since b and c are on opposite sides of the transversal, they are alternate interior angles, which are congruent when the lines are parallel.

questions.q: Lines a ∥ b are cut by transversal t, and ∠2 and ∠6 are same-side interior angles. Another angle, ∠9, is congruent to ∠6. Which statement is always true?
questions.hint: First write what is true about ∠2 and ∠6, then replace ∠6 by ∠9.
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines are supplementary, so m∠2 + m∠6 = 180°. Since ∠9 ≅ ∠6, m∠2 + m∠9 = 180°, so ∠2 and ∠9 are supplementary.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal, but you are NOT told whether the lines are parallel. Match each angle pair to the statement that describes it.

right: congruent only if the lines are parallel
supplementary only if the lines are parallel

questions.hint: Vertical angles and linear pairs do not depend on parallel lines; the transversal-angle pairs do.
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are always congruent and a linear pair always adds to 180°. Corresponding and alternate exterior angles are congruent only when the lines are parallel, and same-side interior angles are supplementary only when the lines are parallel.

questions.q: Lines a ∥ b are cut by transversal t. ∠3 and ∠5 are same-side interior angles. If ∠5 ≅ ∠8 and m∠3 = 113°, find m∠8 in degrees.
questions.hint: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines add to 180°.
questions.explanation: m∠5 = 180° − 113° = 67° because ∠3 and ∠5 are same-side interior angles. Since ∠8 ≅ ∠5, m∠8 = 67°.

questions.q: Lines a and b are cut by transversal t. ∠2 and ∠6 are same-side interior angles and m∠2 + m∠6 = 180°. What can you conclude?
questions.hint: Think about the converse of the Same-Side Interior Angles Theorem.
questions.explanation: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that same-side interior angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel. So a ∥ b. Nothing says the angles are 90°, so the other choices do not follow.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate interior angles measure (x + 97)° and 154°. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Alternate interior angles of parallel lines are congruent.
questions.explanation: Set the angles equal: x + 97 = 154. Subtract 97 to get x = 57.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles measure (17x − 8)° and (15x + 6)°. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Corresponding angles of parallel lines are congruent.
questions.explanation: 17x − 8 = 15x + 6, so 2x = 14 and x = 7. Check: both angles are 111°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of same-side interior angles measure (3x + 10)° and (5x − 30)°. Find x and both angle measures.
questions.hint: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines are supplementary.

questions.q: Each row describes an angle pair formed by two parallel lines and a transversal. Find x.
questions.hint: Congruent pairs: set the expressions equal. Same-side interior: set the sum equal to 180.

questions.q: Lines l and m are cut by transversal t. ∠2 (at l) and ∠6 (at m) are corresponding angles, and ∠1 forms a linear pair with ∠2. If m∠1 = (2x + 40)° and m∠6 = (4x + 20)°, for what value of x is l ∥ m?
questions.hint: Write m∠2 in terms of x using the linear pair, then set it equal to m∠6.
questions.explanation: m∠2 = 180 − (2x + 40) = 140 − 2x. For l ∥ m, corresponding angles must be congruent: 140 − 2x = 4x + 20, so 6x = 120 and x = 20. Check: ∠2 = ∠6 = 100°.

questions.q: Three lines intersect to form triangle ABC. The angle forming a linear pair with interior ∠A measures 130°, and the angle vertical to interior ∠B measures 60°. Angle y is interior ∠A, and angle x is the exterior angle at C (a linear pair with interior ∠C). Find each value.
questions.hint: Use a linear pair at A, vertical angles at B, then the triangle sum.
questions.explanation: y = 180 − 130 = 50. Interior ∠B = 60 (vertical angles). Interior ∠C = 180 − 50 − 60 = 70, so x = 180 − 70 = 110 (also 50 + 60 = 110 by the Exterior Angle Theorem).

questions.q: Lines l and m are cut by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles measure (5x − 12)° and (3x + 20)°. For what value of x is l ∥ m?
questions.hint: The converse of the Corresponding Angles Postulate needs the angles to be congruent.
questions.explanation: Set 5x − 12 = 3x + 20, so 2x = 32 and x = 16. (21.5 comes from wrongly setting the sum equal to 180.)

questions.q: For each triangle, the exterior angle at one vertex equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Complete the table (degrees).
questions.hint: Exterior angle = remote interior 1 + remote interior 2.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, side BA is extended past A to point D. The exterior angle ∠CAD measures (3x + 10)°, ∠B = (x + 20)° and ∠C = 50°. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Use the Exterior Angle Theorem: exterior angle = sum of the two remote interior angles.
questions.explanation: 3x + 10 = (x + 20) + 50, so 3x + 10 = x + 70. Then 2x = 60 and x = 30. Check: the exterior angle is 100° = 50° + 50°.

questions.q: In triangle DEF, side EF is extended past F. The exterior angle at F measures 128° and m∠E = 47°. What is m∠D?
questions.hint: The exterior angle at F equals m∠D + m∠E.
questions.explanation: 128° = m∠D + 47°, so m∠D = 81°. (52° is the interior angle at F, not ∠D.)

questions.q: Lines p and q are parallel, and transversal t is perpendicular to p. One of the angles formed by t and q measures (8x − 6)°. Solve for x.
questions.hint: A line perpendicular to one of two parallel lines is perpendicular to the other.
questions.explanation: Since t ⊥ p and p ∥ q, t ⊥ q, so every angle at q is 90°. 8x − 6 = 90, so 8x = 96 and x = 12.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate exterior angles measure (11x − 7)° and (8x + 23)°. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Alternate exterior angles of parallel lines are congruent.
questions.explanation: 11x − 7 = 8x + 23, so 3x = 30 and x = 10. Both angles measure 103°.

questions.q: Each description involves two parallel lines cut by a transversal. Match each to the value of x.

left: Transversal perpendicular to the lines; one angle is (5x + 15)°

questions.hint: Congruent pairs: set equal. Perpendicular: set equal to 90. Same-side interior: add to 180.

questions.q: Horizontal lines AB ∥ CD ∥ EF, with CD in the middle. A segment goes from point P on line AB down to the right to point D on line CD, then turns and goes down to the left to point E on line EF, so that ∠PDE = 90°. ∠1 is the angle at P between ray PA (pointing left) and segment PD, and m∠1 = 130°. C is to the left of D and F is to the right of E. Find m∠DEF.
questions.hint: Find the angle PD makes with AB on the right, carry it to line CD with alternate interior angles, then use the 90° angle at D.
questions.explanation: At P, the angle between PB and PD is 180° − 130° = 50°. ∠PDC is alternate interior to it, so ∠PDC = 50°. Then ∠CDE = 90° − 50° = 40°. ∠DEF is alternate interior to ∠CDE, so m∠DEF = 40°.

questions.q: Horizontal lines AB ∥ CD ∥ EF, with CD in the middle. A segment goes from P on AB down to the right to D on CD, then down to the left to E on EF, with ∠PDE = 90°. The angle at P between ray PA (pointing left) and PD is 125°. C is left of D; B is right of P; F is right of E. Find each angle.
questions.hint: Linear pair at P, alternate interior angles between AB and CD, the right angle at D, then alternate interior angles between CD and EF.
questions.explanation: ∠BPD = 180° − 125° = 55°. ∠PDC is alternate interior to ∠BPD, so 55°. ∠CDE = 90° − 55° = 35°. ∠DEF is alternate interior to ∠CDE, so 35°.

questions.q: Horizontal lines AB ∥ CD ∥ EF, with CD in the middle. Point P is on AB and point E is on EF. Point D on CD is to the right of both, and segments PD and DE form ∠PDE, which opens to the left. C is left of D and F is right of E. If m∠PDC = 30° and m∠PDE = 80°, what is m∠DEF?
questions.hint: Split ∠PDE into ∠PDC and ∠CDE, then use alternate interior angles with line EF.
questions.explanation: m∠CDE = 80° − 30° = 50°. Because CD ∥ EF, ∠DEF and ∠CDE are alternate interior angles, so m∠DEF = 50°.

questions.q: Lines g ∥ h are cut by transversal q. ∠5 and ∠8 are same-side interior angles. If m∠5 = 104° and m∠8 = (3y + 16)°, find y.
questions.hint: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines are supplementary.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of same-side interior angles measure (4y − 10)° and (2y + 34)°. What is y?
questions.hint: Add the two expressions and set the sum equal to 180.
questions.explanation: (4y − 10) + (2y + 34) = 180 gives 6y + 24 = 180, so 6y = 156 and y = 26. (22 comes from wrongly setting the angles equal.)

questions.q: Lines g ∥ h are cut by a transversal, and ∠5 and ∠8 are same-side interior angles. Complete each row.
questions.hint: m∠5 + m∠8 = 180 in every row.

questions.q: Lines j ∥ k are cut by transversal t, with j above k. At j the angles are numbered ∠1 (above j, left of t), ∠2 (above j, right of t), ∠3 (below j, left of t), ∠4 (below j, right of t). At k they are numbered the same way: ∠5 (above-left), ∠6 (above-right), ∠7 (below-left), ∠8 (below-right). If m∠2 = (3x + 12)° and m∠7 = 108°, find x.
questions.hint: ∠2 and ∠7 are on opposite sides of t and outside the parallel lines.
questions.explanation: ∠2 and ∠7 are alternate exterior angles, so they are congruent: 3x + 12 = 108, so 3x = 96 and x = 32.

questions.q: Lines j ∥ k are cut by transversal t, with j above k. At j the angles are numbered ∠1 (above j, left of t), ∠2 (above j, right of t), ∠3 (below j, left of t), ∠4 (below j, right of t). At k they are numbered the same way: ∠5 (above-left), ∠6 (above-right), ∠7 (below-left), ∠8 (below-right). If m∠3 = (4x + 8)° and m∠8 = 64°, find x.
questions.hint: Relate ∠8 to an angle that is a same-side interior partner of ∠3.
questions.explanation: ∠8 is vertical to ∠5, so m∠5 = 64°. ∠3 and ∠5 are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary: 4x + 8 = 180 − 64 = 116. Then 4x = 108 and x = 27.

questions.q: Lines j ∥ k are cut by transversal t, with j above k. At j the angles are numbered ∠1 (above j, left of t), ∠2 (above j, right of t), ∠3 (below j, left of t), ∠4 (below j, right of t). At k they are numbered the same way: ∠5 (above-left), ∠6 (above-right), ∠7 (below-left), ∠8 (below-right). Match each angle pair to its name.
questions.hint: Interior means between j and k; alternate means on opposite sides of t.
questions.explanation: ∠1 and ∠5 are in the same position at each line (corresponding). ∠3 and ∠6 are between the lines on opposite sides (alternate interior). ∠2 and ∠7 are outside the lines on opposite sides (alternate exterior). ∠4 and ∠6 are between the lines on the same side (same-side interior). ∠1 and ∠4 are opposite each other at one intersection (vertical).

questions.q: Lines j ∥ k are cut by transversal t, with j above k. At j the angles are numbered ∠1 (above j, left of t), ∠2 (above j, right of t), ∠3 (below j, left of t), ∠4 (below j, right of t). At k they are numbered the same way: ∠5 (above-left), ∠6 (above-right), ∠7 (below-left), ∠8 (below-right). If m∠1 = 115°, what is m∠8?
questions.hint: Move from ∠1 to ∠5, then from ∠5 to ∠8.
questions.explanation: ∠1 and ∠5 are corresponding angles, so m∠5 = 115°. ∠5 and ∠8 are vertical angles, so m∠8 = 115°.

questions.q: A ramp connects two parallel horizontal floors and makes a 12° angle with the lower floor. At the top of the ramp, ∠1 is the angle between the ramp and the upper floor, opening back toward the bottom of the ramp (alternate interior to the 12° angle). Find m∠1 in degrees.
questions.hint: The ramp is a transversal of two parallel lines.
questions.explanation: The floors are parallel and the ramp is a transversal. ∠1 and the 12° angle are alternate interior angles, so they are congruent: m∠1 = 12°.

questions.q: A conveyor belt rises in a straight line between two parallel horizontal floors and makes an 18° angle with the lower floor. At the top, what is the obtuse angle between the belt and the upper floor?
questions.hint: The acute angle at the top equals 18° (alternate interior); the obtuse angle forms a linear pair with it.
questions.explanation: The acute angle between the belt and the upper floor is 18° (alternate interior angles). The obtuse angle forms a linear pair with it: 180° − 18° = 162°.

questions.q: An escalator connects two parallel floors and makes a 30° angle with the lower floor. Complete the statements about the angles at the top of the escalator.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Acute angle between escalator and upper floor (degrees):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Angle forming a linear pair with it (degrees):

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The 30° angle and the acute top angle are ___ angles.

questions.hint: Treat the escalator as a transversal of the two parallel floors.
questions.explanation: The acute top angle and the 30° bottom angle are alternate interior angles, so the top angle is 30°. Its linear-pair partner is 180° − 30° = 150°.

questions.q: A carpenter's square (a 90° corner with a long arm and a short arm) has its corner on the bottom edge of a board whose top and bottom edges are parallel. The long arm goes up to the left and the short arm goes up to the right, and both cross the top edge. ∠1 is the angle between the long arm and the top edge, on the right side of the long arm and below the top edge. ∠2 is the angle between the short arm and the bottom edge, to the right of the corner. ∠3 is the angle between the short arm and the top edge, on the right side of the short arm and below the top edge. The long arm makes a 28° angle with the bottom edge (to the left of the corner). Find each angle.
questions.hint: ∠1 is alternate interior to the 28° angle; the angles along the bottom edge at the corner add to 180°.
questions.explanation: ∠1 and the 28° angle are alternate interior angles, so m∠1 = 28°. Along the bottom edge, 28° + 90° + m∠2 = 180°, so m∠2 = 62°. ∠2 and ∠3 are same-side interior angles, so m∠3 = 180° − 62° = 118°.

questions.q: A carpenter's square (a 90° corner with a long arm and a short arm) has its corner on the bottom edge of a board whose top and bottom edges are parallel. The long arm goes up to the left and the short arm goes up to the right, and both cross the top edge. ∠1 is the angle between the long arm and the top edge, on the right side of the long arm and below the top edge. ∠2 is the angle between the short arm and the bottom edge, to the right of the corner. ∠3 is the angle between the short arm and the top edge, on the right side of the short arm and below the top edge. The long arm makes a 40° angle with the bottom edge. What is m∠3?
questions.hint: Find ∠2 first, then use same-side interior angles.
questions.explanation: m∠2 = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. ∠2 and ∠3 are same-side interior angles between the parallel edges, so m∠3 = 180° − 50° = 130°.

questions.q: A carpenter's square (a 90° corner with a long arm and a short arm) has its corner on the bottom edge of a board whose top and bottom edges are parallel. The long arm goes up to the left and the short arm goes up to the right, and both cross the top edge. ∠1 is the angle between the long arm and the top edge, on the right side of the long arm and below the top edge. ∠2 is the angle between the short arm and the bottom edge, to the right of the corner. ∠3 is the angle between the short arm and the top edge, on the right side of the short arm and below the top edge. Complete the table (degrees). The first column is the angle between the long arm and the bottom edge.
questions.hint: m∠1 equals the long-arm angle, the long-arm angle + 90 + m∠2 = 180, and m∠2 + m∠3 = 180.

questions.q: Sara cuts a parallelogram from a long board with parallel top and bottom edges. The first cut makes a 115° interior angle with the bottom edge at the left end of the piece. What interior angle must the second cut make with the bottom edge at the right end of the piece so that the two cut ends are parallel?
questions.hint: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram (same-side interior angles) are supplementary.
questions.explanation: The bottom edge is a transversal of the two parallel cuts. The interior angles at its two ends are same-side interior angles, so they must add to 180°: 180° − 115° = 65°.

questions.q: A board has parallel top and bottom edges. The left cut makes a 72° interior angle with the bottom edge. A second cut is made farther right. Angle x is the angle between the second cut and the bottom edge on the right side of the cut (outside the piece), in the same position as the 72° angle. For the cuts to be parallel, what is x?
questions.hint: x and the 72° angle are in matching positions along the bottom edge.
questions.explanation: The bottom edge is a transversal of the two cuts, and x is in the corresponding position to the 72° angle. Parallel cuts need congruent corresponding angles, so x = 72°.

questions.q: ABCD is a parallelogram (A, B, C, D in order around the shape). Fill in the missing angles in degrees.
questions.hint: Opposite angles are equal; consecutive angles add to 180°.

questions.q: A vertical post joins a stair rail to the bottom board of a staircase. At the bottom of the post, the angle between the post (going up) and the board (going up the stairs) is 52°. ∠1 is the angle at the top of the post between the post (going down) and the rail (going up the stairs). What must m∠1 be for the rail to be parallel to the board?
questions.hint: The post is a transversal; the two angles are same-side interior angles.
questions.explanation: For the rail to be parallel to the board, the same-side interior angles must be supplementary: m∠1 = 180° − 52° = 128°.

questions.q: A builder measures the angles where a vertical post meets a stair rail and the board below it. The same-side interior angles are 131° (at the rail) and 51° (at the board). Is the rail parallel to the board?
options: No, because the angles should be equal
Yes, because the angles are on the same side
questions.hint: Same-side interior angles must add to exactly 180° for the lines to be parallel.
questions.explanation: By the converse of the Same-Side Interior Angles Theorem, the lines are parallel only if the angles add to 180°. Here 131 + 51 = 182, so the rail is not parallel to the board.

questions.q: A staircase board rises at 36° above the horizontal floor. Vertical posts hold a rail parallel to the board. Find the angles (degrees).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Angle at the bottom of a post between the post (up) and the board (uphill):

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Angle at the top of the post between the post (down) and the rail (uphill):

questions.hint: A vertical post makes 90° with the floor; then use same-side interior angles.
questions.explanation: The post is vertical and the board rises 36° from horizontal, so the angle between post and board is 90° − 36° = 54°. The rail is parallel to the board, so the same-side interior angle at the top is 180° − 54° = 126°.

questions.q: In triangle PQR, ∠P ≅ ∠Q. PR = 4x − 7, QR = 2x + 9 and PQ = 20. What is x?
questions.hint: The sides opposite the congruent angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: The side opposite ∠P is QR and the side opposite ∠Q is PR, so PR = QR: 4x − 7 = 2x + 9. Then 2x = 16 and x = 8.

questions.q: In triangle JKL, ∠J ≅ ∠L. JK = 5x − 3, KL = 3x + 11 and JL = 15. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Which sides are opposite ∠J and ∠L?
questions.explanation: KL is opposite ∠J and JK is opposite ∠L, so JK = KL: 5x − 3 = 3x + 11. Then 2x = 14 and x = 7.

questions.q: In triangle DEF, ∠D ≅ ∠E. DF = 3x + 2, EF = 5x − 10 and DE = x + 9. Find each value.
questions.hint: Set the sides opposite the congruent angles equal.
questions.explanation: EF is opposite ∠D and DF is opposite ∠E, so 3x + 2 = 5x − 10, giving x = 6. DF = EF = 20, DE = 6 + 9 = 15, and the perimeter is 20 + 20 + 15 = 55.

questions.q: In triangle XYZ, ∠X ≅ ∠Y. YZ = 2x + 4, XZ = 22 and XY = 3x − 1. What is the length of XY?
questions.hint: Find x from the two congruent sides, then substitute into XY.
questions.explanation: YZ (opposite ∠X) equals XZ (opposite ∠Y): 2x + 4 = 22, so x = 9. Then XY = 3(9) − 1 = 26.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, ∠A ≅ ∠C. AB = 5x − 9, BC = 31 and AC = 2x + 3. Find the length of AC.
questions.hint: First find x using the sides opposite the congruent angles.
questions.explanation: AB is opposite ∠C and BC is opposite ∠A, so 5x − 9 = 31, giving x = 8. Then AC = 2(8) + 3 = 19.

questions.q: In triangle LMN, ∠M ≅ ∠N. LN = 4x − 1, LM = 3x + 4 and MN = x + 8. Find each value.
questions.hint: LN is opposite ∠M and LM is opposite ∠N.
questions.explanation: 4x − 1 = 3x + 4 gives x = 5. LN = LM = 19 and MN = 5 + 8 = 13. The perimeter is 19 + 19 + 13 = 51.

questions.q: Triangle ABC is equilateral. Point D lies on the opposite side of line AB from C, with BD = BA, so ∠CBD = ∠CBA + ∠ABD. If m∠CBD = 150°, what is m∠BAD?
questions.hint: Subtract the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle, then use the base angles of isosceles triangle ABD.
questions.explanation: ∠CBA = 60°, so ∠ABD = 150° − 60° = 90°. Triangle ABD is isosceles with BA = BD, so ∠BAD = ∠BDA = (180° − 90°) ÷ 2 = 45°.

questions.q: Triangle ABC is equilateral. Point D lies on the opposite side of line AB from C, with BD = BA, so ∠CBD = ∠CBA + ∠ABD. If m∠CBD = 100°, find m∠BAD in degrees.
questions.hint: ∠ABD = m∠CBD − 60°.
questions.explanation: ∠ABD = 100° − 60° = 40°. In isosceles triangle ABD, ∠BAD = (180° − 40°) ÷ 2 = 70°.

questions.q: Triangle ABC is equilateral. Point D lies on the opposite side of line AB from C, with BD = BA, so ∠CBD = ∠CBA + ∠ABD. Complete the table (degrees).
questions.hint: ∠ABD = ∠CBD − 60, and ∠BAD = ∠ADB = (180 − ∠ABD) ÷ 2.
questions.explanation: Row 1: 130 − 60 = 70, base angles (180 − 70)/2 = 55. Row 2: 160 − 60 = 100, base angles 40. Row 3: base angles 60 means ∠ABD = 180 − 120 = 60, so ∠CBD = 60 + 60 = 120 and ∠ADB = 60.

questions.q: Triangle PQR is equilateral. PQ = 3(x − 2), QR = 12 and m∠P = (5x + 4y)°. What is y?
questions.hint: Use the sides to find x, then use the fact that each angle is 60°.
questions.explanation: 3(x − 2) = 12 gives x − 2 = 4, so x = 6. Each angle is 60°, so 5(6) + 4y = 60, giving 4y = 30 and y = 7.5.

questions.q: Triangle DEF is equilateral. DE = 4x − 5, EF = 2x + 7 and m∠D = (9y − 3)°. Find each value.
questions.hint: All sides are equal and every angle is 60°.
questions.explanation: 4x − 5 = 2x + 7 gives x = 6, so each side is 4(6) − 5 = 19. 9y − 3 = 60 gives 9y = 63 and y = 7.

questions.q: In an equilateral triangle, one side is 2(x + 3), another side is 16, and one angle is (3x + 2y)°. Find y. Give an exact decimal or fraction.
questions.hint: Find x from the sides first.
questions.explanation: 2(x + 3) = 16 gives x + 3 = 8, so x = 5. Each angle is 60°, so 3(5) + 2y = 60, giving 2y = 45 and y = 22.5.

questions.q: Each row describes an isosceles triangle. Fill in the missing vertex angle (between the two equal sides) or base angle, in degrees.
questions.hint: Vertex angle + 2 × base angle = 180.

questions.q: In isosceles triangle KLM, KL = LM and m∠K = 34°. What is m∠L?
questions.hint: The angles opposite the equal sides are equal.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, AB = BC, m∠B = (2x)° and m∠A = 50°. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Which angle is congruent to ∠A?
questions.explanation: AB = BC, so the angles opposite them, ∠C and ∠A, are congruent: m∠C = 50°. Then m∠B = 180 − 50 − 50 = 80, so 2x = 80 and x = 40.

questions.q: In triangle PQR, ∠P ≅ ∠R. PQ = 4x − 6, QR = 2x + 10 and PR = x + 2. Solve for x.
questions.hint: The sides opposite the congruent angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: QR is opposite ∠P and PQ is opposite ∠R, so 4x − 6 = 2x + 10. Then 2x = 16 and x = 8.

questions.q: In triangle DEF, ∠D ≅ ∠F. DE = 7x − 4, EF = 5x + 6 and DF = 3x. Which equation should you solve to find x?
questions.hint: Find the side opposite ∠D and the side opposite ∠F.
questions.explanation: The side opposite ∠D is EF and the side opposite ∠F is DE. By the Converse of the Base Angles Theorem these sides are congruent, so 7x − 4 = 5x + 6 (which gives x = 5).

questions.q: In triangle XYZ, ∠X ≅ ∠Z. XY = 3x + 1, YZ = 5x − 9 and XZ = 2x. Find each value.
questions.hint: YZ is opposite ∠X and XY is opposite ∠Z.
questions.explanation: 3x + 1 = 5x − 9 gives 2x = 10, so x = 5. XY = YZ = 16 and XZ = 2(5) = 10.

questions.q: In triangle PQR, PQ ≅ PR and m∠P = 60°. QR = 5x − 10 and PQ = 3x + 6. Solve for x.
questions.hint: An isosceles triangle with a 60° vertex angle is equilateral.
questions.explanation: The base angles are (180 − 60)/2 = 60°, so the triangle is equilateral and QR = PQ: 5x − 10 = 3x + 6. Then 2x = 16 and x = 8.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, AB ≅ AC and m∠A = 60°. Which statement must be true?
questions.hint: Find the base angles first.
questions.explanation: Since AB ≅ AC, ∠B ≅ ∠C, and each is (180° − 60°)/2 = 60°. All three angles are 60°, so the triangle is equilateral and all sides are congruent.

questions.q: In triangle LMN, LM ≅ LN and m∠L = 60°. LM = 2x + 3 and MN = 5x − 9. Find each value.
questions.hint: With a 60° vertex angle, the isosceles triangle is equilateral, so LM = MN.
questions.explanation: The triangle is equilateral, so 2x + 3 = 5x − 9, giving 3x = 12 and x = 4. Each side is 11, so the perimeter is 33.

questions.q: In triangles PQR and XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What additional information is needed to prove ΔPQR ≅ ΔXYZ by SAS?
questions.hint: In SAS the angle must be between the two sides.
questions.explanation: ∠Q is formed by sides PQ and QR, and ∠Y by XY and YZ. We already have PQ ≅ XY, so the included-angle pattern needs QR ≅ YZ.

questions.q: For ΔABC and ΔDEF, match each pair of given facts to the third fact needed to prove ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF by SAS.
questions.hint: Each angle is formed by the two sides that share its vertex letter.
questions.explanation: ∠A is between AB and AC, so add AC ≅ DF. ∠B is between AB and BC, so add AB ≅ DE. ∠C is between AC and BC, so add BC ≅ EF. Sides AB and BC meet at B, so add ∠B ≅ ∠E.

questions.q: In ΔJKL and ΔMNO, ∠K ≅ ∠N and KL ≅ NO. Name the other pair of sides that must be congruent to use SAS. Write it like AB ≅ CD.
questions.hint: Which other side of ΔJKL has K as an endpoint?
questions.explanation: ∠K is formed by sides KL and JK, and ∠N by NO and MN. KL ≅ NO is given, so SAS also needs JK ≅ MN.

questions.q: In triangles PQR and STU, ∠P ≅ ∠S and PQ ≅ ST. What additional information is needed to prove ΔPQR ≅ ΔSTU by ASA?
questions.hint: In ASA the side must be between the two angles.
questions.explanation: Side PQ connects vertices P and Q. With ∠P ≅ ∠S, ASA needs the angle at the other end of the side: ∠Q ≅ ∠T. (∠R ≅ ∠U would give AAS, and PR ≅ SU would give SAS.)

questions.q: Match each set of congruent parts of ΔABC and ΔDEF to the postulate or theorem it uses.

left: AB ≅ DE, BC ≅ EF, AC ≅ DF

questions.hint: Check whether the side is between the angles, or the angle is between the sides.
questions.explanation: AB is between ∠A and ∠B: ASA. BC is not between ∠A and ∠B: AAS. ∠A is between AB and AC: SAS. Three pairs of sides: SSS. (SSA is not a valid test.)

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a valid way to prove two triangles congruent?
questions.hint: One pattern with an angle that is not between the two sides does not work.
questions.explanation: SAS, ASA and AAS are valid congruence tests. SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) can produce two different triangles, so it does not prove congruence.

questions.q: Given ΔABC ≅ ΔXZY, m∠B = 64°, m∠C = 76° and m∠Z = (4x + 8)°. What is x?
questions.hint: Match the letters in order: A↔X, B↔Z, C↔Y.
questions.explanation: ∠Z corresponds to ∠B, so 4x + 8 = 64, giving 4x = 56 and x = 14. (17 comes from matching ∠Z with ∠C by mistake.)

questions.q: Given ΔDEF ≅ ΔRTS, write the part of ΔRTS that corresponds to each part of ΔDEF.
questions.hint: The order of the letters gives the correspondence: D↔R, E↔T, F↔S.
questions.explanation: From ΔDEF ≅ ΔRTS: D↔R, E↔T, F↔S. So ∠D↔∠R, ∠E↔∠T, ∠F↔∠S, DE↔RT, EF↔TS and DF↔RS.

questions.q: Given ΔLMN ≅ ΔQSR, LN = 2x + 5 and QR = 23. Solve for x.
questions.hint: Which side of ΔQSR matches LN?
questions.explanation: L↔Q and N↔R, so LN corresponds to QR. Then 2x + 5 = 23, so 2x = 18 and x = 9.

questions.q: Point M is the midpoint of QR and PM ⊥ QR, so ΔPMQ ≅ ΔPMR. If PQ = 3x + 7 and PR = 5x − 3, what is x?
questions.hint: Corresponding sides of congruent triangles are congruent.
questions.explanation: PQ corresponds to PR, so 3x + 7 = 5x − 3. Then 10 = 2x and x = 5. (22 is the length of PQ, not x.)

questions.q: Given ΔABD ≅ ΔCBD (they share side BD). AB = 4x − 1, CB = 2x + 9, AD = y + 3 and CD = 2y − 4. Find each value.
questions.hint: Match AB with CB and AD with CD.
questions.explanation: AB = CB: 4x − 1 = 2x + 9, so x = 5 and AB = 19. AD = CD: y + 3 = 2y − 4, so y = 7.

questions.q: Given ΔJKL ≅ ΔJML (they share side JL). JK = 7x − 10 and JM = 3x + 14. Solve for x.
questions.hint: JK and JM are corresponding sides.
questions.explanation: J↔J and K↔M, so JK ≅ JM: 7x − 10 = 3x + 14. Then 4x = 24 and x = 6.

questions.q: ΔPQR and ΔXYZ are right triangles with right angles at Q and Y. Which information is sufficient to prove ΔPQR ≅ ΔXYZ by the HL Theorem?
questions.hint: HL needs the hypotenuses (opposite the right angles) and one pair of legs.
questions.explanation: The hypotenuses are PR and XZ (opposite the right angles). HL needs PR ≅ XZ plus one pair of legs, such as PQ ≅ XY. Two legs would be SAS, and a hypotenuse with an angle would be AAS.

questions.q: Two right triangles are being compared. Match the congruent parts to the test that proves the triangles congruent.

left: The hypotenuses and one pair of legs
The hypotenuses and one pair of acute angles
One pair of legs and the acute angles next to those legs (not the right angles)

questions.hint: Remember that the right angles are already a pair of congruent angles.
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse and leg is HL. Two legs with the right angle between them is SAS. Hypotenuse and an acute angle, plus the right angles, is AAS. A leg between the right angle and an acute angle is ASA.

questions.q: Right triangles ABC (right angle at C) and EBD (right angle at D) meet at vertex B. AB = 13, EB = 13 and AC = 5. What must ED equal to prove ΔABC ≅ ΔEBD by HL?
questions.hint: AB and EB are the hypotenuses; AC and ED are corresponding legs.
questions.explanation: The hypotenuses AB and EB are congruent (both 13). HL also needs one pair of corresponding legs, so ED must equal AC = 5.

questions.q: Match each description of congruent parts to the postulate or theorem.

left: Two pairs of sides and the angles between them
Two pairs of angles and the sides between them
Two pairs of angles and a pair of sides not between them

questions.hint: The middle letter of SAS and ASA is the part that is included between the other two.
questions.explanation: Three sides is SSS. Two sides with the included angle is SAS. Two angles with the included side is ASA. Two angles with a non-included side is AAS.

questions.q: In ΔABC and ΔFGH, AB ≅ FG, ∠B ≅ ∠G and BC ≅ GH. Which postulate proves ΔABC ≅ ΔFGH?
questions.hint: Is the angle between the two sides?
questions.explanation: ∠B is formed by sides AB and BC, and ∠G by FG and GH. Two sides and the included angle are congruent, so SAS applies.

questions.q: In ΔABC and ΔFGH, ∠A ≅ ∠F, ∠B ≅ ∠G and BC ≅ GH. Which theorem proves ΔABC ≅ ΔFGH?
questions.hint: Is side BC between ∠A and ∠B?
questions.explanation: The side between ∠A and ∠B would be AB. BC is not between them, so the pattern is angle-angle-side: AAS.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(−4, 1), B(−1, 1) and C(−4, 5). Triangle DEF is its reflection in the y-axis, so ΔDEF ≅ ΔABC by SSS. Plot D, E and F (the images of A, B and C).
questions.hint: Reflecting in the y-axis changes (x, y) to (−x, y).
questions.explanation: D = (4, 1), E = (1, 1), F = (4, 5). The side lengths stay the same (DE = 3, DF = 4, EF = 5), so the triangles are congruent by SSS.

questions.q: In ΔJKL, JK has 1 tick mark, KL has 2 and JL has 3. In ΔPQR, QR has 1 tick mark, PR has 2 and PQ has 3. Which triangle is congruent to ΔJKL, written in corresponding order?
questions.hint: A vertex is where two sides meet; match vertices using the tick marks of their two sides.
questions.explanation: J is where the 1-tick and 3-tick sides meet; in ΔPQR that is Q. K joins the 1-tick and 2-tick sides: R. L joins the 2-tick and 3-tick sides: P. So ΔJKL ≅ ΔQRP.

questions.q: In ΔABC, AB has 1 tick mark, BC has 2 and AC has 3. In ΔXYZ, YZ has 1 tick mark, XZ has 2 and XY has 3. Complete the correspondence.
questions.hint: Each vertex is the meeting point of two marked sides.
questions.explanation: A joins the 1- and 3-tick sides, which meet at Y. B joins the 1- and 2-tick sides, which meet at Z. C joins the 2- and 3-tick sides, which meet at X. AB (1 tick) matches YZ, so ΔABC ≅ ΔYZX.

questions.q: In ΔDEF, DE has 1 tick mark, EF has 2 and DF has 3. In ΔMNO, NO has 1 tick mark, MO has 2 and MN has 3. Complete the statement ΔDEF ≅ Δ___ (write the three letters).
questions.hint: Find the vertex of ΔMNO where the 1-tick and 3-tick sides meet; that matches D.
questions.explanation: D (1 and 3 ticks) matches N, where NO and MN meet. E (1 and 2 ticks) matches O, where NO and MO meet. F (2 and 3 ticks) matches M. So ΔDEF ≅ ΔNOM.

questions.q: In ΔABC and ΔPQR, AB ≅ PQ and ∠A ≅ ∠P. If also ∠B ≅ ∠Q, which can you use to prove ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR?
questions.hint: Is AB between ∠A and ∠B?
questions.explanation: AB connects vertices A and B, so it is the side included between ∠A and ∠B. Angle-side-angle with the included side is ASA.

questions.q: In ΔABC and ΔPQR, AB ≅ PQ and ∠A ≅ ∠P. Match each extra fact to what it lets you conclude.
questions.hint: Check where the extra part sits relative to AB and ∠A.
questions.explanation: ∠B with AB and ∠A: the side is between the angles, ASA. ∠C: the side is not between the angles, AAS. AC: ∠A is between AB and AC, SAS. BC: the angle is not between the sides (SSA), which does not prove congruence.

questions.q: In ΔDEF and ΔSTU, ∠E ≅ ∠T and ∠F ≅ ∠U. If you also know EF ≅ TU, which postulate proves ΔDEF ≅ ΔSTU? Write its three-letter name.
questions.hint: EF connects vertices E and F.
questions.explanation: EF is the side between ∠E and ∠F, and TU is between ∠T and ∠U. Two angles and the included side give ASA.

questions.q: To prove ΔABC ≅ ΔLKM by SAS, you know ∠B ≅ ∠K. Which pair of statements is required?
questions.hint: List the two sides that form ∠B in ΔABC, then match them using the order A↔L, B↔K, C↔M.
questions.explanation: ∠B is formed by sides AB and BC. With A↔L, B↔K, C↔M, these correspond to LK and KM. So SAS needs AB ≅ LK and BC ≅ KM.

questions.q: Given: PQ ≅ PS and QR ≅ SR. Prove: ∠Q ≅ ∠S. (Quadrilateral PQRS is a kite with diagonal PR.) Fill in the missing reasons.
questions.hint: A segment is congruent to itself; three pairs of sides give one postulate; then use corresponding parts.
questions.explanation: PR is shared, so PR ≅ PR by the Reflexive Property. With three pairs of congruent sides, ΔPQR ≅ ΔPSR by SSS. Then ∠Q ≅ ∠S because corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC).

questions.q: To prove ΔABC ≅ ΔLKM by SAS, match each known pair of angles to the two pairs of sides that are needed.
questions.hint: The included angle is formed by the two sides that share its vertex.
questions.explanation: ∠A is between AB and AC (matching LK and LM). ∠B is between AB and BC (matching LK and KM). ∠C is between AC and BC (matching LM and KM).

questions.q: In a proof, the statements so far are: 1. AB ≅ DE (Given); 2. ∠B ≅ ∠E (Given); 3. BC ≅ EF (Given). Step 4 says △ABC ≅ △DEF. Which reason justifies Step 4?
questions.hint: Check whether the angle sits between the two sides.
questions.explanation: ∠B is formed by sides AB and BC, and ∠E is formed by DE and EF. So we have two sides and the included angle of each triangle. The triangles are congruent by SAS.

questions.q: Match each set of given facts about △PQR and △XYZ to the postulate or theorem that proves △PQR ≅ △XYZ.

left: PQ ≅ XY, QR ≅ YZ, PR ≅ XZ

questions.hint: Look at whether the side is between the two angles, or the angle is between the two sides.
questions.explanation: Three pairs of sides gives SSS. PQ lies between ∠P and ∠Q, so that set is ASA. ∠Q lies between PQ and QR, so that set is SAS. QR is not between ∠P and ∠Q, so that set is AAS.

questions.q: In △JKL and △MNO, you know JK ≅ MN and ∠K ≅ ∠N. Which pair of sides must also be congruent to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by SAS? Write it like AB ≅ CD.
questions.hint: SAS needs the sides that form the known angle.
questions.explanation: ∠K is formed by sides JK and KL, and ∠N is formed by MN and NO. JK ≅ MN is already known, so the other pair of sides around the angle, KL ≅ NO, is needed.

questions.q: M is the midpoint of AC and BM ⊥ AC. A proof shows AM ≅ CM (definition of midpoint), ∠AMB ≅ ∠CMB (all right angles are congruent) and BM ≅ BM (Reflexive Property). Which reason justifies the final step △ABM ≅ △CBM?
questions.hint: The right angle at M lies between which two sides?
questions.explanation: The right angle ∠AMB is formed by AM and BM, and ∠CMB is formed by CM and BM. So two sides and the included angle match. The reason is SAS.

questions.q: In a proof, Step 2 says ∠1 ≅ ∠2 and Step 3 says ∠2 ≅ ∠3. Step 4 says ∠1 ≅ ∠3. Which reason justifies Step 4?
questions.hint: ∠2 is the 'link' shared by both statements.
questions.explanation: If a ≅ b and b ≅ c, then a ≅ c. This is the Transitive Property of Congruence. Here ∠1 ≅ ∠2 and ∠2 ≅ ∠3 give ∠1 ≅ ∠3.

questions.q: Match each statement to the reason that justifies it.

left: If XY ≅ PQ and PQ ≅ RS, then XY ≅ RS
If M is the midpoint of AB, then AM ≅ MB

questions.hint: Reflexive: same thing; symmetric: swap order; transitive: a chain of two.
questions.explanation: A figure is congruent to itself (Reflexive). Reversing a congruence is Symmetric. A chain XY ≅ PQ ≅ RS gives XY ≅ RS (Transitive). A midpoint splits a segment into two congruent parts (Definition of midpoint).

questions.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF and △DEF ≅ △GHI. Complete the conclusion and its reason.
questions.hint: Both statements share △DEF.
questions.explanation: △ABC is congruent to △DEF, which is congruent to △GHI. By the Transitive Property of Congruence, △ABC ≅ △GHI.

questions.q: △PQR ≅ △STU. If m∠P = (5x − 8)° and m∠S = 62°, find the value of x.
questions.hint: ∠P corresponds to ∠S because they are listed first.
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal, so 5x − 8 = 62. Then 5x = 70 and x = 14.

questions.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. m∠B = (3x + 9)°, m∠D = 50° and m∠F = 70°. Find the value of x.
questions.hint: First find m∠E, then use that ∠B corresponds to ∠E.
questions.explanation: In △DEF, m∠E = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°. ∠B corresponds to ∠E, so 3x + 9 = 60. Then 3x = 51 and x = 17.

questions.q: Segments JL and KM cross at E, forming △JKE and △LME with △JKE ≅ △LME. m∠J = 75°, m∠JEK = 35° and m∠M = (2y + 10)°. Complete:
questions.hint: Match vertices in order: J↔L, K↔M, E↔E.
questions.explanation: ∠L corresponds to ∠J, so m∠L = 75°, and ∠LEM corresponds to ∠JEK, so it is 35°. m∠K = 180° − 75° − 35° = 70°. ∠M corresponds to ∠K, so 2y + 10 = 70 and y = 30.

questions.q: △RST ≅ △XYZ. Match each part of △RST to its corresponding part of △XYZ.
questions.hint: Corresponding letters are in the same position: R↔X, S↔Y, T↔Z.
questions.explanation: R matches X, S matches Y and T matches Z. So ∠R ↔ ∠X, ∠T ↔ ∠Z, ST ↔ YZ and RT ↔ XZ.

questions.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. If AB = 3y + 4 and DE = 25, find y.
questions.hint: AB and DE are corresponding sides.
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides are congruent, so 3y + 4 = 25. Then 3y = 21 and y = 7.

questions.q: △KLM ≅ △PQR. KL = 2a + 1, PQ = 15, LM = 18, QR = 4b − 6 and KM = 20. Complete:
questions.hint: Pair the sides by letter position: KL↔PQ, LM↔QR, KM↔PR.
questions.explanation: 2a + 1 = 15 gives a = 7. 4b − 6 = 18 gives 4b = 24, so b = 6. PR corresponds to KM, so PR = 20.

questions.q: Quadrilateral GHJK has diagonal GJ, and △GHJ ≅ △JKG. If GH = 4x − 3 and JK = 2x + 9, what is GH?
questions.hint: Match G↔J and H↔K, so GH corresponds to JK.
questions.explanation: GH corresponds to JK, so 4x − 3 = 2x + 9. Then 2x = 12 and x = 6. GH = 4(6) − 3 = 21.

questions.q: △ABC ≅ △XYZ with AB = 9, BC = 12 and AC = 14. Complete the table of corresponding sides.
questions.hint: Use the letter order: A↔X, B↔Y, C↔Z.
questions.explanation: AB matches XY, BC matches YZ and AC matches XZ. Corresponding sides have the same length.

questions.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. m∠A = 35°, m∠B = 65°, m∠E = y° and m∠D = (2x − y)°. Find the value of x.
questions.hint: Find y first from ∠E, then use ∠D.
questions.explanation: ∠E corresponds to ∠B, so y = 65. ∠D corresponds to ∠A, so 2x − 65 = 35. Then 2x = 100 and x = 50.

questions.q: △PQR ≅ △MNL. m∠Q = 52° and m∠R = 54°. In △MNL, m∠N = y° and m∠M = (3x − y)°. Complete:
questions.hint: Q↔N and P↔M. Use the angle sum to get m∠P.
questions.explanation: ∠N corresponds to ∠Q, so y = 52. m∠P = 180° − 52° − 54° = 74°, and ∠M corresponds to ∠P. So 3x − 52 = 74, 3x = 126 and x = 42.

questions.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. AB = 2x + y, DE = 17, BC = 9 and EF = x + 4. Find y.
questions.hint: Use BC ↔ EF to find x first.
questions.explanation: BC corresponds to EF, so x + 4 = 9 and x = 5. AB corresponds to DE, so 2(5) + y = 17 and y = 7.

questions.q: Quadrilateral PQRS has diagonal QS. Given: PQ ≅ SR and PQ ∥ SR. Prove: △PQS ≅ △RSQ. Complete the two-column proof.
questions.hint: QS is a transversal of the parallel segments and is shared by both triangles.
questions.explanation: The parallel segments PQ and SR are cut by QS, so ∠PQS and ∠RSQ are congruent alternate interior angles. QS ≅ QS by the Reflexive Property. With PQ ≅ SR, the triangles are congruent by SAS.

questions.q: In △ABC and △DEF, AB ≅ DE and BC ≅ EF. Which additional fact is needed to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by SAS?
questions.hint: SAS needs the angle between the two known sides.
questions.explanation: AB and BC meet at B, and DE and EF meet at E. The included angles are ∠B and ∠E, so ∠B ≅ ∠E is needed. AC ≅ DF would give SSS, not SAS.

questions.q: In △GHJ and △KLM, GH ≅ KL and ∠H ≅ ∠L. Which pair of sides must be congruent to prove the triangles congruent by SAS? Write it like AB ≅ CD.
questions.hint: ∠H is formed by GH and one other side.
questions.explanation: ∠H is between GH and HJ, and ∠L is between KL and LM. GH ≅ KL is known, so HJ ≅ LM completes SAS.

questions.q: Match each proof step to its reason.

left: ∠1 ≅ ∠2 because they are alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines
A segment shared by two triangles is congruent to itself
Two sides and the included angle of one triangle match another

questions.hint: Think about which rule each sentence describes.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines give congruent alternate interior angles. A shared side uses the Reflexive Property. Two sides and the included angle is SAS. Equal lengths mean congruent segments by definition.

questions.q: Given: AB ≅ CB and D is the midpoint of AC. Prove: △ABD ≅ △CBD. Complete the two-column proof.

rows: 2. D is the midpoint of AC

questions.hint: A midpoint splits a segment into two congruent parts, and BD is shared.
questions.explanation: D is the midpoint, so AD ≅ CD by the definition of midpoint. BD ≅ BD by the Reflexive Property. With AB ≅ CB, all three pairs of sides are congruent, so △ABD ≅ △CBD by SSS.

questions.q: In △QRS and △XYZ, QR ≅ XY and RS ≅ YZ. Which one additional fact lets you apply the SSS Postulate directly?
questions.hint: SSS needs all three pairs of sides.
questions.explanation: Two pairs of sides are already congruent. The third pair is QS and XZ, so QS ≅ XZ is needed. ∠R ≅ ∠Y would give SAS instead.

questions.q: In △DEF, DE = 7, EF = 10 and DF = 12. In △GHI, GH = 7 and HI = 10. What must GI equal so that △DEF ≅ △GHI by SSS?
questions.hint: Match the third sides DF and GI.
questions.explanation: DE ↔ GH and EF ↔ HI already match. For SSS the third sides must match too, so GI = DF = 12.

questions.q: A tent pole PQ stands straight up, so it is perpendicular to the ground RS at Q, with Q between R and S. Two ropes PR and PS hold it. Name the postulate or theorem (SSS, SAS, ASA or AAS) that proves △PQR ≅ △PQS in each case.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Using PR ≅ PS, RQ ≅ SQ and PQ ≅ PQ:

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using RQ ≅ SQ, the right angles at Q, and PQ ≅ PQ:

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using ∠R ≅ ∠S, the right angles at Q, and PQ ≅ PQ:

questions.hint: Check where the angle or side sits compared with the others.
questions.explanation: Three pairs of sides gives SSS. The right angle at Q is between RQ and PQ, so (b) is SAS. In (c) the side PQ is not between ∠R and ∠PQR, so it is AAS.

questions.q: In △JKL and △MNP, ∠J ≅ ∠M, ∠K ≅ ∠N and KL ≅ NP. Which postulate or theorem proves △JKL ≅ △MNP?
questions.hint: Is the side between the two angles?
questions.explanation: The side between ∠J and ∠K is JK, not KL. KL is a non-included side, so with two angles the triangles are congruent by AAS.

questions.q: Which set of facts can NOT be used to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF?
options: AB ≅ DE, BC ≅ EF, AC ≅ DF
questions.hint: Look for two sides with an angle that is not between them.
questions.explanation: The first set is two sides and a non-included angle (SSA), which does not prove congruence. The others are SAS, ASA and SSS.

questions.q: Complete the table: write the postulate or theorem (SSS, SAS, ASA or AAS) for each type of given information.

rows: Two angles and the included side
Two sides and the included angle
Two angles and a non-included side

questions.hint: The letter in the middle is the part that is 'included'.
questions.explanation: SSS uses three sides. ASA has the side between the two angles. SAS has the angle between the two sides. AAS has a side that is not between the two angles.

questions.q: Which set of side lengths could form a triangle?
questions.hint: Add the two shorter sides and compare with the longest.
questions.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 < 8, 6 + 6 = 12 is not greater than 12, and 2 + 7 = 9 < 10, so those fail. 5 + 9 = 14 > 13, so 5, 9, 13 forms a triangle.

questions.q: For each set of lengths, find the sum of the two shorter sides and decide if the lengths can form a triangle (yes or no).
questions.hint: The sum must be strictly greater than the longest side.

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle are 5 cm and 11 cm. What is the smallest whole-number length (in cm) the third side can have?
questions.hint: The third side must be greater than the difference of the other two.
questions.explanation: The third side must be greater than 11 − 5 = 6 and less than 11 + 5 = 16. The smallest whole number greater than 6 is 7.

questions.q: Which three lengths CANNOT be the sides of a triangle?
questions.hint: For each set, add the two shorter lengths.
questions.explanation: 7 + 10 = 17 > 15, 9 + 9 = 18 > 17 and 14 + 8 = 22 > 20 all work. For 12, 5, 6: 5 + 6 = 11, which is less than 12, so it cannot be a triangle.

questions.q: Match each set of lengths to the correct description.

right: cannot: the two shorter sides add to less than the longest
cannot: the two shorter sides add to exactly the longest

questions.hint: Compare the sum of the two shorter sides with the longest side.
questions.explanation: 4 + 6 = 10 > 9 and 10 + 3 = 13 > 10, so those form triangles. 3 + 5 = 8 equals 8, so it is flat, not a triangle. 2 + 7 = 9 < 11, so it cannot form a triangle.

questions.q: A triangle has sides of 9 cm and 4 cm, and a third side of n cm, where n is a whole number. What is the largest possible value of n?
questions.hint: The third side must be less than the sum of the other two.
questions.explanation: The third side must be less than 9 + 4 = 13 (and greater than 5). The largest whole number less than 13 is 12.

questions.q: In △ABC, AB = 9, BC = 14 and AC = 11. List the angles from smallest to largest.
questions.hint: The smallest angle is opposite the shortest side.
questions.explanation: AB = 9 is opposite ∠C, AC = 11 is opposite ∠B and BC = 14 is opposite ∠A. Ordering the sides 9 < 11 < 14 gives the angles ∠C, ∠B, ∠A.

questions.q: In △PQR, PQ = 6.2, QR = 8.5 and PR = 7.1. Write the angle opposite each side.
questions.hint: The opposite angle is at the vertex not named in the side.
questions.explanation: PQ does not use R, so it is opposite ∠R. QR is opposite ∠P and PR is opposite ∠Q. So the largest angle, opposite QR = 8.5, is ∠P.

questions.q: In △DEF, m∠D = 48° and m∠E = 71°. Complete:
questions.hint: Find the third angle, then use: larger angle ↔ longer opposite side.
questions.explanation: m∠F = 180° − 48° − 71° = 61°. The largest angle is ∠E (71°), so the longest side is DF. The smallest angle is ∠D (48°), so the shortest side is EF.

questions.q: In △XYZ, m∠X = 35°, m∠Y = 100° and m∠Z = 45°. List the sides from shortest to longest.
questions.hint: Each side is opposite the angle at the vertex it does not touch.
questions.explanation: YZ is opposite ∠X (35°), XY is opposite ∠Z (45°) and XZ is opposite ∠Y (100°). So from shortest to longest: YZ, XY, XZ.

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle measure 12 and 7. What is the possible range for the third side x?
questions.hint: Use the difference and the sum of the two sides.
questions.explanation: The third side must be greater than 12 − 7 = 5 and less than 12 + 7 = 19. The endpoints are not allowed, so 5 < x < 19.

questions.q: In △PQR, QR = 15 and PR = 22. Write the possible range of PQ = x as a compound inequality.
questions.hint: Lower bound: difference; upper bound: sum.
questions.explanation: 22 − 15 = 7 and 22 + 15 = 37. So the third side satisfies 7 < x < 37.

questions.q: For each pair of triangle sides, give the bounds for the third side: it must be greater than ___ and less than ___.
questions.hint: Subtract for the lower bound, add for the upper bound.

questions.q: In △ABC and △DEF, AB ≅ DE and AC ≅ DF. BC = 9 and EF = 12. Which statement must be true?
questions.hint: Compare the third sides; the larger one is opposite the larger included angle.
questions.explanation: Two pairs of sides are congruent. BC is opposite ∠A and EF is opposite ∠D. Since 9 < 12, the Converse of the Hinge Theorem gives m∠A < m∠D.

questions.q: In △PQR and △STU, PQ ≅ ST and PR ≅ SU. QR = 2x − 4, TU = 16 and m∠P < m∠S. Find the range of possible values of x. Write it as a compound inequality.
questions.hint: QR must be shorter than TU, and also longer than 0.
questions.explanation: By the Hinge Theorem, the smaller included angle is opposite the shorter side, so 2x − 4 < 16, giving x < 10. A side length must be positive, so 2x − 4 > 0, giving x > 2. So 2 < x < 10.

questions.q: In △PQR and △STU, PQ ≅ ST, QR = 10 and TU = 7. Nothing else is known. Which statement must be true?
questions.hint: The Hinge Theorem needs TWO pairs of congruent sides.
questions.explanation: Only one pair of sides is known to be congruent. Without a second pair, neither the Hinge Theorem nor its converse applies, so no angle comparison is guaranteed.

questions.q: In △JKL and △MNP, JK ≅ MN and JL ≅ MP. m∠J = 58° and m∠M = 71°. Which statement must be true?
questions.hint: The larger included angle is opposite the longer third side.
questions.explanation: ∠J is between JK and JL, and ∠M is between MN and MP. Since 58° < 71°, the Hinge Theorem says the side opposite ∠J is shorter: KL < NP.

questions.q: Each row describes two triangles with two pairs of congruent sides. Compare the third side of triangle 1 with the third side of triangle 2 using >, < or =.
questions.hint: The wider the angle between the equal sides, the longer the third side.
questions.explanation: 40° < 55°, so the first third side is shorter (<). Equal angles give congruent triangles by SAS, so the sides are equal (=). 110° > 95°, so the first third side is longer (>).

questions.q: Each leg of a drawing compass is 10 cm long. The compass is first opened to 30° and then to 50°. Complete:

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The gap between the tips at 50° is ___ the gap at 30° (greater than / less than / equal to).

questions.hint: The legs stay the same length; only the angle between them changes.
questions.explanation: The two legs form two pairs of congruent sides. The included angle grows from 30° to 50°, so by the Hinge Theorem the side opposite it (the gap) gets longer.

questions.q: Two triangles share a common side. Each also has a side of length 25 attached to the same end of the shared side. The included angle is 40° in the top triangle, whose third side is 22, and (2x − 6)° in the bottom triangle, whose third side is 18. Find the range of possible values of x.
questions.hint: The shorter third side is opposite the smaller included angle; the angle must also be positive.
questions.explanation: Two pairs of sides are congruent and 18 < 22, so 2x − 6 < 40, giving x < 23. The angle must be positive: 2x − 6 > 0 gives x > 3. So 3 < x < 23.

questions.q: Two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides. In the first triangle the included angle is (5x − 10)° and the third side is 15. In the second the included angle is 50° and the third side is 11. Find the range of possible values of x. Write it as a compound inequality.
questions.hint: 15 > 11, so the first included angle is larger; an angle in a triangle is also less than 180°.
questions.explanation: By the Converse of the Hinge Theorem, 5x − 10 > 50, so x > 12. A triangle angle is less than 180°, so 5x − 10 < 180, giving x < 38. So 12 < x < 38.

questions.q: Two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides. The angle opposite the third side 9 is (3x + 6)°, and the angle opposite the third side 13 is 60°. These are the included angles. Complete:
questions.hint: Shorter third side ↔ smaller included angle.
questions.explanation: Since 9 < 13, the angle (3x + 6)° is smaller than 60°: 3x + 6 < 60 gives x < 18. The angle is positive: 3x + 6 > 0 gives x > −2. So −2 < x < 18.

questions.q: In △PQR, PQ = 9 cm, PR = 14 cm and QR = x cm. Complete:
questions.hint: Use the Triangle Inequality, then match angles to opposite sides.
questions.explanation: The third side is between 14 − 9 = 5 and 14 + 9 = 23. With x = 16, the longest side QR is opposite ∠P, so ∠P is largest. The shortest side PQ = 9 is opposite ∠R, so ∠R is smallest.

questions.q: In △DEF, DE = 12, EF = 7 and DF = 10. Which angle is the largest?
questions.hint: Find the longest side, then the angle across from it.
questions.explanation: The longest side is DE = 12. The angle opposite DE is at the vertex not on it, which is F. So ∠F is the largest angle.

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle are 11 m and 18 m. How many different whole-number lengths are possible for the third side?
questions.hint: Find the range first, then count the whole numbers strictly inside it.
questions.explanation: The third side x satisfies 18 − 11 < x < 18 + 11, so 7 < x < 29. The whole numbers are 8, 9, …, 28, which is 28 − 8 + 1 = 21 values.

questions.q: i. Point K is joined to J, L and M, with JK ≅ KL and KM shared by △JKM and △LKM. m∠JKM = 48° and m∠LKM = 55°. ii. Three towers A, B and C form a triangle with m∠A = 72°, m∠B = 48° and m∠C = 60°. A and B are 5 km apart, and each radio has a 5 km range. Complete:
questions.hint: i: Hinge Theorem. ii: compare each angle with 60°, the angle opposite the 5 km side.
questions.explanation: i: The triangles share KM and have JK ≅ KL; 48° < 55°, so JM < LM. ii: AB = 5 km is opposite ∠C = 60°. AC is opposite ∠B = 48° < 60°, so AC < 5 km and they can talk. BC is opposite ∠A = 72° > 60°, so BC > 5 km and they cannot.

questions.q: In △RST, m∠R = 35°, m∠S = 80° and m∠T = 65°. Which side is the longest?
questions.hint: The longest side is opposite the largest angle.
questions.explanation: The largest angle is ∠S = 80°. The side opposite S is RT, so RT is the longest side.

questions.q: In △UVW, m∠U = 50°, m∠V = 60° and m∠W = 70°. Match each side to its description.
questions.hint: Each side is opposite the angle at the vertex it does not touch.
questions.explanation: VW is opposite ∠U (50°), so it is shortest. UW is opposite ∠V (60°), the middle. UV is opposite ∠W (70°), so it is longest.

questions.q: i. Quadrilateral PQRS has diagonal QS, with PQ ≅ RS, PS = 8 and QR = 9.5. ii. Three cities X, Y and Z form a triangle with m∠X = 47°, m∠Y = 68° and m∠Z = 65°. Complete:

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: m∠PQS is ___ m∠QSR (greater than / less than / equal to)

questions.hint: i: Converse of the Hinge Theorem. ii: longest side is opposite the largest angle.
questions.explanation: i: △PQS and △RSQ share QS and have PQ ≅ RS. PS = 8 is opposite ∠PQS and QR = 9.5 is opposite ∠QSR; 8 < 9.5, so m∠PQS < m∠QSR. ii: The largest angle ∠Y is opposite XZ (farthest), and the smallest angle ∠X is opposite YZ (closest).

questions.q: △ABD and △CBD share side BD, and AB ≅ CB. If AD = 7 and CD = 6, which statement is true?
questions.hint: AD is opposite ∠ABD and CD is opposite ∠CBD.
questions.explanation: The triangles have AB ≅ CB and BD ≅ BD. The third sides are AD = 7 and CD = 6. By the Converse of the Hinge Theorem, the angle opposite the longer side is larger, so m∠ABD > m∠CBD.

questions.q: For each △ABC, name the longest and the shortest side.
questions.hint: The side opposite ∠A is BC, opposite ∠B is AC and opposite ∠C is AB.
questions.explanation: Row 1: largest ∠C → AB longest; smallest ∠A → BC shortest. Row 2: largest ∠A → BC; smallest ∠C → AB. Row 3: largest ∠A → BC; smallest ∠B → AC.

questions.q: Which inequality corresponds to the interval (−5, 1]?
questions.hint: A parenthesis means the endpoint is excluded; a bracket means it is included.
questions.explanation: ( at −5 means −5 is not included: −5 < x. ] at 1 means 1 is included: x ≤ 1. So −5 < x ≤ 1.

questions.q: Match each interval with its inequality.
questions.hint: Brackets give ≤ or ≥; parentheses give < or >; ∞ is never included.
questions.explanation: [2, 7) is 2 ≤ x < 7. (−∞, 4] is x ≤ 4. (−1, ∞) is x > −1 (not ≥, because of the parenthesis). [−3, 0] is −3 ≤ x ≤ 0.

questions.q: Write an inequality in x that corresponds to the interval [0, 8).
questions.hint: [ includes 0; ) excludes 8.
questions.explanation: The bracket at 0 means x ≥ 0, and the parenthesis at 8 means x < 8. Together: 0 ≤ x < 8.

questions.q: Write an inequality in x that corresponds to the interval (−4, 6].
questions.hint: ( excludes −4 and ] includes 6.
questions.explanation: The parenthesis at −4 gives x > −4, and the bracket at 6 gives x ≤ 6. Combined: −4 < x ≤ 6.

questions.q: Write an inequality in x for each interval.
questions.hint: Only finite endpoints appear in the inequality.
questions.explanation: (−∞, −2) is all numbers below −2, not including −2: x < −2. [5, ∞) includes 5: x ≥ 5. (1, 9) excludes both ends: 1 < x < 9.

questions.q: Which inequality corresponds to the interval [−7, −1]?
questions.hint: Square brackets on both ends mean both endpoints are included.
questions.explanation: Both endpoints are included, and −7 is the smaller number, so −7 ≤ x ≤ −1.

questions.q: A number line shows a closed (filled) dot at −4 and an open dot at 5, with the segment between them shaded. Write the set in interval notation.
questions.hint: Closed dot → bracket, open dot → parenthesis.
questions.explanation: −4 is included, so use [ ; 5 is not included, so use ). The interval is [−4, 5).

questions.q: Match each number-line description with its interval.

left: open dot at −2, shaded to the right forever
closed dot at 3, shaded to the left forever
closed dots at −1 and 6, shaded between
open dot at 0 and closed dot at 4, shaded between

questions.hint: Shading forever to one side uses ∞ or −∞ with a parenthesis.
questions.explanation: Open dot at −2 going right: (−2, ∞). Closed dot at 3 going left: (−∞, 3]. Closed dots at −1 and 6: [−1, 6]. Open at 0, closed at 4: (0, 4].

questions.q: A number line shows an open circle at −6 and a closed circle at 3, with the segment between them shaded.
questions.hint: An open circle means the endpoint is not included.
questions.explanation: The open circle at −6 gives ( and <, and the closed circle at 3 gives ] and ≤. So the set is (−6, 3], i.e. −6 < x ≤ 3, and −6 is not included.

questions.q: A number line has a closed (filled) dot at 1 with the arrow shaded to the left. Which interval does it show?
questions.hint: Shading left means all smaller numbers.
questions.explanation: The shading goes left forever, so the set starts at −∞. The closed dot means 1 is included. The interval is (−∞, 1].

questions.q: Use interval notation to describe: "Mariam is older than 12 years."
questions.hint: "Older than" does not include 12.
questions.explanation: Older than 12 means age a > 12, with no upper limit given. In interval notation that is (12, ∞).
