questions.explanation: Both closed: [−2, 4]. Open left end: (−2, 4]. Open right end: [−2, 4). A ray going right forever: [−2, ∞).

questions.q: State the domain of f(x) = (x + 2)/(x² − 6x + 9).
questions.hint: Factor the denominator; it is a perfect square.
questions.explanation: x² − 6x + 9 = (x − 3)², which is zero only at x = 3. The numerator does not restrict the domain.

questions.q: Which single value of x is excluded from the domain of f(x) = (x − 4)/(x² + 10x + 25)?
questions.hint: x² + 10x + 25 is a perfect square trinomial.
questions.explanation: x² + 10x + 25 = (x + 5)², which is zero only when x = −5.

questions.q: Match each function with its domain.
questions.hint: Factor each denominator and find its zeros.
questions.explanation: (x − 4)² = 0 only at 4. (x − 4)(x + 4) = 0 at ±4. x² + 16 is always positive, so no restriction. x(x + 4) = 0 at 0 and −4.

questions.q: Given f(x) = −1 if x < −3; f(x) = √(x + 3) if −3 ≤ x ≤ 6; f(x) = x² − 2 if x > 6. Find f(−5).
questions.hint: Check which condition −5 satisfies.
questions.explanation: −5 < −3, so the first piece applies and f(−5) = −1. Using x² − 2 would wrongly give 23.

questions.q: Given f(x) = −1 if x < −3; f(x) = √(x + 3) if −3 ≤ x ≤ 6; f(x) = x² − 2 if x > 6. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Boundary values −3 and 6 belong to the middle piece.

questions.q: Given f(x) = −1 if x < −3; f(x) = √(x + 3) if −3 ≤ x ≤ 6; f(x) = x² − 2 if x > 6. Find f(8).
questions.hint: 8 is greater than 6.

questions.q: Use the continuity test for f(x) = x² + 2x − 1 at x = 2.
questions.hint: Check that f(2) exists, the limit exists, and they are equal.
questions.explanation: f(2) = 4 + 4 − 1 = 7. A polynomial's limit is found by substitution, so the limit is also 7. Since the limit equals f(2), f is continuous at x = 2.

questions.q: Is f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) continuous at x = 2?
options: No, because the limit as x → 2 does not exist.
Yes, because the limit as x → 2 is 4.
questions.hint: Try to evaluate f(2) first.
questions.explanation: Substituting x = 2 gives 0/0, so f(2) is undefined and the first condition of the continuity test fails. The limit does exist (it is 4), but that is not enough.

questions.q: Match each function with the result of the continuity test at x = 1.

left: f(x) = x + 1 for x < 1, and 5 for x ≥ 1
right: the limit exists but is not f(1)

questions.hint: Check the three conditions: f(1) defined, limit exists, limit equals f(1).
questions.explanation: The polynomial has limit 2 = f(1): continuous. (x² − 1)/(x − 1) gives 0/0 at 1. The third has left limit 2 and right limit 5, so no limit. The last has limit 3 but f(1) = 1.

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = −3x³ + 2x² − x + 4. Type ∞ or −∞.
questions.hint: Only the leading term −3x³ matters.
questions.explanation: The leading term −3x³ has odd degree and a negative coefficient, so the graph rises on the left and falls on the right: f → −∞ as x → ∞ and f → ∞ as x → −∞.

questions.q: Match each polynomial with its end behavior.
questions.hint: Look at the degree (even/odd) and the sign of the leading coefficient.
questions.explanation: Even degree, positive: both ends up. Odd degree, negative: up on the left, down on the right. Odd degree, positive: down on the left, up on the right. Even degree, negative: both ends down.

questions.q: Which function has f(x) → ∞ both as x → −∞ and as x → ∞?
questions.hint: You need an even degree and a positive leading coefficient.
questions.explanation: x⁴ − 5x³ has leading term x⁴: even degree, positive coefficient, so both ends rise. −x⁴ + 2 falls on both ends, and the cubics go in opposite directions.

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = 2x⁵ − 3x⁴ + x − 10.
options: lim x→−∞ f(x) = ∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = −∞
lim x→−∞ f(x) = ∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = ∞
lim x→−∞ f(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = −∞
lim x→−∞ f(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = ∞
questions.hint: Use the leading term 2x⁵.
questions.explanation: 2x⁵ has odd degree and a positive coefficient, so f(x) → −∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → ∞ as x → ∞.

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = −x³ + 4x² + 1. Type ∞ or −∞.
questions.hint: The leading term is −x³.
questions.explanation: For large negative x, −x³ is large and positive, so f → ∞. For large positive x, −x³ is large and negative, so f → −∞.

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = 6x − 2x² + 3x⁴.
options: lim x→−∞ f(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = ∞
lim x→−∞ f(x) = ∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = ∞
lim x→−∞ f(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = −∞
lim x→−∞ f(x) = ∞ and lim x→∞ f(x) = −∞
questions.hint: Rewrite in standard form to find the leading term.
questions.explanation: In standard form f(x) = 3x⁴ − 2x² + 6x, so the leading term is 3x⁴: even degree with a positive coefficient. Both ends go to ∞.

questions.q: A particle's position is s(t) = t² − 4t + 6 meters at time t seconds. Find its average rate of change from t = 2 to t = 6, in m/s.
questions.hint: Average rate = (s(6) − s(2))/(6 − 2).

questions.q: The position of an object is s(t) = 2t² + t meters. What is its average velocity from t = 1 to t = 3 seconds?
questions.hint: Divide the change in position by the change in time.

questions.q: For f(t) = t² − 3t + 2, complete the average rate of change over each interval.
questions.hint: Use (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).

questions.q: A shop's revenue from selling x items is R(x) = 50x − x² AED. Find the average rate of change of revenue from x = 10 to x = 20 items, in AED per item.
questions.hint: Compute R(20) and R(10) first.

questions.q: Find the average rate of change of f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2x − 1 on the interval [1, 3].
What is the average rate of change of g(x) = 2x² − 5x + 1 on the interval [−1, 2]?
questions.hint: Find g(2) and g(−1), then divide the change in g by the change in x.

questions.q: For h(x) = x³ − 4x, complete the table. The average rate of change on [a, b] is (h(b) − h(a)) ÷ (b − a).
questions.hint: Substitute each endpoint into h(x) = x³ − 4x before dividing.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2 rises to a peak at (0, 2), falls to a valley at (2, −2), and then rises again. Write each answer as an interval (or 'none').
questions.hint: Read the x-coordinates of the peak and the valley; the function changes direction there.
questions.explanation: Moving left to right, the graph goes up until x = 0, down from x = 0 to x = 2, and up after x = 2. So f is increasing on (−∞, 0) ∪ (2, ∞) and decreasing on (0, 2). A cubic never has a flat piece, so it is constant nowhere.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = −x³ + 3x has a valley at (−1, −2) and a peak at (1, 2), and falls to the right. On which interval is f increasing?
questions.hint: The graph goes up between the valley and the peak.
questions.explanation: Because the leading coefficient is negative, the graph comes down from the left to the valley at x = −1, rises to the peak at x = 1, then falls. So f is increasing only on (−1, 1). The interval (−2, 2) uses y-values, which is a common mistake.

questions.q: A graph is made of three straight pieces: it rises from (−4, −1) to (−1, 3), stays level from (−1, 3) to (2, 3), and falls from (2, 3) to (5, −2). Match each interval to the behaviour of the function.
questions.hint: Check whether the y-values go up, stay the same, or go down as x increases.
questions.explanation: From x = −4 to x = −1 the y-values go from −1 up to 3, so the function is increasing. From x = −1 to x = 2 the y-value stays 3, so it is constant. From x = 2 to x = 5 the y-values drop from 3 to −2, so it is decreasing.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³ flattens out at the origin (without turning) and has a single valley at x = 3. Estimate and classify the extrema.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Type of this minimum (absolute or relative only):

questions.hint: Evaluate f at the valley; a quartic with positive leading coefficient rises without bound at both ends.
questions.explanation: f(3) = 81 − 108 = −27. Both ends go up to ∞, so this lowest point is an absolute minimum. At x = 0 the graph only levels off and keeps falling, so it is not an extremum. Since f(x) → ∞ at both ends, there is no maximum.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 2x² has turning points at x = −1, x = 0 and x = 1. Which statement correctly classifies the extrema?
options: Absolute minimum 0 at x = 0; relative maximum −1 at x = ±1
Absolute minimum −1 at x = ±1; relative maximum 0 at x = 0
No absolute minimum; relative minima −1 at x = ±1
Absolute maximum 0 at x = 0; relative minimum −1 at x = ±1
questions.hint: Find f(−1), f(0) and f(1), and remember both ends rise to ∞.
questions.explanation: f(±1) = 1 − 2 = −1 and f(0) = 0. The graph rises to ∞ at both ends, so the lowest value −1 is an absolute minimum (at x = ±1). The peak at (0, 0) is higher than nearby points but not the highest point overall, so it is a relative maximum.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 8x² turns at x = −2, x = 0 and x = 2. Complete the table. Classify each point as 'absolute minimum', 'relative maximum', etc.
questions.hint: Evaluate f at each turning point and compare; both ends of the graph go up.
questions.explanation: f(±2) = 16 − 32 = −16 and f(0) = 0. Since the graph rises to ∞ at both ends, −16 is the lowest value, so x = ±2 give absolute minima. The point (0, 0) is a peak between them but not the highest point overall, so it is a relative maximum.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x² turns at x = 0 and at x = 2. Estimate and classify the extrema. Give points as (x, y).
questions.hint: Evaluate f at each turning point; a cubic goes to ±∞ at its ends.
questions.explanation: f(0) = 0 and f(2) = 8 − 12 = −4. The graph rises to (0, 0) and then falls to (2, −4) before rising again, so (0, 0) is a relative maximum and (2, −4) a relative minimum. Because a cubic goes to −∞ and ∞ at its ends, there are no absolute extrema.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x³ − 12x turns at x = −2 and x = 2. Which statement classifies the extrema correctly?
questions.hint: Find f(−2) and f(2), then decide which is the peak.
questions.explanation: f(−2) = −8 + 24 = 16 and f(2) = 8 − 24 = −16. The cubic rises to (−2, 16), falls to (2, −16), then rises again. These are relative (not absolute) extrema, because the ends of the graph go to −∞ and ∞.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x + 2 turns at x = −1 and x = 1. Plot the relative maximum and the relative minimum.
questions.hint: Substitute x = −1 and x = 1 into f(x).
questions.explanation: f(−1) = −1 + 3 + 2 = 4 and f(1) = 1 − 3 + 2 = 0. The relative maximum is (−1, 4) and the relative minimum is (1, 0).

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = −2x³ + 5x.
options: f(x) → −∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞
f(x) → −∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → ∞ as x → ∞
f(x) → ∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → ∞ as x → ∞
f(x) → ∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞
questions.hint: Look only at the leading term −2x³: odd degree, negative coefficient.
questions.explanation: For large |x| the term −2x³ dominates. When x is a large negative number, x³ is negative, so −2x³ is positive: f(x) → ∞. When x is a large positive number, −2x³ is negative: f(x) → −∞.

questions.q: Match each function to its end behavior.

right: up on the left, up on the right
down on the left, down on the right
down on the left, up on the right
up on the left, down on the right

questions.hint: Use the degree (even or odd) and the sign of the leading coefficient.
questions.explanation: Even degree with positive leading coefficient (x⁴) goes up at both ends; even with negative (−x²) goes down at both ends. Odd with positive (2x⁵) goes down on the left and up on the right; odd with negative (−x³) goes up on the left and down on the right.

questions.q: Complete the end behavior of f(x) = −x⁴ + 2x³. Type ∞ or −∞.
questions.hint: The leading term −x⁴ has even degree and a negative coefficient.
questions.explanation: For large |x| the term −x⁴ dominates. x⁴ is positive for both large positive and large negative x, so −x⁴ is very negative. So f(x) → −∞ at both ends.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 1 has a peak at (0, 1) and a valley at (2, −3). On which interval is f decreasing?
questions.hint: The graph goes down from the peak to the valley; use x-values.
questions.explanation: Reading left to right, the graph rises to the peak at x = 0, falls to the valley at x = 2, then rises again. So f is decreasing on (0, 2). (−3, 1) uses the y-values instead of the x-values.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = −x³ + 12x has a valley at (−2, −16) and a peak at (2, 16). Write the interval on which f is increasing, in interval notation.
questions.hint: With a negative leading coefficient, the graph falls on the far left and far right.
questions.explanation: The graph comes down from the left to the valley at x = −2, rises to the peak at x = 2, then falls. So f is increasing on (−2, 2).

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x has a peak at (1, 4) and a valley at (3, 0). Match each interval to the behavior of f.
questions.hint: A positive cubic rises, turns at the peak, falls to the valley, then rises.
questions.explanation: Left of the peak at x = 1 the graph is going up, so f is increasing on (−∞, 1). Between the peak and the valley it goes down, so it is decreasing on (1, 3). After the valley at x = 3 it goes up again, so it is increasing on (3, ∞).

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are true about g(x) = |x + 3| + 5 compared with f(x) = |x|?
I. Moved 3 units left
II. Moved 5 units down
III. Moved 5 units up
questions.hint: x + 3 inside the bars shifts horizontally; + 5 outside shifts vertically.
questions.explanation: |x + 3| = |x − (−3)|, so the graph moves 3 units left (I is true). Adding 5 outside the absolute value moves it 5 units up (III is true, II is false). So the answer is I and III only.

questions.q: Match each function to how its graph is obtained from y = |x|.
questions.hint: y = |x − h| + k moves the vertex from (0, 0) to (h, k).
questions.explanation: The vertex of y = |x − h| + k is (h, k). So |x − 2| + 1 has vertex (2, 1): right 2, up 1. |x + 2| − 1 has vertex (−2, −1): left 2, down 1. |x − 1| − 2 has vertex (1, −2), and |x + 1| + 2 has vertex (−1, 2).

questions.q: Graph y = |x − 4| − 2 by plotting its vertex and its two x-intercepts (connect them in order from left to right).
questions.hint: The vertex is (h, k) for y = |x − h| + k; then solve |x − 4| = 2.
questions.explanation: The graph is y = |x| moved 4 right and 2 down, so the vertex is (4, −2). Setting y = 0 gives |x − 4| = 2, so x = 2 or x = 6. The points are (2, 0), (4, −2) and (6, 0).

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = |x| is vertically compressed by a factor of 1/3, reflected across the x-axis and then shifted 4 units up. Which is the new function?
questions.hint: Apply the compression and reflection to the coefficient, then add the vertical shift outside.
questions.explanation: Compressing by 1/3 gives (1/3)|x|. Reflecting across the x-axis makes it −(1/3)|x|. Shifting up 4 adds 4 outside: g(x) = −(1/3)|x| + 4.

questions.q: The graph of f(x) = |x| is vertically stretched by a factor of 5, shifted 2 units left and then 3 units down. Write the equation of the new function g(x).
questions.hint: A shift left by 2 replaces x with x + 2.
questions.explanation: Stretching by 5 gives 5|x|. Shifting 2 units left replaces x with x + 2: 5|x + 2|. Shifting 3 units down subtracts 3: g(x) = 5|x + 2| − 3.

questions.q: Describe g(x) = −3|x − 1| + 2 as a transformation of f(x) = |x|.
questions.hint: Compare with a|x − h| + k: vertex (h, k), a gives stretch and reflection.
questions.explanation: Here a = −3, h = 1 and k = 2. The vertex is (1, 2). The negative sign reflects the graph so it opens down, and |a| = 3 is a vertical stretch by 3. The graph is shifted 1 unit right and 2 units up.

questions.q: Graph g(x) = −2|x| + 3 by plotting its vertex and the points where x = −2 and x = 2 (connect them from left to right).
questions.hint: Find g(0), g(−2) and g(2).
questions.explanation: g(0) = 3, so the vertex is (0, 3). g(2) = −4 + 3 = −1 and g(−2) = −1. The graph is an upside-down V through (−2, −1), (0, 3) and (2, −1).

questions.q: The graph of y = |x| is vertically stretched by a factor of 3, translated 1 unit right and then translated 2 units up. Write the equation of the new function.
questions.hint: Right 1 means x − 1 inside the absolute value; up 2 means + 2 outside.
questions.explanation: Stretching by 3 gives 3|x|. Moving right 1 replaces x with x − 1: 3|x − 1|. Moving up 2 adds 2: y = 3|x − 1| + 2.

questions.q: The graph of y = x² is vertically compressed by a factor of 0.25, translated 3 units left and then 1 unit down. Which equation describes the new graph?
questions.hint: A left shift adds inside the parentheses; a compression multiplies by a number between 0 and 1.
questions.explanation: Compression by 0.25 gives 0.25x². Moving 3 units left gives 0.25(x + 3)². Moving 1 unit down gives y = 0.25(x + 3)² − 1.

questions.q: The graph of y = |x| is compressed vertically by a factor of 0.5, translated 2 units right and 1 unit down, giving y = 0.5|x − 2| − 1. Plot its vertex and its two x-intercepts (connect from left to right).
questions.hint: The vertex is (2, −1); solve 0.5|x − 2| = 1 for the intercepts.
questions.explanation: The vertex moves from (0, 0) to (2, −1). Setting y = 0 gives 0.5|x − 2| = 1, so |x − 2| = 2 and x = 0 or x = 4. Plot (0, 0), (2, −1) and (4, 0).

questions.q: The graph of y = x² is reflected in the x-axis, vertically stretched by a factor of 3, translated 1 unit left and then 4 units down. Write the equation of the new function.
questions.hint: Reflection and stretch give the coefficient −3; left 1 gives (x + 1).
questions.explanation: Reflecting and stretching gives −3x². Moving 1 unit left gives −3(x + 1)². Moving 4 units down gives y = −3(x + 1)² − 4.

questions.q: Which sequence of transformations of y = x² produces y = −(x − 4)² + 1?
options: Reflect in the y-axis, translate 4 right and 1 up
Reflect in the x-axis, translate 4 left and 1 up
Reflect in the x-axis, translate 1 right and 4 up
Reflect in the x-axis, translate 4 right and 1 up
questions.hint: Compare with a(x − h)² + k.
questions.explanation: Here a = −1, h = 4 and k = 1. The negative sign is a reflection in the x-axis, (x − 4) is a shift 4 units right, and + 1 is a shift 1 unit up.

questions.q: For y = −2(x + 3)² + 5, describe the transformation of y = x².
questions.hint: Write the equation as a(x − h)² + k with h = −3.
questions.explanation: y = −2(x − (−3))² + 5, so the vertex is (−3, 5). Because a = −2 is negative, the parabola is reflected and opens down. |a| = 2 is a vertical stretch by a factor of 2.

questions.q: Graph y = −(x − 1)² + 4 by plotting the five points with x = −1, 0, 1, 2 and 3 (connect them in order).
questions.hint: Start at the vertex (1, 4) and use the symmetry about x = 1.

questions.q: Match each function to its parent function.
questions.hint: Ignore the shifts and look at the basic operation applied to x.
questions.explanation: √(x − 2) + 1 is a shifted √x, so its parent is the square root function. |x + 3| − 2 comes from |x|, (x − 1)² + 4 from x², and (x + 2)³ from x³. None of them is linear.

questions.q: A graph starts at the endpoint (−2, 1) and curves upward to the right through (−1, 2), (2, 3) and (7, 4).
questions.hint: A curve that starts at an endpoint and flattens out is a square-root graph; the endpoint gives (h, k).
questions.explanation: The shape is the square root graph moved so its starting point (0, 0) goes to (−2, 1): 2 left and 1 up. So g(x) = √(x + 2) + 1. Check: g(2) = √4 + 1 = 3 and g(7) = √9 + 1 = 4.

questions.q: A V-shaped graph opens upward with its vertex at (3, −2) and passes through (1, 0) and (5, 0). Which function is it?
questions.hint: The vertex (h, k) gives g(x) = a|x − h| + k; check the slope from the vertex.
questions.explanation: The parent is |x|. The vertex moved to (3, −2), so g(x) = a|x − 3| − 2. From (3, −2) to (5, 0) the graph rises 2 over 2, so a = 1 and g(x) = |x − 3| − 2.

questions.q: An upside-down V graph has its vertex at (−1, 3) and passes through (−3, 1) and (1, 1). Write g(x) as a transformation of f(x) = |x|.
questions.hint: Opening down means the coefficient is negative; the vertex gives the shifts.
questions.explanation: The vertex (−1, 3) means a shift 1 left and 3 up. From (−1, 3) to (1, 1) the graph falls 2 over 2, so a = −1. So g(x) = −|x + 1| + 3, the graph of |x| reflected in the x-axis and translated 1 left and 3 up.

questions.q: The graph of g(x) has the same shape as f(x) = x³, but its point of symmetry (inflection point) is at (2, 0) instead of (0, 0). How are the graphs related?
options: g is f translated 2 units left; g(x) = (x + 2)³
g is f translated 2 units up; g(x) = x³ + 2
g is f translated 2 units right; g(x) = x³ − 2
g is f translated 2 units right; g(x) = (x − 2)³
questions.hint: A horizontal shift changes the x inside the cube.
questions.explanation: The inflection point moved from (0, 0) to (2, 0), which is 2 units right. A shift right by 2 replaces x with x − 2, so g(x) = (x − 2)³. x³ − 2 would be a shift down, not right.

questions.q: The graph of g(x) has the same shape as f(x) = x³, but its inflection point is at (0, 4). Write an equation for g(x).
questions.hint: The point moved straight up.
questions.explanation: The inflection point moved from (0, 0) to (0, 4), so the graph is f translated 4 units up. Adding 4 outside gives g(x) = x³ + 4.

questions.q: Let f(x) = x³ and g(x) = x³ − 2. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Each g-value is the f-value minus 2.
questions.explanation: f(−1) = −1 and f(1) = 1. Subtracting 2 from every f-value gives g: −10, −3, −2, −1, 6. The graph of g is the graph of f translated 2 units down.

questions.q: Graph g(x) = (x + 1)³ by plotting the points with x = −3, −2, −1, 0 and 1 (connect them in order).
questions.hint: This is y = x³ moved 1 unit left, so the inflection point is (−1, 0).
questions.explanation: g(−3) = (−2)³ = −8, g(−2) = (−1)³ = −1, g(−1) = 0, g(0) = 1 and g(1) = 2³ = 8. These are the points of x³ shifted 1 unit left.

questions.q: Given f(x) = x² − 9 and g(x) = x + 3, find (f + g)(x).
questions.hint: Add the like terms of the two expressions.

questions.q: Given f(x) = 3x² + 2x − 5 and g(x) = x² − 4x + 1, find (f − g)(x) in simplest form.
questions.hint: Subtract every term of g, so change all its signs.

questions.q: Let f(x) = x² − 1 and g(x) = 2x + 3. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Find f(x) and g(x) first, then add and multiply them.
questions.explanation: f(−1) = 0 and g(−1) = 1, so the sum is 1 and the product 0. f(0) = −1 and g(0) = 3, giving 2 and −3. f(2) = 3 and g(2) = 7, giving 10 and 21.

questions.q: Given f(x) = x + 5 and g(x) = x − 5:

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Value excluded from the domain of f/g: x ≠

questions.hint: Multiply using the difference of squares; division needs g(x) ≠ 0.
questions.explanation: (f · g)(x) = (x + 5)(x − 5) = x² − 25. (f/g)(x) = (x + 5)/(x − 5), and the denominator is 0 when x = 5, so x ≠ 5.

questions.q: If f(x) = 3x + 2 and g(x) = x², find g(f(−2)).
questions.hint: Work from the inside out: find f(−2) first.
questions.explanation: f(−2) = 3(−2) + 2 = −4. Then g(−4) = (−4)² = 16. (14 is f(g(−2)), the composition in the wrong order.)

questions.q: If f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = 2x − 3, find f(g(3)).
questions.hint: Find g(3) first, then put the result into f.

questions.q: Let f(x) = x − 4 and g(x) = 2x. Complete the table.
questions.hint: For g(f(x)) double f(x); for f(g(x)) double x first, then subtract 4.

questions.q: Given f(x) = 3x − 2, find f(f(x)).
questions.hint: Replace x in f(x) with the whole expression 3x − 2.

questions.q: Given f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = x − 3, find f(g(x)) in expanded form.
questions.hint: Substitute x − 3 into f, then expand (x − 3)².

questions.q: Let f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 1. Match each composition to its simplified form.
questions.hint: Work from the inside out each time.

questions.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x² + 3, x ≥ 0.
questions.hint: Swap x and y, then solve for y, keeping the positive root.
questions.explanation: Write x = y² + 3. Then y² = x − 3, so y = √(x − 3) (positive root because the original x ≥ 0). So f⁻¹(x) = √(x − 3).

questions.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x² − 4, x ≥ 0.
questions.hint: Swap x and y and solve; take the positive square root.
questions.explanation: x = y² − 4 gives y² = x + 4, so y = √(x + 4). Since the original domain is x ≥ 0, the inverse uses the positive root: f⁻¹(x) = √(x + 4).

questions.q: Let f(x) = (x − 2)², x ≥ 2.
questions.hint: The domain of f⁻¹ is the range of f, and the range of f⁻¹ is the domain of f.
questions.explanation: Swap: x = (y − 2)², so y − 2 = √x (positive since y ≥ 2) and f⁻¹(x) = √x + 2. f has range y ≥ 0, so f⁻¹ has domain x ≥ 0. f has domain x ≥ 2, so f⁻¹ has range y ≥ 2.

questions.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = √(x − 3).
questions.hint: Swap x and y, then square both sides.
questions.explanation: x = √(y − 3), so x² = y − 3 and y = x² + 3. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse has domain x ≥ 0.

questions.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = √(2x + 1). (Its domain is x ≥ 0.)
questions.hint: Swap x and y, square both sides, then solve for y.
questions.explanation: x = √(2y + 1), so x² = 2y + 1, 2y = x² − 1 and y = (x² − 1)/2. So f⁻¹(x) = (x² − 1)/2 for x ≥ 0.

questions.q: Let f(x) = √(x + 5). Complete the table of values for f and for its inverse f⁻¹.
questions.hint: The inverse undoes f: if f(a) = b then f⁻¹(b) = a.
questions.explanation: f(−5) = √0 = 0, f(−1) = √4 = 2, f(4) = √9 = 3 and f(11) = √16 = 4. The inverse swaps inputs and outputs, so f⁻¹(0) = −5, f⁻¹(2) = −1, f⁻¹(3) = 4 and f⁻¹(4) = 11. This agrees with f⁻¹(x) = x² − 5.

questions.q: Use f(x) = 2x/(x + 1) to state the domain and range of f⁻¹.
questions.hint: The domain of f⁻¹ is the range of f, and the range of f⁻¹ is the domain of f.
questions.explanation: f has domain x ≠ −1 and horizontal asymptote y = 2, so its range is y ≠ 2. f is one-to-one, so f⁻¹ exists with domain (−∞, 2) ∪ (2, ∞) and range (−∞, −1) ∪ (−1, ∞).

questions.hint: Swap x and y, multiply out and collect the y-terms on one side.
questions.explanation: x = (y + 4)/(y − 3) gives xy − 3x = y + 4, so y(x − 1) = 3x + 4 and f⁻¹(x) = (3x + 4)/(x − 1). The domain of f⁻¹ is x ≠ 1 (the range of f). The range of f⁻¹ is y ≠ 3 (the domain of f).

questions.q: Let f(x) = 5x/(x − 4). Write the domain of f⁻¹ in interval notation.
questions.hint: The domain of f⁻¹ equals the range of f; find the horizontal asymptote of f.
questions.explanation: The degrees of top and bottom are equal, so f has horizontal asymptote y = 5/1 = 5 and its range is y ≠ 5. So the domain of f⁻¹ is (−∞, 5) ∪ (5, ∞).

questions.q: Which pair of functions are inverses of each other?
questions.hint: Check whether f(g(x)) = x for each pair.
questions.explanation: For x³ + 1 and ∛(x − 1): f(g(x)) = (x − 1) + 1 = x and g(f(x)) = ∛(x³) = x, so they are inverses. For the others: 4(2√x)² = 16x, 2(½x + 1) + 1 = x + 3, and (5 − x) − 5 = −x, none of which is x.

questions.q: Let f(x) = 4x² and g(x) = 3√(x + 2). Simplify f(g(x)).
questions.hint: Square g(x) first: (3√(x + 2))² = 9(x + 2).
questions.explanation: f(g(x)) = 4(3√(x + 2))² = 4 · 9(x + 2) = 36x + 72. Since this is not x, f and g are not inverses.

questions.q: Determine whether f(x) = 2x² and g(x) = √(2x) are inverses.
questions.hint: Square √(2x), then multiply by 2.
questions.explanation: f(g(x)) = 2(√(2x))² = 2 · 2x = 4x. For inverses we need f(g(x)) = x, so they are not inverses.

questions.q: Determine whether f(x) = 3x + 12 and g(x) = ⅓x − 4 are inverse functions.
options: Yes, because f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x
questions.hint: Compute both compositions.
questions.explanation: f(g(x)) = 3(⅓x − 4) + 12 = x − 12 + 12 = x and g(f(x)) = ⅓(3x + 12) − 4 = x + 4 − 4 = x. Both give x, so they are inverses.

questions.q: Let f(x) = 4x − 8 and g(x) = ¼x + 2.
questions.hint: Substitute each function into the other and simplify.
questions.explanation: f(g(x)) = 4(¼x + 2) − 8 = x + 8 − 8 = x. g(f(x)) = ¼(4x − 8) + 2 = x − 2 + 2 = x. Both compositions are x, so f and g are inverses.

questions.q: Let f(x) = 5x + 10 and g(x) = ⅕x + 2. Simplify f(g(x)).
questions.hint: Distribute the 5, then add 10.
questions.explanation: f(g(x)) = 5(⅕x + 2) + 10 = x + 10 + 10 = x + 20. Since this is not x, the functions are not inverses (the inverse of f would be ⅕x − 2).

questions.q: Match each function to its inverse.
questions.hint: Undo the operations in reverse order.
questions.explanation: 2x − 6: add 6 then halve, giving ½x + 3. 3x + 1: subtract 1 then divide by 3, giving (x − 1)/3. x/4 is undone by 4x, and x + 7 by x − 7.

questions.q: A line passes through (0, 3) and (1, 1). Graph its inverse.
questions.hint: Swap the x- and y-coordinates of points on the original line.
questions.explanation: Swapping the coordinates of (0, 3) and (1, 1) gives (3, 0) and (1, 1). The original line is y = −2x + 3 and its inverse is y = (3 − x)/2, which passes through these points.

questions.q: Graph the inverse of f(x) = 3x − 3.
questions.hint: Find two points on f, then swap their coordinates.
questions.explanation: f passes through (0, −3) and (1, 0). Swapping gives (−3, 0) and (0, 1), which lie on f⁻¹(x) = (x + 3)/3 = ⅓x + 1.

questions.q: A line passes through (0, −4) and (2, 0). Which equation is its inverse?
questions.hint: Find the line's equation, then swap x and y.
questions.explanation: The slope is (0 − (−4)) ÷ 2 = 2, so y = 2x − 4. Swapping gives x = 2y − 4, so y = (x + 4)/2 = ½x + 2. Check: it passes through the swapped points (−4, 0) and (0, 2).

questions.q: A line passes through (0, 1) and (2, 7). Write the equation of its inverse as y = …
questions.hint: The slope of the line is (7 − 1)/(2 − 0).
questions.explanation: The slope is 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so the line is y = 3x + 1. Swapping x and y: x = 3y + 1, so y = (x − 1)/3.

questions.q: Match each relation to the correct description.

left: x = y² (a parabola opening to the right)
right: function; inverse is not a function
not a function; inverse is a function
not a function; inverse is not a function

questions.hint: Use the vertical line test for the relation and the horizontal line test for its inverse.
questions.explanation: y = x³ passes both tests. y = x² passes the vertical line test but fails the horizontal one. A sideways parabola fails the vertical test but passes the horizontal test (its inverse is y = x²). A circle fails both tests.

questions.q: For which function is the inverse also a function?
questions.hint: The inverse is a function only if the graph passes the horizontal line test.
questions.explanation: |x|, x² − 4 and x⁴ all give the same y-value for x and −x, so they fail the horizontal line test. The line y = 2x + 5 is one-to-one, so its inverse is a function.

questions.q: Consider the relation {(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 3), (4, 7)}. Answer yes or no.
questions.hint: The inverse swaps every pair; check for repeated first coordinates.
questions.explanation: Each x-value 1, 2, 3, 4 appears once, so the relation is a function. The inverse is {(3, 1), (5, 2), (3, 3), (7, 4)}, where 3 is paired with both 1 and 3, so the inverse is not a function.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (3x + 4)/x and g(x) = 2x + 1. Write each answer as a single fraction.
questions.hint: For the sum, write g(x) over the denominator x; for f(g(x)), replace every x in f with 2x + 1.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (x + 2)/x and g(x) = 3x − 1, find f(g(x)).
questions.hint: Replace every x in f(x) with 3x − 1.
questions.explanation: f(g(x)) = ((3x − 1) + 2)/(3x − 1) = (3x + 1)/(3x − 1). (2x + 6)/x is g(f(x)), the composition in the other order.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (4x − 2)/x and g(x) = x + 5, find (f + g)(x) as a single fraction.
questions.hint: Rewrite x + 5 as (x² + 5x)/x.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (2x + 8)/x and g(x) = 3x − 2. Write fractions in simplest form.
questions.hint: Subtract every term of g; for the composition, the new denominator must not be 0.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (x + 6)/x and g(x) = x − 3, find (f − g)(x).
questions.hint: Write g(x) as (x² − 3x)/x and subtract the whole numerator.
questions.explanation: (f − g)(x) = (x + 6)/x − (x² − 3x)/x = (x + 6 − x² + 3x)/x = (−x² + 4x + 6)/x. Forgetting to change the sign of −3x gives the wrong answer (−x² − 2x + 6)/x.

questions.q: Given f(x) = (5x − 1)/x and g(x) = 2x + 3, find f(g(x)) as a single fraction.
questions.hint: Replace each x in f with 2x + 3.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = 2^(−x). Give fractions where needed.
questions.hint: 2^(−x) = (½)^x, so a negative x gives a positive power of 2.

questions.q: Describe f(x) = (1/4)^x.
questions.hint: The base 1/4 is between 0 and 1.
questions.explanation: Any real x can be used, so the domain is (−∞, ∞). Powers of 1/4 are always positive, so the range is (0, ∞) and y = 0 is a horizontal asymptote. f(0) = 1 is the y-intercept. Because 0 < 1/4 < 1, the function is decreasing everywhere.

questions.q: Plot the points of f(x) = 2^(−x) for x = −3, −2, −1 and 0.
questions.hint: 2^(−x) doubles each time x decreases by 1.

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = 5^(−x).
options: f(x) → 0 as x → −∞ and f(x) → ∞ as x → ∞
f(x) → −∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → 0 as x → ∞
f(x) → ∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → 0 as x → ∞
f(x) → ∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞
questions.hint: 5^(−x) = (1/5)^x is a decaying exponential.
questions.explanation: For large negative x, −x is large and positive, so 5^(−x) grows without bound. For large positive x, 5^(−x) = 1/5^x gets close to 0 but stays positive.

questions.q: Which of the following is the y-intercept of f(x) = log₂(x + 8) − 1?
questions.hint: Find f(0) and check that 0 is in the domain.
questions.explanation: The domain is x > −8, which includes 0. f(0) = log₂8 − 1 = 3 − 1 = 2, so the y-intercept is 2.

questions.q: Let f(x) = log₅(x + 25) − 3.
questions.hint: The argument must be positive; for the x-intercept, solve log₅(x + 25) = 3.
questions.explanation: x + 25 > 0 gives x > −25. f(0) = log₅25 − 3 = 2 − 3 = −1. Setting f(x) = 0 gives log₅(x + 25) = 3, so x + 25 = 125 and x = 100.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = log₂(x − 1) + 2, and give the domain.
questions.hint: x − 1 is 1, 2, 4 and 8 for these x-values.
questions.explanation: log₂1 = 0, log₂2 = 1, log₂4 = 2 and log₂8 = 3; adding 2 gives 2, 3, 4 and 5. The argument x − 1 must be positive, so the domain is x > 1 (and there is no y-intercept).

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true about f(x) = a·b^(x − h) + k?
options: If h > 0, the graph is shifted h units left
The horizontal asymptote is y = k
If a < 0, the graph is reflected in the x-axis
If 0 < |a| < 1, the graph is compressed vertically
questions.hint: Remember that x − h with h > 0 moves the graph right.
questions.explanation: Replacing x with x − h moves the graph h units to the right when h > 0, so the first statement is false. The asymptote y = 0 moves to y = k, a small |a| compresses, and a negative a reflects in the x-axis, so the other three are true.

questions.q: For f(x) = −3·2^(x + 4) − 5, match each part of the equation to its effect on the graph of y = 2^x.

right: reflection in the x-axis and vertical stretch by 3

questions.hint: Compare with a·b^(x − h) + k: here h = −4 and k = −5.
questions.explanation: a = −3 is negative and |a| = 3 > 1, so it reflects the graph in the x-axis and stretches it by 3. x + 4 = x − (−4), so h = −4 means 4 units left. k = −5 moves the graph 5 units down.

questions.hint: k gives the asymptote; for the y-intercept find g(0).
questions.explanation: k = 4, so the asymptote is y = 4. Since a = 2 > 0, the graph lies above it and the range is y > 4. g(0) = 2·3^(−1) + 4 = 2/3 + 4 = 14/3.

questions.q: Fatima invests AED 1200 at 5% annual interest for 8 years with no other deposits or withdrawals. Complete the table with the balance in AED, to the nearest fils (0.01).
questions.hint: Use A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) with n = 1, 4 and 12.

questions.q: Omar deposits AED 2000 at 6% annual interest compounded monthly. What is the balance after 5 years?
questions.hint: n = 12, so the monthly rate is 0.06/12 = 0.005 and there are 60 periods.
questions.explanation: A = 2000(1 + 0.06/12)^(12·5) = 2000(1.005)^60 ≈ AED 2697.70. AED 2676.45 compounds annually, AED 2600.00 is simple interest and AED 2699.72 compounds continuously.

questions.q: Sara invests AED 3000 at 3% annual interest compounded semiannually. What is the balance after 6 years? Round to the nearest fils (0.01) and give the number of AED.
questions.hint: Semiannually means n = 2, so use 1.015 and 12 periods.

questions.q: Khalid invests AED 1500 at 4% interest compounded continuously. What is the balance after 12 years? Round to the nearest fils (0.01) and give the number of AED.
questions.hint: Use A = Pe^(rt).

questions.q: Noura invests AED 2500 at 3.5% interest compounded continuously. What is the balance after 20 years?
questions.hint: Compute rt = 0.035 × 20 first.
questions.explanation: A = 2500e^(0.035·20) = 2500e^0.7 ≈ 2500 × 2.01375 ≈ AED 5034.38. AED 4974.47 compounds annually and AED 4250.00 is simple interest.

questions.q: AED 600 is invested at 6% interest compounded continuously. Complete the table with the balance in AED, to the nearest fils (0.01).
questions.hint: A = 600e^(0.06t) with t = 5 and t = 10.

questions.q: A town of 25,000 people is declining at a rate of 4% per year. Complete the table of predicted populations (to the nearest whole person) for each model.
A village has 8,500 people and grows by 3% per year (compounded annually). What is the predicted population after 7 years?
questions.explanation: P = 8500(1.03)^7 ≈ 8500 × 1.22987 ≈ 10,454. 10,285 adds 3% simple growth each year, 10,486 is the continuous model, and 6,868 uses decline instead of growth.

questions.q: A city of 40,000 people decreases by 5% each year (compounded annually), so P = 40000(0.95)^t. Complete the table.
questions.hint: Each year the population is multiplied by 0.95.

questions.q: Mariam invests AED 5000 in an account paying 4% annual interest compounded quarterly. She makes no other deposits or withdrawals. What is her balance after 6 years, to the nearest fils?
questions.hint: Use A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) with n = 4.
questions.explanation: A = 5000(1 + 0.04/4)^(4·6) = 5000(1.01)^24 ≈ 5000 × 1.26973 ≈ AED 6348.67. AED 6326.60 compounds only once a year, AED 6200 is simple interest, and AED 6356.25 is continuous compounding.

questions.q: Omar deposits AED 3000 in a savings account that pays 6% annual interest compounded monthly. How much is in the account after 4 years? Round to the nearest dirham (give the number only).
questions.hint: Monthly compounding means n = 12, so the rate per period is 0.06/12 = 0.005.

questions.q: AED 1000 is invested at 12% annual interest for 2 years. Complete the table of final balances A = 1000(1 + 0.12/n)^(2n) for each compounding frequency. Round to the nearest hundredth of a dirham.
questions.hint: n is the number of times interest is added each year.
questions.explanation: Semiannually n = 2: 1000(1.06)^4 ≈ 1262.48. Quarterly n = 4: 1000(1.03)^8 ≈ 1266.77. Monthly n = 12: 1000(1.01)^24 ≈ 1269.73. More frequent compounding gives a slightly larger balance.

questions.q: Match each function to the behaviour it shows.
questions.hint: Rewrite each function as bᵗ and compare b with 1.
questions.explanation: 3^(0.5t) = (√3)ᵗ with √3 > 1: growth. (4/5)^(−t) = (5/4)ᵗ: growth. 7^(−2t) = (1/49)ᵗ: decay. 0.9ᵗ has base less than 1: decay.

questions.q: Which function shows exponential decay?
questions.hint: A negative exponent flips the base: b^(−t) = (1/b)ᵗ.
questions.explanation: 4^(−0.5t) = (4^(−0.5))ᵗ = (1/2)ᵗ, and 1/2 < 1, so it decays. (3/2)ᵗ and e^(0.2t) have bases above 1, and (1/5)^(−t) = 5ᵗ, so those three all grow.

questions.q: For each model, state whether it shows growth or decay, and give the percent rate of change per period (a number followed by %).
questions.hint: Write the base as 1 + r or 1 − r.
questions.explanation: 0.85 = 1 − 0.15, so the first model decays by 15% each period. 1.06 = 1 + 0.06, so the second grows by 6% each period.

questions.q: Plot the points of y = (1/2)ˣ for x = −3, −2, −1 and 0.
questions.explanation: (1/2)^(−3) = 8, (1/2)^(−2) = 4, (1/2)^(−1) = 2 and (1/2)⁰ = 1. The values halve each time x increases by 1, which is exponential decay.

questions.q: Evaluate each expression exactly.
questions.hint: Ask: what power of the base gives the number?
questions.explanation: 2⁵ = 32, 7⁻² = 1/49 and 5^(1/3) = ∛5, so the first three are 5, −2 and 1/3. 10³ = 1000 gives 3. The inverse properties give ln e⁷ = 7 and 5^(log₅ 9) = 9.

questions.q: What is the value of log₉ 27?
questions.hint: Write both 9 and 27 as powers of 3.
questions.explanation: 9 = 3² and 27 = 3³. If 9ˣ = 27 then 3^(2x) = 3³, so 2x = 3 and x = 3/2.

questions.q: Complete the table for y = log₃ x. Give exact values.
questions.hint: log₃ x = y means 3ʸ = x.
questions.explanation: 3⁻² = 1/9, 3⁻¹ = 1/3, 3⁰ = 1, 3² = 9 and 3³ = 27, so the missing values are −2, −1, 0, x = 9 and 3.

questions.q: Match each expression to its value.
questions.hint: Use the inverse properties, and remember that a log's argument must be positive.
questions.explanation: e^(ln 8) = 8, ln 1 = 0 because e⁰ = 1, log 0.01 = −2 because 10⁻² = 0.01, log₄ 2 = 1/2 because √4 = 2, and log(−5) is undefined because the argument is negative.

questions.q: Complete the table of values for f(x) = 2 log₂(x − 1). Give exact values.
questions.hint: First find x − 1, then its log base 2, then double.
questions.explanation: x − 1 takes the values 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8, whose logs base 2 are −1, 0, 1, 2 and 3. Doubling gives −2, 0, 2, 4 and 6.

questions.q: Plot the points of f(x) = log₂(x − 3) where x − 3 equals 1, 2, 4 and 8.
questions.hint: When x − 3 = 1, f(x) = log₂ 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: x − 3 = 1, 2, 4, 8 gives x = 4, 5, 7, 11 with f(x) = 0, 1, 2, 3. So the points are (4, 0), (5, 1), (7, 2) and (11, 3), and the graph has vertical asymptote x = 3.

questions.q: Describe the features of f(x) = 3 log₂(x + 2).
questions.hint: The argument x + 2 must be positive; f(x) = 0 when x + 2 = 1.
questions.explanation: x + 2 > 0 gives domain (−2, ∞) with asymptote x = −2. The range of any log function is all real numbers. f(x) = 0 when x + 2 = 1, so x = −1. The coefficient 3 is positive and the base 2 > 1, so f increases, and f(x) → −∞ as x → −2 from the right.

questions.q: Which statement describes the end behaviour of f(x) = −log₃(x − 1)?
questions.hint: First describe log₃(x − 1), then reflect across the x-axis.
questions.explanation: log₃(x − 1) rises to ∞ as x → ∞ and drops to −∞ as x → 1⁺. The negative sign reflects this, so f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞ and f(x) → ∞ as x → 1⁺. The domain is x > 1, so x cannot approach −∞.

questions.q: Match each function to the transformation of its parent function (ln x or log x).

right: Vertical stretch by a factor of 3
Reflection across the x-axis, then shift left 2
Vertical compression by a factor of 1/3

questions.hint: Changes inside the log act on x (horizontal); changes outside act on y (vertical).
questions.explanation: x − 3 moves the graph right 3 and +1 moves it up 1. The factor 3 outside stretches vertically. Replacing x by −x reflects in the y-axis. The minus sign outside reflects in the x-axis and x + 2 moves the graph left 2.

questions.q: Which function is the graph of y = ln x shifted 5 units left and 3 units down?
questions.hint: A shift left by h replaces x with x + h.
questions.explanation: Moving left 5 replaces x with x + 5, and moving down 3 subtracts 3 from the whole function, so y = ln(x + 5) − 3.

questions.q: The graph of y = log₂ x passes through (1, 0), (2, 1), (4, 2) and (8, 3). Plot the images of these four points on the graph of g(x) = log₂(x + 3) − 1.
questions.hint: Move every point 3 units left and 1 unit down.
questions.explanation: x + 3 shifts the graph 3 left and −1 shifts it 1 down, so (x, y) → (x − 3, y − 1). The points become (−2, −1), (−1, 0), (1, 1) and (5, 2).

questions.q: Describe how f(x) = −2 log(x − 5) + 4 is obtained from y = log x.
questions.hint: Read the transformation from each number: the −2 outside, the −5 inside and the +4 at the end.
questions.explanation: The −2 multiplies the output, which reflects the graph in the x-axis and stretches it by 2. x − 5 shifts the graph right 5, and +4 shifts it up 4. The asymptote x = 0 moves to x = 5.

questions.q: Which equation is equivalent to log₃(1/81) = x?
questions.hint: log_b a = c means b^c = a.
questions.explanation: The base 3 is raised to the answer x to give 1/81, so 3ˣ = 1/81 (and x = −4).

questions.q: Match each logarithmic equation to its equivalent exponential equation.
questions.hint: The base of the log becomes the base of the power.
questions.explanation: log_b a = c is the same as b^c = a: 2⁴ = 16, 5⁰ = 1, 10⁻³ = 0.001 (common log, base 10) and eʸ = 7 (natural log, base e).

questions.q: Write log₆ 216 = 3 in exponential form.
questions.hint: The base 6 is raised to the power 3.
questions.explanation: log₆ 216 = 3 means 6 raised to the power 3 equals 216, so 6³ = 216.

questions.q: Rewrite log₂(1/32) = x in exponential form and solve for x.
questions.hint: Write 1/32 as a power of 2.
questions.explanation: log₂(1/32) = x means 2ˣ = 1/32 = 2⁻⁵, so x = −5.

questions.q: Complete the table for f(x) = log_(1/2) x. Give exact values, or round to two decimal places where needed.
questions.hint: Ask what power of 1/2 gives x; for x = 5 use log 5 / log(1/2).

questions.q: Plot the points of f(x) = log_(1/3) x at x = 1, 3 and 9.
questions.explanation: (1/3)⁰ = 1, (1/3)⁻¹ = 3 and (1/3)⁻² = 9, so the points are (1, 0), (3, −1) and (9, −2). The graph falls from left to right because the base is between 0 and 1.

questions.q: Describe f(x) = log_(1/4) x.
questions.hint: The base 1/4 is between 0 and 1.
questions.explanation: Only positive x have a logarithm, so the domain is (0, ∞) with asymptote x = 0, and the range is all real numbers. log_(1/4) 1 = 0 gives the intercept (1, 0). A base between 0 and 1 makes the function decreasing.

questions.q: Which statement is true for f(x) = log_(1/5) x?
questions.hint: A log with base between 0 and 1 is decreasing.
questions.explanation: f is decreasing, so f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞ and f(x) → ∞ as x → 0⁺. f(5) = −1 because (1/5)⁻¹ = 5.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are true about f(x) = −3 log₂(x + 1)?  I. Domain: (−1, ∞)   II. Range: all real numbers   III. lim f(x) as x → ∞ is ∞
questions.hint: Check the sign of the coefficient −3 for the end behaviour.
questions.explanation: x + 1 > 0 gives domain (−1, ∞), so I is true. Every log function has range all real numbers, so II is true. Because of the factor −3, f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞, so III is false.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are true about f(x) = log₄(x − 2) + 3?  I. The vertical asymptote is x = 2.   II. The x-intercept is (3, 0).   III. f is increasing on its domain.
questions.hint: Test II by computing f(3).
questions.explanation: x − 2 > 0 puts the asymptote at x = 2, so I is true. f(3) = log₄ 1 + 3 = 3, not 0, so II is false. The base 4 > 1 and the coefficient is positive, so f increases and III is true.

questions.q: Match each feature of f(x) = ln(x + 3) − 2 to its value.
questions.hint: The argument x + 3 must be positive.
questions.explanation: x + 3 > 0 gives domain (−3, ∞) and asymptote x = −3. The range of a log function is (−∞, ∞). As x approaches −3 from the right, ln(x + 3) → −∞, so f(x) → −∞.

questions.q: Write a logarithmic equation that is equivalent to 7^(x + 2) = 3y.
questions.hint: The exponent is the logarithm; the base stays the base.
questions.explanation: In bᶜ = a the exponent c equals log_b a. Here b = 7, c = x + 2 and a = 3y, so log₇(3y) = x + 2.

questions.q: Which logarithmic equation is equivalent to e^(2x) = 5?
questions.hint: The natural log has base e.
questions.explanation: e^(2x) = 5 means 2x is the power of e that gives 5, so 2x = ln 5. Using log 5 would mean base 10, which is wrong.

questions.q: Match each exponential equation to its equivalent logarithmic equation.
questions.hint: bᶜ = a becomes log_b a = c.
questions.explanation: Each base becomes the base of the log, and each exponent becomes the value of the log: log 1000 = 3, log₄ 2 = 1/2, log₂(1/8) = −3 and log₉ y = x.

questions.q: Complete the table by rewriting each exponential equation in logarithmic form, log_b a = c. Give the value of c.
questions.hint: The exponent in the exponential form is the value of the log.
questions.explanation: In bᶜ = a the exponent c is log_b a, so the values are 4, −2 and 1/3.

questions.q: What is the domain of f(x) = 4 ln(10 − 5x) + 1? Write your answer in interval notation.
questions.hint: Set the argument of the logarithm greater than 0.
questions.explanation: 10 − 5x > 0 gives 5x < 10, so x < 2. The domain is (−∞, 2); the 4 and the + 1 do not affect it.

questions.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log(3x + 9) − 2?
questions.hint: Solve 3x + 9 > 0.
questions.explanation: 3x + 9 > 0 gives 3x > −9, so x > −3. The domain is (−3, ∞).

questions.q: Match each function to its domain.
questions.hint: Each argument must be positive.
questions.explanation: x − 7 > 0 gives x > 7. 12 − 4x > 0 gives x < 3. 2x + 8 > 0 gives x > −4. x² + 1 is always positive, so its domain is all real numbers.

questions.q: For f(x) = −3 log(8 − 2x) + 5:
questions.hint: The asymptote is where the argument equals 0.
questions.explanation: 8 − 2x = 0 at x = 4, which is the vertical asymptote. 8 − 2x > 0 gives x < 4, so the domain is (−∞, 4).

questions.q: Lemon juice has a pH of 2.0 and a soft drink has a pH of 5.2. Use pH = −log[H⁺]. Write each concentration in mol/L as a decimal or a power of 10.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: [H⁺] for the soft drink = ___ × 10⁻⁶ (round to two decimal places)

questions.q: A solution has a hydrogen-ion concentration of 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol/L. What is its pH, to the nearest hundredth? (pH = −log[H⁺])
questions.hint: Compute log(2.5 × 10⁻⁴) and change the sign.

questions.q: Complete the table using pH = −log[H⁺]. Write each concentration as a decimal.
questions.hint: [H⁺] = 10^(−pH), and pH = −log[H⁺].

questions.q: Solution A has pH 3 and solution B has pH 5. How many times greater is the hydrogen-ion concentration of A than of B?
questions.hint: Find [H⁺] for each, then divide.
questions.explanation: [H⁺] for A is 10⁻³ and for B is 10⁻⁵. 10⁻³ ÷ 10⁻⁵ = 10² = 100, so A has 100 times the concentration of B.

questions.q: Express each logarithm in terms of log 3 and log 5.
questions.hint: Factor each number into powers of 3 and 5.
questions.explanation: 45 = 3²·5, so log 45 = 2 log 3 + log 5. 9/125 = 3²/5³, so log(9/125) = 2 log 3 − 3 log 5. 15 = 3·5, so log 15 = log 3 + log 5.

questions.q: If log 2 = a and log 3 = b, which expression equals log 18?
questions.explanation: log 18 = log(2·3²) = log 2 + 2 log 3 = a + 2b. The power rule gives 2 log 3, not (log 3)².

questions.q: Given log 3 ≈ 0.477 and log 5 ≈ 0.699, find log(27/5). Round to three decimal places.
Match each logarithm to its form in terms of log 2 and log 5.
questions.hint: Factor each number: 20 = 2²·5, and so on.
questions.explanation: 20 = 2²·5, 40 = 2³·5, 50 = 2·5² and 0.8 = 4/5 = 2²/5. The product and quotient rules give the matches shown.

questions.q: Evaluate each expression exactly.
questions.hint: Write each argument as a power of the base.

questions.q: What is log₅ ∛25?
Evaluate 2 log₄ 8 + ln(1/e²). Give an exact number.
questions.hint: log₄ 8: write 8 as a power of 4, since 4^(3/2) = 8.
questions.explanation: 4^(3/2) = 8, so log₄ 8 = 3/2 and 2 log₄ 8 = 3. ln(1/e²) = ln e⁻² = −2. The total is 3 − 2 = 1.

questions.q: Match each expression to its exact value.
questions.hint: Write each argument as a power of the base.

questions.q: Expand each expression completely.
questions.hint: Product → sum, quotient → difference, power → coefficient.
questions.explanation: log₇(5x²y³) = log₇ 5 + 2 log₇ x + 3 log₇ y. ln[(2x − 1)/(3√x)] = ln(2x − 1) − ln 3 − ½ ln x, since √x = x^(1/2). ln(2x − 1) cannot be split further.

questions.q: Which is the expanded form of log₂(8x⁴/y)?
questions.hint: log₂ 8 is a number.
questions.explanation: log₂(8x⁴/y) = log₂ 8 + log₂ x⁴ − log₂ y = 3 + 4 log₂ x − log₂ y.

questions.q: Match each logarithm to its expanded form.
questions.hint: There is no rule for the log of a sum.
questions.explanation: log(x³y) = 3 log x + log y. log(x/y³) = log x − 3 log y. log(y√x) = log y + ½ log x. log(x³ + y) is the log of a sum, so it cannot be expanded.

questions.q: Condense each expression into a single logarithm.
questions.hint: Move coefficients up as powers first, then combine.
questions.explanation: 2 log₃ x + 4 log₃(x − 2) = log₃ x² + log₃(x − 2)⁴ = log₃[x²(x − 2)⁴]. ln(2x + 1) − ln x³ − ln(x + 4) = ln[(2x + 1)/(x³(x + 4))].

questions.q: Condense −2 log₅(x + 3) + 4 log₅(2x).
questions.explanation: 4 log₅(2x) = log₅(2x)⁴ = log₅ 16x⁴, and −2 log₅(x + 3) = −log₅(x + 3)². The difference is log₅[16x⁴/(x + 3)²].

questions.q: Write 3 log 2 + 2 log 5 − log 4 as a single logarithm log N. Give the answer as log N with N simplified.
questions.hint: 3 log 2 = log 8 and 2 log 5 = log 25.
questions.explanation: 3 log 2 + 2 log 5 − log 4 = log 8 + log 25 − log 4 = log(8 · 25 / 4) = log 50.

questions.q: Match each expression to its condensed form.
questions.hint: Coefficients become powers, sums become products, differences become quotients.
questions.explanation: log x + log(x + 1) = log[x(x + 1)]. 3 log x − log(x + 1) = log[x³/(x + 1)]. log(x + 1) − log x² = log[(x + 1)/x²]. log x² + log(x + 1)² = log[x²(x + 1)²].

questions.q: Use the change of base formula to evaluate each logarithm. Round to three decimal places.
questions.hint: log_b a = log a / log b.

questions.q: Which expression is equal to log₃ 20?
questions.hint: The argument goes on top.
questions.explanation: Change of base: log₃ 20 = log 20 / log 3 ≈ 2.727. log(20/3) and log 20 − log 3 are the same quantity, and neither is log₃ 20.

questions.q: Complete the table for y = log₅ x. Round to three decimal places.
questions.hint: log₅ x = ln x / ln 5.

questions.q: Match each logarithm to its approximate value (change of base).
questions.hint: log_b a = ln a / ln b; a base less than 1 gives a negative value here.

questions.q: Express log 72 in terms of log 2 and log 3.
questions.hint: Factor 72 into primes.

questions.q: Which expression equals log 48?
questions.explanation: 48 = 2⁴ · 3, so log 48 = 4 log 2 + log 3. The product rule gives a sum, not a product.

questions.q: Match each logarithm to its form in terms of log 2 and log 3.
questions.hint: Write each number as 2ᵃ · 3ᵇ.
questions.explanation: 12 = 2²·3, 54 = 2·3³, 24 = 2³·3 and 36 = 2²·3². So the logs are 2 log 2 + log 3, log 2 + 3 log 3, 3 log 2 + log 3 and 2 log 2 + 2 log 3.

questions.q: Given log 2 ≈ 0.3010 and log 3 ≈ 0.4771, find log 72. Round to three decimal places.
questions.hint: log 72 = 3 log 2 + 2 log 3.

questions.q: Condense 3 log₂ x − ½ log₂(x + 1) into a single logarithm.
questions.hint: ½ log₂(x + 1) = log₂ √(x + 1).
questions.explanation: 3 log₂ x = log₂ x³ and ½ log₂(x + 1) = log₂ √(x + 1). Subtracting gives log₂[x³/√(x + 1)].

questions.q: Condense 2 ln x + ⅓ ln(x − 4).
questions.hint: A coefficient of ⅓ becomes a cube root.
questions.explanation: 2 ln x = ln x² and ⅓ ln(x − 4) = ln ∛(x − 4). Adding logs multiplies the arguments: ln[x² ∛(x − 4)].

questions.q: Condense each expression into a single logarithm.
questions.hint: Turn each coefficient into a power, then use the product or quotient rule.
questions.explanation: ½ log y + 2 log z = log √y + log z² = log(z²√y). 4 log₅ a − ⅓ log₅ b = log₅ a⁴ − log₅ ∛b = log₅(a⁴/∛b).

questions.q: Condense the expression: ln(x + 2) − 2 ln x + 3 ln(x − 1).
questions.hint: Positive terms go in the numerator, negative terms in the denominator.
questions.explanation: −2 ln x = −ln x² and 3 ln(x − 1) = ln(x − 1)³. So the expression is ln(x + 2) + ln(x − 1)³ − ln x² = ln[(x + 2)(x − 1)³/x²].

questions.q: Match each expression to its condensed form.
questions.hint: Coefficients become powers; subtraction becomes division.
questions.explanation: log x + log y² = log(xy²). log x − log y² = log(x/y²). log x² − log y = log(x²/y). −(log x + log y²) = −log(xy²) = log[1/(xy²)].

questions.q: Evaluate log 4 + log 25 exactly.
questions.hint: Combine into one logarithm first.
questions.explanation: log 4 + log 25 = log(4 · 25) = log 100 = 2.

questions.q: If log₃ 2 ≈ 0.6309 and log₃ 5 ≈ 1.4650, find the approximate value of log₃ 10.
questions.explanation: log₃ 10 = log₃ 2 + log₃ 5 ≈ 0.6309 + 1.4650 = 2.0959. 0.9243 multiplies the logs, 0.8341 subtracts them and 2.3221 divides them; none of these is a log rule for 10.

questions.q: If log₂ 3 ≈ 1.5850 and log₂ 5 ≈ 2.3219, find the approximate value of log₂ 45. Give four decimal places.
Given log₇ 2 ≈ 0.3562 and log₇ 3 ≈ 0.5646, complete the table using the properties of logarithms. Give four decimal places.
2 log₃ 6 − log₃ 4 is equal to ______.
questions.hint: 2 log₃ 6 = log₃ 36.
questions.explanation: 2 log₃ 6 − log₃ 4 = log₃ 36 − log₃ 4 = log₃(36/4) = log₃ 9 = 2.

questions.q: log₂ 40 − 2 log₂ 5 + log₂ 10 is equal to ______.
questions.hint: 2 log₂ 5 = log₂ 25.
questions.explanation: log₂ 40 − log₂ 25 + log₂ 10 = log₂(40 · 10 / 25) = log₂ 16 = 4.

questions.q: Evaluate 3 log₆ 2 + 2 log₆ 3 − log₆ 2 exactly.
questions.hint: Rewrite each term as the log of a power, then combine.
questions.explanation: 3 log₆ 2 + 2 log₆ 3 − log₆ 2 = log₆ 8 + log₆ 9 − log₆ 2 = log₆(8 · 9 / 2) = log₆ 36 = 2.

questions.q: Write each expression as a single number.
questions.hint: Combine into one logarithm, then evaluate.
questions.explanation: log₂(12/3) = log₂ 4 = 2. log₄(8 · 2) = log₄ 16 = 2. log₃(36/4) = log₃ 9 = 2. log(5 · 2) = log 10 = 1.

questions.q: Solve each equation by writing both sides with the same base. Give exact answers.

questions.explanation: 49^(x + 1) = 7^(2x + 2). Setting the exponents equal: 2x + 2 = 3x − 2, so x = 4.

questions.q: Solve each exponential equation. Give exact answers (fractions where needed).
questions.hint: Write both sides as powers of the same prime.

questions.q: Solve each logarithmic equation. Round to the nearest hundredth where needed.
questions.hint: Isolate the log, then rewrite in exponential form.
questions.explanation: i: x = e^3.2 ≈ 24.53. ii: 5 log(2x) = 15, so log(2x) = 3, 2x = 1000 and x = 500. iii: x² + 7 = 2⁵ = 32, so x² = 25 and x = ±5 (both give a positive argument).

questions.q: Solve log₄(3x + 1) = 3.
questions.hint: Rewrite as 4³ = 3x + 1.
questions.explanation: 4³ = 64, so 3x + 1 = 64, 3x = 63 and x = 21. (x = 11/3 comes from wrongly using 4 × 3 = 12.)

questions.q: Solve 6 − 2 ln x = 1. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Isolate ln x first.

questions.q: Solve each logarithmic equation. Give exact answers.
questions.hint: Rewrite each equation in exponential form.

questions.q: Solve each equation. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Take a logarithm of both sides to bring the exponents down.

questions.q: Solve 5^(2x) = 40. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Take logs: 2x log 5 = log 40.
questions.explanation: 2x = log 40/log 5 ≈ 1.6021/0.6990 ≈ 2.292, so x ≈ 1.15. 2.29 forgets to divide by 2.

questions.q: Solve 10^(x − 3) = 45. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Take the common log of both sides.

questions.q: Solve each equation using natural logarithms. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Isolate the power of e, then take ln of both sides.

questions.q: Solve log₃(5x + 4) = log₃(2x) + log₃ 3 and check your answer.
questions.hint: Combine the right side into one logarithm.
questions.explanation: log₃(2x) + log₃ 3 = log₃(6x), so 5x + 4 = 6x and x = 4. Check: 5(4) + 4 = 24 and 6(4) = 24, and every argument is positive.

questions.q: Solve log₂(x + 6) − log₂ x = log₂ 4.
questions.hint: Use the quotient rule on the left side.
questions.explanation: log₂[(x + 6)/x] = log₂ 4, so x + 6 = 4x, 3x = 6 and x = 2. Check: log₂ 8 − log₂ 2 = 3 − 1 = 2 = log₂ 4.

questions.q: Solve log₅(x² − 4) = log₅(3x).
questions.hint: Set the arguments equal, solve the quadratic, then check each answer in the original equation.
questions.explanation: x² − 4 = 3x gives x² − 3x − 4 = 0, so (x − 4)(x + 1) = 0 and x = 4 or x = −1. x = −1 makes 3x negative, so it is rejected. x = 4 gives log₅ 12 on both sides, so it is the only solution.

questions.q: Solve the equations.
questions.hint: Use base 2 in part i; combine the logs on the right in part ii.
questions.explanation: i: 2^(3x − 3) = 2^(2x + 2), so 3x − 3 = 2x + 2 and x = 5. ii: log₅ x = log₅[4(x − 3)], so x = 4x − 12 and x = 4. Check: 4 − 3 > 0.

questions.q: Solve 27ˣ = 9^(x + 2).
questions.hint: Write both sides as powers of 3.

questions.q: Solve log₂ x + log₂(x − 2) = 3.
questions.hint: Combine the logs, then rewrite in exponential form.
questions.explanation: log₂[x(x − 2)] = 3 gives x² − 2x = 8, so (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0. x = −2 is rejected because log₂(−2) is undefined, so x = 4.

questions.q: Match each equation to its solution.
questions.hint: Rewrite with a common base, or combine the logs and set the arguments equal.
questions.explanation: 2^(2x + 2) = 2^(3x) gives x = 2. 3^(2x − 4) = 3^x gives x = 4. x = 2(x − 1) gives x = 2, and 2 − 1 > 0. x + 3 = 2x − 1 gives x = 4, and both arguments are positive.

questions.q: A bacteria culture grows according to N(t) = 50(1.25)ᵗ, where t is in hours. After how many hours will there be 2000 bacteria? Round to the nearest tenth.
questions.hint: Divide by 50 first, then take logs.

questions.q: A population is modelled by P(t) = 200 · 2^(t/3), where t is in hours. When will the population reach 6400?
questions.explanation: 2^(t/3) = 32 = 2⁵, so t/3 = 5 and t = 15 hours. 5 hours forgets to multiply by 3.

questions.q: An investment grows according to V(t) = 300(1.08)ᵗ, where t is in years. Complete the table of times needed to reach each value. Round to the nearest tenth of a year.
questions.hint: Solve 1.08ᵗ = factor, so t = log(factor)/log 1.08.

questions.q: The amount of a medicine in the body is A(t) = 400(0.85)ᵗ milligrams after t hours. After how many hours will 100 mg remain? Round to the nearest tenth.
If 5³ = 2ˣ, what is the approximate value of x?
questions.hint: Take logs: x log 2 = 3 log 5.

questions.q: Solve 7ˣ = 30. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: x = log 30 / log 7.

questions.q: Solve each equation for x. Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: For bˣ = N, x = log N / log b.
questions.explanation: log 10/log 2 ≈ 3.32, log 50/log 4 ≈ 2.82, log 3/log 6 ≈ 0.61 and log 20/log 1.5 ≈ 7.39.

questions.q: What is the solution of log(x − 15) = 2 − log x?
questions.hint: Move log x to the left and combine.
questions.explanation: log[x(x − 15)] = 2 gives x² − 15x = 100, so (x − 20)(x + 5) = 0. x = −5 makes log x undefined, so the only solution is x = 20.

questions.q: Solve log₂ x + log₂(x + 6) = 4.
questions.hint: Combine the logs, then write 2⁴ = x(x + 6).
questions.explanation: x(x + 6) = 16 gives x² + 6x − 16 = 0, so (x + 8)(x − 2) = 0. x = −8 is rejected because log₂(−8) is undefined. The solution is x = 2.

questions.q: Solve ln(x + 1) + ln(x − 1) = ln 8.
questions.hint: Combine the left side into ln[(x + 1)(x − 1)].
questions.explanation: (x + 1)(x − 1) = 8 gives x² = 9, so x = ±3. x = −3 makes the arguments negative, so x = 3.

questions.q: Solve log₃ x + log₃(x − 8) = 2 by completing the table.
questions.hint: log₃[x(x − 8)] = 2 means x(x − 8) = 3².
questions.explanation: x² − 8x = 9 gives x² − 8x − 9 = 0, so (x − 9)(x + 1) = 0. x = −1 is rejected because log₃(−1) is undefined, so x = 9.

questions.q: What is the value of n if log₂(3n + 1) = 4?
questions.hint: Rewrite as 2⁴ = 3n + 1.
questions.explanation: 2⁴ = 16, so 3n + 1 = 16, 3n = 15 and n = 5. 7/3 comes from wrongly using 2 × 4 = 8.

questions.q: Solve log₅(2n − 3) = 2.
questions.hint: Rewrite in exponential form.

questions.q: Solve each equation for n.
questions.hint: log_b A = c means A = b^c.
questions.explanation: n + 4 = 9 gives n = 5. 2n = 64 gives n = 32. 5n = 100 gives n = 20. n − 1 = 6⁰ = 1 gives n = 2.

questions.q: Which of the following is equal to sec²x − 1?
questions.hint: Start from 1 + tan²x = sec²x.
questions.explanation: Subtract 1 from both sides of the identity 1 + tan²x = sec²x. This gives sec²x − 1 = tan²x.

questions.q: Match each expression to the single term it equals.
questions.hint: Use the three Pythagorean identities.
questions.explanation: 1 + tan²x = sec²x and 1 + cot²x = csc²x. From sin²x + cos²x = 1 we get 1 − sin²x = cos²x. Rearranging 1 + tan²x = sec²x gives sec²x − tan²x = 1.

questions.q: If tan x = 3, find the value of sec²x.
questions.hint: Use sec²x = 1 + tan²x.
questions.explanation: sec²x = 1 + tan²x = 1 + 3² = 1 + 9 = 10.

questions.q: Simplify (sec²x − 1) / tan²x.
questions.hint: Replace sec²x − 1 with a single term.
questions.explanation: sec²x − 1 = tan²x, so the expression is tan²x / tan²x = 1.

questions.q: Which of the following is equal to csc²x − cot²x?
questions.hint: Rearrange 1 + cot²x = csc²x.
questions.explanation: From 1 + cot²x = csc²x, subtract cot²x from both sides: csc²x − cot²x = 1.

questions.q: If cot x = 2, find the value of csc²x.
questions.hint: Use csc²x = 1 + cot²x.
questions.explanation: csc²x = 1 + cot²x = 1 + 2² = 5.

questions.q: Use the identity 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ to complete the table. Give fractions in simplest form.
questions.hint: Square cot θ, then add 1.

questions.q: Which expression is equal to cot²x?
questions.hint: Subtract 1 from both sides of 1 + cot²x = csc²x.
questions.explanation: Since 1 + cot²x = csc²x, subtracting 1 gives cot²x = csc²x − 1. Note sec²x − 1 equals tan²x, not cot²x.

questions.q: The expression (1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ) is equivalent to:
questions.hint: Multiply out as a difference of squares.
questions.explanation: (1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ) = 1 − cos²θ. Since sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, this equals sin²θ.

questions.q: The expression (sec θ − 1)(sec θ + 1) is equivalent to:
questions.hint: Difference of squares, then a Pythagorean identity.
questions.explanation: (sec θ − 1)(sec θ + 1) = sec²θ − 1. From 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, this equals tan²θ.

questions.q: Match each product to the expression it simplifies to.
questions.hint: Each product is a difference of squares a² − b².
questions.explanation: csc²θ − 1 = cot²θ, 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, sec²θ − 1 = tan²θ and 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ.

questions.q: Simplify (2 + 2 sin θ)(1 − sin θ). Write your answer as a single term.
questions.hint: Factor out 2 first.
questions.explanation: (2 + 2 sin θ)(1 − sin θ) = 2(1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ) = 2(1 − sin²θ). Since 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, the result is 2cos²θ.

questions.q: If csc θ = 2 and cos θ < 0, then cot θ is:
questions.hint: Find sin θ, decide the quadrant, then find cos θ.
questions.explanation: sin θ = 1/2 > 0 and cos θ < 0, so θ is in Quadrant II. cos θ = −√(1 − 1/4) = −√3/2. cot θ = cos θ / sin θ = (−√3/2)/(1/2) = −√3.

questions.q: If sec θ = −3 and sin θ > 0, find tan θ. Give an exact answer in simplest radical form.
questions.hint: cos θ = −1/3; which quadrant has sin positive and cos negative?
questions.explanation: cos θ = −1/3 and sin θ > 0, so θ is in Quadrant II. sin θ = √(1 − 1/9) = √8/3 = 2√2/3. tan θ = (2√2/3)/(−1/3) = −2√2.

questions.q: Given cos θ = −4/5 and tan θ > 0, complete the following. Give fractions in simplest form.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Quadrant of θ (I, II, III or IV):

questions.hint: Cosine negative and tangent positive happens in only one quadrant.
questions.explanation: cos θ < 0 and tan θ > 0 means θ is in Quadrant III, where sin θ < 0. sin θ = −√(1 − 16/25) = −3/5. tan θ = (−3/5)/(−4/5) = 3/4 and csc θ = 1/sin θ = −5/3.

questions.q: Complete the table with the sign (+ or −) of each function in each quadrant.
questions.hint: sin follows the y-coordinate, cos the x-coordinate, and tan = sin/cos.
questions.explanation: In Quadrant II, x < 0 and y > 0, so cos is − and tan is −. In Quadrant III both are negative, so sin is − and tan is +. In Quadrant IV, x > 0 and y < 0, so sin is − and cos is +.

questions.q: The expression (1 − sin²x)sec²x is equivalent to:
questions.hint: Replace 1 − sin²x first.
questions.explanation: 1 − sin²x = cos²x and sec²x = 1/cos²x. So the product is cos²x · 1/cos²x = 1.

questions.q: The expression (sec²x − 1)cos²x is equivalent to:
questions.hint: sec²x − 1 is a single squared function.
questions.explanation: sec²x − 1 = tan²x = sin²x/cos²x. Multiplying by cos²x gives sin²x.

questions.q: Simplify (1 + tan²x)cos²x.
questions.hint: 1 + tan²x is a single squared function.
questions.explanation: 1 + tan²x = sec²x = 1/cos²x, so (1 + tan²x)cos²x = cos²x/cos²x = 1.

questions.q: Match each expression to its simplest form.
questions.hint: Rewrite each in terms of sin x and cos x.
questions.explanation: sin²x · 1/sin²x = 1. (csc²x − 1)sin²x = cot²x sin²x = cos²x. cos²x sec²x = 1, so subtracting 1 gives 0. tan x cos x = (sin x/cos x)cos x = sin x.

questions.q: If csc θ = 13/5 and sec θ = 13/12, find tan θ. Give a fraction in simplest form.
questions.hint: Take reciprocals to get sin θ and cos θ.

questions.q: If sin θ = 8/17 and cos θ = 15/17, then cot θ is:
questions.hint: cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.

questions.q: Complete the table. Give tan θ as a fraction in simplest form (rationalize any radical).
questions.hint: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = (1/csc θ)/(1/sec θ) = sec θ/csc θ.

questions.q: Given csc θ = 17/8 and sec θ = 17/15, complete. Give fractions in simplest form.
questions.hint: Sine and cosine are the reciprocals of cosecant and secant.
questions.explanation: sin θ = 1/csc θ = 8/17 and cos θ = 1/sec θ = 15/17. tan θ = (8/17)/(15/17) = 8/15 and cot θ is its reciprocal, 15/8.

questions.q: If cos θ = 0.62, find sin(π/2 − θ).
questions.hint: Use a cofunction identity.
questions.explanation: sin(π/2 − θ) = cos θ, so sin(π/2 − θ) = 0.62.

questions.q: If tan θ = 2.5, find cot(π/2 − θ).
questions.hint: cot(π/2 − θ) equals one of the basic functions of θ.
questions.explanation: By the cofunction identity, cot(π/2 − θ) = tan θ = 2.5.

questions.q: If cos θ = −0.28, find sin(θ − π/2).
questions.hint: Sine is odd: sin(θ − π/2) = −sin(π/2 − θ).

questions.q: Match each expression to an equal function of θ.
questions.hint: Each function of (π/2 − θ) equals its cofunction of θ.
questions.explanation: The cofunction pairs are sine/cosine, tangent/cotangent and secant/cosecant. So cos(π/2 − θ) = sin θ, sin(π/2 − θ) = cos θ, tan(π/2 − θ) = cot θ and sec(π/2 − θ) = csc θ.

questions.q: Given tan θ = 2 and sin θ < 0, find cos θ. Give an exact answer with a rational denominator.
questions.hint: Use 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, then decide the sign.
questions.explanation: sec²θ = 1 + 4 = 5. tan θ > 0 and sin θ < 0 means Quadrant III, so cos θ < 0 and sec θ = −√5. cos θ = −1/√5 = −√5/5.

questions.q: Given cot θ = −3 and sin θ > 0, find sin θ.
questions.hint: Use 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
questions.explanation: csc²θ = 1 + 9 = 10. Since sin θ > 0, csc θ = √10 and sin θ = 1/√10 = √10/10.

questions.q: Given cot θ = 4/3 and cos θ < 0, complete. Give fractions in simplest form.
questions.hint: cot θ > 0 with cos θ < 0 puts θ in Quadrant III.
questions.explanation: csc²θ = 1 + 16/9 = 25/9. In Quadrant III sin θ < 0, so csc θ = −5/3 and sin θ = −3/5. cos θ = cot θ · sin θ = (4/3)(−3/5) = −4/5.

questions.q: Simplify each expression to a single trigonometric function.

parts.label: i
parts.prompt: csc θ − cot θ cos θ =

parts.label: ii
parts.prompt: sec θ csc θ − tan θ =

questions.hint: Write everything in terms of sin θ and cos θ and combine over a common denominator.
questions.explanation: i: 1/sin θ − cos²θ/sin θ = (1 − cos²θ)/sin θ = sin²θ/sin θ = sin θ. ii: 1/(sin θ cos θ) − sin θ/cos θ = (1 − sin²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = cos²θ/(sin θ cos θ) = cot θ.

questions.q: Simplify tan θ sin θ + cos θ.
questions.hint: Write tan θ sin θ as one fraction over cos θ.
questions.explanation: tan θ sin θ + cos θ = sin²θ/cos θ + cos²θ/cos θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/cos θ = 1/cos θ = sec θ.

questions.q: Match each expression to an equivalent expression.
questions.hint: Rewrite in sine and cosine and use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
questions.explanation: sin θ · cos θ/sin θ = cos θ and cos θ · sin θ/cos θ = sin θ. csc θ − sin θ = (1 − sin²θ)/sin θ = cos²θ/sin θ = cos θ cot θ. sec θ − cos θ = (1 − cos²θ)/cos θ = sin²θ/cos θ = sin θ tan θ.

questions.q: Simplify sin θ(csc θ − sin θ) to a single term.
questions.hint: Distribute first; sin θ csc θ = 1.
questions.explanation: sin θ csc θ − sin²θ = 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ.

questions.q: Simplify each expression. Write each answer as a single power of one function.
questions.hint: Use sec(π/2 − θ) = csc θ and cos(π/2 − θ) = sin θ, then factor.
questions.explanation: i: −csc θ − cot²θ csc θ = −csc θ(1 + cot²θ) = −csc θ · csc²θ = −csc³θ. ii: cos²θ sin θ − sin θ = sin θ(cos²θ − 1) = sin θ(−sin²θ) = −sin³θ.

questions.q: Simplify cos(π/2 − θ) − sin θ cos²θ.
questions.hint: Replace cos(π/2 − θ) with sin θ, then factor out sin θ.
questions.explanation: cos(π/2 − θ) = sin θ. So the expression is sin θ − sin θ cos²θ = sin θ(1 − cos²θ) = sin θ · sin²θ = sin³θ.

questions.q: Simplify cot(π/2 − θ) + tan³θ as a product of two trigonometric functions.
questions.hint: cot(π/2 − θ) = tan θ; then factor out tan θ.
questions.explanation: cot(π/2 − θ) = tan θ, so the expression is tan θ + tan³θ = tan θ(1 + tan²θ) = tan θ sec²θ.

questions.q: Simplify −csc(π/2 − θ) + sec θ sin²θ.
questions.hint: csc(π/2 − θ) = sec θ; factor out −sec θ.
questions.explanation: −sec θ + sec θ sin²θ = −sec θ(1 − sin²θ) = −sec θ cos²θ = −(1/cos θ)cos²θ = −cos θ.

questions.q: Simplify sin θ/(1 + cos θ) + (1 + cos θ)/sin θ to a single term.
questions.hint: Use the common denominator sin θ(1 + cos θ).
questions.explanation: Numerator: sin²θ + (1 + cos θ)² = sin²θ + 1 + 2cos θ + cos²θ = 2 + 2cos θ = 2(1 + cos θ). Dividing by sin θ(1 + cos θ) gives 2/sin θ = 2csc θ.

questions.q: Simplify 1/(1 − sin θ) + 1/(1 + sin θ).
questions.hint: The common denominator is a difference of squares.
questions.explanation: Combining gives [(1 + sin θ) + (1 − sin θ)] / (1 − sin²θ) = 2/cos²θ = 2sec²θ.

questions.q: Simplify cos θ/(1 − sin θ) + (1 − sin θ)/cos θ step by step.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Numerator after expanding and using sin²θ + cos²θ = 1:

questions.hint: Expand (1 − sin θ)² and replace sin²θ + cos²θ with 1.
questions.explanation: Over the denominator cos θ(1 − sin θ), the numerator is cos²θ + (1 − sin θ)² = cos²θ + 1 − 2sin θ + sin²θ = 2 − 2sin θ = 2(1 − sin θ). Cancelling (1 − sin θ) leaves 2/cos θ = 2sec θ.

questions.q: Simplify 1/(1 − cos θ) − 1/(1 + cos θ).
questions.hint: Combine over 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ.
questions.explanation: [(1 + cos θ) − (1 − cos θ)] / (1 − cos²θ) = 2cos θ/sin²θ = 2 · (cos θ/sin θ) · (1/sin θ) = 2cot θ csc θ.

questions.q: Rewrite sin²θ/(1 + cos θ) as an expression that does not involve a fraction.
questions.hint: Write sin²θ as 1 − cos²θ and factor.
questions.explanation: sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ = (1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ). Cancelling (1 + cos θ) leaves 1 − cos θ.

questions.q: Rewrite cos²θ/(1 + sin θ) as an expression without a fraction.
questions.hint: cos²θ = (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ).
questions.explanation: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ = (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ). Dividing by (1 + sin θ) gives 1 − sin θ.

questions.q: Match each fraction to the equivalent expression with no fraction.
questions.hint: Write each numerator as a difference of squares that contains the denominator.
questions.explanation: tan²θ = sec²θ − 1 = (sec θ − 1)(sec θ + 1), leaving sec θ + 1. cot²θ = (csc θ − 1)(csc θ + 1), leaving csc θ − 1. sin²θ = (1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ), leaving 1 + cos θ. 1 − sin²θ = (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ), leaving 1 − sin θ.

questions.q: Simplify (sec θ − 1)(sec θ + 1) / sec²θ to a single term.
questions.hint: Multiply out the numerator first.
questions.explanation: (sec θ − 1)(sec θ + 1) = sec²θ − 1 = tan²θ. Then tan²θ/sec²θ = (sin²θ/cos²θ) · cos²θ = sin²θ.

questions.q: Which of the following is equal to tan θ + cot θ?
questions.hint: Add sin θ/cos θ and cos θ/sin θ over a common denominator.
questions.explanation: tan θ + cot θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ csc θ.

questions.q: Simplify (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) / (tan θ + cot θ) by completing each step.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Denominator as a product of two functions:

questions.hint: sec²θ − tan²θ is a Pythagorean identity.
questions.explanation: The numerator is sec²θ − tan²θ = 1. The denominator is (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ csc θ. So the expression is 1 ÷ (1/(sin θ cos θ)) = sin θ cos θ.

questions.q: Simplify (1 + cot²θ) / (1 + tan²θ).
questions.hint: Replace the numerator and denominator with single squared functions.
questions.explanation: 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ and 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ. csc²θ/sec²θ = (1/sin²θ)·cos²θ = cos²θ/sin²θ = cot²θ.

questions.q: Solve 5 tan x = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
questions.hint: tan x = 0 when sin x = 0.
questions.explanation: tan x = 0 when sin x = 0, which happens at x = 0 and x = π in [0, 2π). 2π is not included in the interval.

questions.q: Solve 3 cos x = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
questions.hint: Where is the x-coordinate on the unit circle equal to 0?
questions.explanation: cos x = 0 at the top and bottom of the unit circle: x = π/2 and x = 3π/2. Negative angles are outside the interval.

questions.q: Match each equation to its solutions for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
questions.hint: Isolate the trig function first.
questions.explanation: cot x = 0 means cos x = 0: π/2, 3π/2. sin x = 0: 0, π. cos x = −1: π. sin x = 1: π/2.

questions.q: How many solutions does 9 cot x = 0 have for 0 ≤ x < 4π?
questions.hint: cot x = 0 exactly when cos x = 0; the interval covers two full turns.
questions.explanation: cot x = 0 when cos x = 0, which is x = π/2 and 3π/2 in each turn. Over [0, 4π) this gives π/2, 3π/2, 5π/2 and 7π/2: 4 solutions.

questions.q: Solve tan x + 2 = 3 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
questions.hint: tan x = 1; tangent is positive in Quadrants I and III.
questions.explanation: tan x = 1. The reference angle is π/4 and tangent is positive in Quadrants I and III, so x = π/4 and 5π/4.

questions.q: Solve √3 tan x + 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
questions.hint: tan x = −1/√3; tangent is negative in Quadrants II and IV.
questions.explanation: tan x = −1/√3 = −√3/3, with reference angle π/6. Tangent is negative in Quadrants II and IV, so x = π − π/6 = 5π/6 and x = 2π − π/6 = 11π/6.

questions.q: Complete the table of solutions for 0 ≤ x < 2π (each equation has one solution in each interval).
questions.hint: Find the reference angle, then use the period π of tangent to get the second solution.
questions.explanation: tan x = −√3 has reference angle π/3 and negative tangent: 2π/3 and 5π/3. tan x = √3/3 has reference angle π/6: π/6 and 7π/6. tan x = −1 has reference angle π/4: 3π/4 and 7π/4. In each row the second solution is the first plus π.

questions.q: Solve cos θ + 1 = 0 for all θ in radians (k is any integer).
questions.hint: cos θ = −1 at only one point of the unit circle.
questions.explanation: cos θ = −1 only at θ = π in one turn. Cosine repeats every 2π, so θ = π + 2kπ.

questions.q: Solve sin θ + 1 = 0 for all θ in radians (k is any integer).
questions.hint: sin θ = −1 at the bottom of the unit circle.
questions.explanation: sin θ = −1 only at θ = 3π/2 in one turn. Sine has period 2π, so θ = 3π/2 + 2kπ. Note −3π/2 + 2kπ gives the points where sin θ = 1.

questions.q: Match each equation to its general solution (k is any integer).
questions.hint: Find the solutions in one turn, then look for a pattern.
questions.explanation: cos θ = 1 only at 0, so θ = 2kπ. sin θ = 0 at 0 and π, which repeat every π: θ = kπ. tan θ = 1 at π/4 and tangent has period π: θ = π/4 + kπ. cos θ = 0 at π/2 and 3π/2, which are π apart: θ = π/2 + kπ.

questions.q: Solve 2 cos θ − 2 = 0 for all θ in radians, where k is any integer.
